docs.title: Presenton OS Internals
docs.text:
Source snapshot: presenton/presenton at the commit mirrored in this repository (v0.9.12-beta line, November 2026) · Tutorial repository: debnathSD/presenton-os

This site is a code-level tutorial on Presenton, the open-source AI presentation generator, followed by a complete engineering design for bringing the same "prompt plus template, out comes a deck" workflow to Apache Superset with slides that are bound to live data instead of screenshots.

It was written by reading the repository file by file. Every chapter cites the exact source paths (and line numbers where they matter) so you can open the code next to the text and verify each claim.

docs.title: How the book is organised
docs.text: Part What it covers Read it if you want to I · Orientation What Presenton is, repository layout, the process topology in Docker and Electron, running it locally Get a mental map before touching code II · Backend FastAPI startup, configuration precedence, the data model, the Standard generation pipeline, prompts, SSE streaming, document ingestion, images/icons/web search, Smart mode, editing and chat, the REST/MCP API surface Change how decks are generated III · Templates The Template v2 JSON format, how a template becomes a JSON schema for the LLM and a rendered slide, custom templates from PPTX, themes and fonts Add or modify designs IV · Frontend Next.js app architecture, the user journey, the slide editor, settings and auth UI Change the UI V · Export How slides become an editable PPTX and a PDF Change the output files VI · Auth, infra, ops Authentication and multi-user isolation, Docker image, Electron app, CI and security Deploy or operate it VII · Superset integration A step-by-step design for a Superset extension plus a generation service that produces data-bound decks, pages and documents from prompts and templates Build the same thing for Superset

docs.title: Reading paths
docs.text:
• "I just want to know how a prompt becomes a PPTX." Read What Presenton is, Runtime topology, then Standard generation pipeline, From template to schema to slide and PPTX and PDF export.
  • "I want to add a new template." Read Part III in order.
  • "I want to integrate Presenton-style generation into my own product." Read REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP and then all of Part VII.
  • "I am going to build the Superset version." Read Parts I, II, III and V first; Part VII assumes them.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Paths are relative to the repository root, for example servers/fastapi/api/main.py.
  • path:line references point at the mirrored snapshot. Line numbers drift as upstream changes, so treat them as "near here".
  • Diagrams are Mermaid; sequence diagrams show request flows, flowcharts show data flows.
  • Blocks marked Gotcha describe behaviour that is easy to get wrong when modifying the code.

docs.title: Where the code is
docs.text:
The mirrored source lives in this same repository, one directory above this tutorial:

presenton-os/
├── servers/fastapi/     Python backend (FastAPI, SQLModel, llmai, python-pptx)
├── servers/nextjs/      Next.js 16 frontend (React 19, Redux Toolkit, Tiptap, Konva)
├── templates/           16 built-in Template v2 designs (template.json + static assets)
├── electron/            Desktop app wrapper
├── scripts/             Build, sync and security helper scripts
├── start.js             Process supervisor used inside the Docker image
├── Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, nginx.conf
└── tutorial/            This site (MkDocs Material)

Start with Part I · Orientation.

docs.title: Endpoint index
docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/**, servers/fastapi/api/v2/**, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py, servers/nextjs/app/api/**/route.ts, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts, nginx.conf · Builds on: REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP, Auth and multi-user · Time: ~30 min (reference)

This appendix is a complete, mechanically built index of every HTTP surface in the Presenton snapshot: all 102 FastAPI application routes, the 11 Next.js API route files, the MCP tools, and every nginx location block. For each FastAPI route you get the method, the full path after all router prefixes, the handler function, the exact decorator line, the access class enforced by SessionAuthMiddleware and the handler, and a one-line purpose. The first steps explain how the index was produced and how to read the access column, so you can rebuild it after upstream changes.

docs.title: Step 1: How the full paths are assembled
docs.text:
FastAPI composes a route's public path from the prefix of every APIRouter it is nested in. Presenton nests routers at most three levels deep. servers/fastapi/api/main.py:68 to servers/fastapi/api/main.py:74 include seven top-level routers on the app:

servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt)
app = FastAPI(lifespan=app_lifespan)

# Routers
app.include_router(API_V1_PPT_ROUTER)
app.include_router(API_V1_WEBHOOK_ROUTER)
app.include_router(API_V1_MOCK_ROUTER)
app.include_router(API_V1_AUTH_ROUTER)
app.include_router(API_V1_ADMIN_ROUTER)
app.include_router(API_V1_ASYNC_TASKS_ROUTER)
app.include_router(API_V2_ROUTER)

API_V1_PPT_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:22, prefix /api/v1/ppt) includes seventeen endpoint routers, API_V1_AUTH_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:27) includes the Presenton Cloud provider router at servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:28, and API_V2_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v2/router.py:6, prefix /api/v2) includes API_V2_PPT_ROUTER (prefix /ppt), which includes PRESENTATION_V2_ROUTER (prefix /presentation).

docs.title: Step 2: How the index was built and checked
docs.text:
The route rows below were extracted with a short Python script that parses every file under servers/fastapi/api/ with the standard ast module, finds every decorator of the form @<NAME>.get|post|put|patch|delete|api_route(...), reads the literal path argument, and joins it with the effective prefix of <NAME> from the table in Step 1. That produced 101 decorated routes. A second pass with grep -E "_ROUTER\.(get|post|put|patch|delete|api_route)" found 102 matches; the extra one is the only route in the codebase registered without decorator syntax:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py (excerpt)
FONTS_ROUTER.post("/check", response_model=FontCheckResponse)(
    check_fonts_in_pptx_handler
)

There is no add_api_route, no @app.get, no api_route and no websocket route anywhere outside the tests. The only other decorator on app is the HTTP middleware at servers/fastapi/api/main.py:106.

As an independent cross-check, the committed OpenAPI document servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json (the file the MCP server loads) contains 93 paths and 100 operations. Every operation in it appears in this index. Two routes in the code are absent from that file: POST /api/v1/ppt/images/test and POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/regenerate.

Gotcha

openai_spec.json is a static snapshot written by servers/fastapi/scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py (json.dumps(app.openapi(), ...)). It is not regenerated at startup. The MCP server reads it at import time (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:281), so if you add or change a route that an MCP tool maps to, you must regenerate the file or the MCP tool keeps the old schema. In this snapshot the file already lags the code by two routes.

Total: 102 FastAPI application routes. On top of those, FastAPI itself serves /openapi.json, /docs, /docs/oauth2-redirect and /redoc, and the app mounts /static (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:86) plus seven owner-scoped static mounts /app_data/{exports,fonts,images,pptx-to-html,pptx-to-json,templates,uploads} created by mount_app_data_assets (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:39) when APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is set.

Route count by area:

Area Routes Area Routes Auth (local + Presenton Cloud link) 9 Images 7 Admin 10 Icons 1 Async tasks 2 Fonts 5 Webhook 2 Templates 14 Mock 2 Providers (models, Ollama, Codex, generation defaults) 15 Presentation (v1) 17 Chat 5 Outlines 3 Community 2 Slide 2 Presentation (v2, Smart) 2 Files 4 Total 102

docs.title: Step 3: How the access class is decided
docs.text:
Access control is applied in two layers. The first is SessionAuthMiddleware.dispatch (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:55), which runs for every request. The second is a per-handler dependency on a few routers.

flowchart TD
    R["Incoming request"] --> D{"PRESENTON_ELECTRON is true"}
    D -->|"yes"| DG["desktop_request_denied: Host, Origin, desktop token"]
    D -->|"no"| A{"DISABLE_AUTH truthy"}
    DG -->|"denied"| X503["503, 403 or 401"]
    DG -->|"allowed"| A
    A -->|"yes"| CP["Presenton Cloud proxy check, then route"]
    A -->|"no"| P{"OPTIONS, public auth path, or path not protected"}
    P -->|"yes"| ROUTE["Route handler"]
    P -->|"no"| U{"Any row in user table"}
    U -->|"no"| E428["428 Login setup is required"]
    U -->|"yes"| PR{"Principal from cookie or Bearer API key"}
    PR -->|"none"| E401["401 Unauthorized"]
    PR -->|"found"| AD{"Admin-only path"}
    AD -->|"yes, and not a JWT admin"| E403["403 Admin browser session required"]
    AD -->|"no, or JWT admin"| OWN["Set owner context vars, cloud proxy, app_data ownership"]
    OWN --> ROUTE

The relevant lists, verbatim:

servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py (excerpt)
class SessionAuthMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    _PUBLIC_AUTH_PATHS = {
        "/api/v1/auth/status",
        "/api/v1/auth/verify",
        "/api/v1/auth/setup",
        "/api/v1/auth/login",
        "/api/v1/auth/logout",
    }
    _PUBLIC_AUTH_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    _PUBLIC_APP_DATA_PREFIXES = (
        "/app_data/fonts/",
        "/app_data/templates/",
    )
    _PROTECTED_NON_API_PATHS = {"/docs", "/openapi.json", "/redoc"}
# ...
            admin_only = (
                path.startswith("/api/v1/admin/")
                or path.startswith("/api/v1/ppt/codex/auth/")
                or (
                    path.startswith("/api/v1/ppt/fonts/")
                    and request.method in {"POST", "DELETE"}
                )
                or path in {
                    "/api/v1/ppt/ollama/models/pull",
                    "/api/v1/ppt/ollama/models/available",
                    "/api/v1/ppt/openai/models/available",
                    "/api/v1/ppt/images/test",
                    "/api/v1/ppt/openrouter/providers/available",
                }
            )

A principal is resolved by resolve_request_principal (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py:22): first the presenton_session cookie (a JWT, method="jwt"), then an Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... API key (method="api_key"). The admin-only check requires principal.method == "jwt" and is_admin, which is why an administrator's API key is still rejected on admin paths.

The legend used in the Access column:

Access value Meaning Public Listed in _PUBLIC_AUTH_PATHS; the middleware lets it through without a principal. The handler may still check the cookie itself. User Any principal: a browser session cookie or a valid user API key. Rows the user does not own are filtered by the ORM owner scope described in Auth and multi-user. Admin (JWT) Matched by the middleware admin_only rule: the caller must be an administrator using a browser session cookie. API keys get 403. User, handler admin The middleware accepts any principal, but the handler dependency (get_current_admin, require_settings_admin or require_presenton_manager) reads only the session cookie and requires is_superuser.

Gotcha

DISABLE_AUTH=true (the Electron runtime) short-circuits the middleware completely: every route is reachable without a principal. However, the admin handlers that depend on get_current_admin (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:219) still read the cookie, find no user, and return 401. So in auth-disabled mode /api/v1/admin/api-keys and /api/v1/admin/users are unusable, while /api/v1/admin/provider-settings works because require_settings_admin returns early when auth is disabled (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:136).

Gotcha

The font rule is method based: every POST or DELETE under /api/v1/ppt/fonts/ is admin only. That includes POST /api/v1/ppt/fonts/check, which only analyzes a PPTX. The custom template hook calls it (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/hooks/useTemplateCreation.ts:150), so a non-admin user running that flow receives a 403 from this call.

Middleware order also matters. Starlette wraps the most recently added middleware outermost, so for a request the order is static_icon_fallback_middleware (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:106), then SessionAuthMiddleware, then UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware, then CORSMiddleware, then the router. A 401 or 403 produced by SessionAuthMiddleware is therefore returned before the CORS layer runs.

docs.title: Step 4: FastAPI routes, auth and admin
Local authentication
docs.text: Method Path Handler Source Access Purpose GET /api/v1/auth/status get_status servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:58 Public Returns configured, authenticated, username, user_id, role for the session cookie. With auth disabled it always answers username: "electron", role: "admin". GET /api/v1/auth/verify verify_session servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:81 Public (handler requires principal) Resolves cookie or API key, 401 if none. If X-Original-URI is present it applies the /app_data ownership rule (403 on mismatch). This is nginx's auth_request target. POST /api/v1/auth/setup setup_credentials servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:110 Public Creates the first account as is_superuser=True, admin_slot="primary". 409 once any user exists. Does not log in (authenticated: false). POST /api/v1/auth/login login servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:155 Public Case-insensitive username lookup, password verify with transparent rehash, sets the presenton_session cookie (30 days, httponly, samesite=lax). 428 before setup. POST /api/v1/auth/logout logout servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:191 Public Deletes the session cookie and returns {"success": true}.

docs.title: Presenton Cloud provider link (OAuth device flow)
docs.text: Method Path Handler Source Access Purpose GET /api/v1/auth/presenton/status presenton_provider_status servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:120 User Reports linked, can_manage, cloud_generation_enabled; email only when the caller can manage the provider. POST /api/v1/auth/presenton/logout logout_presenton_account servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:141 User, handler admin Revokes and clears the global cloud credential. If LLM was presenton, saves LLM: None so the UI must pick a new provider. POST /api/v1/auth/presenton/device/start start_presenton_provider_connection servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:164 User, handler admin Calls {issuer}/oauth/device_authorization; returns the device payload with verification_uri_complete forced to the plain URI, Cache-Control: no-store. POST /api/v1/auth/presenton/device/poll poll_presenton_provider_connection servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/presenton_oauth.py:217 User, handler admin Exchanges device_code at {issuer}/oauth/token; 202 {"status": "pending"} while pending; on success validates userinfo and stores the encrypted token.

docs.title: Admin
docs.text:
Method Path Handler Source Access Purpose GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys list_api_keys servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:44 Admin (JWT) All API keys, newest first, as ApiKeyPublic (no secret). POST /api/v1/admin/api-keys create_api_key servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:60 Admin (JWT) 201. Body user_id, label (default "API client", 1 to 120 chars), expiry_days (default 90, 1 to 365). Response includes the token once. GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys/{api_key_id}/token get_api_key_token servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:85 Admin (JWT) Decrypts and reveals a stored token; 410 if revoked, 409 if not revealable; sends Cache-Control: no-store. POST /api/v1/admin/api-keys/{api_key_id}/revoke revoke_api_key servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:111 Admin (JWT) Sets revoked_at (idempotent) and returns the key. GET /api/v1/admin/provider-settings read_provider_settings servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:144 Admin (JWT) The singleton provider settings row plus PRESENTON_CONNECTED and PRESENTON_EMAIL. PUT /api/v1/admin/provider-settings update_provider_settings servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:158 Admin (JWT) Merges and saves an arbitrary JSON object via save_provider_settings, then reloads env with update_env_with_user_config(). GET /api/v1/admin/users list_users servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:169 Admin (JWT) Users ordered by created_at desc, username asc. POST /api/v1/admin/users create_user servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:182 Admin (JWT) 201. Creates a non-admin user; 409 on a case-insensitive duplicate. PUT /api/v1/admin/users/{user_id}/password reset_user_password servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:215 Admin (JWT) Rehashes the password and increments auth_version, which invalidates the user's existing JWTs. Refuses the admin itself and any superuser. DELETE /api/v1/admin/users/{user_id} delete_user servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:236 Admin (JWT) 204. Deletes a non-admin user (rows cascade) and removes users/{id} under images, exports, uploads, pptx-to-html and pptx-to-json, plus {id} directly under the temp directory. 403 for the admin itself or any superuser.

Gotcha

The admin router rules are enforced twice: by the middleware path rule and by Depends(get_current_admin) or Depends(require_settings_admin). If you move an admin route out of /api/v1/admin/, the middleware stops protecting it and only the dependency remains. If you add a route to API_V1_ADMIN_ROUTER and forget the dependency, the middleware still protects it, but only while auth is enabled.

docs.title: Presentation (v1)
docs.text:
Method Path Handler Source Access Purpose GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all get_all_presentations servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1499 User Dashboard list, newest first. include_slides=true (default) inner-joins the slide with index == 0; version filters v1-standard or v2-standard. GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} get_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1551 User One presentation with all slides ordered by index. Also the data source of the export runtime. DELETE /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} delete_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1572 User 204. Deletes the row; slides cascade through the foreign key. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/duplicate duplicate_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1584 User Deep copies the presentation and its slides with new ids; appends " (Copy)" to the title. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/regenerate regenerate_smart_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1615 User 204. Smart only: deletes the saved slides so the next /stream/{id} starts over. 400 when the provider is Presenton Cloud or the deck is not a generated Smart deck. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export export_existing_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1642 User Body {"export_as": "pptx"} or "pdf". Re-runs the export for a stored deck; returns presentation_id, path, edit_path. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create create_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1681 User Step 1 of the UI flow: inserts a presentations row (version="v2-standard", n_slides=0 meaning auto). No LLM call. Validates slide counts, TOC rule, and community ids (Smart only, max 3). POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create/blank create_blank_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1783 User 201. A one-slide deck titled "Untitled Presentation" with layout __blank_slide__, optionally tied to a template_id. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare prepare_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1840 User Step 3: body presentation_id, outlines, layout (template id, custom- prefix accepted), title. Stores the outline, copies the template layout, and computes structure (LLM unless the layout is ordered), inserting TOC slides. GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/{id} stream_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2281 User Step 4, SSE. Standard: per-slide content, chunk and slide_assets events, then complete. Smart decks are delegated to stream_smart_presentation (slide_html, fonts, generation_metrics). PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update update_presentation servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2527 User Updates n_slides and title; when slides is sent, deletes the caller's slides for the deck and inserts the new list. Used by editor auto-save. PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/slide_update update_presentation_slide servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2585 User Body {"slide": {...}}. Updates one slide in place, excluding id, presentation and index; 400 if the slide belongs to a different deck. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate generate_presentation_sync servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3169 User One-shot API: outline, structure, slides, assets and export in one blocking request. Body GeneratePresentationRequest. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async generate_presentation_async servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3240 User Same work in a BackgroundTasks job. Returns an AsyncTaskModel of type presentation.generate. MCP tool start_standard_presentation. GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/status/{id} check_async_presentation_generation_status servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3282 User Older polling path over the same async_tasks table as /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id}. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/edit edit_presentation_with_new_content servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3301 User Body EditPresentationRequest (presentation_id, slides[{index, content}], export_as). Deep-merges content into matching slides, replaces them, re-exports the same deck. POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/derive derive_presentation_from_existing_one servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3352 User Same body; copies the deck to a new id with the content overrides applied and exports the copy.

A typical async start returns this shape (fields from servers/fastapi/models/sql/async_task.py; owner_id and payload are excluded from serialization):

POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async (response shape)
{
  "id": "task-<64 hex characters>",
  "type": "presentation.generate",
  "status": "pending",
  "message": "Queued for generation",
  "error": null,
  "data": {
    "created_slides": 0,
    "remaining_slides": 8,
    "presentation_id": "<uuid>"
  },
  "created_at": "<timestamp>",
  "updated_at": "<timestamp>"
}

Gotcha

GeneratePresentationRequest.trigger_webhook (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:44) is declared but never read anywhere in the code. generate_presentation_handler dispatches presentation.generation.completed or presentation.generation.failed to every matching subscription unconditionally (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3133 and :3150). Setting trigger_webhook: false does not suppress webhooks.

Gotcha

POST /presentation/edit, /derive, /generate, /generate/async, /status/{id} and /{id}/export are API-surface routes. The Next.js UI does not call them; it exports through its own POST /api/export-presentation route (Step 10). If you change their payloads, only external API and MCP clients are affected.

Both slide endpoints deliberately assign slide.id = uuid.uuid4() before committing. Any client that holds the old slide id (for example to call slide_update next) must read the id from the response. Both mock handlers are named mock_presentation_generation_completed. FastAPI registered each when its decorator ran, so both routes work, but the second definition shadows the first in the module namespace. The two still get distinct OpenAPI operation ids because FastAPI appends the path and method: openai_spec.json lists mock_presentation_generation_completed_api_v1_mock_presentation_generation_failed_get for the failure route.

The webhook POST itself is sent by WebhookService.send_request_to_webhook (servers/fastapi/services/webhook_service.py:36) as JSON with Authorization: Bearer <secret> when a secret was given. Failures are printed and swallowed; there is no retry.

docs.title: Step 9: Paths the Presenton Cloud proxy intercepts
docs.text:
When an administrator links Presenton Cloud and selects LLM=presenton, SessionAuthMiddleware forwards certain requests to the cloud instead of the local handler, through maybe_proxy_presenton_cloud_request (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:407). The matching rule is should_proxy_presenton_cloud (servers/fastapi/services/presenton_cloud_proxy.py:105):

Set Paths CLOUD_GENERATION_PATHS /api/v1/ppt/files/upload, /api/v1/ppt/files/decompose, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/create, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare CLOUD_EDIT_PATHS /api/v1/ppt/slide/edit, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/slide_update CLOUD_SMART_PATHS /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate-html/init, /api/v2/ppt/presentation/update CLOUD_API_PATH_PREFIXES /api/v1/async-tasks, /api/v1/ppt/outlines/, /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/, /api/v1/ppt/template/, /api/v1/ppt/community/presentations, /api/v1/ppt/chat/, /api/v2/ppt/presentation/stream/ CLOUD_PRIVATE_ASSET_PATH_PREFIXES /app_data/images/, /app_data/exports/, /app_data/uploads/, /app_data/pptx-to-html/, /app_data/pptx-to-json/

Gotcha

CLOUD_SMART_PATHS and the /api/v2/ppt/presentation/stream/ prefix name paths that have no local FastAPI route in this snapshot. They only exist upstream on Presenton Cloud. With any other provider selected, a request to them falls through to the router and returns 404. Do not count them as local endpoints. The community prefix is GET-only through the proxy (_READ_ONLY_CLOUD_PREFIXES).

How the cloud proxy rewrites and persists results is outside this index; see Configuration and LLM providers.

docs.title: Step 10: Next.js API routes
docs.text:
The Next.js server exposes its own /api/* routes, separate from FastAPI. All of them pass through proxy.ts first (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:97), whose matcher covers every path except _next/static and favicon.ico. For /api/*, proxy.ts requires a session unless the path is exempt:

servers/nextjs/proxy.ts (excerpt)
function isApiAuthExempt(pathname: string): boolean {
  return (
    pathname.startsWith("/api/v1/auth/") ||
    pathname === "/api/telemetry-status" ||
    /** Public image transform used as a browser/Konva image source. */
    pathname === "/api/update-svg" ||
    pathname.startsWith("/api/export-presentation-data/")
  );
}

It also rewrites /api/v1/*, /api/v2/*, /app_data/* and /static/* to FastAPI (rewriteToFastApi, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:43). In Docker nginx catches those paths first, so the rewrite matters in Electron and in direct next dev setups. A request carrying Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... to a non-FastAPI path gets 403 "API keys are only accepted by the Presenton API".

Route file Methods Access Purpose servers/nextjs/app/api/export-presentation/route.ts POST (:92) Session (also checked in handler) Body {id, format, title}, format pptx or pdf. Runs the bundled export runtime with the caller's cookies, moves the result into exports/users/<user_id>/, returns {success: true, path: "/api/export-presentation/file?name=..."}. servers/nextjs/app/api/export-presentation/file/route.ts GET (:58) Session Query name; rejects traversal and other users' paths; streams the PDF, PPTX or ZIP with Content-Disposition: attachment and Cache-Control: no-store. servers/nextjs/app/api/export-presentation-data/[id]/route.ts GET (:17) Exempt from proxy.ts; requires x-export-cookie header Bridge for the headless export browser: forwards the header value as Cookie to FastAPI GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id} and relays the body and status. servers/nextjs/app/api/github-stars/route.ts GET (:12) Session Fetches stargazers_count of presenton/presenton from the GitHub API; revalidate = 3600; 502 on failure. servers/nextjs/app/api/has-required-key/route.ts GET (:6) Session {hasKey}: whether OPENAI_API_KEY is set in userConfig.json or the environment. servers/nextjs/app/api/read-file/route.ts POST (:8) Session (also checked in handler) Body {filePath}; reads a local file through readReadableLocalFile restricted to the caller's app-data and temp roots. servers/nextjs/app/api/runtime-config/route.ts GET (:7) Session readRuntimeProviderConfig(): provider config from userConfig.json with credential fields replaced by __configured__ and AUTH_* keys dropped. servers/nextjs/app/api/telemetry-status/route.ts GET (:6) Exempt {telemetryEnabled} from DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_TRACKING in env or userConfig.json. servers/nextjs/app/api/update-svg/route.ts GET (:168) Exempt Recolors a local /static/icons/... SVG (max 5 MiB) using color, stroke, fill, strokeWidth, opacities, line cap and join; returns image/svg+xml. servers/nextjs/app/api/upload-image/route.ts POST (:12) Session (also checked in handler) Multipart file up to 20 MiB; saved as <32 hex>.png under uploads/users/<user_id>/; returns {success, filePath}. servers/nextjs/app/api/user-config/route.ts GET (:39), POST (:69) GET: session; POST: admin GET: admins receive FastAPI GET /api/v1/admin/provider-settings, other users the redacted runtime config. POST: requires Content-Type: application/json (415 otherwise) and forwards to PUT /api/v1/admin/provider-settings.

Gotcha

export-presentation-data is exempt from the session check because the headless browser cannot carry the user's cookie jar. It is protected only by requiring the x-export-cookie header, whose value FastAPI then validates as a normal session cookie. The PDF maker page reads that value from the exportCookie query parameter or from the URL fragment (servers/nextjs/app/(export)/pdf-maker/PdfMakerPage.tsx:146), and servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py puts it in the fragment. Browsers do not send fragments to servers, and export_from_url strips the fragment before logging the URL (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:430). See PPTX and PDF export.

For completeness, the Electron preload exposes two IPC channels instead of HTTP routes: export-presentation and read-file (electron/app/preloads/index.ts), handled in electron/app/ipc/export_handlers.ts and electron/app/ipc/read_file.ts. See Electron desktop app.

docs.title: Step 11: MCP tools
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py builds an MCP server with FastMCP.from_openapi over the static openai_spec.json. It runs on 127.0.0.1:8001 with transport http (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:457), forwards every tool call to FastAPI at http://127.0.0.1:8000 with a 600 s read timeout and 15 s connect timeout, and exposes only an allowlist of routes. Everything else is excluded by the final RouteMap(mcp_type=MCPType.EXCLUDE) (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:124).

MCP tool name Generated name it renames HTTP route Enabled when PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE is start_standard_presentation generate_presentation_async_api_v1_ppt_presentation_generate_async_post POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async standard, both list_templates template_list GET /api/v1/ppt/template/all standard, both upload_template_assets mcp_template_upload POST /api/v1/ppt/template/mcp-upload standard, both start_template_generation create_template_api_v1_ppt_template_async_post POST /api/v1/ppt/template/async standard, both start_smart_presentation generate_smart_presentation_async POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart/async smart, both upload_files mcp_files_upload POST /api/v1/ppt/files/mcp-upload always get_job_status check_async_task_status_api_v1_async_tasks_status__id__get GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id} always

The default mode is both (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:24), so a stock deployment advertises all seven tools.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as MCP client
    participant N as nginx /mcp
    participant M as FastMCP on 8001
    participant F as FastAPI on 8000
    C->>N: tools/call with Bearer sk-presenton key
    N->>M: proxy_pass, Host localhost:8001
    M->>M: PresentonTokenVerifier.verify_token
    M->>F: HTTP call with Cookie presenton_session (1 hour JWT)
    F-->>M: JSON result, links made absolute
    M-->>C: tool result

Authentication works as follows. When auth is enabled, create_mcp_auth_provider returns a PresentonTokenVerifier (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:285) that accepts only tokens starting with sk-presenton-, verifies them with the same verify_api_key the REST API uses, and mints an internal session JWT with MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60. attach_request_auth_header (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:365) then sends that JWT to FastAPI as the presenton_session cookie and adds X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, so the long-lived API key never reaches a REST handler. The MCP header makes absolute_mcp_result_links qualify path, edit_path and preview_url with PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL or the forwarded host.

Gotcha

The MCP server is disabled entirely when PRESENTON_ELECTRON is truthy (is_mcp_server_enabled, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:319). It also enforces a host allowlist (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) and origin protection. That is why nginx rewrites the Host header to localhost:8001 for /mcp. A reverse proxy in front of the MCP port that preserves the public Host header gets rejected.

docs.title: Step 12: nginx-served paths
docs.text:
nginx.conf defines one server listening on port 80 with client_max_body_size 100M at the http level. The map blocks at nginx.conf:16 and nginx.conf:20 preserve an outer proxy's X-Forwarded-Proto and X-Forwarded-Host, falling back to nginx's own scheme and Host.

location Line Target Auth Notes / nginx.conf:29 http://localhost:3000 (Next.js) Next.js proxy.ts and layouts WebSocket upgrade headers, Host $http_host, 30 min read and connect timeouts. Also catches /api/* routes that are not v1 or v2, and /redoc. /api/v1/ nginx.conf:45 http://localhost:8000 FastAPI middleware client_max_body_size 110M; 413 handled by @request_entity_too_large; 30 min timeouts. /api/v2/ nginx.conf:59 http://localhost:8000 FastAPI middleware Inherits the 100M body limit; no custom 413 page. @request_entity_too_large nginx.conf:71 none none Returns 413 {"detail":"File size must be less than 100MB."} as JSON. /mcp/ nginx.conf:77 http://localhost:8001/mcp/ FastMCP bearer verifier client_max_body_size 145M; Host localhost:8001. /mcp nginx.conf:94 http://localhost:8001/mcp FastMCP bearer verifier Same settings for the path without a trailing slash. /docs nginx.conf:110 http://localhost:8000/docs FastAPI protected non-API path Swagger UI; needs a session because /docs is in _PROTECTED_NON_API_PATHS. /openapi.json nginx.conf:120 http://localhost:8000/openapi.json FastAPI protected non-API path The live schema (not the static openai_spec.json). = /_auth_check nginx.conf:133 http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/verify internal only Subrequest with X-Original-URI, Cookie and Authorization passed through; body dropped. /static/ nginx.conf:153 alias /app/servers/fastapi/static/ public expires 1y, Cache-Control: public, immutable. The trailing slash is a deliberate traversal fix (comment at nginx.conf:144). /app_data/images/ nginx.conf:159 alias /app_data/images/ auth_request /_auth_check disable_symlinks on, private one-year cache. /app_data/exports/ nginx.conf:167 alias /app_data/exports/ auth_request /_auth_check Same. /app_data/uploads/ nginx.conf:175 alias /app_data/uploads/ auth_request /_auth_check Same. /app_data/fonts/ nginx.conf:183 alias /app_data/fonts/ public Matches _PUBLIC_APP_DATA_PREFIXES in FastAPI. /app_data/templates/ nginx.conf:190 alias /app_data/templates/ public Same. /app_data/pptx-to-html/ nginx.conf:197 alias /app_data/pptx-to-html/ auth_request /_auth_check Same as images. /app_data/pptx-to-json/ nginx.conf:205 alias /app_data/pptx-to-json/ auth_request /_auth_check Same as images.

    B["Browser or API client :80"] --> NG["nginx"]
    NG -->|"/"| NX["Next.js :3000"]
    NG -->|"/api/v1/ and /api/v2/"| FA["FastAPI :8000"]
    NG -->|"/mcp and /mcp/"| MC["FastMCP :8001"]
    NG -->|"/docs and /openapi.json"| FA
    NG -->|"/static/"| ST["files on disk, public"]
    NG -->|"/app_data/private roots"| AR["auth_request /_auth_check"]
    AR --> FA
    AR -->|"2xx"| AD["files on disk"]
    NG -->|"/app_data/fonts and templates"| AD
    MC --> FA
    NX -->|"server-side fetch"| FA

Gotcha

nginx and FastAPI must agree on which /app_data roots are public. nginx hardcodes the five private roots with auth_request and leaves fonts and templates open; FastAPI encodes the same split in PRIVATE_APP_DATA_ROOTS and SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:10) and in _PUBLIC_APP_DATA_PREFIXES. If you add a new asset root, update all three, or nginx will serve it through / to Next.js, which rewrites it back to FastAPI with different auth behavior.

How these processes are started and supervised is covered in Docker build and deployment and Runtime topology.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• The snapshot declares exactly 102 FastAPI routes: 101 decorated handlers plus POST /api/v1/ppt/fonts/check, registered imperatively. The committed openai_spec.json lists 100 of them.
  • Every full path is the concatenation of at most three router prefixes, all listed in Step 1. Five /auth paths are public, a fixed set of paths and prefixes is admin-only with a browser session, and everything else under /api/ accepts any session or user API key.
  • Webhooks fire for every /generate call regardless of trigger_webhook. Several Presenton Cloud proxy paths have no local handler.
  • Next.js adds 11 API route files of its own (12 handlers), guarded by proxy.ts. Four paths are exempt from the session check there.
  • MCP exposes at most seven tools, renamed from OpenAPI operation ids and filtered by PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE. It authenticates with sk-presenton- keys and calls FastAPI with a short-lived session cookie.
  • nginx routes /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ to FastAPI, /mcp to the MCP server, /static/ and /app_data/ straight from disk (private roots gated by /_auth_check), and everything else to Next.js.

Reads: the whole repository at snapshot 571461f · Builds on: Repository tour · Time: reference, skim as needed

This appendix is an annotated map of roughly 320 source and configuration files, grouped by directory, chosen because they carry behavior you will meet when reading or changing Presenton. Each row gives the file's line count at the snapshot, a one-line statement of its responsibility written after reading it, and the chapter that explains it in depth. Use it as a lookup table: find the file behind a stack trace, an endpoint, or a concept, then jump to the chapter.

The UI enforces limits from servers/nextjs/utils/presentationLimits.ts, while FastAPI enforces MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES and MAX_OUTLINE_WORDS from servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py. All 16 template folders share this shape plus a static/ asset folder. 16

Gotcha

templates/<name>/template.json is not read at request time. import_default_templates_on_startup copies it into the template_v2 table on every boot (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:64). Editing a built-in template file requires a restart, and edits made to a default template through the API are blocked (_require_private_template) because the next boot would overwrite them.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Where every major responsibility lives: routers in servers/fastapi/api, persistence in models/sql and services/database.py, generation in utils/llm_calls and templates/v2, and UI in servers/nextjs/app and components/slide-editor.
  • Which files are the largest and densest: presentation.py (3393 lines), template.py (2175), services/chat/memory_layer.py (4131), templates/v2/certified_generation.py (4633), slide-editor/surface/nodes.tsx (6548) and lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts (4145).
  • Which concerns are duplicated across FastAPI, Next.js and Electron and must change together.
  • That built-in templates are imported from templates/*/template.json at startup, not served from disk.
