docs.title: 9.2 Packing rules (new)
docs.text:
These are GCK's rules, chosen to produce dashboards that look hand-built at 12 columns.

Blocks in a section Components section title HEADER (MEDIUM_HEADER) in the grid or tab, never in a row (rows cannot hold headers) heading block HEADER (LARGE_HEADER for level 1, MEDIUM_HEADER for 2, SMALL_HEADER for 3) 1 to 4 consecutive metric blocks one ROW; width floor(12 / n), remainder added to the last; height 25 (the bundled example's big number height) more than 4 metrics rows of 4 at width 3 chart followed by text blocks, or layoutHint: "chart_with_notes" one ROW: CHART width 8 height 50 and a MARKDOWN width 4 height 50 with the following text blocks chart alone, or two consecutive charts with layoutHint: "two_up" ROW with one chart at width 12 or two at width 6; height 50 table ROW with a CHART at width 12, height 50 consecutive text blocks (paragraph, list, quote, callout, image) one MARKDOWN at width 12, height estimated from text length, clamped to 5 to 100 units divider DIVIDER in the grid or tab

The layout catalog for this target lists the hints the engine may choose: auto, kpi_strip, chart_with_notes, two_up and full_width.

docs.title: 9.3 toNative
9.4 json_metadata and apply
docs.text:
Superset's own editor does not save layouts through position_json. It puts the layout into json_metadata.positions and PUTs that (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/dashboard/components/Header/index.tsx:465). On the backend, DashboardDAO.set_dash_metadata (apache/superset: superset/daos/dashboard.py:820) reads positions, rebuilds the dashboard's chart membership (dashboard.slices) from the CHART nodes, writes uuid into every chart node, and stores the result as position_json (dashboard.py:920). Create runs the same function when json_metadata is present (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/create.py:67). The adapter therefore always sends the layout inside json_metadata.positions, and also as position_json.

DashboardPostSchema (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/schemas.py:460) accepts dashboard_title (up to 500 characters), slug, description, editors, viewers, position_json (validated only as JSON, validate_json, schemas.py:115), css, theme_id, json_metadata (validated against DashboardJSONMetadataSchema, which includes positions, schemas.py:201 and :222), published, certified_by, certification_details, is_managed_externally, external_url and uuid. The endpoint is POST /api/v1/dashboard/ (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/api.py:1029), answering 201 with id, result and uuid (api.py:1085). Updates go to PUT /api/v1/dashboard/<pk> (api.py:1097, schema DashboardPutSchema, schemas.py:535).

gck/packages/target-superset-dashboard/src/apply.ts (new)
import type { ApplyMode, ApplyResult } from "@gck/protocol";
import type { HostApi } from "@gck/core";
import type { DashboardNative, LayoutNode, Positions } from "./to-native";

type SupersetHttp = { request(path: string, init: { method: string; body?: unknown }): Promise<any> };  // CSRF handled by host
const POSITION_LIMIT_DEFAULT = 65535;

export async function applyDashboard(n: DashboardNative, host: HostApi, requested: ApplyMode,
                                     target?: { dashboardId: number }): Promise<ApplyResult> {
  // No applyPatch in v1: "patch" is not in applyModes and falls back to "replace".
  const mode: ApplyMode = requested === "patch" ? "replace" : requested;
  const warnings = [...(requested === "patch"
    ? ["patch_unsupported: superset-dashboard has no patch mode in v1, applied as replace"] : []), ...n.warnings];
  const http = host.capability<SupersetHttp>("superset.http");
  const limit = host.capability<number>("superset.positionLimit") ?? POSITION_LIMIT_DEFAULT;
  if (!http) return { ok: false, mode, warnings: ["no superset.http capability"] };

  if (!target) {                                                    // new dashboard
    const positions = n.positions;
    if (JSON.stringify(positions).length >= limit) return { ok: false, mode, warnings: ["layout exceeds position limit"] };
    const metadata = { positions, color_scheme: "", label_colors: {}, refresh_frequency: 0,
                       expanded_slices: {}, timed_refresh_immune_slices: [], cross_filters_enabled: true };
    const res = await http.request("/api/v1/dashboard/", { method: "POST", body: {
      dashboard_title: n.title.slice(0, 500), published: false,
      position_json: JSON.stringify(positions), json_metadata: JSON.stringify(metadata) } });
    return { ok: true, mode, nativeRef: { dashboardId: res.id, uuid: res.uuid }, warnings };
  }

  // Add one tab to an existing dashboard (or rebuild this artifact's own tab), keeping every existing id.
  const current = (await http.request(`/api/v1/dashboard/${target.dashboardId}`, { method: "GET" })).result;
  const before = JSON.parse(current.position_json || "{}") as Positions;
  const meta = JSON.parse(current.json_metadata || "{}");
  const merged = addAsTab(before, n, mode === "replace");
  if (JSON.stringify(merged).length >= limit) return { ok: false, mode, warnings: ["layout exceeds position limit"] };
  await http.request(`/api/v1/dashboard/${target.dashboardId}`, { method: "PUT", body: {
    position_json: JSON.stringify(merged), json_metadata: JSON.stringify({ ...meta, positions: merged }) } });
  return { ok: true, mode, nativeRef: { dashboardId: target.dashboardId }, warnings,
           undo: async () => { await http.request(`/api/v1/dashboard/${target.dashboardId}`, { method: "PUT", body: {
             position_json: JSON.stringify(before), json_metadata: JSON.stringify({ ...meta, positions: before }) } }); } };
}

export function addAsTab(before: Positions, n: DashboardNative, replace = false): Positions {
  const p: Positions = structuredClone(before);
  if (!p.ROOT_ID) {                                          // legacy dashboards can have an empty position_json
    p.DASHBOARD_VERSION_KEY = "v2";
    p.ROOT_ID = { type: "ROOT", id: "ROOT_ID", children: ["GRID_ID"] };
    p.GRID_ID = { type: "GRID", id: "GRID_ID", children: [], parents: ["ROOT_ID"] };
  }
  const root = p.ROOT_ID as LayoutNode;
  let tabs = (p[root.children[0]] as LayoutNode | undefined);
  if (!tabs || tabs.type !== "TABS") {                       // wrap the flat grid into a first tab
    const grid = p.GRID_ID as LayoutNode;
    tabs = { type: "TABS", id: "TABS-gck-root", children: [], meta: {} };
    const first: LayoutNode = { type: "TAB", id: "TAB-gck-overview", children: [...grid.children], meta: { text: "Overview" } };
    p[tabs.id] = tabs; p[first.id] = first; tabs.children.push(first.id);
    grid.children = []; root.children = [tabs.id];
  }
  const tabId = `TAB-gck-${n.key}`;
  const existing = p[tabId] as LayoutNode | undefined;
  if (existing && !replace) throw new Error("this artifact was already added to the dashboard");
  const newTab: LayoutNode = existing ?? { type: "TAB", id: tabId, children: [], meta: {} };
  if (existing) {                                            // replace: empty the artifact's own tab, keep its id
    const drop = (id: string) => { (p[id] as LayoutNode).children.forEach(drop); delete p[id]; };
    existing.children.forEach(drop);
    existing.children = [];
  } else {
    p[tabId] = newTab; tabs.children.push(tabId);
  }
  newTab.meta = { ...newTab.meta, text: n.title };
  const src = n.positions[n.rootContainerId] as LayoutNode;  // GRID_ID of the generated layout (tabs: false)
  const copy = (id: string) => {
    if (p[id]) throw new Error(`component ${id} already exists`);
    const c = structuredClone(n.positions[id] as LayoutNode); p[id] = c; c.children.forEach(copy);
  };
  src.children.forEach((id) => { copy(id); newTab.children.push(id); });
  const visit = (id: string, trail: string[]) => {           // recompute parents for the whole tree
    const node = p[id] as LayoutNode;
    if (id !== "ROOT_ID") node.parents = trail;
    node.children.forEach((c) => visit(c, [...trail, id]));
  };
  visit("ROOT_ID", []);
  return p;
}

The undo for an existing dashboard is "PUT the previous layout back", which is the blueprint's rule for this host (keep the previous position_json for revert). For a new dashboard, undo is deletion, which the UI offers as an explicit action rather than an automatic one.

The adapter, createSupersetDashboardTarget({ tabs, chartNames, dashboardId? }), returns a TargetAdapter<DashboardNative> whose toNative is toPositions and whose apply is applyDashboard: without dashboardId it creates a new dashboard, with one it adds the artifact as a tab of that dashboard, and in that case it always calls toPositions with tabs: false, because addAsTab copies the children of the generated GRID_ID. Its manifest lists applyModes: ["append", "replace"]. On an existing dashboard, append adds the artifact's tab and refuses if it is already there; replace rebuilds the artifact's own tab (TAB-gck-<key>, where the key comes from the artifact id, which an edit run keeps) and leaves every other tab alone. The adapter has no applyPatch in v1: position-level patching would need block-to-component bookkeeping across ROW packing, and rebuilding one tab is cheap. A "patch" request is applied as replace with a patch_unsupported warning.

Gotcha: replace keeps the tab id on purpose

addAsTab with replace empties the existing TAB-gck-<key> and refills it, instead of deleting the tab and adding a new one. A report scheduled on that tab therefore survives the edit; a new tab id would make process_tab_diff deactivate it (see "keep existing tab ids" below). Component ids inside the tab are derived from block ids, so unchanged blocks also get their old component ids back.

Gotcha: charts must exist and be readable, and the dashboard must be yours to edit

set_dash_metadata resolves every chartId in the layout. A node whose chart does not resolve to any row is replaced by a markdown placeholder (_repair_dangling_chart_nodes, apache/superset: superset/daos/dashboard.py:185), a non-numeric chartId fails the save (_reject_malformed_chart_nodes, :254), and a chart the caller cannot read is refused unless the caller is an admin (_raise_for_unreadable_new_charts, :325). A PUT additionally requires the user to be an editor of the dashboard (security_manager.raise_for_editorship, apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/update.py:170). The engine's I10 check (only allowedChartIds) and the catalog's per-user listing make the first two unlikely; the third is checked by the host before it offers "Add as tab", using the dashboard's editors.

Gotcha: always send the full metadata back

When positions is present, set_dash_metadata rebuilds default_filters from the payload (dashboard.py:952), drops color_namespace if absent (:965), and resets shared_label_colors, map_label_colors and color_scheme_domain to empty when they are missing. A PUT whose json_metadata is only {"positions": ...} would quietly reset those. applyDashboard spreads the dashboard's current json_metadata and replaces only positions, exactly as Superset's own save does.

Gotcha: keep existing tab ids

UpdateDashboardCommand.process_tab_diff (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/update.py:286) compares the incoming position_json with the stored tabs and deactivates every report that targeted a tab that disappeared, emailing its owners. Regenerating ids for existing tabs while adding a new one would trigger that. addAsTab only adds nodes; when it wraps a flat grid into a first tab, no tab existed before, so nothing can be deactivated.

Gotcha: the layout has a size limit

SUPERSET_DASHBOARD_POSITION_DATA_LIMIT defaults to 65,535 characters (apache/superset: superset/config.py:251), and Superset's editor refuses to save a larger layout (Header/index.tsx:472). Markdown code counts toward that limit, so long generated narratives in many MARKDOWN components can exceed it on a busy dashboard. The adapter checks before sending, and the host can pass the server's configured value as the superset.positionLimit capability.

Chart types come from the saved chart

A chart block's chartType is ignored by this target: the CHART component renders the saved chart with its own visualization type. The engine's prompt for this target says so, and the preview draws the saved chart's thumbnail instead of a Chart.js rendering.

docs.title: Step 10: @gck/target-text
docs.text:
The text target is the simplest and the most reused: the dashboard target uses it for MARKDOWN components, and the Superset host uses it for alert and report narratives and for the "text" surfaces described in Host integrations. It has four output profiles.

Profile Used for Headings Data blocks Escaping markdown Superset Markdown components, chat # levels chart and table as a Markdown table from the snapshot, metric as bold value Markdown punctuation escaped in plain segments plain SMS, notifications, title fields none (uppercased line) Label: value lines none html Superset Markdown components when HTML is wanted h2 to h4 <table> full HTML escaping, then sanitizing email report description (email body) <p><strong> <table> allowlist of Superset's email sanitizer

Superset renders Markdown components with SafeMarkdown (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/dashboard/components/gridComponents/Markdown/Markdown.tsx:348), which uses remark-gfm (so pipe tables work) and rehype-sanitize when HTML_SANITIZATION is on, its default (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1646). Report emails take the schedule's description (apache/superset: superset/commands/report/execute.py:1729) and clean it with nh3 against a fixed allowlist: a, abbr, acronym, b, blockquote, br, code, div, em, i, li, ol, p, strong, ul and the table tags (ALLOWED_TAGS, apache/superset: superset/reports/notifications/email.py:50; nh3.clean, :295).

gck/packages/target-text/src/index.ts (new)
import type { Artifact, Block, ChartSnapshot, RichText, TableSnapshot } from "@gck/protocol";
import { resolveToken } from "@gck/core";

export type TextProfile = "markdown" | "plain" | "html" | "email";
export type TextOptions = { headings?: boolean; maxChars?: number };

const escMd = (s: string) => s.replace(/([\\`*_[\]#|<>])/g, "\\$1");
const escHtml = (s: string) => s.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&", "<": "<", ">": ">", '"': """, "'": "'" })[c]!);
const safeHref = (h?: string) => (h && /^(https?:|mailto:)/i.test(h) ? h : undefined);

function inline(rt: RichText, a: Artifact, p: TextProfile): string {
  return rt.map((s) => {
    const raw = s.token ? resolveToken(a.bindings[s.token.bindingId], s.token.field, s.token.format).display : s.text;
    if (p === "plain") return raw;
    const m = new Set(s.marks ?? []);
    if (p === "markdown") {
      let t = escMd(raw);
      if (m.has("code")) t = `\`${raw.replace(/`/g, "")}\``;
      if (m.has("bold")) t = `**${t}**`;
      if (m.has("italic")) t = `*${t}*`;
      const href = safeHref(s.href);
      return m.has("link") && href ? `[${t}](${href})` : t;
    }
    let t = escHtml(raw);
    if (m.has("code")) t = `<code>${t}</code>`;
    if (m.has("bold")) t = `<strong>${t}</strong>`;
    if (m.has("italic")) t = `<em>${t}</em>`;
    const href = safeHref(s.href);
    return m.has("link") && href ? `<a href="${escHtml(href)}">${t}</a>` : t;
  }).join("");
}

function dataRows(b: Extract<Block, { bindingId: string }>, a: Artifact): { head: string[]; rows: string[][] } | null {
  const binding = a.bindings[b.bindingId];
  if (!binding?.snapshot || binding.status === "forbidden") return null;
  if (binding.kind === "chart") {
    const s = binding.snapshot as ChartSnapshot;
    return { head: ["", ...s.series.map((x) => x.name)],
             rows: s.categories.map((c, i) => [c, ...s.series.map((x) => resolveFormatted(binding, x.values[i]))]) };
  }
  if (binding.kind === "table") {
    const s = binding.snapshot as TableSnapshot;
    const cols = (b.type === "table" && b.columns) || s.columns;
    const limit = (b.type === "table" && b.maxRows) || 10;
    return { head: cols, rows: s.rows.slice(0, limit).map((_, r) =>
      cols.map((c) => resolveToken(binding, `cell:${r}:${c}`).display)) };
  }
  return null;
}
const resolveFormatted = (b: any, v: number | undefined) =>
  v == null ? "" : resolveToken({ ...b, kind: "metric", snapshot: { value: v } }, "value").display;

function blockText(b: Block, a: Artifact, p: TextProfile, o: TextOptions): string {
  const md = p === "markdown", html = p === "html" || p === "email";
  switch (b.type) {
    case "heading": {
      if (o.headings === false || p === "plain") return p === "plain" ? inline(b.text, a, p).toUpperCase() : `**${inline(b.text, a, p)}**`;
      if (md) return `${"#".repeat(b.level + 1)} ${inline(b.text, a, p)}`;
      return p === "email" ? `<p><strong>${inline(b.text, a, p)}</strong></p>` : `<h${b.level + 1}>${inline(b.text, a, p)}</h${b.level + 1}>`;
    }
    case "paragraph": return html ? `<p>${inline(b.text, a, p)}</p>` : inline(b.text, a, p);
    case "quote": case "callout": {
      const label = b.type === "callout" ? { info: "Note", warning: "Warning", success: "Success" }[b.tone] : "";
      const body = inline(b.text, a, p);
      if (md) return `> ${label ? `**${label}:** ` : ""}${body}`;
      if (html) return `<blockquote>${label ? `<strong>${label}:</strong> ` : ""}${body}</blockquote>`;
      return `${label ? `${label}: ` : ""}${body}`;
    }
    case "list": {
      const items = b.items.map((it) => inline(it, a, p));
      if (html) return `<${b.ordered ? "ol" : "ul"}>${items.map((i) => `<li>${i}</li>`).join("")}</${b.ordered ? "ol" : "ul"}>`;
      return items.map((i, n) => `${b.ordered ? `${n + 1}.` : "-"} ${i}`).join("\n");
    }
    case "metric": {
      const binding = a.bindings[b.bindingId];
      const value = resolveToken(binding, "value").display;
      const delta = b.compare ? ` (${resolveToken(binding, "delta_pct").display} vs previous period)` : "";
      if (md) return `**${escMd(b.label)}:** ${value}${delta}`;
      if (html) return `<p><strong>${escHtml(b.label)}:</strong> ${escHtml(value + delta)}</p>`;
      return `${b.label}: ${value}${delta}`;
    }
    case "chart": case "table": {
      const t = dataRows(b, a);
      const caption = b.type === "chart" ? b.title ?? "" : "";
      if (!t) return md ? `*${escMd(caption || "Data not available")}*` : caption || "Data not available";
      if (md) return [caption && `**${escMd(caption)}**`, `| ${t.head.map(escMd).join(" | ")} |`,
        `|${t.head.map(() => " --- ").join("|")}|`, ...t.rows.map((r) => `| ${r.map(escMd).join(" | ")} |`)].filter(Boolean).join("\n");
      if (html) return `<table><thead><tr>${t.head.map((h) => `<th>${escHtml(h)}</th>`).join("")}</tr></thead><tbody>${
        t.rows.map((r) => `<tr>${r.map((c) => `<td>${escHtml(c)}</td>`).join("")}</tr>`).join("")}</tbody></table>`;
      return t.rows.map((r) => r.join(", ")).join("\n");
    }
    case "image": {
      if (!b.url || !/^https:/.test(b.url) || p === "email" || p === "plain") return b.alt;
      return md ? `![${escMd(b.alt)}](${b.url})` : `<img src="${escHtml(b.url)}" alt="${escHtml(b.alt)}">`;
    }
    case "divider": return md ? "---" : html ? (p === "email" ? "<br>" : "<hr>") : "";
  }
}

export function render(a: Artifact, p: TextProfile, o: TextOptions = {}): string {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const max = o.maxChars ?? Infinity;
  let used = 0;
  for (const s of a.sections) {
    const parts = [
      ...(s.title && o.headings !== false ? [blockText({ id: s.id, type: "heading", level: 1, text: [{ text: s.title }] }, a, p, o)] : []),
      ...s.blocks.map((b) => blockText(b, a, p, o)),
    ].filter(Boolean);
    for (const part of parts) {
      if (used + part.length + 2 > max) { out.push(p === "markdown" || p === "plain" ? "…" : "<p>…</p>"); return out.join("\n\n"); }
      out.push(part); used += part.length + 2;
    }
  }
  return out.join(p === "html" || p === "email" ? "\n" : "\n\n");
}

export const toMarkdown = (a: Artifact, o?: TextOptions) => render(a, "markdown", o);

Two details carry the safety story. Every plain segment is escaped for its profile before any markup is added, so model text can never introduce tags or Markdown links; and links pass safeHref, which allows only http, https and mailto. The HTML the adapter produces is still sanitized again by the consumer (Superset's rehype-sanitize or nh3), which is the right layering: treat model output as untrusted twice. Truncation (maxChars) only cuts at block boundaries and appends an ellipsis block, so a table or list is never cut in half; this is how the text target honors limits such as a notification length. The package's adapter, textTarget: TargetAdapter<TextNative>, uses type TextNative = { markdown: string } and fills it with toMarkdown; hosts that need another profile call render directly.

gck/packages/target-text/src/adapter.ts (new, excerpt)
import type { TargetAdapter } from "@gck/core";
import { toMarkdown } from "./index";

export type TextNative = { markdown: string };

export const textTarget: TargetAdapter<TextNative> = {
  manifest: {
    id: "text", version: "1.0.0",
    blocks: ["heading", "paragraph", "list", "callout", "quote", "divider"],
    sectionKinds: ["section"],
    limits: { maxSections: 6, maxBlocksPerSection: 12, maxCharsPerBlock: 1200 },
    applyModes: ["replace", "append", "insert_at_cursor", "patch"],
    promptHints: "Plain business prose. Short paragraphs. Numbers only as data tokens. No HTML.",
  },
  toNative: (a) => ({ markdown: toMarkdown(a) }),
  // loadPreview: the text preview from "@gck/target-text/react"
  // apply: commits nothing itself; hosts act on gck.applied or wrap apply (Host integrations)
  async apply(_native, _host, mode) { return { ok: true, mode, warnings: [] }; },
  // Text has no stable sub-structure to patch: re-render the final artifact and commit it as a replace.
  async applyPatch(_native, _diff, artifact, host) {
    const result = await this.apply({ markdown: toMarkdown(artifact) }, host, "replace");
    return { ...result, mode: "patch" };
  },
};

applyPatch goes through this.apply rather than calling the function above directly, so a host that spreads textTarget and replaces apply with its own commit (the Superset Markdown target in Host integrations) also gets patch for free: an edit run on a Markdown component overwrites meta.code exactly like replace. The controller calls applyPatch as a method of the registered adapter, which is what makes this the host's wrapper.

Gotcha: the email profile has no headings and no images

ALLOWED_TAGS for report emails contains no h1 to h6 and no img, so nh3 would strip them and leave bare text. The email profile renders headings as <p><strong> and images as their alt text, which survives the sanitizer unchanged.

docs.title: Step 11: Worked example
docs.text:
A user on the EMEA Sales dashboard types:

Write a QBR summary for EMEA from the Sales dashboard: headline numbers, the revenue trend, and where revenue came from.

The run carries target: tiptap-doc (the user is in a Tiptap page) and data.allowedChartIds: [410, 411, 412, 413, 414]. The catalog turns them into b_c410 (revenue, big number, metric), b_c411 (orders, metric), b_c412 (average deal size, metric), b_c413 (revenue by month, bar, chart) and b_c414 (top countries, table). Snapshot values are illustrative.

The Artifact (full JSON) 
{
  "id": "art_01JCB7Q2Z8X4N5K6M7P8R9S0T1",
  "version": "gck.artifact/1",
  "title": "EMEA quarterly business review",
  "language": "en",
  "target": "tiptap-doc",
  "sections": [
    {
      "id": "sec_k3m9q200", "kind": "section", "title": "Quarter at a glance", "layoutHint": null,
      "blocks": [
        {"id": "blk_k3m9q20000", "type": "paragraph", "text": [
          {"text": "EMEA closed the quarter at "},

"Sep 2026" is a token here because it is data (the best month could change on refresh); written as plain text it would also pass, through the calendar allowlist, but it would then be frozen. The table binding shows why per-column formats exist: without format.columns.revenue_share, the share column would be rendered through the binding's currency format and print $0 for 0.359. docs.title: Step 12: Testing adapters
docs.text:
Adapters are pure, so their tests need no LLM and no running host.

Golden files. Each target keeps fixtures/artifacts/*.json (shared across targets, including the worked example and edge cases: empty sections, forbidden bindings, unknown block types, maximum limits) and golden/<target>/*.json|md|html. The test serializes, pretty-prints with sorted keys, and compares. Updating a golden file is an explicit command, so a change in output always shows up in review.

gck/packages/target-superset-dashboard/test/golden.test.ts (new)
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { expect, test } from "vitest";
import { toPositions } from "../src/to-native";

const dir = new URL("../../../fixtures/artifacts/", import.meta.url);
for (const file of readdirSync(dir)) {
  test(`positions for ${file}`, async () => {
    const artifact = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL(file, dir), "utf8"));
    const out = toPositions(artifact, { tabs: false, chartNames: { 410: "Revenue", 413: "Revenue by month" } });
    await expect(JSON.stringify(out, null, 2)).toMatchFileSnapshot(`../golden/${file}`);
  });
}

Structural checks against the host's own rules. Golden files prove stability, not validity. The dashboard tests also walk every generated layout with a port of Superset's nesting table (isValidChild.ts:58) and assert that every row's widths sum to at most 12; the Tiptap tests build a real editor schema from [StarterKit, ...gckNodes] with getSchema from @tiptap/core and call schema.nodeFromJSON(doc).check() on every output; the text tests run the email profile through an nh3-equivalent sanitizer with Superset's allowlist and assert the output is unchanged by sanitizing.

Round-trip tests. For the Tiptap target the core property is fromHost(toNative(a)) equals a, ids included (they travel in gckBlockId), except for the lossy cases listed in 8.1 and the section fields the document does not hold (layoutHint):

gck/packages/target-tiptap/test/roundtrip.test.ts (new)
import { expect, test } from "vitest";
import { toProseMirror } from "../src/to-native";
import { fromProseMirror } from "../src/from-host";
import example from "../../../fixtures/artifacts/qbr-emea.json";

const normalize = (sections: any[]) => sections.map((s) => ({ id: s.id, title: s.title, blocks: s.blocks }));

test("tiptap round trip keeps ids, blocks, tokens and data nodes", () => {
  const doc = toProseMirror(example as any, { includeTitle: true, hasImageNode: false, maxHeading: 6 });
  const back = fromProseMirror(doc);
  expect(back.title).toBe(example.title);
  expect(normalize(back.sections!)).toEqual(normalize(example.sections));
});

The comparison drops text caches of token segments only if the fixture was produced with different snapshots; with the fixture's own snapshots, the cached display equals the re-rendered one and the test compares them too. Marks on token segments (the bold $591k) survive because inline puts them on the gckToken node and rich reads them back.

Patch tests. patchEditor runs against a real editor. Tiptap 3 can create an editor without an element (element: null), so the test needs no mounting; it checks the document after the patch, that content the artifact does not own survives, and that one undo restores the original:

gck/packages/target-tiptap/test/patch.test.ts (new)
// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { Editor } from "@tiptap/core";
import StarterKit from "@tiptap/starter-kit";
import { expect, test } from "vitest";
import { createHost } from "@gck/core";
import type { Artifact } from "@gck/protocol";
import { GckBlockIds } from "../src/block-ids";
import { fromProseMirror } from "../src/from-host";
import { patchEditor } from "../src/patch";
import { toProseMirror, type TiptapOptions } from "../src/to-native";

const o: TiptapOptions = { includeTitle: false, hasImageNode: false, maxHeading: 6 };
const para = (id: string, text: string) => ({ id, type: "paragraph" as const, text: [{ text }] });
const base: Artifact = {
  id: "art_01JCB7Q2Z8X4N5K6M7P8R9S0T1", version: "gck.artifact/1", title: "Notes", target: "tiptap-doc",
  bindings: {}, provenance: { runId: "run_test", createdAt: "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z", prompt: "notes" },
  sections: [{ id: "sec_test00", kind: "section", title: "Plan",
               blocks: [para("blk_test0000", "First idea"), para("blk_test0001", "Second idea")] }],
};
const handTyped = { type: "paragraph", content: [{ type: "text", text: "Typed by hand" }] };
const text = (e: Editor) => e.getText({ blockSeparator: "|" });

test("patch changes, removes and adds blocks in one undo step", async () => {
  const editor = new Editor({ element: null, extensions: [StarterKit, GckBlockIds],
    content: { type: "doc", content: [...toProseMirror(base, o).content!, handTyped] } });
  const next: Artifact = { ...base, sections: [{ ...base.sections[0], title: "Plan B",
    blocks: [para("blk_test0000", "First idea, sharper"), para("blk_test0002", "Third idea")] }] };

  const result = await patchEditor(toProseMirror(next, o),
    { added: ["blk_test0002"], removed: ["blk_test0001"], changed: ["blk_test0000"] },
    next, createHost("tiptap", { "tiptap.editor": editor }));

  expect(result.ok).toBe(true);
  expect(text(editor)).toBe("Plan B|First idea, sharper|Third idea|Typed by hand");
  const back = fromProseMirror(editor.getJSON() as any);
  expect(back.sections![0].id).toBe("sec_test00");
  expect(back.sections![0].blocks.slice(0, 2).map((b) => b.id)).toEqual(["blk_test0000", "blk_test0002"]);

  editor.commands.undo();
  expect(text(editor)).toBe("Plan|First idea|Second idea|Typed by hand");
});

test("a changed block the user deleted fails the patch instead of skipping it", async () => {
  const editor = new Editor({ element: null, extensions: [StarterKit, GckBlockIds], content: { type: "doc", content: [handTyped] } });
  const result = await patchEditor(toProseMirror(base, o), { added: [], removed: [], changed: ["blk_test0000"] },
    base, createHost("tiptap", { "tiptap.editor": editor }));
  expect(result).toMatchObject({ ok: false, warnings: ["patch_anchor_missing: blk_test0000"] });
});

The section title change ("Plan" to "Plan B") is not in the diff; the first test also proves that patchEditor reconciles headings from the artifact. The text target's equivalent test is a single assertion in its own package: textTarget.applyPatch hands apply the Markdown of the final artifact with mode replace, and returns that result with mode: "patch". A property-based variant (fast-check) generates random Artifacts within the manifest and checks the same equality, which is how mark-ordering and empty-segment bugs are found.

Schema contract tests shared with the engine. @gck/protocol publishes artifact-1.schema.json and a fixture corpus split into valid/ and invalid/ (each invalid file names the expected issue code). Three suites consume the same files:

Suite Language Assertion protocol TypeScript (Ajv, draft 2020-12) every valid/ file passes the schema, every invalid/ file that is a shape error fails it engine models Python (pytest) Artifact.model_validate accepts valid/ and rejects shape errors; validate_artifact returns exactly the expected codes for invariant errors schema drift Python every property in Artifact.model_json_schema() exists in artifact-1.schema.json with a compatible type, and vice versa gck_engine/tests/test_contract.py (new)
import json
import pathlib

import pytest
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator

from gck_engine.spec.artifact import Artifact
from gck_engine.spec.validate import validate_artifact

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).parents[2] / "gck" / "packages" / "protocol"
SCHEMA = json.loads((ROOT / "schemas" / "artifact-1.schema.json").read_text())


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", sorted((ROOT / "fixtures" / "valid").glob("*.json")))
def test_valid_fixtures(path, test_manifest, allowed_ids, display):
    doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
    Draft202012Validator(SCHEMA).validate(doc)
    assert validate_artifact(Artifact.model_validate(doc), test_manifest, allowed_ids, display) == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", sorted((ROOT / "fixtures" / "invalid").glob("*.json")))
def test_invalid_fixtures(path, test_manifest, allowed_ids, display):
    case = json.loads(path.read_text())
    try:
        artifact = Artifact.model_validate(case["artifact"])
    except Exception:
        assert case["expect"] == "SHAPE"
        return
    codes = {i.code for i in validate_artifact(artifact, test_manifest, allowed_ids, display)}
    assert case["expect"] in codes

The engine also snapshot-tests build_response_schema for every published manifest, and runs each resulting schema through ensure_strict_json_schema (servers/fastapi/utils/schema_utils.py:92): a manifest change that produced a schema the strict normalizer would rewrite (a missing required, an object without additionalProperties) fails CI before any provider sees it. Storybook stories for each target's preview component (loaded through loadPreview) replay these same fixtures through a mock engine (Frontend engineering and quality).

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• The Artifact is a small, versioned IR (gck.artifact/1): ordered sections of ten block types, RichText segments with marks and data tokens, and DataBindings with the Part VIII shape and normative snapshot shapes. Ids are stamped by the engine, never by the model.
  • The same contract exists three times (TypeScript types, a draft 2020-12 JSON Schema, Pydantic models with extra="forbid"), held together by a shared fixture corpus and eleven invariants, including "numbers only in tokens".
  • A TargetManifest becomes the per-run response schema: block types become an anyOf union, limits become maxItems and maxLength, the layout catalog and data catalog become enums, and data blocks without compatible bindings disappear. This generalizes Presenton's get_template_schema.
  • The slides target chooses Template v2 layouts by slot compatibility and fills the exact content JSON Presenton's hydrator consumes; the Tiptap target maps to StarterKit nodes plus gckChart, gckMetric, gckDataTable and gckToken, both ways; the dashboard target emits a verified position_json tree that references saved charts and saves through json_metadata.positions; the text target renders Markdown, plain text and sanitizer-compatible HTML.
  • Edit runs end in an ArtifactDiff (added, removed and changed block ids). applyPatch(native, diff, artifact, host) applies it in place: the Tiptap target finds blocks through the gckBlockId global attribute that GckBlockIds adds and rewrites them in one transaction (one undo step), the text target re-renders, and the slides and dashboard targets have no patch mode in v1 and apply "patch" as replace with a patch_unsupported warning.
  • Each target has host-specific failure modes (sample data in unfilled slots, editors with reduced schemas, chart readability and editorship in Superset, metadata resets, report deactivation on tab changes, layout size limits) and the adapters check for them before applying.
  • Adapters are tested without an LLM: golden files, host-rule checks, Tiptap round trips and patch tests on an unmounted editor, and schema contract tests shared with the engine.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Run protocol and client to see how Artifacts are streamed to the browser as patches, how runs are started, reviewed, cancelled and resumed, and how @gck/client reads the event stream.

docs.title: Run protocol and client
docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/utils/sse.py, servers/fastapi/models/sse_response.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py, servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/header.ts · Builds on: Artifact Spec and targets · Time: ~45 min

This chapter specifies the wire contract between the browser and the GCK Engine and builds both ends of it: the run lifecycle and endpoints, every stream event with a JSON example, ordering and idempotency, block-level JSON Patch plus text.delta, outline review, the error model, resume with Last-Event-ID from a server-side event log, heartbeats, auth and CORS. You get the full TypeScript for @gck/protocol events and the @gck/client transport, an AG-UI mapping, and a FastAPI sketch of the event log that generalizes Presenton's SSE helpers.

Files under gck/ are new code for Part IX; files under servers/ are Presenton at snapshot 571461f.

docs.title: Step 1: What the protocol must fix in Presenton's streams
docs.text:
Streaming (SSE) covers Presenton's streams; four of their properties block reuse.

  1. The stream is the generation. A dropped outline or Standard stream restarts all LLM calls (the hooks reset their buffers before retrying, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:82-100); a Smart stream re-runs the generator, which replays checkpointed slides and continues (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1941-1993).
  2. Frames carry no id. SSEResponse.to_string() writes only event: and data: lines (servers/fastapi/models/sse_response.py:10-11), so the browser has nothing to send back as Last-Event-ID.
  3. The browser uses EventSource, which can only GET without custom headers (useOutlineStreaming.ts:105-109). Auth therefore rides on the session cookie, which resolve_request_principal checks before any Bearer API key (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py:22-57).
  4. Errors are a string plus optional metadata. Smart streams add source, status_code, error_type, retryable, completed_slides and total_slides (presentation.py:2246-2267); outline and Standard streams send only detail.

A component mounted inside Superset, a Tiptap page or a third-party site needs the opposite on every point: generation that survives the connection, numbered events, header-based auth with no cookie, and machine-readable errors.

docs.title: Step 2: The run lifecycle and endpoints
docs.text:
A run is one request to turn a prompt plus host context into an Artifact (the IR from Artifact Spec and targets). The engine executes the run as a background task; HTTP connections only observe it.

Paths below are relative to the engine base URL {engine}, the engineUrl given to GckClient. It never contains /v1 (the client appends /v1/runs... itself): a standalone engine is https://gck.example.com, an engine behind a same-origin ingress is for example /gck-engine, and an engine mounted inside Presenton is /api/gck (Extracting the engine from Presenton). The URLs in RunCreated are absolute paths that include that mount prefix; the client does not rely on them.

Method and path Request Success response Idempotency POST /v1/runs RunRequest JSON, headers Authorization, optional Idempotency-Key 201 {runId, streamUrl, inputUrl, cancelUrl, createdAt}; with Accept: text/event-stream instead 200 and the event stream, run id in header GCK-Run-Id same key within 24 h returns the same run (200) GET /v1/runs/{runId}/events headers Authorization, optional Last-Event-ID 200 text/event-stream safe to repeat GET /v1/runs/{runId} none 200 RunSummary (state, lastEventId, artifactVersion, pending input, error) safe GET /v1/runs/{runId}/artifact none 200 {version, lastEventId, artifact} safe POST /v1/runs/{runId}/input {inputId, kind, decision, outline?} 202 {accepted: true} same inputId and same body returns 202 again; a different body returns 409 input_already_resolved POST /v1/runs/{runId}/cancel {reason?} 202 {state} always 202; a terminal run reports its final state

The request body is the one fixed in the blueprint:

POST /v1/runs (request body)
{
  "intent": "generate",
  "prompt": "Create a QBR page for EMEA from the Sales dashboard",
  "target": { "id": "tiptap-doc", "manifestVersion": "1.0.0", "manifest": {} },
  "context": { "host": "superset", "surface": "dashboard", "dashboardId": 37, "selection": null,
               "document": null, "locale": "en", "theme": {} },
  "data": { "provider": "superset", "allowedChartIds": [412, 413] },
  "options": { "reviewOutline": true, "maxSections": 8, "tone": "professional" }
}

The other two intents use the same body and differ in what context carries. A transform sends the content to rewrite in context.selection, as Artifact blocks (the target's fromHost output for the user's selection), and is applied with replace by default:

POST /v1/runs (transform request)
{
  "intent": "transform",
  "prompt": "Turn the selected text into one chart block. Use only charts from the data catalog.",
  "target": { "id": "tiptap-doc", "manifestVersion": "1.0.0", "manifest": {} },
  "context": { "host": "tiptap", "surface": "document", "locale": "en",
               "selection": [
                 { "id": "blk_u4k9x2m7qa", "type": "paragraph",
                   "text": [{ "text": "Pipeline grew fastest in Germany and France this quarter." }] }],
               "document": { "outline": ["## Pipeline by region"], "before": "", "after": "" } },
  "data": { "provider": "superset", "allowedChartIds": [412, 413] },
  "options": { "reviewOutline": false }
}

An edit sends the artifact it changes in context.document: the artifact applied earlier, re-read from the host with fromHost so it includes the user's own edits since, with its id, bindings and provenance kept. It is applied with patch by default:

POST /v1/runs (edit request)
{
  "intent": "edit",
  "prompt": "Make the pipeline section shorter and add a revenue KPI",
  "target": { "id": "tiptap-doc", "manifestVersion": "1.0.0", "manifest": {} },
  "context": { "host": "tiptap", "surface": "document", "locale": "en",
               "document": {
                 "id": "art_01JC8Q4M6X2N7YB5K3P9R2T8VW", "version": "gck.artifact/1", "title": "EMEA QBR", "target": "tiptap-doc",
                 "sections": [
                   { "id": "sec_q7x2m400", "kind": "section", "title": "EMEA at a glance", "blocks": [] },
                   { "id": "sec_q7x2m401", "kind": "section", "title": "Pipeline by region", "blocks": [
                     { "id": "blk_q7x2m40100", "type": "paragraph", "text": [{ "text": "Pipeline reached a record level across EMEA, led by Germany, France and the Nordics." }] },
                     { "id": "blk_q7x2m40101", "type": "chart", "bindingId": "b_c413", "chartType": "bar" }] }],
                 "bindings": {
                   "b_c412": { "kind": "metric", "source": { "type": "superset_chart", "chart_id": 412 }, "mapping": {} },
                   "b_c413": { "kind": "chart", "source": { "type": "superset_chart", "chart_id": 413 }, "mapping": {} } },
                 "provenance": { "runId": "run_01JC8Q4M6X2N7Y", "createdAt": "2026-11-03T10:15:03Z", "prompt": "Create a QBR page for EMEA" } } },
  "data": { "provider": "superset", "allowedChartIds": [412, 413] },
  "options": { "reviewOutline": false }
}
Intent context.selection context.document Version line starts at Default apply mode generate optional host hint (a convention per host) optional compact digest empty, the first patch is a root replace to version 1 the host's choice (insert_at_cursor, append, replace) transform required: Block[] to rewrite optional compact digest empty, as for generate replace (the selection) edit optional: blocks to focus on required: the base Artifact the base, as version 0 (Step 5) patch

Engine run states are queued, planning, awaiting_input, generating, resolving_data, completed, failed, cancelled and expired; the browser machine in React SDK and UI kit adds composing, submitting, ready, applying and applied.

The two-step form (201, then GET) gives the browser a run id before the stream connects, so a reload or a cancel button can address the run; the one-shot form is for server-to-server callers and tests.

docs.title: Step 3: The event envelope and every event type
docs.text:
Each SSE frame carries one event: id: is the sequence number, event: repeats the type for curl and devtools, and data: is one line of compact JSON:

One frame on the wire
id: 7
event: artifact.patch
data: {"v":1,"id":7,"runId":"run_01JC8Q4M6X2N7Y","ts":"2026-11-03T10:15:09.402Z","type":"artifact.patch","data":{"baseVersion":3,"version":4,"ops":[{"op":"add","path":"/sections/1/blocks/-","value":{"id":"blk_q7x2m40100","type":"paragraph","text":[]}}]}}

Envelope fields: v (protocol major, 1), id (gapless from 1), runId, ts (ISO 8601), type, data, and an optional progress {phase, message?, completed?, total?} that replaces Presenton's free-text status frames. The client trusts the JSON type, not the event: line.

type data When run.started {runId, target: {id, manifestVersion}} first event of every run plan.proposed {outline: OutlineItem[], planVersion, final} after planning; again with final: true after review run.awaiting_input {kind: "outline_review", inputId, expiresAt} only when options.reviewOutline artifact.patch {baseVersion, version, ops: JsonPatchOp[]} primary content channel text.delta {blockId, path, delta, format, baseVersion} optional, inside one block binding.resolved {bindingId, snapshot, snapshotAt, status} per data binding run.warning {code, message, blockId?} non-fatal problems run.completed {artifactVersion, usage} terminal, success run.failed {code, message, retryable, retryAfterMs?, details?, completedSections?, totalSections?} terminal, failure or cancel

Examples of each payload (envelope fields other than type omitted):

Event payloads
{"type":"run.started","data":{"runId":"run_01JC8Q4M6X2N7Y","target":{"id":"tiptap-doc","manifestVersion":"1.0.0"}}}

{"type":"plan.proposed","data":{"planVersion":1,"final":false,"outline":[
  {"sectionId":"sec_q7x2m400","title":"EMEA at a glance","summary":"Headline revenue and growth","layoutHint":null,"bindings":["b_c412"]},
  {"sectionId":"sec_q7x2m401","title":"Pipeline by region","summary":"Bar chart, top 5 countries","layoutHint":null,"bindings":["b_c413"]}]}}

{"type":"run.awaiting_input","data":{"kind":"outline_review","inputId":"in_4c1","expiresAt":"2026-11-03T10:45:05Z"}}

{"type":"artifact.patch","data":{"baseVersion":0,"version":1,"ops":[{"op":"replace","path":"","value":{"id":"art_01JC8Q4M6X2N7YB5K3P9R2T8VW",
  "version":"gck.artifact/1","title":"EMEA QBR","target":"tiptap-doc","sections":[],"bindings":{},"provenance":{"runId":"run_01JC8Q4M6X2N7Y","createdAt":"2026-11-03T10:15:03Z","prompt":"Create..."}}}]}}

{"type":"text.delta","data":{"blockId":"blk_q7x2m40100","path":"/text/0/text","delta":"Revenue grew in every ","format":"text","baseVersion":4}}

{"type":"binding.resolved","data":{"bindingId":"b_c412","status":"ok","snapshotAt":"2026-11-03T10:15:11Z",
  "snapshot":{"value":1840000,"previous":1610000}}}

{"type":"run.warning","data":{"code":"binding_dropped","message":"Chart 413 is not visible to you and was left out.","blockId":"blk_q7x2m40101"}}

{"type":"run.completed","data":{"artifactVersion":17,"usage":{"inputTokens":5120,"outputTokens":2210,"durationMs":14890,"model":"gpt-4.1"}}}

{"type":"run.failed","data":{"code":"rate_limited","message":"The model provider is rate limiting requests.","retryable":true,"retryAfterMs":20000,"completedSections":2,"totalSections":6}}

completedSections and totalSections are the generalization of Smart mode's completed_slides and total_slides error metadata (presentation.py:2258-2267).

docs.title: Step 4: Ordering and idempotency
docs.text:
Three counters keep the client consistent, each with one job.

Counter Scope Rule on the client Event id per run, gapless from 1 Drop any event with id <= lastEventId (a replay duplicate). If id > lastEventId + 1, a frame was lost: abort and reconnect with Last-Event-ID: lastEventId. Artifact version per run, increments by exactly 1 per artifact.patch Apply only when baseVersion === store.version. If version <= store.version, skip (already applied). Otherwise call GET /v1/runs/{id}/artifact and replace the store. planVersion per run The newest plan.proposed wins; final: true locks the outline.

text.delta, binding.resolved and run.warning never change the artifact version. A text.delta whose baseVersion is older than its block's last replace is discarded. Binding runtime state (snapshot, snapshotAt, status) lives in an overlay beside the artifact, because the browser's data provider (@gck/data-superset) may also resolve bindings and must not fork the engine's version line.

On the request side, POST /v1/runs honors an Idempotency-Key header (the client generates a UUID per user submission), so a retried POST after a network timeout cannot start two paid runs. POST /input is keyed by the engine-issued inputId. POST /cancel is idempotent by definition.

Gotcha

Presenton's Standard slide chunks concatenate without commas into invalid JSON, so the client parses each chunk alone (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationStreaming.ts:454-510). In GCK every artifact.patch is complete JSON; the only partial JSON is a format: "json" text.delta for one block.

docs.title: Step 5: JSON Patch at block granularity, plus text.delta
docs.text:
artifact.patch uses RFC 6902 JSON Patch (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6902) over JSON Pointers (RFC 6901, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901). The engine follows four rules that keep patches cheap to apply and easy to render:

  1. The first patch is a root replace ("path": "", the whole document in RFC 6901) that installs the skeleton at version 1, except in an edit run, which starts from the base (below). The same op doubles as the resync snapshot after log compaction (Step 9).
  2. Blocks are the unit of change. Ops target /sections/-, /sections/{i}/blocks/-, /sections/{i}/blocks/{j}, /bindings/{id} or top-level fields such as /title, never anything deeper than a block. Renderers key by block id, not by index.
  3. Only add, replace and remove are emitted. move and copy complicate index bookkeeping in a streaming renderer; test is reserved for client-side edit patches.
  4. A patch is atomic. RFC 6902 requires that a patch with a failing op is not applied at all; the client applier in React SDK and UI kit copies on write and commits only after the last op.

A typical section arrives as three patches:

Three artifact.patch payloads for one section
{"baseVersion":3,"version":4,"ops":[{"op":"add","path":"/sections/-","value":{"id":"sec_q7x2m401","kind":"section","title":"Pipeline by region","blocks":[]}}]}
{"baseVersion":4,"version":5,"ops":[{"op":"add","path":"/sections/1/blocks/-","value":{"id":"blk_q7x2m40100","type":"paragraph","text":[]}}]}
{"baseVersion":5,"version":6,"ops":[{"op":"replace","path":"/sections/1/blocks/0","value":{"id":"blk_q7x2m40100","type":"paragraph",
  "text":[{"text":"Pipeline reached "},{"text":"","token":{"bindingId":"b_c413","field":"total:","format":",.2s"}},{"text":" across EMEA."}]}}]}

An edit run has no skeleton to install: the stream starts from the base artifact in context.document, which is version 0 on both sides. The engine sends no root replace; its first artifact.patch has baseVersion: 0 and changes the base in place, block by block, and run.completed carries the final version. Untouched blocks are never re-sent, changed blocks are replaced under their existing id, removed blocks are removed and new blocks get new ids, so the client can diff the final artifact against the base by block id (the run controller exposes that diff as run.diff). For the edit request above:

The edit run's stream (payloads only)
{"type":"artifact.patch","data":{"baseVersion":0,"version":1,"ops":[{"op":"replace","path":"/sections/1/blocks/0","value":{"id":"blk_q7x2m40100","type":"paragraph",
  "text":[{"text":"Pipeline hit a record, led by Germany and France."}]}}]}}
{"type":"artifact.patch","data":{"baseVersion":1,"version":2,"ops":[{"op":"add","path":"/sections/0/blocks/-","value":{"id":"blk_q7x2m40102","type":"metric","bindingId":"b_c412","label":"Revenue","compare":"previous_period"}}]}}
{"type":"binding.resolved","data":{"bindingId":"b_c412","status":"ok","snapshotAt":"2026-11-03T10:31:40Z","snapshot":{"value":1840000,"previous":1610000}}}
{"type":"run.completed","data":{"artifactVersion":2,"usage":{"inputTokens":3410,"outputTokens":420,"durationMs":5210,"model":"gpt-4.1"}}}

A client therefore resets its store to the base at version 0 before it reads the stream (createRunController and runToCompletion both do). GET /v1/runs/{runId}/artifact on an edit run returns the base with the patches applied, and after log compaction the resync snapshot is a root replace at baseVersion: 0 like in any other run, which replaces the store but keeps every block id.

Between version 5 and 6, text.delta events let the paragraph type itself out. Two formats exist:

format path delta Client behavior text pointer inside the block, for example /text/0/text plain string to append append to a draft copy of the block json "" raw JSON text of the whole block, in pieces append to a buffer, run jsonrepair, parse, show as a provisional block

The json format streams lists, tables and callouts. It is the technique Presenton's outline hook applies to the whole outline (useOutlineStreaming.ts:133-139), narrowed to one block so a failed repair only affects that block. The block's final replace always wins and clears the draft.

Gotcha

Pointers use array indexes, so they are only safe while the engine is the sole writer. The client store is read-only from submitting until ready; user edits during a run are limited to the outline review form, which is sent through POST /input, not patched locally. Allowing local edits mid-stream would shift indexes under the engine's next op.

docs.title: Step 6: Human-in-the-loop outline review
docs.text:
When options.reviewOutline is true, the engine pauses after planning for the user to confirm the outline: the checkpoint Presenton implements as a whole page (User journey), here a pause inside one run.

  1. The engine emits plan.proposed (final: false) then run.awaiting_input with an inputId and an expiresAt (default 30 minutes).
  2. The stream stays open and sends heartbeats. The client may disconnect; the run stays parked.
  3. The client posts the decision:
POST /v1/runs/{runId}/input
{
  "inputId": "in_4c1",
  "kind": "outline_review",
  "decision": "edit",
  "outline": [
    { "sectionId": "sec_q7x2m401", "title": "Pipeline by region", "summary": "Top 5 countries only", "layoutHint": null, "bindings": ["b_c413"] },
    { "sectionId": null, "title": "Risks", "summary": "Three risks with owners", "layoutHint": null, "bindings": [] }
  ]
}

decision is approve (no outline), edit (full replacement list: reorder, delete, rename and add are all expressed by the list) or cancel. New sections have sectionId: null; the engine assigns ids.

  1. The engine validates: at most limits.maxSections from the manifest, titles of at most 200 characters, and bindings a subset of what the planner offered (no chart ids outside allowedChartIds). Failures return 422 and leave the run waiting.
  2. On success the engine emits plan.proposed with planVersion: 2, final: true (normalized, all ids assigned), then artifact.patch events.
  3. If expiresAt passes, the run ends with run.failed {code: "input_expired", retryable: false}.
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant C as GckClient
    participant E as GCK Engine
    participant L as Event log
    C->>E: POST /v1/runs with reviewOutline true
    E-->>C: 201 runId
    C->>E: GET events
    E->>L: append run.started and plan.proposed
    E->>L: append run.awaiting_input
    L-->>C: events 1 to 3
    Note over C,E: heartbeat comments every 15 s while waiting
    U->>C: reorder, delete, rename sections
    C->>E: POST input decision edit
    E-->>C: 202 accepted
    E->>L: append plan.proposed final and artifact.patch
    L-->>C: events 4 to n
    E->>L: append run.completed
    L-->>C: run.completed

docs.title: Step 7: The error model
docs.text:
Every error, whether returned as an HTTP response body or as run.failed, has the same shape:

Error body
{ "error": { "code": "rate_limited", "message": "The model provider is rate limiting requests.",
             "retryable": true, "retryAfterMs": 20000, "details": { "provider": "openai" } } }
code HTTP retryable Meaning and client action invalid_request 400 / 422 false Validation failed; show message. unauthorized 401 false No or bad token. token_expired 401 true Refresh the token once, retry. forbidden 403 false Not allowed for this target, host or run. not_found 404 false Unknown run, or someone else's. conflict / input_already_resolved 409 false Stale input or duplicate decision. rate_limited 429 true Wait retryAfterMs (also sent as Retry-After). quota_exceeded 429 false Tenant budget spent. context_too_large 413 / stream false Ask the user to narrow context. model_output_invalid stream true The model failed schema validation after the engine's own retries. model_unavailable 502 / 503 / stream true Provider down or timed out. data_forbidden stream false A required binding is not visible to the user (row-level security). data_unavailable stream true The data provider failed. input_expired stream false Outline review timed out. cancelled stream false Cancel endpoint or engine shutdown. internal 500 / stream true Anything else.

For unclassified exceptions, retryable follows Presenton's Smart rule: true for 408, 429 and 500 or more (presentation.py:2257-2264). A retryable run.failed means "a new run with the same request may succeed"; the run itself is terminal. Transport problems (dropped connection, heartbeat timeout, proxy 502 on GET /events) never produce run.failed; the client reconnects (Step 9).

Gotcha

Presenton's outline hook retries on a server error frame (useOutlineStreaming.ts:210-229), which re-runs the whole LLM pipeline up to three times without asking. GCK separates the two concerns: the client reconnects transparently, but it never restarts a failed run on its own. Restarting is a user action ("Try again") because it costs tokens.

docs.title: Step 8: Why fetch-based SSE, not EventSource
docs.text:
The WHATWG HTML standard defines EventSource with one option, withCredentials; there is no way to set the method or request headers (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html). That is why Presenton's stream routes are GETs keyed by an id in the path (useOutlineStreaming.ts:105-109, usePresentationStreaming.ts:300). For GCK the limits are blocking:

Need EventSource fetch + ReadableStream Authorization: Bearer header not possible; cookie only yes POST with a JSON body (one-shot mode) no yes Read the JSON body of a 401 or 429 no; any non-200 fails the connection and only fires error yes Control reconnect timing and give up browser-controlled; the spec reconnects after network errors fully client-controlled Last-Event-ID on reconnect automatic, but only for its own reconnects the client sets it explicitly on every reconnect it makes; after a page reload the run is found again by its id Cancel with AbortSignal close() only yes Detect a silent dead connection no heartbeat watchdog

Presenton already has a fetch-based reader for chat: it POSTs with an AbortSignal (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/chat.ts:104-116), reads response.body with a TextDecoder and splits frames on " " (chat.ts:294-308; quoted in Story 4). @gck/client keeps that structure and fixes three things for a general transport: it splits lines on CR, LF and CRLF as the SSE grammar requires (the chat reader looks for " " before it strips inside processSseFrame, chat.ts:136, so a CRLF-framed stream would never split), it honors id: and retry: fields (ignored by the chat reader, chat.ts:141-149), and it treats comment lines as heartbeats.

Gotcha

Presenton's getHeader() sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods and Access-Control-Allow-Headers as request headers (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/header.ts:1-9). Those are response headers; on a request they do nothing except force a CORS preflight and require the server to allow them. It works today only because FastAPI allows every header (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:94-100). Do not copy getHeader() into the kit.

docs.title: Step 9: Resume, the event log, backpressure and heartbeats
9.1 Resume with Last-Event-ID
docs.text:
The SSE standard says that a non-empty last event id is sent in a Last-Event-ID header on reconnection, and that an id containing U+0000 is ignored. GCK uses the same header for its own reconnects, set by the client:

  1. The client remembers lastEventId, the highest event id it has processed (not just received).
  2. On reconnect it sends GET /v1/runs/{id}/events with Last-Event-ID: 41.
  3. The engine reads events with seq > 41 from the event log, sends them, then tails new events live.
  4. If the log was compacted past 41, the engine first sends a synthetic root-replace artifact.patch with baseVersion: 0, which the client treats as "reset the store" (isSnapshotPatch, Step 11).

A page reload can resume too: with a resumeKey, @gck/react keeps the active run's {runId} in sessionStorage and, after the reload, replays that run's log from the first event into a fresh store (React SDK and UI kit).

This generalizes what Presenton does for Smart mode. There, slides are checkpointed to the database before they are emitted:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
            # Checkpoint before emitting. If the model later runs out of tokens
            # or the SSE client reconnects, generation resumes after this slide
            # instead of throwing away the accepted prefix.
            async with async_session_maker() as checkpoint_session:

(presentation.py:2075-2078.) On reconnect, stream_smart_presentation replays every saved slide as a slide_html frame and resumes from the next slide (presentation.py:1941-1993). GCK keeps the rule (persist before you emit) and changes two things: it persists events, not domain rows, so any target can replay; and generation is a background task, so a reconnect only replays and tails. In Presenton the generation task is cancelled when the stream generator exits early (presentation.py:2189-2192); in GCK only POST /cancel cancels.

docs.title: 9.2 Backpressure
docs.text: The log is the buffer. The run task appends and notifies; each subscriber reads the log at its own pace, by sequence number, in pages of 200. A slow browser costs a cursor and a database read, never a growing in-memory queue. At the source, the engine coalesces text.delta per block into at most one event per 50 ms, and marks those rows ephemeral so they are pruned once the block's final replace is committed. On the client, the store notifies React at most once per animation frame, so a burst of replayed events renders once.

docs.title: 9.3 Heartbeats
docs.text:
No Presenton SSE endpoint sends keepalives; the bundled nginx relies on 30-minute read timeouts (nginx.conf:45-69). That fails behind a load balancer with a 60-second idle timeout, which is where an embedded component lives. The WHATWG standard suggests a comment line about every 15 seconds. The engine writes : hb every 15 seconds of silence, and the client aborts and reconnects after 45 seconds without any bytes (three missed heartbeats). The engine also sends Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform and X-Accel-Buffering: no so nginx-style proxies do not buffer the stream.

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as GckClient
    participant P as Proxy
    participant E as GCK Engine
    participant L as Event log
    C->>P: GET events, no Last-Event-ID
    P->>E: forward
    E->>L: read seq after 0
    L-->>C: events 1 to 41
    Note over C,P: proxy drops the idle connection
    C->>C: no bytes for 45 s, abort, backoff 1 s
    C->>P: GET events, Last-Event-ID 41
    P->>E: forward
    E->>L: read seq after 41
    L-->>C: events 42 to 57 replayed
    E->>L: append event 58
    L-->>C: event 58 live
    Note over C: ids 1 to 41 never re-applied

docs.title: Step 10: Authentication, tokens and CORS
docs.text:
The kit never holds a long-lived secret. The host passes a token provider callback:

type TokenProvider = (opts: { forceRefresh: boolean }) => Promise<string | null>;
  • The client calls it before every request, including every reconnect, so a token that expired during a long review pause is replaced transparently. Hosts cache the token until shortly before expiry.
  • Tokens are short-lived (5 minutes) and audience-scoped to the engine, minted by the host's own backend (Host integrations).
  • On 401 token_expired the client calls the provider once with forceRefresh: true and retries once.
  • Requests use credentials: "omit": no cookie, so no third-party-cookie blocking and no CSRF surface.

When the engine is cross-origin, every GCK request is preflighted (an Authorization header and Last-Event-ID are not CORS-safelisted). The engine's CORS policy should be:

Header Value Access-Control-Allow-Origin the exact host origin from an allowlist, never * for authenticated routes Access-Control-Allow-Methods GET, POST, OPTIONS Access-Control-Allow-Headers Authorization, Content-Type, Accept, Last-Event-ID, Idempotency-Key, GCK-Protocol Access-Control-Expose-Headers GCK-Run-Id, Retry-After Access-Control-Max-Age 600 (fewer preflights on reconnect storms) Access-Control-Allow-Credentials omitted (no cookies)

Presenton's policy is a single origin from NEXT_PUBLIC_URL, or * as a development fallback, with credentials allowed (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:88-100). The engine needs a per-tenant origin list, because one engine serves several hosts.

Gotcha

Without Access-Control-Expose-Headers, response.headers.get("Retry-After") returns null in the browser on a cross-origin 429, and the client silently falls back to its own backoff. That is why retryAfterMs is also inside the JSON error body.

docs.title: Step 11: @gck/protocol event types
docs.text:
The protocol package is types plus JSON Schemas with zero runtime dependencies. This file covers runs and events; Artifact, DataBinding and TargetId come from src/artifact.ts and TargetManifest from src/target.ts, both specified in Artifact Spec and targets. The package index re-exports all three files (export * from "./artifact", "./target", "./run"), so run.ts does not re-export Artifact itself. HostContext in target.ts is an alias of RunContext below: one JSON object, the run request's context, under two names.

gck/packages/protocol/src/run.ts (new)
import type { Artifact, DataBinding, TargetId } from "./artifact";
import type { TargetManifest } from "./target";

export const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1 as const;

export type JsonPointer = string;
export type JsonPatchOp =
  | { op: "add"; path: JsonPointer; value: unknown }
  | { op: "remove"; path: JsonPointer }
  | { op: "replace"; path: JsonPointer; value: unknown }
  | { op: "move"; from: JsonPointer; path: JsonPointer }
  | { op: "copy"; from: JsonPointer; path: JsonPointer }
  | { op: "test"; path: JsonPointer; value: unknown };

export type RunIntent = "generate" | "transform" | "edit";

export interface RunContext {
  host: string;                       // "superset" | "tiptap" | "presenton" | "web" | "element"
  surface?: string;                   // conventions: dashboard, dashboard_markdown, sqllab, alert, document, presentation, page
  locale?: string;
  theme?: Record<string, unknown>;
  selection?: unknown;                // generate: host-defined hint; transform: Block[] from the target's fromHost
  document?: unknown;                 // generate, transform: compact digest; edit: the base Artifact (version 0)
  [key: string]: unknown;             // host-specific ids such as dashboardId
}

export interface RunRequest {
  intent: RunIntent;
  prompt: string;
  target: { id: TargetId; manifestVersion: string; manifest?: TargetManifest };
  context: RunContext;
  data?: { provider: string; allowedChartIds?: number[] };
  options?: { reviewOutline?: boolean; maxSections?: number; tone?: string };
}

export interface RunCreated {
  runId: string; streamUrl: string; inputUrl: string; cancelUrl: string; createdAt: string;
}

export type EngineRunState =
  | "queued" | "planning" | "awaiting_input" | "generating"
  | "resolving_data" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "expired";

export interface RunSummary {
  runId: string;
  state: EngineRunState;
  lastEventId: number;
  artifactVersion: number;
  pendingInput?: { kind: "outline_review"; inputId: string; expiresAt: string };
  error?: GckErrorBody;
}

export interface OutlineItem {
  sectionId: string | null;           // null only in client edits (new section)
  title: string;
  summary: string;
  layoutHint?: string | null;
  bindings: string[];
}

export type OutlineDecision =
  | { inputId: string; kind: "outline_review"; decision: "approve" }
  | { inputId: string; kind: "outline_review"; decision: "edit"; outline: OutlineItem[] }
  | { inputId: string; kind: "outline_review"; decision: "cancel" };

export type GckErrorCode =
  | "invalid_request" | "unauthorized" | "token_expired" | "forbidden" | "not_found"
  | "conflict" | "input_already_resolved" | "rate_limited" | "quota_exceeded"
  | "context_too_large" | "model_output_invalid" | "model_unavailable"
  | "data_forbidden" | "data_unavailable" | "input_expired" | "cancelled" | "internal";

export interface GckErrorBody {
  code: GckErrorCode;
  message: string;
  retryable: boolean;
  retryAfterMs?: number;
  details?: Record<string, unknown>;
  completedSections?: number;
  totalSections?: number;
}

export interface Usage {
  inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number; durationMs: number; model?: string;
}

export interface Progress {
  phase: "planning" | "generating" | "resolving_data";
  message?: string; completed?: number; total?: number;
}

export type GckEventBody =
  | { type: "run.started"; data: { runId: string; target: { id: TargetId; manifestVersion: string } } }
  | { type: "plan.proposed"; data: { outline: OutlineItem[]; planVersion: number; final: boolean } }
  | { type: "run.awaiting_input"; data: { kind: "outline_review"; inputId: string; expiresAt: string } }
  | { type: "artifact.patch"; data: { baseVersion: number; version: number; ops: JsonPatchOp[] } }
  | { type: "text.delta"; data: { blockId: string; path: JsonPointer; delta: string;
                                  format: "text" | "json"; baseVersion: number } }
  | { type: "binding.resolved"; data: { bindingId: string; snapshot: unknown;
                                        snapshotAt: string; status: NonNullable<DataBinding["status"]> } }
  | { type: "run.warning"; data: { code: string; message: string; blockId?: string } }
  | { type: "run.completed"; data: { artifactVersion: number; usage: Usage } }
  | { type: "run.failed"; data: GckErrorBody };

export type GckEvent = GckEventBody & {
  v: typeof PROTOCOL_VERSION;
  id: number;
  runId: string;
  ts: string;
  progress?: Progress;
};

export type GckEventType = GckEvent["type"];
export type EventOf<T extends GckEventType> = Extract<GckEvent, { type: T }>;

export const TERMINAL_EVENTS: ReadonlySet<GckEventType> = new Set(["run.completed", "run.failed"]);

export function isGckEvent(value: unknown): value is GckEvent {
  if (!value || typeof value !== "object") return false;
  const v = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  return v.v === PROTOCOL_VERSION && typeof v.id === "number" &&
    typeof v.type === "string" && typeof v.runId === "string" && "data" in v;
}

/** A root replace at baseVersion 0 is a full snapshot (initial or after compaction). */
export function isSnapshotPatch(e: GckEvent): boolean {
  return e.type === "artifact.patch" && e.data.baseVersion === 0 &&
    e.data.ops.length === 1 && e.data.ops[0].op === "replace" && e.data.ops[0].path === "";
}

isGckEvent is a structural guard only; full validation uses JSON Schemas shared with the engine's Pydantic models (Frontend engineering and quality).

Gotcha

An unknown type from a newer engine must be ignored, not treated as an error: every switch over events ends in a default branch that drops it. Breaking changes bump v; the engine rejects a client whose GCK-Protocol header is too old with invalid_request and details.minProtocol.
