import asyncio

from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse, StreamingResponse
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from api.v1.auth.context import get_current_owner_id, reset_current_owner_id, set_current_owner_id
from services.database import async_session_maker, get_async_session
from gck_engine.models import GckRunModel
from gck_engine.protocol import OutlineDecision, RunRequest
from gck_engine.runs.event_log import stream_run_events
from gck_engine.runs.router import EVENT_LOG, RUN_TASKS, RUNS_ROUTER, run_guard
from gck_engine.targets import resolve_manifest

ENGINE_BASE = "/api/gck"  # where Presenton mounts the engine (Step 7.1)
SSE_HEADERS = {"Cache-Control": "no-cache, no-transform", "X-Accel-Buffering": "no"}
INPUT_WAITERS: dict[str, asyncio.Future] = {}  # by inputId, kept until the run ends


class GckHttpError(HTTPException):
    """Rendered as {"error": {code, message, retryable}} by one app exception handler."""

    def __init__(self, status: int, code: str, message: str, retryable: bool = False):
        super().__init__(status_code=status,
                         detail={"code": code, "message": message, "retryable": retryable})
        self.gck_code = code  # classify() in the run router reads it


async def load_run_for_principal_or_404(run_id: str, principal) -> GckRunModel:
    # The owner filter is added by Presenton's do_orm_execute hook (database.py:67-97);
    # principal is None when auth is disabled (Electron), see the gotcha below.
    async with async_session_maker() as session:
        run = await session.scalar(select(GckRunModel).where(GckRunModel.id == run_id))
    if run is None:  # unknown, or another owner's: the same 404
        raise GckHttpError(404, "not_found", "Run not found")
    return run


async def _owned(run_id: str, body: RunRequest, owner_id) -> None:
    token = set_current_owner_id(owner_id)
    try:
        await run_guard(run_id, body)
    finally:
        reset_current_owner_id(token)


def _created(run: GckRunModel) -> dict:
    base = f"{ENGINE_BASE}/v1/runs/{run.id}"
    return {"runId": run.id, "streamUrl": f"{base}/events", "inputUrl": f"{base}/input",
            "cancelUrl": f"{base}/cancel", "createdAt": run.created_at.isoformat()}


@RUNS_ROUTER.post("", status_code=201)
async def create_run(body: RunRequest, request: Request,
                     sql_session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_async_session)):
    key = request.headers.get("Idempotency-Key")
    if key:  # 24-hour window check omitted
        existing = await sql_session.scalar(
            select(GckRunModel).where(GckRunModel.idempotency_key == key))
        if existing is not None:
            return JSONResponse(_created(existing), status_code=200)
    manifest = resolve_manifest(body.target)  # 400 invalid_request: unknown target or version
    run = GckRunModel(intent=body.intent, target_id=manifest.id,
                      manifest_version=manifest.version, state="queued",
                      request=body.model_dump(mode="json"), idempotency_key=key)
    sql_session.add(run)
    await sql_session.commit()
    RUN_TASKS[run.id] = asyncio.create_task(_owned(run.id, body, get_current_owner_id()))
    if request.headers.get("accept", "").startswith("text/event-stream"):
        return StreamingResponse(
            stream_run_events(EVENT_LOG, run.id, 0, request.is_disconnected),
            media_type="text/event-stream", headers={**SSE_HEADERS, "GCK-Run-Id": run.id})
    return _created(run)


@RUNS_ROUTER.post("/{run_id}/input", status_code=202)
async def answer_run(run_id: str, body: OutlineDecision, request: Request):
    run = await load_run_for_principal_or_404(
        run_id, getattr(request.state, "auth_principal", None))
    waiter = INPUT_WAITERS.get(body.inputId)
    if waiter is not None and waiter.done():
        if waiter.result() == body:  # same inputId and same body: 202 again
            return {"accepted": True}
        raise GckHttpError(409, "input_already_resolved", "This input was already answered")
    if waiter is None or (run.pending_input or {}).get("inputId") != body.inputId:
        raise GckHttpError(409, "conflict", "No pending input with this inputId")
    waiter.set_result(body)  # the run task is awaiting this future
    return {"accepted": True}

A repeated identical decision (a client retry after a dropped response) is answered with 202 again; only a different body for an input that was already answered gets 409 input_already_resolved, as the run protocol requires. Every error leaves the engine in the protocol's shape, {"error": {"code", "message", "retryable"}}, through one exception handler for GckHttpError registered on the app next to the router (Step 7.1).

The run task body is execute_run, which run_guard awaits. It is a plain coroutine on the event loop, the same mechanism Smart mode uses for generate_smart_presentation (presentation.py:2128):

NEW: servers/fastapi/gck_engine/runs/execute.py (excerpt)
async def execute_run(run_id: str, body: RunRequest, log: EventLog) -> None:
    await log.append(run_id, "run.started", {"runId": run_id, "target": {
        "id": body.target.id, "manifestVersion": body.target.manifestVersion}})
    ctx = await build_context(run_id, body)              # manifest, documents, web search, data catalog
    await set_state(run_id, "planning")
    plan = await plan_sections(ctx)                      # Step A
    plan = await choose_section_layouts(ctx, plan)       # Step B
    await log.append(run_id, "plan.proposed", {
        "outline": plan.outline(), "planVersion": 1, "final": not ctx.review_outline})
    if ctx.review_outline:
        plan = await await_outline_review(ctx, log, plan)  # run.awaiting_input, INPUT_WAITERS
    patcher = ArtifactPatcher(run_id, log)               # owns baseVersion and version
    if body.intent == "edit":
        patcher.start_from(ctx.base_artifact)            # validated context.document is version 0; no root replace
    else:
        await patcher.replace_root(ctx.empty_artifact(plan))   # generate, transform: skeleton at version 1
    await set_state(run_id, "generating")
    async for section_id, blocks in generate_all_sections(ctx, plan):  # Step C
        await patcher.set_blocks(section_id, blocks)
    await set_state(run_id, "resolving_data")
    await resolve_assets_and_bindings(ctx, patcher, log)  # Steps D and E
    await materialize_for_target(ctx, patcher.artifact)   # slides: rows; others: no-op
    await set_state(run_id, "completed")
    await log.append(run_id, "run.completed", {
        "artifactVersion": patcher.version, "usage": ctx.usage()})

The intent changes the inputs, not the pipeline. build_context puts a transform's context.selection (Artifact blocks from the target's fromHost) into the planning prompt as the content to rewrite, and validates an edit's context.document as an Artifact, which becomes ctx.base_artifact. For edit, start_from sets the patcher's version to 0 without emitting anything, because the client already holds the base as version 0, and set_blocks then emits replace and remove ops only for blocks that changed and add ops with new ids for new ones; the client diffs the result by block id and applies it with the target's patch mode (Run protocol and client). In this sketch plan_sections plans the changed sections for an edit; that edit planning prompt is new engine work (roadmap work package 2.3), modeled on the per-slide edit prompts listed in Step 1.

generate_all_sections runs Step C with a bounded asyncio.Semaphore and yields sections as they finish. That sits between Presenton's two existing policies: the web UI stream generates one slide at a time (presentation.py:2366-2381), and the one-shot API runs batches of 10 with asyncio.gather (presentation.py:2985). Because patches address sections by id, finishing out of order is harmless.

docs.title: 7.1 Mounting the router inside Presenton
docs.text:
Four layers decide whether a request for /api/gck/... reaches the engine with an identity:

Layer Today Change FastAPI app Routers are included one by one (api/main.py:68-74) app.include_router(RUNS_ROUTER, prefix="/api/gck"), so {engine} is /api/gck and the runs endpoint is /api/gck/v1/runs; one exception handler renders GckHttpError as {"error": {...}} Docker nginx Only /api/v1/ and /api/v2/ are proxied to port 8000 (nginx.conf:45-69); everything else goes to Next.js (nginx.conf:29-30) Add location /api/gck/ with the same 30-minute timeouts plus proxy_buffering off; Next.js proxy.ts (Electron and dev) isFastApiApiPath matches only /api/v1 and /api/v2 (proxy.ts:25-32); a Bearer header is forwarded only for sk-presenton- API keys, anything else must carry a session cookie (proxy.ts:146-171) Match /api/gck and forward its requests to FastAPI without the cookie check; FastAPI authenticates them FastAPI auth SessionAuthMiddleware requires a principal for any /api/ path (api/middlewares.py:44-53); a principal comes from the session cookie or a Bearer API key (api/v1/auth/principal.py:22-57) Accept a short-lived Bearer JWT as well (below)

The last row matters because @gck/client sends credentials: "omit" and an Authorization header from its token provider (Run protocol and client), and an API key must never reach a browser. The fix reuses Presenton's own JWT machinery: a small endpoint, behind the normal cookie session, returns await get_jwt_strategy(lifetime_seconds=300).write_token(user) (get_jwt_strategy takes the lifetime as a parameter, api/v1/auth/users.py:176-182), and resolve_request_principal tries Bearer values that are not API keys as JWTs before giving up. Presenton's getToken callback calls that endpoint.

Gotcha

If you add only the FastAPI router, the Docker image still serves /api/gck/... from Next.js through the catch-all location /, and in development proxy.ts rejects the cookie-less request with 401 before FastAPI sees it. Either way you debug an auth error on the wrong server. Change nginx, proxy.ts and the principal resolution in the same commit as the router.

Gotcha

With DISABLE_AUTH (the Electron runtime), SessionAuthMiddleware calls the next handler before it sets request.state.auth_principal (api/middlewares.py:59-72). Code that reads request.state.auth_principal directly raises AttributeError there; read it with getattr(..., None) as answer_run does, and let the owner context (which is None in that mode) decide visibility.

Gotcha

SSEResponse.to_string() writes event: and data: but no id: (models/sse_response.py:10-11), so no Presenton stream can resume with Last-Event-ID today. Do not reuse it for GCK frames; use the run protocol's to_sse, which adds the id: line and the envelope. For the same reason, do not wrap the event stream in safe_sse_stream (utils/sse.py:10-38): a database error while tailing the log must close the stream so the client reconnects, not announce that the run failed.

Gotcha

The in-process EventLog notifier, RUN_TASKS and INPUT_WAITERS work in Presenton because FastAPI runs as one uvicorn process with no workers argument (servers/fastapi/server.py:23-29). The limit stays invisible until the engine is deployed on its own with workers or replicas; the run protocol chapter lists the fix.

docs.title: Step 8: Keep the slides target on Template v2 and export
docs.text:
The slides target must produce exactly what the Presenton editor and exporter already understand: a presentations row whose layout is a Template v2 payload and slides rows whose content and ui are hydrated. The materializer, run in the engine at the end of a slides run, reuses Presenton's own functions:

  1. Resolve the template with _resolve_prepare_layout(layout, sql_session), which extracts the template id from the layout reference and returns the layout payload, the PresentationLayoutModel and fonts (presentation.py:1448-1470).
  2. For each IR section, convert blocks back to the layout's content shape by slot key (heading or paragraph segments to text, with bold and italic as Markdown emphasis so _template_text_runs_from_markdown can parse it, presentation.py:1157; list items to text-list; chart blocks to {chart_type, categories, series} filled from the binding snapshot, the shape Part VIII resolution produces (Story 1, dynamic data and refresh); image blocks to image_prompt plus the resolved image_url).
  3. Build SlideModel(layout_group=<template reference>, layout=<layout id>, index=i, speaker_note=<popped speakerNote>, content=..., ui=_template_slide_ui(...)) as the stream does (presentation.py:2383-2391), then _hydrate_template_slide_ui (presentation.py:309-319).
  4. Commit the presentation and slides in one transaction, and store presentation_id on the run row.

That path creates a new deck at the end of a run. Applying an artifact into a deck that is already open goes through the browser instead: the @gck/target-slides adapter's apply reads the presenton.api capability (fetch, presentationId, afterIndex) and posts its native slides to the one new endpoint, POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/slides/from-content, which Artifact Spec and targets specifies and which is built from the same functions (_template_slide_ui, process_slide_and_fetch_assets, _apply_template_content_to_ui).

The browser side of @gck/target-slides previews the same IR with a browser port of the hydrator and the moved renderer (templateV2UiToHtmlFragment, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:172-186), so the preview during streaming and the deck in the editor share the renderer, and a golden test keeps the ported hydrator equal to _apply_template_content_to_ui. Export stays exactly where it is: POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export calls export_presentation(presentation_id, title, export_as, cookie_header) (presentation.py:1642-1678, utils/export_utils.py:43-48) (PPTX and PDF export).

Gotcha

The slides materializer is the only code that writes Presenton tables. Keep presentation_id handling inside materialize_for_target; if it leaks into the generic pipeline, a Tiptap run starts to need a presentations row.

docs.title: Step 9: Keep existing Presenton endpoints working
docs.text:
AI Slides (Part VIII) and the Presenton web UI call the existing endpoints. The extraction must not change their behavior, so the plan adds new code beside the old instead of rewriting it.

Endpoint Until slides parity (M6) Optional bridge, behind a flag GET /api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/{id} (outlines.py:84) unchanged translate plan.proposed into legacy chunk and complete frames POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare (presentation.py:1840) unchanged unchanged GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/stream/{id} (presentation.py:2281) unchanged translate artifact.patch into legacy chunk and slide_assets frames POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate and /generate/async (presentation.py:3169, :3240) unchanged run as a slides run, keeping the response and async_tasks contract POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart unchanged unchanged (Smart is not a GCK target) Part VIII routes (bindings, refresh, prompt library) unchanged, reused by @gck/data-superset unchanged

The rules that keep this safe:

  • Shared functions change only additively. The extra_validator keyword in Step 5 defaults to None, so every existing caller of generate_structured_with_schema_retries behaves as before.
  • Golden tests pin the legacy paths. servers/fastapi/tests/integration/test_presentation_generation_flow.py already covers the prepare normalization (test_presentation_generation_flow.py:891) and template-schema content generation (test_presentation_generation_flow.py:1066). Run it on every GCK change; add a test that a slides run and the legacy stream produce slides with the same layout, content keys and ui element types for a fixed fake LLM.
  • The bridge is optional. Its flag defaults to off; if it never ships, the legacy endpoints simply keep their own code paths.

Gotcha

The legacy slide stream concatenates slide chunks without commas (presentation.py:2360-2363, presentation.py:2448-2451), and the browser relies on parsing each chunk on its own (Streaming (SSE)). A bridge must reproduce that framing byte for byte, including the opening { "slides": [ and closing ] } chunks, or usePresentationStreaming will silently drop slides.

docs.title: Step 10: Carve the @gck packages out of servers/nextjs
docs.text:
Most of the kit is new code, because Presenton's frontend is wired to Redux, next/navigation and Mixpanel. What moves is small and valuable: the renderer, the chart loader and proven interaction patterns.

Source Destination How lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts and its import closure (components/slide-editor/text/template-v2-text, text-runs, layout/flowLayout, charts/chart-data, infographics/infographic-editing, text/local-fonts, lib/math, lib/svg-color) @gck/target-slides/renderer Move; replace @/utils/api with an injected resolveAssetUrl lib/chart-browser.ts and public/vendor/chart-4.5.1.umd.min.js, chartjs-plugin-datalabels-2.2.0.min.js with their license files @gck/target-slides/charts Move; script URLs become options, keep the per-window promise cache (chart-browser.ts:105-106) Partial JSON handling in useOutlineStreaming.ts:133-174 @gck/core ArtifactStore.applyTextDelta (text.delta with format: "json") Rewrite as a pure function over jsonrepair, with tests Retry policy (MAX_STREAM_RETRIES = 3, delay 1000 ms * attempt, useOutlineStreaming.ts:14-15, :77-103) @gck/client Rewrite; reconnect with Last-Event-ID so a retry resumes instead of restarting EventSource usage (useOutlineStreaming.ts:107-109, usePresentationStreaming.ts:300-302) @gck/client fetch reader Rewrite Outline reorder and add (useOutlineManagement.ts:11-42), outline cards @gck/react/ui OutlineReview Rewrite without Redux; @dnd-kit/sortable as a dependency of the UI subpath only Everything under (pg)/presentation, store/*, services/api/* stays

The transport rewrite is the core of the frontend extraction. EventSource can only GET and cannot set headers, which is why Presenton's stream routes are GET routes keyed by an id in the path (Streaming (SSE)). A host such as Superset needs an Authorization header with a short-lived token, a POST body and resume.

Before, the outline page opens a stream like this:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts (excerpt)
    const openStream = () => {
      closeEventSource();
      eventSource = new EventSource(
        getApiUrl(`/api/v1/ppt/outlines/stream/${presentationId}`)
      );

      eventSource.addEventListener("response", (event) => {

After, the same job goes through GckClient from Run protocol and client, whose stream() reconnects with Last-Event-ID, drops duplicates and detects gaps:

NEW: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/gck/client.ts
import { GckClient } from "@gck/client";

export const gckClient = new GckClient({
  engineUrl: "/api/gck",               // Presenton mounts the engine here (Step 7.1)
  getToken: async () => {
    // Cookie session in, five-minute bearer JWT out (Step 7.1); never an API key.
    const res = await fetch("/api/v1/auth/gck-token", { credentials: "same-origin" });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`token request failed: ${res.status}`);
    return (await res.json()).token as string;
  },
});

Because the engine replays from its log, a reconnect costs nothing. Compare that with Presenton, where an outline or Standard stream retry opens a new request and the server regenerates from the beginning, paying for every LLM call again (Streaming (SSE)); the hook even resets accumulatedChunks before reconnecting (useOutlineStreaming.ts:90).

Gotcha

EventSource hides the response body of a failed request: it fires onerror and nothing else, which is why Presenton shows a generic "Failed to connect to the server" after retries (Streaming (SSE)). With fetch, a 401, 403 or 409 from the engine is readable, so @gck/client maps them to typed errors: a 401 refreshes the token once and retries once, a 403 or 409 is never retried. Retrying a 401 with the same expired token, as a blind retry loop would, never succeeds.

docs.title: Step 11: Make Presenton consume the kit (strangler pattern)
docs.text:
The strangler pattern replaces a system piece by piece: new code grows around the old, callers move one at a time, and the old code is removed only when nothing calls it. Presenton is the first and best test host, because its outline page already does what OutlineReview does.

The first cut keeps OutlinePage untouched. useOutlineStreaming keeps its signature and return shape (useOutlineStreaming.ts:18-21, :257-263) but gets a second implementation behind a build-time flag:

NEW: servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts (facade)
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { useDispatch } from "react-redux";
import { setOutlines } from "@/store/slices/presentationGeneration";
import { gckClient } from "../../gck/client";
import { buildSlidesRunRequest, outlineToMarkdown } from "../../gck/bridge";
import { legacyUseOutlineStreaming } from "./legacyUseOutlineStreaming";

const USE_GCK = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GCK_OUTLINE === "1";

export const useOutlineStreaming = USE_GCK ? gckUseOutlineStreaming : legacyUseOutlineStreaming;

function gckUseOutlineStreaming(presentationId: string | null, enabled = true) {
  const dispatch = useDispatch();
  const [streaming, setStreaming] = useState(false);
  const [statusMessage, setStatusMessage] = useState("Preparing your presentation outline");

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!enabled || !presentationId) return;
    const abort = new AbortController();
    (async () => {
      setStreaming(true);
      const request = await buildSlidesRunRequest(presentationId); // from the presentations row
      const { runId } = await gckClient.startRun(request, { signal: abort.signal });
      for await (const event of gckClient.stream(runId, { signal: abort.signal })) {
        if (event.progress?.message) setStatusMessage(event.progress.message);
        if (event.type === "plan.proposed") {
          dispatch(setOutlines(outlineToMarkdown(event.data.outline)));
        }
        if (event.type === "run.awaiting_input") {
          // S1 is plan-only: the legacy /prepare path continues from the reviewed outline.
          await gckClient.cancel(runId, "handoff_to_prepare");
          break;
        }
      }
      setStatusMessage("Outline ready");
    })()
      .catch((error) => setStatusMessage(String(error?.message ?? error)))
      .finally(() => setStreaming(false));
    return () => abort.abort();
  }, [presentationId, enabled, dispatch]);

  return { isStreaming: streaming, isLoading: streaming, activeSlideIndex: null,
           highestActiveIndex: -1, statusMessage };
}

setOutlines still runs limitOutlines (store/slices/presentationGeneration.ts:128-130), so every downstream component, including /prepare, sees the same {content} list as before. The stages after this:

Stage Change in Presenton Old code removed when S1 Outline page plans through @gck/client behind NEXT_PUBLIC_GCK_OUTLINE; the run is cancelled at the review point the flag has been on by default for one release with no regressions S2 Template preview thumbnails render through @gck/target-slides/renderer (same code, new import path) lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts is a re-export shim, then deleted S3 Outline page renders OutlineReview instead of OutlineContent OutlineContent, OutlineItem, useOutlineManagement have no importers S4 "Generate" answers the run's run.awaiting_input (no more cancel) instead of calling /prepare and the slide stream the presentation page can load a materialized deck by id (it already can, through GET /presentation/{id}) S5 AI Slides (Part VIII) moves to the same run API Part VIII's own release plan allows it

Gotcha

S1 is not invisible to users. The legacy hook highlights the outline card that is still being written, because it re-parses partial JSON on every chunk (useOutlineStreaming.ts:142-164); plan.proposed arrives whole, so the facade returns activeSlideIndex: null and the cards appear at once. Either accept that change explicitly when you turn the flag on, or have the engine emit plan.proposed with final: false more than once while Step A is still writing, and restore the highlight from the newest outline item. text.delta cannot carry the plan: it addresses a block of the artifact (blockId), and the plan is not part of the artifact.

Gotcha

Do not let S4 remove the legacy slide stream while usePresentationStreaming still handles Smart mode through the same URL (usePresentationStreaming.ts:407-452). Smart is not a GCK target, so /presentation/stream/{id} keeps serving Smart decks forever, and the hook stays in Presenton.

docs.title: Step 12: Choose a repository strategy
docs.text:
Two layouts are realistic.

Concern A: packages inside the fork (presenton-os/packages/*) B: gck/ monorepo next to the fork Upstream rebase cost High: root package.json (no workspaces today, package.json:1-26), servers/nextjs/package-lock.json, Dockerfile, Electron build all change Low: the fork gains only dependency lines and the seam files below Docker build servers/nextjs is installed alone with npm ci from its own lock file (Dockerfile:42-44); file: links to ../../packages are outside that layer Unchanged; @gck/* come from a registry like any dependency Iteration speed One commit spans kit and Presenton Two commits; use a local registry or npm pack tarballs during development Other hosts (Superset extension, Tiptap apps) Must depend on a slides product repository Depend on a small, focused repository Protocol contract Easy to share The engine exports its Pydantic models as JSON Schemas and opens a pull request against @gck/protocol

Recommendation: B for the frontend, plus an engine module inside the fork. The @gck/* packages live in gck/ (pnpm workspaces and Turborepo, per the blueprint). The GCK Engine is a generalized Presenton FastAPI, so its code lives in the fork, in a new directory servers/fastapi/gck_engine/ that upstream never touches. The protocol contract flows from the engine to the kit: the engine's Pydantic models (gck_engine.protocol) are the source of truth, as Presenton's own response schemas are (generate_presentation_outlines.py:362-365 derives one with model_json_schema()), and a script exports them into gck/packages/protocol/schemas/ through a pull request; Frontend engineering and quality shows the script and the contract tests on both sides. The kit consumes the engine the way Presenton consumes export-core, by a pinned version (package.json:4), never by reaching into the fork's tree.

The fork's footprint outside servers/fastapi/gck_engine/ is a short list of seams, and this list is what you re-check on every rebase:

Seam Lines changed servers/fastapi/api/main.py one include_router, one exception handler servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/gck_slides.py new file: POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/slides/from-content on PRESENTATION_ROUTER (Step 8), plus one import so the route registers servers/fastapi/services/database.py two entries in the create_all list, one in _STRICT_OWNER_MODELS servers/fastapi/alembic/versions/<new>.py new file servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py one call to fail_interrupted_runs next to fail_interrupted_async_tasks (lifespan.py:62) servers/fastapi/utils/llm_utils.py the extra_validator keyword nginx.conf, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts one location; one path test and its cookie-check bypass servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py, api/v1/auth/router.py accept a short-lived Bearer JWT; one token endpoint servers/nextjs/package.json @gck/* dependencies Facade hooks in servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/ strangler stages

Keeping in sync with upstream (presenton/presenton) then has a known cost. The fork already carries upstream and origin remotes; rebase onto upstream on a fixed cadence, and before each rebase list what upstream changed in the modules GCK imports: utils/llm_calls/, utils/llm_utils.py, utils/schema_utils.py, templates/v2/, and the hydration helpers in api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py. Those imports are the real coupling, and the integration tests in Step 9 are what tells you whether an upstream change broke them.

Move code upstream, not sideways

Importing _apply_template_content_to_ui from an endpoint module is the cheapest option today and the most fragile one over time. The durable fix is an upstream pull request that moves the hydration helpers into a module such as templates/v2/hydration.py with no behavior change. Until it merges, keep the import and a test that fails loudly if the function disappears.

docs.title: Step 13: Licensing
docs.text:
Presenton is licensed under the Apache License 2.0 (LICENSE:1-3), with "Copyright 2025 presenton" in the appendix (LICENSE:190). Any @gck/* file that starts from Presenton code (the renderer, the chart loader, prompt text, schema helpers) is a Derivative Work. Section 4 of the license sets four conditions (LICENSE:90-122):

Condition What it means for GCK 4(a) give recipients a copy of the License Ship LICENSE (Apache-2.0) in every @gck/* package tarball and in gck/ 4(b) modified files carry prominent change notices A header on each moved or adapted file: origin path, "modified by", date 4(c) retain copyright, patent, trademark and attribution notices Keep existing notices and vendored license headers 4(d) include the attribution notices from the NOTICE file See below

Presenton's NOTICE is not a short attribution line. It is a 26,825-line list of third-party licenses with a PYTHON PACKAGES section (NOTICE:2) and a NODE PACKAGES section (NOTICE:3783), duplicated at servers/fastapi/NOTICE. Condition 4(d) excludes the notices "that do not pertain to any part of the Derivative Works" (LICENSE:107-111). So each package's NOTICE should contain a line attributing Presenton plus the third-party notices for what that package actually ships: for @gck/target-slides, at least Chart.js and the datalabels plugin, whose license files are vendored next to the scripts (servers/nextjs/public/vendor/chart-4.5.1-LICENSE.md, chartjs-plugin-datalabels-2.2.0-LICENSE.md), and KaTeX, which lib/math.ts imports (servers/nextjs/lib/math.ts:1) and which therefore moves with the renderer. Generate the third-party part from each package's lock file in CI rather than editing it by hand.

Section 6 grants no right to use the licensor's names or marks (LICENSE:139-142), so name the kit GCK and describe Presenton only factually ("derived from Presenton"). You may add terms for your own modifications (LICENSE:124-129), but the Presenton-derived parts stay Apache-2.0, so licensing all of @gck/* under Apache-2.0 avoids mixed-license packages. This is an engineering reading of the license, not legal advice.

Gotcha

@presenton/export-core cannot be a dependency of any new target. It is installed as a prebuilt archive, presenton-export-core-opensource-<version>.tgz, downloaded from the presenton/presenton-export releases at a pinned version (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:32-33, :170-172, package.json:4), its install directory is git-ignored (.gitignore:30-32), and its source and license text are not part of this repository, which is why PPTX and PDF export treats it as a closed engine. The slides target may keep calling Presenton's export endpoint, which uses export-core at runtime exactly as Presenton does today. Tiptap, dashboard and text targets export natively (ProseMirror JSON, HTML and Markdown, Superset dashboard JSON), and no @gck/* package may bundle or import export-core.

docs.title: Step 14: Migration plan with checkpoints
docs.text:
Each milestone ends with a checkpoint that is objective and can be automated. The order follows Roadmap and tracker: text first, then Tiptap and dashboards, and slides last, because AI Slides already works through Part VIII and moving it onto the kit is a refactor that is safest once the kit is proven on the other targets. Nothing before M6 changes Presenton's visible behavior.

Milestone Roadmap phase Work Checkpoint (all must pass) M0 Baseline before P0 Fork rebased on upstream; seam list recorded; CI runs FastAPI tests (uv run --locked python -m pytest, CI, tests, security) and node --test in servers/nextjs (servers/nextjs/package.json:11) Both suites green on the fork M1 Protocol P0 gck_engine.protocol Pydantic models in the fork; docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Which Presenton modules GCK keeps (llmai, provider helpers, schema_utils, web search, documents, auth), generalizes (the three LLM steps, structured retries, SSE, async tasks, Smart checkpoints), leaves slides-only (Template v2, hydration, Smart, the editor) or drops.
  • How generate_ppt_outline, generate_presentation_structure and slide content generation become plan, layout choice and block steps driven by a TargetManifest, with prompts that keep Presenton's authority and voice rules but replace invented chart data with bindings.
  • How the canonical build_response_schema is narrowed per section with schema_utils, how number discipline is enforced in prompt, schema, validator and adapter, and why the Template v2 chart schema cannot be reused as is.
  • How gck_runs and gck_run_events generalize AsyncTaskModel and Smart checkpoints into a replayable log, and how the /api/gck/v1/runs router, nginx and proxy.ts fit together.
  • How to carve @gck/* out of servers/nextjs, make Presenton consume the kit through facades, keep the fork cheap to rebase with a gck/ monorepo beside it, and meet Apache-2.0 obligations without export-core.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Frontend engineering and quality to set up the gck/ monorepo, builds, bundle budgets, testing with recorded event logs and release management for the packages carved out here.

docs.title: Frontend engineering and quality
docs.text:
Reads: servers/nextjs/package.json, servers/nextjs/eslint.config.mjs, servers/nextjs/cypress.config.ts, servers/nextjs/cypress/security/dependencies.cy.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/SmartHtmlSlide.tsx, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/useSmartChartInjection.ts, servers/nextjs/lib/chart-browser.ts, servers/nextjs/utils/mixpanel.ts, apache/superset: superset-frontend/webpack.config.js, apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/extensions/ExtensionsLoader.ts, apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/theme/*, apache/superset: superset/config.py · Builds on: Architecture, React SDK and UI kit, Host integrations · Time: ~50 min

The previous chapters defined what the Generative Content Kit (GCK) does: the Artifact Spec, the run protocol, the React SDK, the host integrations and the extraction plan. This chapter is about how the kit is built, shipped and kept correct. You will lay out the gck/ monorepo file by file, write the package.json exports maps, build configs and bundle budgets, package the kit three ways (npm packages, a Module Federation remote inside a Superset extension, and a web component), and then work through theming, i18n, accessibility, performance, security, testing, release engineering and telemetry, each with concrete config and code. Where Presenton or Superset already does something relevant, the chapter cites the source so you can see which constraints are real and which are design choices.

What is source and what is new

Every code block whose title ends in "(new)" is design code for the GCK and does not exist in either repository. Blocks with a path title and no "(new)" are verbatim excerpts. Presenton paths are relative to the Presenton repository root at 571461f. Superset paths are prefixed apache/superset: and refer to master at cabd8d4.

docs.title: Step 1: The monorepo layout
docs.text: The blueprint fixes the shape: one repository gck/, pnpm workspaces, Turborepo, the eleven @gck/* packages listed in Architecture. The tree below adds the folders every package needs to be built, tested and documented.

docs.title: 1.1 The directory tree
docs.text:
gck/ (new)
gck/
├── package.json                  # private root: scripts, devDependencies, packageManager
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── turbo.json
├── tsconfig.base.json            # shared compilerOptions
├── tsconfig.json                 # solution file: references only
├── .size-limit.json              # bundle budgets (Step 3)
├── .changeset/                   # changesets config and pending changesets (Step 12)
├── .github/workflows/
│   ├── ci.yml                    # Step 11
│   └── release.yml               # Step 12
├── tooling/
│   ├── eslint-config/            # @gck/eslint-config (private)
│   ├── tsconfig/                 # @gck/tsconfig (private): base, dom, node presets
│   └── testing/                  # @gck/testing (private): MSW replay handlers, fast-check arbitraries
├── packages/
│   ├── protocol/                 # @gck/protocol: types + JSON Schemas, zero runtime deps
│   │   ├── schemas/              # *.schema.json exported from the engine (Step 10.2)
│   │   ├── fixtures/             # valid/ and invalid/ Artifacts (Artifact Spec chapter)
│   │   └── src/
│   ├── client/                   # @gck/client: fetch SSE reader, retries, token provider
│   ├── core/                     # @gck/core: run machine, IR store, JSON Patch, registry
│   │   └── src/workers/          # patch-and-repair worker (Step 8.4)
│   ├── react/                    # @gck/react: hooks, GckProvider, headless primitives
│   │   └── src/ui/               # @gck/react/ui styled kit + gck.css
│   ├── element/                  # @gck/element: <gck-generate> web component
│   ├── target-slides/            # @gck/target-slides: Template v2 JSON; /react, /renderer, /charts subpaths
│   ├── target-tiptap/            # @gck/target-tiptap: ProseMirror JSON + GckGenerate; /react node views
│   ├── target-superset-dashboard/
│   ├── target-text/
│   ├── host-superset/            # @gck/host-superset: extension glue, theme bridge
│   └── data-superset/            # @gck/data-superset: chart catalog + refresh
├── apps/
│   ├── storybook/                # one Storybook for all UI packages (Step 10.4)
│   ├── docs/                     # docs site (Step 12.5)
│   └── superset-extension/       # the .supx frontend: webpack + Module Federation (Step 4.2)
├── examples/                     # private, built in CI, never published
│   ├── react-vite-tiptap/
│   ├── nextjs-app-router/
│   ├── plain-html-element/
│   └── presenton-ai-slides/
├── fixtures/
│   ├── event-logs/               # recorded runs as JSONL (Step 10.3)
│   └── artifacts/                # golden Artifacts per target
├── e2e/                          # Playwright: projects per host (Step 10.5)
└── engine/                       # optional: GCK Engine (Python, uv) if co-located

engine/ is optional. If the GCK Engine lives in a separate repository (for example as a fork of Presenton's FastAPI server, see Extracting the engine from Presenton), the schema export in Step 10.2 runs there and opens a pull request against packages/protocol/schemas/.

docs.title: 1.2 Workspace files
docs.text:
gck/pnpm-workspace.yaml (new)
packages:
  - "packages/*"
  - "tooling/*"

  - "e2e"

{
  "name": "gck-monorepo",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "packageManager": "pnpm@10.12.1",
  "engines": { "node": ">=20.19" },
  "scripts": {
    "build": "turbo run build",
    "dev": "turbo run dev --parallel",
    "lint": "turbo run lint",
    "typecheck": "tsc -b",
    "test": "turbo run test",
    "size": "size-limit",
    "e2e": "pnpm --filter @gck/e2e test",
    "changeset": "changeset",
    "release": "turbo run build --filter=./packages/* && changeset publish"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@changesets/cli": "^2.29.0",
    "@size-limit/preset-small-lib": "^11.2.0",
    "size-limit": "^11.2.0",

    "typescript": "^5.8.0"
  }
}
gck/turbo.json (new)
{
  "$schema": "https://turbo.build/schema.json",
  "tasks": {
    "build": { "dependsOn": ["^build"], "outputs": ["dist/**"] },
    "dev": { "cache": false, "persistent": true },
    "lint": { "dependsOn": ["^build"] },

    "storybook:build": { "dependsOn": ["^build"], "outputs": ["storybook-static/**"] }

Type checking runs once for the whole graph with tsc -b (Step 1.4), not per package through Turborepo, because project references already give incremental, ordered checking and a second layer of caching only adds confusion about which cache is stale.

docs.title: 1.3 Package manifests and exports maps
docs.text:
Every published package is ESM-only, declares "type": "module", ships dist/ plus its own README, and resolves through an exports map with types listed first. Four manifests show the patterns.

@gck/protocol has no runtime dependencies. Its JSON Schemas (schemas/artifact-1.schema.json and the run schemas of Step 10.2) and the Artifact fixture corpus (fixtures/valid/, fixtures/invalid/, see Artifact Spec and targets) are files, exposed through subpaths so that runtime code never imports them by accident:

packages/protocol/package.json (new)
{
  "name": "@gck/protocol",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "files": ["dist", "schemas", "fixtures"],
  "exports": {
    ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" },
    "./schemas/*.json": "./schemas/*.json",
    "./fixtures/*": "./fixtures/*",
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  }
}

@gck/react has two entry points and ships CSS. It depends on @gck/core, @gck/client and @gck/protocol (the provider constructs the GckClient); intl-messageformat is the ICU formatter proposed in Step 6.1. React is a peer that accepts both majors, because Superset master is on React 18.3 (apache/superset: superset-frontend/package.json:196) while Presenton is on React 19.2.6 (servers/nextjs/package.json:59):

packages/react/package.json (new)
{
  "name": "@gck/react",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "module",
  "sideEffects": ["**/*.css"],
  "files": ["dist"],
  "exports": {
    ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" },
    "./ui": { "types": "./dist/ui/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/ui/index.js" },
    "./ui/gck.css": "./dist/ui/gck.css",
    "./package.json": "./package.json"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@gck/client": "workspace:^",
    "@gck/core": "workspace:^",
    "@gck/protocol": "workspace:^",
    "intl-messageformat": "^10.7.0"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.0 || ^19.0.0",
    "react-dom": "^18.3.0 || ^19.0.0"
  }
}

@gck/target-tiptap supports Tiptap 2 and 3 through an internal compatibility module (src/compat/), so @tiptap/core is a peer with two ranges. Like every target, its main entry is React-free and DOM-free (createTiptapTarget, toProseMirror, fromProseMirror, applyToEditor, the GckGenerate extension); the React node views (gckNodes, GckChart, GckMetric, GckDataTable, GckToken) live in a /react subpath. The React peers are therefore optional, because the main entry also works with a vanilla Tiptap editor:

packages/target-tiptap/package.json (excerpt, new)
{
  "name": "@gck/target-tiptap",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" },
    "./react": { "types": "./dist/react/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/react/index.js" }
  },
  "dependencies": { "@gck/core": "workspace:^", "@gck/protocol": "workspace:^" },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@gck/react": "workspace:^",
    "@tiptap/core": "^2.10.0 || ^3.0.0",
    "@tiptap/pm": "^2.10.0 || ^3.0.0",
    "@tiptap/react": "^2.10.0 || ^3.0.0",
    "react": "^18.3.0 || ^19.0.0"
  },
  "peerDependenciesMeta": {
    "@gck/react": { "optional": true },
    "@tiptap/react": { "optional": true },
    "react": { "optional": true }
  }
}

@gck/host-superset treats @apache-superset/core as an optional peer. The package exports two kinds of code: extension glue that only makes sense inside Superset (commands, views, context providers), and pure functions such as supersetThemeToGck() (Step 5) that an app embedding Superset dashboards through the Embedded SDK can call with its own antd tokens, without @apache-superset/core installed:

packages/host-superset/package.json (excerpt, new)
{
  "name": "@gck/host-superset",
  "sideEffects": false,
  "exports": {
    ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" },
    "./theme": { "types": "./dist/theme.d.ts", "import": "./dist/theme.js" }
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@gck/react": "workspace:^",
    "@gck/target-superset-dashboard": "workspace:^",
    "@gck/target-text": "workspace:^",
    "@gck/data-superset": "workspace:^"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@apache-superset/core": ">=0.1.0 <1.0.0",
    "antd": "^6.0.0",
    "react": "^18.3.0 || ^19.0.0"
  },
  "peerDependenciesMeta": {
    "@apache-superset/core": { "optional": true },
    "antd": { "optional": true }
  }
}

Gotcha: sideEffects: false deletes your CSS

A bundler that trusts "sideEffects": false drops any import that binds no names, which is exactly what import "@gck/react/ui/gck.css" is. Packages that ship CSS must list it ("sideEffects": ["**/*.css"]). The same applies to @gck/element: customElements.define(...) is a side effect, so it lives in a separate define entry that is listed in sideEffects, while the class itself stays tree-shakable.

Gotcha: ESM-only meets Jest

Superset's frontend tests run on Jest. An ESM-only package inside node_modules is not transformed by default, so a host that unit-tests code importing @gck/* must add the scope to transformIgnorePatterns (or mock the kit). Document this in each package README rather than shipping a CommonJS build that doubles the test matrix.

docs.title: 1.4 TypeScript project references
docs.text:
gck/tsconfig.base.json (new)
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "strict": true,
    "exactOptionalPropertyTypes": true,
    "noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "composite": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": true,
    "emitDeclarationOnly": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
packages/core/tsconfig.json (new)
{
  "extends": "../../tsconfig.base.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "lib": ["ES2022", "WebWorker"],
    "rootDir": "src",
    "outDir": "dist/types-check"
  },
  "include": ["src"],
  "references": [{ "path": "../protocol" }, { "path": "../client" }]
}

The lib setting is the cheapest architecture test you will ever write: @gck/core is framework-agnostic and "no DOM" per the blueprint, so its tsconfig omits "DOM". Any accidental document.querySelector in core fails type checking. WebWorker is included because the patch worker (Step 8.4) lives there. UI packages extend a dom preset from tooling/tsconfig that adds "DOM", "DOM.Iterable" and "jsx": "react-jsx". The root tsconfig.json lists every package in references and has "files": [].

docs.title: 1.5 Building with tsup (and Vite library mode for the element)
docs.text:
Libraries are built with tsup: ESM output, declaration files, and no bundling of dependencies or peers (tsup externalizes both by default, so no external list is needed).

packages/react/tsup.config.ts (new)
import { defineConfig } from "tsup";

export default defineConfig({
  entry: { index: "src/index.ts", "ui/index": "src/ui/index.ts" },
  format: ["esm"],
  dts: true,
  sourcemap: true,
  clean: true,
  treeshake: true,
  splitting: true,          // shared chunks between index and ui, and lazy import() chunks
  target: "es2020",
  platform: "browser",
  banner: { js: '"use client";' },
  loader: { ".css": "copy" },
  onSuccess: "cp src/ui/gck.css dist/ui/gck.css",
});

The "use client" banner matters for Next.js App Router hosts such as Presenton: without it, importing a hook-using component from a server component fails at build time. @gck/core, @gck/client and @gck/protocol use the same config without the banner and with platform: "neutral".

Gotcha: tsup is in maintenance

The tsup README now states that the project "is not actively maintained anymore" and points to tsdown, which has a "Migrate from tsup" guide (https://github.com/egoist/tsup, https://tsdown.dev/guide/). The options used above (entry, format, dts, platform, sourcemap, clean) are the basic set; check each against the migration guide before switching rather than assuming a one-to-one mapping.

@gck/element is different: it must bundle React because its hosts (Angular, Vue, plain pages) do not provide one. Vite library mode suits that (https://vite.dev/guide/build.html#library-mode): with multiple entries the default formats are es and cjs, so restrict to es.

packages/element/vite.config.ts (new)
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  define: { "process.env.NODE_ENV": JSON.stringify("production") },
  build: {
    lib: {
      entry: { index: "src/index.ts", define: "src/define.ts" },
      formats: ["es"],
    },
    sourcemap: true,
    target: "es2020",
  },
});

docs.title: 1.6 CSS strategy
docs.text:
The kit must look native in Superset (antd 6, Emotion), in Tiptap apps (often Tailwind or shadcn), in Presenton (Tailwind 3 plus a browser Tailwind 4 runtime for Smart slides, see Next.js architecture) and on plain pages. No single CSS-in-JS library is shared by all of them, so the kit uses none:

  1. Headless first. @gck/react primitives render no styles at all; hosts that want full control style them with their own system.
  2. One plain stylesheet for @gck/react/ui, gck.css. All selectors are prefixed .gck- and wrapped in @layer gck { ... }, so any unlayered host rule wins without !important.
  3. Every visual value is a --gck-* custom property (Step 5), set on the kit's root element (the .gck-root wrapper that GckProvider renders). Host theming is a mapping function into GckProvider's theme prop, not an override war.
  4. Logical properties only (margin-inline-start, padding-block), so RTL works without a second stylesheet (Step 6).
  5. No runtime style injection by default. Hosts import @gck/react/ui/gck.css through their bundler. For hosts that cannot (a Superset extension built with the stock template has no CSS loader, Step 4.2), a proposed helper injectGckStyles({ nonce }) in @gck/react/ui appends one <style> element with an optional nonce.
  6. Inside the web component, the stylesheet is adopted into the shadow root. CSS custom properties inherit through the shadow boundary, so --gck-* tokens set on the host page still apply.

Three rules keep the graph honest, enforced by an ESLint no-restricted-imports block per package in tooling/eslint-config:

Rule Enforced by Why protocol, client, core never import React or the DOM tsconfig lib (Step 1.4) plus a lint rule banning react* imports the core must run in a worker, in Node tests and under any framework Targets depend on core, never on react, in their main entry; previews and node views live in a /react subpath reached through loadPreview lint rule a server-side or worker consumer of toNative() must not pull React Only host-* packages import host SDKs (@apache-superset/core) lint rule keeps every other package host-agnostic

Presenton's lint config turns off sixteen rules, including @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any and react-hooks/rules-of-hooks (servers/nextjs/eslint.config.mjs:10-27). Code extracted into the kit (Extracting the engine from Presenton) lands in packages with those rules on; fix violations during the move instead of copying the overrides.

docs.title: Step 3: Bundle budgets and lazy loading
3.1 The budgets
docs.text:
The blueprint sets two numbers; the rest are proposals that follow from them and are labeled as such.

Bundle Budget (gzip) Source Notes @gck/core incl. its @gck/client and @gck/protocol runtime < 15 kB blueprint includes jsonrepair (the store's format: "json" drafts) and d3-format (resolveToken); if the budget is exceeded, jsonrepair is the first candidate for a dynamic import() on the first JSON text.delta @gck/react + @gck/react/ui, excluding renderers < 40 kB blueprint React and react-dom excluded (peers) @gck/target-text < 5 kB proposal pure serializers @gck/target-tiptap (eager part) < 12 kB proposal Tiptap excluded (peer) @gck/target-slides (eager part: manifest + adapter) < 8 kB proposal renderer and Chart.js are lazy @gck/target-slides lazy preview chunk < 120 kB proposal see measurement below @gck/element full bundle < 110 kB proposal includes React, react-dom, core, ui Superset extension initial chunk (remoteEntry + ./index) < 60 kB proposal React, antd and @apache-superset/core come from the host

The slides preview budget comes from what Presenton ships today: Chart.js 4.5.1 as a 208,522-byte UMD file (70,529 bytes gzipped at level 9), the datalabels plugin (5,275 bytes gzipped), both under servers/nextjs/public/vendor/, and the Template v2 renderer servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts (4,145 lines, 191,674 bytes of unminified TypeScript). The UMD build registers every chart controller; importing only the controllers that ChartKind needs from the ESM build is the main lever. Measure the minified renderer chunk once it is extracted.

docs.title: 3.2 Enforcing them with size-limit
docs.text:
size-limit measures Brotli by default; "gzip": true switches to gzip so the numbers match the budgets. The import field measures the tree-shaken cost of what a consumer actually imports, and ignore keeps peers out of the total (https://github.com/ai/size-limit).

gck/.size-limit.json (new)
[
  { "name": "core", "path": "packages/core/dist/index.js",
    "import": "{ createRunController, createArtifactStore, createRegistry }", "gzip": true, "limit": "15 kB" },
  { "name": "react kit", "path": ["packages/react/dist/index.js", "packages/react/dist/ui/index.js"],
    "import": "*", "gzip": true, "limit": "40 kB",
    "ignore": ["react", "react-dom", "react/jsx-runtime"] },
  { "name": "target-tiptap", "path": "packages/target-tiptap/dist/index.js",
    "import": "{ createTiptapTarget, GckGenerate }", "gzip": true, "limit": "12 kB",
    "ignore": ["@tiptap/core", "@tiptap/pm"] },
  { "name": "target-slides eager", "path": "packages/target-slides/dist/index.js",
    "import": "{ createSlidesTarget }", "gzip": true, "limit": "8 kB" },
  { "name": "target-slides preview (lazy)", "path": ["packages/target-slides/dist/react/*.js", "packages/target-slides/dist/charts/*.js"],
    "gzip": true, "limit": "120 kB", "ignore": ["react", "react-dom"] },
  { "name": "element", "path": "packages/element/dist/index.js",
    "gzip": true, "limit": "110 kB" }
]

In CI (Step 11) pnpm size fails the job when any limit is exceeded, and the andresz1/size-limit-action@v1 step posts the diff against main on the pull request. A budget is raised only in the same pull request that explains why, reviewed like an API change.

docs.title: 3.3 Lazy renderers
docs.text:
A target adapter keeps its manifest and serializer eager (the engine needs the manifest on every run, see Artifact Spec and targets) and its preview lazy, behind TargetAdapter.loadPreview. The slides target loads its renderer and Chart.js only the first time a slides preview mounts:

packages/target-slides/src/index.ts (excerpt, new)
import type { TargetAdapter } from "@gck/core";
import type { LayoutSummary } from "@gck/protocol";
import type { SlidesNative } from "./types";
// No static import from ./react/*: it would pull the renderer and Chart.js into the main entry.

export function createSlidesTarget(templateId: string, catalog: LayoutSummary[]): TargetAdapter<SlidesNative> {
  return {
    manifest: buildManifest(catalog),                     // eager: sent with every run
    toNative: (a) => toSlides(templateId, catalog, a),    // deterministic serializer: small, eager, no DOM
    // Preview: Template v2 renderer + Chart.js, fetched on first mount only.
    loadPreview: () => import("./react/preview").then((m) => m.SlidesPreview),
    apply: applySlides,
  };
}

buildManifest, toSlides and applySlides stand for the manifest, toNative and apply code shown in Artifact Spec and targets. Chart.js itself is reached through the @gck/target-slides/charts subpath. Extracting the engine from Presenton first moves lib/chart-browser.ts there as is, with the script URLs turned into options; for hosts that do not serve Presenton's /vendor/ files (Superset, any bundled host), the subpath's loader becomes a module-scoped ESM import:

packages/target-slides/src/charts/chart-runtime.ts (new)
import type { Chart as ChartType } from "chart.js";

let runtime: Promise<typeof ChartType> | undefined;

export function loadChartRuntime(): Promise<typeof ChartType> {
  runtime ??= Promise.all([import("chart.js"), import("chartjs-plugin-datalabels")])
    .then(([chartjs, datalabels]) => {
      const { Chart, BarController, LineController, PieController, DoughnutController,
        ScatterController, RadarController, BarElement, LineElement, PointElement, ArcElement,
        CategoryScale, LinearScale, RadialLinearScale, Legend, Tooltip, Filler } = chartjs;
      Chart.register(BarController, LineController, PieController, DoughnutController,
        ScatterController, RadarController, BarElement, LineElement, PointElement, ArcElement,
        CategoryScale, LinearScale, RadialLinearScale, Legend, Tooltip, Filler, datalabels.default);
      return Chart;
    })
    .catch((error) => { runtime = undefined; throw error; });
  return runtime;
}

useTargetPreview wraps loadPreview in React.lazy (cached per adapter), and StreamingPreview renders it inside a Suspense boundary whose fallback is the same skeleton the streaming state already shows (React SDK and UI kit), so the lazy load never causes a layout jump.

Gotcha: Presenton's chart runtime is a global script

Presenton loads Chart.js by appending <script src="/vendor/chart-4.5.1.umd.min.js"> and caches the promise on window.__PRESENTON_CHART_BROWSER_RUNTIME__ (servers/nextjs/lib/chart-browser.ts:1-3, :58-96, :98-136). That works only where /vendor/ is served from the same origin and nothing else defines window.Chart. Inside a Superset extension the path does not exist, and a host that already uses Chart.js would share (or clobber) the global. Outside Presenton, the kit therefore uses the module-scoped ESM loader above, which webpack or Vite turns into a hashed chunk next to the rest of the bundle.

docs.title: 4.1 npm packages for React apps
docs.text:
React hosts (Presenton, any Vite or Next.js app with Tiptap) install the packages they need and get one copy of React, Tiptap and the kit, deduplicated by their package manager:

pnpm add @gck/react @gck/target-tiptap @tiptap/core @tiptap/pm @tiptap/react
examples/react-vite-tiptap/src/GckRoot.tsx (excerpt, new)
import "@gck/react/ui/gck.css";
import { useMemo, type ReactNode } from "react";
import type { Editor } from "@tiptap/core";
import { createHost } from "@gck/core";
import { GckProvider } from "@gck/react";
import { createTiptapTarget } from "@gck/target-tiptap";

export function GckRoot({ editor, children }: { editor: Editor; children: ReactNode }) {
  const targets = useMemo(() => [createTiptapTarget(editor)], [editor]);   // stable array
  const host = useMemo(() => createHost("tiptap", { "tiptap.editor": editor }), [editor]);
  return (
    <GckProvider
      engineUrl="/gck-engine"                // same-origin proxy to the GCK Engine
      getToken={getEngineToken}              // Step 9.4
      host={host}
      targets={targets}
      locale={navigator.language}
      telemetry={sendToOurPipeline}          // Step 13
    >
      {children}
    </GckProvider>
  );
}

docs.title: 4.2 A Module Federation remote inside a Superset extension
docs.text:
Superset loads extension frontends as webpack Module Federation remotes. The host declares four shared singletons, all eager:

apache/superset: superset-frontend/webpack.config.js:187-211
  new ModuleFederationPlugin({
    name: 'superset',
    filename: 'remoteEntry.js',
    shared: {
      react: {
        singleton: true,
        eager: true,
        requiredVersion: packageConfig.dependencies.react,
      },
      'react-dom': {
        singleton: true,
        eager: true,
        requiredVersion: packageConfig.dependencies['react-dom'],
      },
      antd: {
        singleton: true,
        requiredVersion: packageConfig.dependencies.antd,
        eager: true,
      },
      '@apache-superset/core': {
        singleton: true,
        eager: true,
      },
    },
  }),

The extension template generated by the Superset extensions CLI mirrors this on the remote side with import: false, which means the remote ships no fallback copy and always uses the host's:

apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/templates/frontend/webpack.config.js.j2:44-64
        shared: {
          react: {
            singleton: true,
            requiredVersion: packageConfig.peerDependencies.react,
            import: false,
          },
          "react-dom": {
            singleton: true,
            requiredVersion: packageConfig.peerDependencies["react-dom"],
            import: false,
          },
          antd: {
            singleton: true,
            requiredVersion: packageConfig.peerDependencies["antd"],
            import: false,
          },
          "@apache-superset/core": {
            singleton: true,
            import: false,
          },
        },

At load time ExtensionsLoader builds a custom share scope in which @apache-superset/core resolves to window.superset with extensions.getContext pre-bound to that extension (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/extensions/ExtensionsLoader.ts:204-220, :234-244), and window.superset itself is the host's real @apache-superset/core namespaces plus the host implementations (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/extensions/ExtensionsStartup.tsx:56-68). Everything the kit needs from Superset therefore arrives through one import of the package root.

apps/superset-extension is the .supx frontend. It bundles every @gck/* package it uses (they are not in Superset's share scope, so they cannot be shared) and takes React, react-dom, antd and @apache-superset/core from the host:

apps/superset-extension/webpack.config.js (excerpt, new)
const path = require("path");
const { ModuleFederationPlugin } = require("webpack").container;
const packageConfig = require("./package");
const extensionConfig = require("../extension.json");

module.exports = (env, argv) => ({
  // ...
  output: {
    clean: true,
    chunkFilename: "[name].[contenthash].js",
    path: path.resolve(__dirname, "dist"),
    // Lazy chunks (slides preview, Chart.js, patch worker) resolve against this path.
    publicPath: `/api/v1/extensions/${extensionConfig.publisher}/${extensionConfig.name}/`,
  },
  module: {
    rules: [
      { test: /\.tsx?$/, use: "ts-loader", exclude: /node_modules/ },
      { test: /\.css$/, use: ["style-loader", "css-loader"] },   // not in the stock template
    ],
  },
  plugins: [
    new ModuleFederationPlugin({
      name: "gck_superset",
      filename: "remoteEntry.[contenthash].js",
      exposes: { "./index": "./src/index.tsx" },
      shared: {
        react: { singleton: true, requiredVersion: packageConfig.peerDependencies.react, import: false },
        "react-dom": { singleton: true, requiredVersion: packageConfig.peerDependencies["react-dom"], import: false },
        antd: { singleton: true, requiredVersion: packageConfig.peerDependencies.antd, import: false },
        "@apache-superset/core": { singleton: true, import: false },
        // Deliberately NOT shared: @gck/*, chart.js, @emotion/*. See the gotchas below.
      },
    }),
  ],
});
apps/superset-extension/package.json (excerpt, new)
{
  "private": true,
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@apache-superset/core": "*",
    "antd": "^6.0.0",
    "react": "^18.3.0",
    "react-dom": "^18.3.0"
  }
}

Gotcha: the stock template references a peer it does not declare

The template's webpack config reads packageConfig.peerDependencies["antd"] (webpack.config.js.j2:55-59), but the generated package.json.j2 declares only @apache-superset/core, react and react-dom as peers (package.json.j2:16-20), so requiredVersion for antd is undefined. Add antd to peerDependencies explicitly, as above, so webpack can warn about a mismatch with the host's antd ("antd": "^6.6.7" in apache/superset: superset-frontend/package.json:159).

Gotcha: only the package root is shared

webpack's Module Federation docs state that to share anything below a package's root you must "append / to the package name" in shared (https://webpack.js.org/plugins/module-federation-plugin/). Superset shares '@apache-superset/core' without the slash, so a runtime import of a subpath such as @apache-superset/core/theme is not resolved from the host scope and would be bundled from the extension's devDependency instead. Inside the extension, import runtime values from the root only (import { theme } from "@apache-superset/core"); subpath imports are safe only for import type, which TypeScript erases.

Gotcha: never bundle a second React, and never import Emotion directly

import: false means a mismatch is not papered over: if @gck/react resolves its own react (for example through a pnpm link to the monorepo during development), hooks throw "Invalid hook call". Build the extension from published or packed tarballs, and add a CI check that greps the production bundle for React's internals marker. Emotion is not in the share scope either. @apache-superset/core's useTheme() reads Emotion's context through the host's own Emotion instance (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/theme/index.tsx:50-59); an extension that imports @emotion/react itself gets a separate context and finds no theme. The kit reads the theme only through theme.useTheme() from the shared root (Step 5).

The host runs React 18.3, so everything that ends up in the remote must work on React 18: no use() hook, no React 19 ref-as-prop. The React peer range in Step 1.3 is a promise the test matrix must keep (Step 10.5). Extensions are behind the ENABLE_EXTENSIONS feature flag, which defaults to False (apache/superset: superset/config.py:788), and are only loaded once a user id is known (ExtensionsStartup.tsx:50-51, :70-72).

docs.title: 4.3 The web component bundle
docs.text:
@gck/element defines <gck-generate> for hosts without React. Its attribute, property and event contract, and the full GckGenerateElement class, are in Host integrations (Step 6.1); this section only covers what matters for packaging it:

  • Shadow root. The element renders the React kit into a gck-root mount inside an open shadow root, so host CSS cannot break it and its CSS cannot leak out. Inside, it renders GckProvider with only its documented props and composes the five @gck/react/ui components itself; there is no packaged "whole flow" component and no portalContainer prop.
  • Stylesheet. The kit stylesheet (@gck/react/ui/gck.css) is written into the bundle as a string at build time (KIT_CSS from src/styles.generated.ts) and adopted on the shadow root with CSSStyleSheet.replaceSync, with a <style> element as the fallback.
  • Properties, not attributes. context, tokenProvider (a TokenProvider from @gck/client) and data are objects or functions, so they are properties only. The connected callback re-applies values a framework set before the element was defined.
  • Apply hand-off. The element applies nothing itself: it dispatches gck-apply with the native value and waits for the page to call reportApplied(result).
  • No side effects in the class module. src/index.ts only exports GckGenerateElement; registration lives in a separate define entry, which is the one listed in sideEffects (Step 1.3) and the one pages import as @gck/element/define:
packages/element/src/define.ts (new)
import { GckGenerateElement } from "./GckGenerateElement";
if (!customElements.get("gck-generate")) customElements.define("gck-generate", GckGenerateElement);

The element emits gck-apply ({ target, mode, native, artifact }, the host commits native), gck-state and gck-error; composed: true lets them cross the shadow boundary. Never load @gck/element inside Superset or another React host: it carries its own React, which doubles the bundle and splits context. React hosts use the npm packages; Superset uses the remote in Step 4.2.

docs.title: 4.4 The iframe fallback
docs.text: Hosts that cannot run third-party script at all mount the same standalone app in an iframe, the pattern Part VIII uses for AI Slides (Story 5, analytics menu and iframe). Context is posted in and apply results are posted out, with typed, origin-checked messages (Step 9.4). It is a fallback, not the default.

docs.title: 4.5 The compatibility matrix
docs.text:
Package line Protocol React Host versions Tiptap Notes @gck/protocol 1.x gck.artifact/1, run API v1 none any none independent semver (Step 12) @gck/core, @gck/client 1.x 1.0 to 1.latest none any none sends GCK-Protocol: 1 on every request @gck/react 1.x 1.x 18.3, 19.x any React host none tested on both majors @gck/target-tiptap 1.x 1.x 18.3, 19.x (optional) any 2.10+, 3.x Presenton uses Tiptap 3.30.5 (servers/nextjs/package.json:40-44) @gck/host-superset 1.x 1.x 18.3 (host) Superset 6.1 and master none extension menus differ by version, see Host integrations @gck/element 1.x 1.x bundled 19.x any page none not for React hosts @gck/target-slides 1.x 1.x 18.3, 19.x Presenton 0.9.x Template v2 none renderer extracted from lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts

The matrix lives in the docs site and is generated from the e2e job's actual matrix, so it cannot drift from what CI tests.

docs.title: 5.1 The token set
docs.text:
All styled components read these properties and nothing else. Defaults live in gck.css under .gck-root (React SDK and UI kit); hosts override them through GckProvider's theme prop (Partial<GckTheme>, keys accent, bg, fg, border, danger, radius, font), which the provider writes as --gck-<key> on its .gck-root wrapper.

Token Default (light, gck.css) GckTheme key From Superset theme token From a Tiptap host (shadcn variables) --gck-accent #1f6feb accent colorPrimary hsl(var(--primary)) --gck-bg #fff bg colorBgContainer hsl(var(--background)) --gck-fg #1c1c1c fg colorText hsl(var(--foreground)) --gck-border #e5e7eb border colorBorder hsl(var(--border)) --gck-danger #b42318 danger colorError hsl(var(--destructive)) --gck-radius 8px radius borderRadius (number, add px) var(--radius) --gck-font inherit font fontFamily computed font-family of the editor element --gck-space 8px none (stylesheet only) sizeUnit times 2 (number, add px) 8px

The eight properties above are the 1.0 contract. The rest of this chapter (focus ring, target size, reduced motion) also relies on the following additions, proposed for a 1.x minor (new tokens are a minor change, Step 12.2); each extends GckTheme with the same key minus the --gck- prefix when it ships:

Proposed token From Superset theme token From a Tiptap host --gck-fg-muted colorTextSecondary hsl(var(--muted-foreground)) --gck-accent-hover / --gck-on-accent colorPrimaryHover / colorTextLightSolid computed / hsl(var(--primary-foreground)) --gck-focus-ring controlOutline hsl(var(--ring)) --gck-warning / -success / -info colorWarning / colorSuccess / colorInfo defaults --gck-font-mono fontFamilyCode default --gck-font-size / --gck-line-height fontSize (number) / lineHeight (unitless) computed font-size / line-height --gck-control-height controlHeight (number) 2.25rem --gck-shadow-popover boxShadowSecondary default --gck-motion-duration motionDurationMid default --gck-z-overlay zIndexPopupBase host z-index scale

Every Superset name in both tables is in Superset's allowlist of antd tokens that make up SupersetTheme (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/theme/types.ts:277-500, type at :511), so the mapping uses the public theme contract rather than antd internals.

docs.title: 5.2 The Superset theme bridge
5.3 Dark mode and density
docs.text:
• Dark mode in Superset. Superset's dark theme already has dark values for colorBgContainer, colorText and the rest, so the bridge needs no separate dark table. Because it re-derives the theme object whenever the Emotion theme object changes, a user switching Superset between light, dark and system mode (ThemeMode, types.ts:56-60) re-themes the kit without a reload. isThemeDark(theme) is tinycolor(theme.colorBgContainer).isDark() (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/theme/utils/themeUtils.ts:55-57), exported from the theme namespace; a host can use it to set color-scheme on its own container so native scrollbars and form controls match.
  • Dark mode elsewhere. The gck.css defaults are light. A host with its own dark mode passes dark values through theme; class-based hosts (Presenton's Tailwind config uses darkMode: ["class"], servers/nextjs/tailwind.config.ts:4) derive them from their own state. A default dark set under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) for hosts that pass nothing is a proposed stylesheet addition; GckConfig has no colorScheme prop.
  • Density. antd's compact algorithm (ThemeAlgorithm.COMPACT, types.ts:43-47) produces smaller sizes. --gck-space is not a GckTheme key, so a host maps density with an unlayered stylesheet rule on .gck-root (for example sizeUnit times 2 in px), which wins over the layered gck.css default and tightens every padding defined as a multiple of --gck-space; the proposed --gck-control-height would follow controlHeight the same way.

Gotcha: antd numbers and shadcn triplets are not CSS values

antd tokens such as fontSize, borderRadius, controlHeight and sizeUnit are numbers, and lineHeight is a unitless ratio; writing --gck-radius: 6 produces an invalid length that silently falls back. shadcn-style hosts, including Presenton's own stylesheet, store colors as bare HSL components (--background: 0 0% 100%;, servers/nextjs/app/globals.css:40), which must be wrapped as hsl(var(--background)). The mapping functions own these conversions so components never do.

For Tiptap hosts without design tokens, a proposed helper themeFromElement(editor.view.dom) in @gck/target-tiptap/react (it reads the DOM, so it cannot live in the React-free main entry) reads getComputedStyle() of the editor element (font family, text and background colors) once on mount and returns a Partial<GckTheme>, so generated content previews in the same typography as the document it will be inserted into.

docs.title: 6.1 ICU messages
docs.text:
In 1.0, every kit string has a typed key (MessageKey), defaultMessages in src/messages.ts holds the English text, and GckContextValue.t(key, vars) substitutes {name} placeholders (React SDK and UI kit). That is enough for English and breaks on plurals. The proposal for 1.x keeps the keys and the t signature and swaps the formatter: messages become ICU MessageFormat strings in per-locale JSON catalogs inside @gck/react, formatted with intl-messageformat. ICU gives plurals, selects and number formatting that work across languages, which Presenton's UI does not need today (its chrome is English-only) and Superset handles with gettext through Jed.

packages/react/src/i18n/en.json (excerpt, new, proposal)
{
  "composer.placeholder": "Describe what to create",
  "status.planning": "Planning the outline",
  "status.generating": "Writing {completed, number} of {total, plural, one {# section} other {# sections}}",
  "status.resolving_data": "Fetching data for {total, plural, one {# chart} other {# charts}}",
  "status.ready": "Draft ready. Review it, then apply.",
  "preview.progress": "{n, plural, one {# section} other {# sections}} generated",
  "apply.done": "Applied.",
  "apply.undoNote": "Undo with {undoKey}."
}

The variables are the ones the components already pass: completed and total come from the event's progress, n from the section count.

packages/react/src/i18n/format.ts (new, proposal)
import IntlMessageFormat from "intl-messageformat";
import type { MessageKey } from "../messages";

const cache = new Map<string, IntlMessageFormat>();

export function format(locale: string, catalog: Partial<Record<MessageKey, string>>, id: MessageKey,
                       values?: Record<string, unknown>): string {
  const key = `${locale}\u0000${id}`;
  let msg = cache.get(key);
  if (!msg) {
    msg = new IntlMessageFormat(catalog[id] ?? id, locale);
    cache.set(key, msg);
  }
  return String(msg.format(values));
}

Catalogs for locales other than English are loaded with dynamic import() so that only the active locale ships. Hosts can override any message key through GckProvider messages={...} (a Partial<Messages>, already in 1.0), which is how a host aligns wording with its own product.

docs.title: 6.2 Host locale
docs.text:
Host Where the locale comes from Normalization Superset the language pack the page bootstraps into window.__SUPERSET_LANGUAGE_PACK__ and that @apache-superset/core's translator reads (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/translation/TranslatorSingleton.ts:39-59); its locale_data.superset[""].lang is a Superset Locale (translation/types/index.ts:26-72) Superset uses underscores (pt_BR, zh_TW, sr_Latn); convert to BCP 47 (pt-BR, zh-TW, sr-Latn) before calling Intl Tiptap app GckProvider locale from the app's i18n library already BCP 47 in most apps Presenton the presentation's language field for content; the UI stays English content language and UI locale are separate Web component locale attribute, else document.documentElement.lang as given

The window global is an implementation detail, not a documented extension API, so @gck/host-superset reads it only as a fallback, and one Superset e2e project (Step 10.5) runs in French to catch a change.

docs.title: 6.3 RTL and content language
docs.text:
Two directions coexist: the UI direction (from the UI locale) and the artifact direction (from Artifact.language, which the engine sets from the prompt or context.locale). An Arabic user can generate an English report, and the reverse. The kit sets dir and lang separately on the chrome and on the preview root:

packages/react/src/i18n/direction.ts (new)
const RTL_LANGUAGES = new Set(["ar", "fa", "he", "ur", "ps", "dv", "ku", "yi", "sd", "ug"]);

export function toBcp47(tag: string): string {
  return tag.replace(/_/g, "-");
}

export function directionOf(tag: string | undefined): "ltr" | "rtl" {
  if (!tag) return "ltr";
  const base = toBcp47(tag).split("-")[0]!.toLowerCase();
  return RTL_LANGUAGES.has(base) ? "rtl" : "ltr";
}

Superset's own catalog list includes two RTL locales, ar and fa (translation/types/index.ts:27, :33), so RTL is a real requirement, not a hypothetical. Because the stylesheet uses logical properties only (Step 1.6), flipping dir is all the layout needs. Streaming text in a mixed-direction paragraph is wrapped in <bdi> per data token so that a number or an English product name inside Arabic prose does not reorder its neighbors.

docs.title: 7.1 A WCAG 2.2 AA checklist for streaming UIs
docs.text:
