Criterion What it means for the kit How it is met 4.1.3 Status Messages state changes are announced without moving focus one role="status" live region per kit instance, aria-live="polite" (7.2) 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide streaming content auto-updates for more than five seconds next to other content Cancel stops the run; "Pause preview" freezes rendering while patches keep buffering 1.3.1 Info and Relationships the preview is not a pile of divs targets render semantic headings, lists and tables; charts get a text alternative from their binding title and data summary 2.1.1 Keyboard, 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap every action is reachable and leavable keyboard map (7.4); Escape always returns focus to the invoker 2.4.3 Focus Order, 2.4.7 Focus Visible focus moves predictably focus is moved only on user-initiated transitions (7.3); a 2 px outline in --gck-accent (the proposed --gck-focus-ring once it ships) 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) the floating ApplyBar must not cover the focused element ApplyBar reserves its height with scroll-padding-block-end on the preview scroller 2.5.7 Dragging Movements outline reordering cannot require a drag every outline row has Move up and Move down buttons in addition to drag 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) buttons are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels enforced by a min-block-size and min-inline-size of 24 px on every control in gck.css, which no density override can shrink 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast host-mapped tokens can fail contrast the Storybook a11y run checks every theme preset (Step 10.8); the bridge does not invent colors 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA, adopted) and reduced motion typing effects and shimmer are motion all animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (7.5) 3.3.1 Error Identification failures are explained in text run.failed and apply errors render a message plus a Retry button when retryable

Presenton already has the right instinct in places: the outline page renders a visually hidden role="status" aria-live="polite" region with the stream's status message (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/components/OutlineContent.tsx:84-89), and spinners use motion-reduce:animate-none (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/SlidePreviewLoader.tsx:15). The kit makes these rules systematic.

docs.title: 7.2 Announcing a stream without flooding the screen reader
docs.text:
A live region that receives every text.delta makes a screen reader read fragments forever. The kit announces state transitions immediately and progress at most every five seconds:

packages/react/src/a11y/useRunAnnouncer.ts (new)
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { RunState } from "@gck/core";
import type { GckContextValue } from "../provider";

const PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS = 5000;

export function useRunAnnouncer(state: RunState, t: GckContextValue["t"]) {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState("");
  const lastStatus = useRef(state.status);
  const lastProgressAt = useRef(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    const vars = { completed: state.progress?.completed ?? 0, total: state.progress?.total ?? 0 };
    if (state.status !== lastStatus.current) {      // transitions: always announce
      lastStatus.current = state.status;
      lastProgressAt.current = performance.now();
      setMessage(t(`status.${state.status}`, vars));
      return;
    }
    if (state.status === "generating" && performance.now() - lastProgressAt.current > PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS) {
      lastProgressAt.current = performance.now();
      setMessage(t("status.generating", vars));
    }
  }, [state.status, state.progress, t]);

  return message;   // rendered into <div role="status" aria-live="polite" className="gck-sr-only">
}

Components call it with run.state from useGenerationRun and t from useGckContext().

The preview container carries aria-busy="true" while the run is in generating or resolving_data, so assistive technology does not read half-built content as final. Failures use a separate role="alert" region, the only assertive announcement the kit makes.

docs.title: 7.3 Focus after apply
docs.text:
Focus moves only when the user caused the transition. After Apply, focus goes to the applied content in the host, and the ApplyBar announces apply.done with the target's undo hint (apply.undoNote, for example "Undo with Ctrl+Z"):

Target Focus after apply tiptap-doc editor.chain().focus().setTextSelection(insertedRange.to).scrollIntoView().run(): caret at the end of the inserted range, inside the same undo group slides the first new slide's thumbnail in the side panel superset-dashboard the new tab's title (or the dashboard title for a new dashboard) after navigation text the Markdown component that received the text

When a run finishes generating while the user is typing elsewhere (for example in the outline review), focus stays where it is; the status region announces readiness instead.

docs.title: 7.4 Keyboard map
docs.text:
Key Context Action /ai then Enter Tiptap editor open the composer at the cursor (GckGenerate slash command) Mod+Enter composer submit Escape composer, review, preview cancel the run if running, else close; focus returns to the invoker Alt+ArrowUp / Alt+ArrowDown outline row move the section up or down Enter outline review approve the outline Mod+Shift+Enter preview apply with the default mode Mod+Z host, after apply undo the whole application (one undo step, see React SDK and UI kit)

Shortcuts are registered on the kit's root element, not on window, so they never collide with host shortcuts.

docs.title: 7.5 Reduced motion
8.1 Throttle rendering to one frame
docs.text:
The engine can emit dozens of artifact.patch and text.delta events per second. Re-rendering after each one is wasted work, because the screen can only show one frame per refresh. Presenton debounces outline Markdown rendering with a 60 ms timer (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/components/OutlineItem.tsx:120-140); the kit generalizes that into the artifact store of @gck/core (React SDK and UI kit). createArtifactStore(schedule?) applies every patch to its snapshot immediately and batches only the notification: the first change in a frame calls schedule(emit), later changes in the same frame do nothing, and the default schedule is requestAnimationFrame behind a typeof guard, with a 16 ms setTimeout where it does not exist (Node tests, old workers). One frame, one notification, one React render.

requestAnimationFrame does not fire in background tabs, so subscribers hear about patches only when the tab becomes visible again. @gck/core cannot check document.hidden (it never touches the DOM), so a visibility-aware scheduler belongs in @gck/react. Passing it needs a schedule option on RunControllerOptions, which the 1.0 controller does not have (it calls createArtifactStore() with the default); this is proposed for 1.x:

packages/react/src/schedule.ts (new, proposal)
/** Frame-aligned while visible, timer-driven while hidden (rAF pauses in background tabs). */
export function visibilityAwareSchedule(fn: () => void): void {
  if (typeof document !== "undefined" && !document.hidden && typeof requestAnimationFrame === "function") {
    requestAnimationFrame(fn);
  } else {
    setTimeout(fn, 100);
  }
}

Gotcha: data is current, subscribers are not

store.getSnapshot() always reflects every event received so far, so the controller's apply() never sees an artifact missing its last patches. What lags by up to a frame is React: a value captured in a render can be one frame old. Code that acts on what the user sees (custom apply buttons, tests asserting on rendered output) calls store.flush() first, which delivers the pending notification synchronously; tests can also pass (fn) => fn() as schedule.

docs.title: 8.2 Re-render only what changed
docs.text:
The IR store applies JSON Patch with structural sharing: unchanged sections and blocks keep their object identity. React components subscribe per block through useArtifact (which wraps useSyncExternalStore) with a selector that returns one block, so a patch to block 37 re-renders block 37 only:

packages/react/src/use-block.ts (new)
import { useCallback } from "react";
import type { ArtifactSnapshot, ArtifactStore } from "@gck/core";
import type { Block } from "@gck/protocol";
import { useArtifact } from "./hooks";

export function useBlock(store: ArtifactStore, blockId: string): Block | undefined {
  const select = useCallback((s: ArtifactSnapshot) => {          // stable selector, as useArtifact requires
    const ref = s.index[blockId];
    return s.drafts[blockId] ?? (ref ? s.artifact?.sections[ref.section]?.blocks[ref.block] : undefined);
  }, [blockId]);
  return useArtifact(store, select);   // Object.is: an unchanged block keeps its identity, so no re-render
}

Presenton's presentation stream does the opposite: each chunk dispatches a whole new presentationData into Redux (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationStreaming.ts:482-502), and every subscriber of that slice re-renders. That is acceptable for 50 slides with block-level content; it does not scale to a 200-page Tiptap document.

docs.title: 8.3 Virtualize long artifacts
docs.text:
The preview list virtualizes once an artifact has more than 40 sections. Two levels are used:

  1. content-visibility: auto with contain-intrinsic-size on each section, which costs nothing and skips layout and paint for off-screen sections.
  2. A windowed list (for example TanStack Virtual) for the StreamingPreview and the slides thumbnail strip when the count is large enough that DOM node count itself is the problem. Measured heights are cached per section id so a streaming section that grows does not make the scroll position jump.

The slides preview renders a Template v2 slide to HTML only when its thumbnail intersects the viewport (IntersectionObserver), and Chart.js canvases are created only for visible slides and destroyed when they leave, the same cleanup Presenton does on re-render with Chart.getChart(canvas)?.destroy() (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx:309-317).

docs.title: 8.4 A worker for patch and repair
docs.text:
Presenton repairs partial JSON by appending each chunk to a string and running jsonrepair plus JSON.parse over the whole accumulated text on every chunk:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/hooks/useOutlineStreaming.ts:133-137
          case "chunk":
            accumulatedChunks += data.chunk;
            try {
              const repairedJson = jsonrepair(accumulatedChunks);
              const partialData = JSON.parse(repairedJson);

The same pattern is in the presentation stream (usePresentationStreaming.ts:455, :482-483). The work per chunk grows with the document, so total work grows with the square of its length, all on the main thread. The kit keeps block-level artifact.patch as the primary channel (small, already valid JSON) and confines repair to text.delta events with format: "json", where ArtifactStore.applyTextDelta runs jsonrepair over one block's buffer only. When the artifact is large, the same store runs in a worker:

packages/core/src/workers/patch.worker.ts (new)
/// <reference lib="webworker" />
import { createArtifactStore, selectRenderable } from "../artifact-store";
import type { WorkerRequest, WorkerResponse } from "./messages";

const store = createArtifactStore((fn) => fn());          // no frames in a worker: notify synchronously

self.onmessage = (event: MessageEvent<WorkerRequest>) => {
  const req = event.data;
  let patch: WorkerResponse["patch"];
  if (req.kind === "reset") store.reset(req.artifact, req.version);
  if (req.kind === "event") {
    const e = req.event;                                   // a GckEvent from the stream
    if (e.type === "artifact.patch") patch = store.applyPatch(e.data);   // "conflict": controller resyncs
    if (e.type === "text.delta") store.applyTextDelta(e.data);          // format "json": this block only
    if (e.type === "binding.resolved") store.resolveBinding(e.data);
  }
  const res: WorkerResponse = { kind: "snapshot", seq: req.seq, patch,
                                artifact: selectRenderable(store.getSnapshot()) };
  (self as unknown as DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope).postMessage(res);
};
packages/core/src/workers/create.ts (new)
export function createPatchWorker(): Worker | null {
  try {
    // Bundlers (webpack 5, Vite) emit this as a separate same-origin chunk.
    return new Worker(new URL("./patch.worker.js", import.meta.url), { type: "module" });
  } catch {
    return null;   // CSP worker-src, or an old bundler: fall back to the main thread
  }
}

The worker is used when the proposed patchWorker flag (Step 13.3) is "auto" (the default) and the artifact exceeds 200 blocks or 256 kB serialized; below that the structured-clone cost of posting snapshots exceeds the savings. In production the worker posts only changed sections, not the whole artifact; the excerpt posts snapshots for clarity. A "conflict" result is posted back so the controller can resync with getArtifact, exactly as it does on the main thread (React SDK and UI kit).

Gotcha: workers and CSP

Superset's production policy allows workers from 'self' and blob: (apache/superset: superset/config.py:3130), so a same-origin chunk served from the extension's publicPath loads. A host whose policy has no worker-src falls back to script-src (and then default-src) for workers; if neither allows the chunk's origin, the constructor throws or the worker fails to load, and the kit must keep working on the main thread. That is why createPatchWorker() returns null instead of throwing, and why the worker also listens for its own error event and the store falls back on the first failure.

docs.title: 9.1 Threat model for the frontend
docs.text:
The model output is untrusted, the host page is trusted, and the kit sits between them. The rules mirror the server-side design in Security, RLS, auth: never trust model text, never give the browser a secret it does not need, and fail closed.

# Threat Vector Mitigation in the kit Test F1 XSS via model output model emits <img onerror>, javascript: links, or HTML inside a paragraph the IR has no HTML block; RichText is text plus marks; href allowlist (https:, http:, mailto:, host-relative); any HTML the kit renders goes through SafeHtml (DOMPurify) fuzzing with hostile strings (10.7), Storybook play tests, axe F2 Prompt injection rendering into the host injected instructions in data labels or documents come back as content content is content: adapters serialize only IR fields into host-native nodes; no adapter creates host commands, links to host admin routes, or embeds; the preview shows exactly what apply will write golden-file tests with an injection corpus F3 Script execution from generated slides an LLM-generated <script> executed in the page the slides target uses Template v2 JSON only; charts are data in data-chart-config, hydrated by JSON.parse; no code from model output is ever executed lint rule bans new Function, eval, script.textContent = F4 CSP violations break the host or force weaker policies inline scripts, eval, remote script URLs no inline scripts, no eval, no new Function (including in dependencies), all chunks same-origin with the bundle, styles via stylesheet or nonce e2e runs under Superset's production Talisman policy F5 Token theft long-lived engine keys in browser storage or logs getToken callback (TokenProvider) returning short-lived tokens, kept in memory only, never logged unit tests on the client, bundle scan for key patterns F6 Cross-origin message spoofing another frame posts gck:apply to the host iframe mode checks event.origin and event.source, uses an explicit targetOrigin, validates message schema unit tests with forged messages F7 Data leakage through telemetry prompts, document text, chart values in events typed telemetry with no free text; host-owned sink; off unless the host passes telemetry to GckProvider type tests, payload snapshot tests F8 Over-broad host writes apply writes outside the selection or to another dashboard ApplyMode is checked against the manifest; host APIs are called with ids from context, never from model output adapter unit tests F9 Supply chain compromised dependency in a package that runs inside Superset with the user's session lockfile, minimal dependencies, provenance-signed npm publishes, Dependabot, CodeQL CI (Step 11)

docs.title: 9.2 Sanitization: what Presenton does and what the kit keeps
docs.text:
Presenton already depends on DOMPurify ("dompurify": "^3.4.17", servers/nextjs/package.json:49) and uses it for Smart-mode HTML slides with an explicit profile:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/SmartHtmlSlide.tsx:25-40
const SANITIZE_CONFIG: DOMPurifyConfig = {
  USE_PROFILES: { html: true, svg: true, svgFilters: true },
  FORBID_TAGS: [
    "base",
    "embed",
    "form",
    "iframe",
    "link",
    "meta",
    "object",
    "script",
    "style",
  ],
  FORBID_ATTR: ["autofocus", "contenteditable", "srcdoc"],
  ALLOW_DATA_ATTR: true,
};

It is applied at SmartHtmlSlide.tsx:118 and the result is rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML at :197. The Cypress spec servers/nextjs/cypress/security/dependencies.cy.ts:3-22 checks that DOMPurify with the same USE_PROFILES setting (not the full SANITIZE_CONFIG) keeps headings, SVG and img src while removing <script>, onload, onerror and the href of a javascript: link. Reading the rest of the Next.js source shows three things the kit must not copy:

  1. Model-written scripts run in the page. SmartHtmlSlide passes the original, unsanitized html to useSmartChartInjection (SmartHtmlSlide.tsx:122-123), which parses it, takes the text of every <script>, wraps it in a scoped function and appends it to document.body as an inline script (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/useSmartChartInjection.ts:41-100). Sanitizing the markup does not help when the script text is executed separately. This is the Smart-mode design (LLM-generated chart code), and it is incompatible with both the kit's threat model and any CSP without 'unsafe-inline'. The kit does not support Smart-mode HTML as a target.
  2. Markdown is rendered without sanitization. The outline cards render marked.parse(...) output with dangerouslySetInnerHTML (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/outline/components/OutlineItem.tsx:129, :146, :155-158, :196, :201, :232), as do servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/documents-preview/components/MarkdownRenderer.tsx:17, :31 and servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/MarkdownInlineText.tsx:27, :51. marked does not sanitize. Outline text is LLM output, so the outline review UI that the kit reuses (Extracting the engine from Presenton) must route Markdown through SafeHtml.
  3. Template v2 HTML relies on escaping alone. templateV2UiToHtmlFragment() escapes every text and attribute with escapeHtml/escapeAttribute (servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:4105-4116) and stores chart configs as escaped JSON in data-chart-config (:1080-1086), which the preview hydrates with JSON.parse (TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx:295-319). That design is sound and is what the slides target reuses, but the result is inserted with dangerouslySetInnerHTML without a sanitizer (TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx:251-254, :468). One missed escape in a 4,145-line renderer becomes XSS. The kit adds DOMPurify after the renderer as defense in depth.

The kit funnels every HTML insertion through one component:

packages/react/src/security/SafeHtml.tsx (new)
import DOMPurify, { type Config } from "dompurify";
import { memo, useMemo } from "react";

export const GCK_SANITIZE: Config = {
  USE_PROFILES: { html: true, svg: true, svgFilters: true },
  FORBID_TAGS: ["base", "embed", "form", "iframe", "link", "meta", "object", "script", "style", "template"],
  FORBID_ATTR: ["autofocus", "contenteditable", "srcdoc", "formaction", "style"],
  ALLOW_DATA_ATTR: true,               // data-chart-config, data-gck-block-id
  ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP: /^(?:https?:|mailto:|\/(?!\/)|#)/i,
};

export const SafeHtml = memo(function SafeHtml(
  { html, as: Tag = "div", ...rest }: { html: string; as?: "div" | "span" } & Record<string, unknown>,
) {
  const clean = useMemo(() => DOMPurify.sanitize(html, GCK_SANITIZE) as string, [html]);
  // eslint-disable-next-line gck/no-raw-html -- the only allowed call site
  return <Tag {...rest} dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: clean }} />;
});

The slides target's sanitizer variant allows the style attribute, because Template v2 positions every element with inline styles; text and URLs inside those styles are still escaped by the renderer. A custom ESLint rule gck/no-raw-html flags dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML =, outerHTML =, insertAdjacentHTML and document.write everywhere except SafeHtml.tsx.

Gotcha: sanitize at render, not at receipt

Do not sanitize model output when it arrives and then trust the stored string. Patches keep modifying the same blocks, adapters concatenate fragments, and a value that was harmless alone can complete a tag when joined with the next delta. Sanitize the final HTML string immediately before it touches the DOM, every time.

Host-side sanitization is a second layer, not a replacement. Superset sanitizes Markdown component HTML by default (HTML_SANITIZATION = True, apache/superset: superset/config.py:1646), and ProseMirror only accepts nodes and marks in the editor's schema. The text target still emits Markdown with HTML disabled, and the tiptap-doc target emits ProseMirror JSON that never contains an html node.

docs.title: 9.3 CSP compatibility
docs.text:
Superset's production Content Security Policy is the strictest host on the list:

Directive Superset value Consequence for the kit script-src 'self' 'strict-dynamic' plus a per-request nonce (apache/superset: superset/config.py:3156-3158) no inline scripts, no eval; dynamically loaded chunks are allowed because a trusted script loads them connect-src 'self' plus map tile hosts (:3131-3145) the engine must be reachable same-origin (a proxy route under Superset) or the operator must add its origin worker-src 'self' blob: (:3130) same-origin worker chunks load (Step 8.4) style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' plus theme font domains (:3147-3151) a runtime <style> works in Superset, but not on stricter hosts object-src 'none' no plugins, ever

The kit's rules follow: no eval or new Function in the kit or its runtime dependencies (this excludes runtime JSON Schema compilers such as Ajv in the browser; validation in the browser uses Ajv's standalone, precompiled validators or none at all, and full validation happens in tests and in the engine); no inline event handlers; every chunk, worker and font is served from the bundle's own origin; and the proposed injectGckStyles({ nonce }) (Step 1.6) accepts a nonce for hosts that require one.

Gotcha: Superset's development policy hides eval

TALISMAN_DEV_CONFIG allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' in script-src (apache/superset: superset/config.py:3203), with the comment that React needs eval in dev mode. Code (or a dependency) that uses eval works in a Superset dev instance and fails in production. Run the Superset e2e project (Step 10.5) against the production Talisman config, and fail the test on any securitypolicyviolation event.

docs.title: 9.4 Tokens and postMessage
docs.text:
The browser never holds a provider API key. Every engine request carries a short-lived engine token as Authorization: Bearer with credentials: "omit", so no cookie reaches the engine (Run protocol and client). The host's own backend mints the token under its own session: in Superset the extension endpoint POST /extensions/gck/host-superset/v1/engine-token is called with the session cookie and X-CSRFToken from authentication.getCSRFToken() (Host integrations, Security, RLS, auth). The kit's contract is the TokenProvider type from @gck/client, (opts: { forceRefresh: boolean }) => Promise<string | null>, passed as GckProvider getToken. Caching is the host's job; a small wrapper does it:

examples/react-vite-tiptap/src/engine-token.ts (new, host code)
import type { TokenProvider } from "@gck/client";

/** Memory-only cache, one mint in flight, refresh 30 s before expiry. */
export function cachedTokenProvider(mint: () => Promise<{ token: string; expiresAt: number }>): TokenProvider {
  let current: { token: string; expiresAt: number } | undefined;   // epoch ms; never persisted
  let inflight: Promise<string> | undefined;
  return async ({ forceRefresh }) => {
    if (!forceRefresh && current && current.expiresAt - Date.now() > 30_000) return current.token;
    inflight ??= mint()
      .then((t) => { current = t; return t.token; })
      .finally(() => { inflight = undefined; });
    return inflight;
  };
}

GckClient calls getToken({ forceRefresh: false }) before every request, including each SSE reconnect with Last-Event-ID, and on 401 token_expired calls it once with forceRefresh: true and retries once; a null token sends no Authorization header. Tokens are never written to localStorage, sessionStorage, URLs or telemetry.

For the iframe fallback:

packages/element/src/frame-bridge.ts (new)
export function connectFrame(iframe: HTMLIFrameElement, engineOrigin: string,
                             onMessage: (msg: GckFrameMessage) => void) {
  const expected = new URL(engineOrigin).origin;          // normalize once, never "*"
  const listener = (event: MessageEvent) => {
    if (event.origin !== expected) return;                // wrong sender origin
    if (event.source !== iframe.contentWindow) return;    // right origin, wrong frame
    const msg = parseGckFrameMessage(event.data);         // schema + version check
    if (msg) onMessage(msg);
  };
  window.addEventListener("message", listener);
  return {
    send: (msg: GckFrameMessage) => iframe.contentWindow?.postMessage(msg, expected),
    disconnect: () => window.removeEventListener("message", listener),
  };
}

docs.title: 9.5 Privacy of telemetry
docs.text:
Presenton's telemetry is a useful counterexample. Its Mixpanel setup defaults to enabled when the status endpoint fails (servers/nextjs/utils/mixpanel.ts:224-226) and initializes session recording for every session with text masking turned off:

servers/nextjs/utils/mixpanel.ts:246-255
  mixpanel.init(MIXPANEL_TOKEN as string, {
    track_pageview: false,
    autocapture: false,
    api_host: 'https://api-eu.mixpanel.com',
    record_sessions_percent: 100,
    record_mask_text_selector: '',
    record_block_selector: '',
    record_collect_fonts: true,
    record_canvas: true,
  });

It does have good habits worth keeping: error messages are collapsed to one line and capped at 240 characters, and sizes are bucketed instead of exact (servers/nextjs/utils/analytics.ts:1-35). The kit's policy: the kit itself sends nothing anywhere; it calls the host's telemetry callback with typed events (Step 13) that contain ids, timings, counts and enum values only; no prompt text, no artifact text, no data values, no user names; and an absent callback means no telemetry, so failure is closed by construction. Session replay of the kit's UI is the host's decision, and the kit marks its preview root with data-gck-sensitive so hosts can block it in their replay tool.

docs.title: Step 10: Testing strategy
docs.text:
Presenton's frontend tests today are node --test files, ESLint, a production build and Cypress component specs (nine *.cy.ts(x) files, three of them under servers/nextjs/cypress/security/) (.github/workflows/test-all.yml:98-111, servers/nextjs/cypress.config.ts:3-11); there is no browser end-to-end test against a running app (CI, tests, security). The kit needs more because it runs in hosts it does not control.

Layer Tool Scope Runs Unit Vitest protocol helpers, client, run machine, JSON Patch, adapters, i18n every PR Contract Vitest + Ajv fixtures and recorded logs against engine-exported JSON Schemas every PR, and in the engine repo Component Storybook + MSW every component in every state, themes, locales every PR (build + play tests) Visual Playwright screenshots of Storybook pixel diffs per story every PR Accessibility axe (Storybook and Playwright) WCAG 2.2 AA rules every PR Fuzz fast-check adapters and patch apply with hostile and truncated input every PR (short), nightly (long) End-to-end Playwright real hosts: Tiptap demo, Presenton, Superset every PR (Tiptap), nightly and pre-release (all)

docs.title: 10.1 Unit tests
10.2 Contract tests shared with the engine
docs.text:
The engine's Pydantic models are the source of truth, as in Presenton, which already derives LLM response schemas with model_json_schema() (for example servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_outlines.py:363). An export script writes the schemas into @gck/protocol, under the file names and $id the Artifact Spec fixes (artifact-1.schema.json, Artifact Spec and targets):

engine/scripts/export_schemas.py (new)
import json
import pathlib

from gck_engine.protocol import GckEvent, OutlineDecision, RunRequest  # GckEvent: proposed addition
from gck_engine.spec.artifact import Artifact

OUT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "packages" / "protocol" / "schemas"
MODELS = {"artifact-1": Artifact, "run-request-1": RunRequest,
          "outline-decision-1": OutlineDecision, "gck-event-1": GckEvent}

for name, model in MODELS.items():
    schema = model.model_json_schema(mode="serialization")
    schema["$id"] = f"https://gck.dev/schemas/{name}.schema.json"
    path = OUT / f"{name}.schema.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(schema, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

gck_engine.protocol holds RunRequest and OutlineDecision today (Extracting the engine from Presenton); GckEvent is a Pydantic discriminated union mirroring the TypeScript GckEvent of Run protocol and client, proposed here so that events get the full schema validation that isGckEvent (a structural guard only) does not give. The TypeScript types in @gck/protocol stay hand-written (src/artifact.ts, src/target.ts, src/run.ts); a type test generates declarations from the schema files with json-schema-to-typescript into src/generated/ (never exported) and asserts that both sides are mutually assignable, and CI fails when regenerating produces a diff, so a field renamed in Python breaks the frontend build in the same pull request. Pydantic v2 emits JSON Schema draft 2020-12, so the tests use Ajv's 2020 build. The contract test lives in @gck/core, because it replays patches through the real store and @gck/protocol must not depend on @gck/core:

packages/core/test/contract.test.ts (new)
import Ajv2020 from "ajv/dist/2020";
import addFormats from "ajv-formats";
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import gckEvent from "@gck/protocol/schemas/gck-event-1.schema.json" with { type: "json" };
import artifact from "@gck/protocol/schemas/artifact-1.schema.json" with { type: "json" };
import { createArtifactStore } from "../src/artifact-store";

const ajv = addFormats(new Ajv2020({ allErrors: true, strict: false }));
const validateEvent = ajv.compile(gckEvent);
const validateArtifact = ajv.compile(artifact);
const LOGS = new URL("../../../fixtures/event-logs/", import.meta.url);

describe.each(readdirSync(LOGS).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".jsonl")))("%s", (file) => {
  const lines = readFileSync(new URL(file, LOGS), "utf8").trim().split("\n").map((l) => JSON.parse(l));
  it("every event matches the engine schema", () => {
    for (const { t, ...event } of lines) expect(validateEvent(event), JSON.stringify(validateEvent.errors)).toBe(true);
  });
  it("replaying patches yields a valid Artifact", () => {
    const store = createArtifactStore((fn) => fn());
    for (const e of lines) if (e.type === "artifact.patch") expect(store.applyPatch(e.data)).not.toBe("conflict");
    expect(validateArtifact(store.getSnapshot().artifact), JSON.stringify(validateArtifact.errors)).toBe(true);
  });
});

The engine repository runs the mirror image: it loads the same fixtures/event-logs/ (published as a tarball artifact of @gck/protocol) and validates them with Pydantic, so neither side can drift alone.

docs.title: 10.3 A mock engine with MSW replaying recorded event logs
docs.text:
Recorded runs are the kit's most valuable test data: real event timing, real patch sizes, real failure shapes. The engine already keeps a run event log for Last-Event-ID resume; an export command writes a run as JSONL, one GckEvent envelope per line (v, id, runId, ts, type, data, optional progress) plus t in ms since start, after scrubbing prompt and data values. MSW then replays the log through the real @gck/client, because the client uses fetch and MSW can return a ReadableStream body (https://mswjs.io/docs/http/mocking-responses/streaming). The handlers live in the private @gck/testing package, so msw never becomes a dependency of a published package:

tooling/testing/src/replay.ts (new)
import { delay, http, HttpResponse } from "msw";
import type { GckEvent } from "@gck/protocol";

/** One line of a recorded log: the event envelope plus `t`, ms since the run started. */
export type RecordedEvent = GckEvent & { t: number };

export function replayRun(runId: string, events: RecordedEvent[], { speed = 1 } = {}) {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const base = `/v1/runs/${runId}`;
  return [
    http.post("*/v1/runs", () => HttpResponse.json({ runId, streamUrl: `${base}/events`,
      inputUrl: `${base}/input`, cancelUrl: `${base}/cancel`, createdAt: new Date().toISOString() }, { status: 201 })),
    http.post("*/v1/runs/:id/input", () => HttpResponse.json({ accepted: true }, { status: 202 })),
    http.post("*/v1/runs/:id/cancel", () => HttpResponse.json({ state: "cancelled" }, { status: 202 })),
    http.get("*/v1/runs/:id/events", ({ request }) => {
      const after = Number(request.headers.get("Last-Event-ID") ?? 0);   // resume support
      const pending = events.filter((e) => e.id > after);
      const stream = new ReadableStream({
        async start(controller) {
          let previous = pending[0]?.t ?? 0;
          for (const { t, ...event } of pending) {
            await delay(Math.max(0, (t - previous) / speed));
            previous = t;
            controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(
              `id: ${event.id}\nevent: ${event.type}\ndata: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n`));
          }
          controller.close();
        },
      });
      return new HttpResponse(stream, { headers: { "Content-Type": "text/event-stream",
        "Cache-Control": "no-cache, no-transform" } });
    }),
  ];
}

The same handlers serve Vitest (through msw/node), Storybook (through the browser worker) and local development of host integrations without an engine or an LLM key. Variants inject faults: cut the stream after event N (tests reconnect), duplicate an event id (tests idempotence), return 401 token_expired once (tests the token provider's forceRefresh path), and emit run.failed {retryable: true} (tests Retry).

docs.title: 10.4 Storybook stories for every state
docs.text:
Every styled component has one story per run state (idle, composing, submitting, planning, awaiting_review, generating, resolving_data, ready, applying, applied, cancelled, failed retryable and not), plus cross-cutting variants: dark, compact, RTL (ar), long artifact (300 sections), forbidden binding, and slow network. Streaming stories use the replay handlers:

packages/react/src/ui/StreamingPreview.stories.tsx (excerpt, new)
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from "@storybook/react-vite";
import { replayRun } from "@gck/testing";
import qbr from "../../../../fixtures/event-logs/tiptap-qbr-emea.json";   // { runId, events } built from the JSONL
import { StreamingPreview } from "./StreamingPreview";
import { withGckRun } from "../../.storybook/decorators";   // GckProvider + useGenerationRun; supplies `run`

const meta = {
  component: StreamingPreview,
  args: { targetId: "tiptap-doc" },
  decorators: [withGckRun({ target: "tiptap-doc" })],
} satisfies Meta<typeof StreamingPreview>;
export default meta;
type Story = StoryObj<typeof meta>;

export const Generating: Story = {
  parameters: { msw: replayRun(qbr.runId, qbr.events, { speed: 1 }) },
};
export const GeneratingRtl: Story = {
  ...Generating,
  globals: { locale: "ar" },
};
export const AwaitingReview: Story = {
  parameters: { msw: replayRun(qbr.runId, qbr.events.filter((e) => e.id <= 3)) },
};

The MSW integration uses msw-storybook-addon; its README documents mswLoader() with handlers passed in parameters.msw for CSF 3 (https://github.com/mswjs/msw-storybook-addon). The addon's API has changed across versions, so pin it and follow the README for the version you install.

docs.title: 10.5 End-to-end tests per host
docs.text:
e2e/playwright.config.ts (excerpt, new)
import { defineConfig, devices } from "@playwright/test";

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./tests",
  retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0,
  use: { trace: "retain-on-failure" },
  projects: [
    { name: "tiptap-react18", testMatch: /tiptap\/.*\.spec\.ts/,
      use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"], baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:5173" } },
    { name: "tiptap-react19", testMatch: /tiptap\/.*\.spec\.ts/,
      use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"], baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:5174" } },
    { name: "presenton", testMatch: /presenton\/.*\.spec\.ts/,
      use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"], baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:3000" } },
    { name: "superset", testMatch: /superset\/.*\.spec\.ts/,
      use: { ...devices["Desktop Chrome"], baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:8088", locale: "en-US" } },
    { name: "superset-fr", testMatch: /superset\/.*\.spec\.ts/,
      use: { ...devices["Desktop Firefox"], baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:8088", locale: "fr-FR" } },
  ],
});
  • Tiptap demo (examples/react-vite-tiptap, built twice with React 18.3 and 19): slash command, streaming insertion, one-step undo, apply at cursor and replace selection.
  • Presenton: the AI Slides flow from Part VIII with the slides target, against Presenton's Docker image.
  • Superset dev instance: Superset from its own docker-compose-light.yml with FEATURE_FLAGS = {"ENABLE_EXTENSIONS": True}, the production Talisman config, the .supx built from apps/superset-extension, and a fixture dashboard. Tests open the dashboard menu, generate a text artifact into a Markdown component and a superset-dashboard artifact into a new tab, and revert. Each test listens for securitypolicyviolation and fails on any.

The engine in e2e is a real GCK Engine with a scripted LLM provider that replays recorded model outputs, the same idea as Presenton's regression test that feeds fixed chunks through a patched stream (CI, tests, security). No e2e test calls a real model.

docs.title: 10.6 Visual regression
docs.text: A Playwright job loads every Storybook story (from storybook-static/index.json), waits for the replay to reach its last event (stories expose data-gck-settled="true"), and calls expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() in light, dark and RTL. Streaming stories are captured at fixed event ids, never at wall-clock times, so diffs are deterministic. Baselines are generated in the same Linux container CI uses, because font rendering differs across operating systems.

docs.title: 10.7 Fuzzing adapters with LLM-shaped output
docs.text:
Adapters must survive anything a model can produce, including output that passed schema validation but is semantically odd. Property tests generate artifacts from the schema and mutate them:

packages/target-tiptap/test/fuzz.test.ts (new)
import fc from "fast-check";
import { getSchema } from "@tiptap/core";
import StarterKit from "@tiptap/starter-kit";
import { it, expect } from "vitest";
import { arbArtifact, hostileText } from "@gck/testing/arbitraries";
import { toProseMirror, type TiptapOptions } from "../src";
import { gckNodes } from "../src/react";            // the node definitions live in the /react subpath

const schema = getSchema([StarterKit, ...gckNodes]);
const options: TiptapOptions = { includeTitle: true, hasImageNode: false, maxHeading: 3 };

it("toProseMirror always yields a document the editor schema accepts", () => {
  fc.assert(fc.property(arbArtifact({ target: "tiptap-doc", text: hostileText }), (artifact) => {
    const json = toProseMirror(artifact, options);
    expect(() => schema.nodeFromJSON(json).check()).not.toThrow();
    const serialized = JSON.stringify(json);
    expect(serialized).not.toMatch(/"type":"html"|javascript:/i);
    expect(toProseMirror(artifact, options)).toEqual(json);          // deterministic
  }), { numRuns: process.env.NIGHTLY ? 20_000 : 500 });
});

hostileText mixes <script>, <img onerror>, javascript: URLs, double-brace token syntax, bidi override characters (U+202E), zero-width joiners, lone surrogates, 100,000-character strings and every ASCII control character. Patch fuzzing applies random prefixes of recorded patch streams, reorders adjacent ops, and duplicates ops, asserting that the store either applies them or rejects them with a typed error, never corrupts state.

docs.title: 10.8 Accessibility tests
docs.text:
The Storybook test runner runs axe on every story, and Playwright runs axe on each host page after apply:

e2e/tests/tiptap/a11y.spec.ts (new)
import AxeBuilder from "@axe-core/playwright";
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";

test("composer, review and preview have no WCAG 2.2 AA violations", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/");
  await page.keyboard.type("/ai");
  await page.keyboard.press("Enter");
  for (const step of ["composer", "review", "preview"]) {
    await page.locator(`[data-gck-step="${step}"]`).waitFor();
    const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
      .include(".gck-root")
      .withTags(["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa", "wcag22aa"])
      .analyze();
    expect(results.violations, step).toEqual([]);
    await page.keyboard.press("Mod+Enter");
  }
});

axe cannot judge live-region verbosity or focus after apply; those get explicit e2e assertions on :focus and a manual VoiceOver and NVDA pass before each minor release.

docs.title: Step 11: The CI pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart TD
  PR["pull request or push to main"] --> I["pnpm install --frozen-lockfile"]
  I --> L["lint, typecheck (tsc -b)"]
  I --> G["regenerate protocol types, fail on diff"]
  L --> U["unit and contract tests (Vitest)"]
  G --> U
  U --> B["build packages (turbo, cached)"]
  B --> S["size-limit budgets"]
  B --> SB["Storybook build"]
  SB --> VR["visual regression (Playwright)"]
  SB --> AX["axe on every story"]
  B --> E1["e2e: Tiptap React 18 and 19"]
  B --> EX["build examples and Superset .supx"]
  EX --> E2["e2e nightly: Presenton and Superset"]
  S --> GATE["required checks"]
  VR --> GATE
  AX --> GATE
  E1 --> GATE
  GATE -->|"main only"| REL["changesets: version PR or publish, canary"]
.github/workflows/ci.yml (excerpt, new)
name: ci
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: { fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false }
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: "22", cache: pnpm }
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @gck/protocol generate && git diff --exit-code packages/protocol/src/generated
      - run: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck
      - run: pnpm turbo run test build --filter="...[origin/main]"
      - run: pnpm size
      - run: pnpm turbo run storybook:build && pnpm --filter @gck/storybook test:visual && pnpm --filter @gck/storybook test:a11y
      - run: pnpm --filter @gck/e2e exec playwright test --project=tiptap-react18 --project=tiptap-react19

Like Presenton's workflows, the default token is read-only (permissions: contents: read, for example .github/workflows/test-all.yml:10-11), and, as Presenton's CodeQL workflow does (.github/workflows/codeql.yml:34), the checkout does not persist credentials (CI, tests, security). Only the release workflow gets id-token: write (for npm provenance) and the npm publish token.

docs.title: 12.1 Changesets
docs.text:
Every pull request that changes a published package adds a changeset (pnpm changeset) naming the packages and the bump. On main, the changesets action opens or updates a "Version packages" pull request; merging it publishes.

gck/.changeset/config.json (new)
{
  "$schema": "https://unpkg.com/@changesets/config@3.1.1/schema.json",
  "changelog": ["@changesets/changelog-github", { "repo": "OWNER/gck" }],
  "commit": false,
  "fixed": [["@gck/client", "@gck/core", "@gck/react", "@gck/element"]],
  "linked": [],
  "access": "public",
  "baseBranch": "main",
  "updateInternalDependencies": "patch"
}

fixed keeps the runtime packages a host installs together on one version number, so "which @gck/core goes with @gck/react 1.4?" has one answer. Targets, hosts and @gck/protocol version independently.

docs.title: 12.2 Semver policy
docs.text:
Package Major (breaking) Minor Patch @gck/protocol removing or renaming a field, event type or enum value; changing a field's meaning; gck.artifact/1 to /2 new optional fields, new event types, new block types, new enum values that old clients may ignore doc and schema description fixes @gck/client, @gck/core public API removal, state machine semantics change new options, hooks, events bug fixes @gck/react, @gck/element prop removal, DOM structure changes that styled hosts rely on (class names, data-gck-* attributes), token renames new props, components, tokens, messages visual fixes within the token contract targets toNative output change that alters existing host content on re-apply new block support, new apply modes fixes that make output match the documented mapping @gck/host-superset dropping a Superset version from the matrix supporting a new Superset version or contribution point fixes

Two rules make protocol minors safe. Clients must ignore unknown event types and unknown fields (the test in Step 10.1). And the engine must accept every client within the current major, which the client advertises with the GCK-Protocol request header (PROTOCOL_VERSION, 1); a breaking change bumps v, and the engine rejects a client whose header is too old with invalid_request and details.minProtocol (Run protocol and client).

docs.title: 12.3 Deprecation policy
docs.text:
1. Deprecate in a minor: @deprecated JSDoc with the replacement, a changeset entry, and a one-time console.warn in development builds only.
  2. Keep it for at least one further minor and at least six months.
  3. Remove it in the next major, listed in a migration guide on the docs site.
  4. Protocol majors: the engine serves the current and the previous protocol major for at least twelve months after a new major ships, because embedded hosts (a Superset extension pinned in a customer deployment) upgrade slowly.

docs.title: 12.4 Canary releases
docs.text:
Every merge to main also publishes a snapshot under a dist-tag, so hosts can test unreleased changes without affecting latest. Changesets documents the two commands: changeset version --snapshot <name> produces versions such as 0.0.0-<name>-<timestamp>, and changeset publish --tag <name> publishes without moving latest (https://github.com/changesets/changesets/blob/main/docs/snapshot-releases.md):

.github/workflows/release.yml (canary step, new)
      - run: pnpm changeset version --snapshot canary
      - run: pnpm turbo run build --filter="./packages/*"
      - run: pnpm changeset publish --tag canary --no-git-tag
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"

Longer pre-releases (a 2.0.0-next.N series) use changesets pre mode (changeset pre enter next). The Superset extension is released as a .supx attached to a GitHub release with a pinned set of @gck/* versions recorded in its manifest.

docs.title: 12.5 Docs site and example apps
docs.text:
• Docs site (apps/docs): host guides plus generated references (compatibility matrix, tokens from gck.css, message keys from defaultMessages, TypeDoc API, protocol from the JSON Schemas).
  • Storybook, published per release, whose replay stories are live demos that need no engine.
  • Examples (examples/*), private packages built in CI on every PR, so a change that breaks a real consumer setup (Next.js App Router, Vite, a plain page with the element) fails before release.

docs.title: Step 13: Observability, errors and feature flags
13.1 Client telemetry hooks
docs.text:
The kit's telemetry contract is the TelemetryEvent of @gck/core, { name, targetId, runId?, status?, code? }, passed through GckProvider telemetry to every controller. In 1.0 the controller emits one event name, gck.status, on every status transition, with the new RunStatus and, on failure, the protocol error code (React SDK and UI kit). There is deliberately no text and no timing in the event; the host's sink adds both clocks and context:

examples/presenton-ai-slides/src/telemetry.ts (new, host code)
import type { TelemetryEvent } from "@gck/core";

/** Timestamps status transitions on receipt; the kit never measures or sends anything itself. */
export function createTelemetrySink(send: (metric: Record<string, string | number>) => void) {
  const submittedAt = new Map<string, number>();                 // targetId -> performance.now()
  return (e: TelemetryEvent) => {
    const now = performance.now();
    if (e.status === "submitting") submittedAt.set(e.targetId, now);
    performance.mark(`gck:${e.targetId}:${e.status ?? e.name}`);  // visible in devtools
    send({ name: e.name, target: e.targetId, run: e.runId ?? "", status: e.status ?? "",
           code: e.code ?? "", ms: Math.round(now - (submittedAt.get(e.targetId) ?? now)) });
  };
}

From those transitions a host dashboard derives time to first content (ms at the first generating, p50 and p95), completion (ready), cancel (cancelled) and failure rates by code, outline review rate (awaiting_review), and apply success (applied) versus apply failure (applying followed by ready with a code). Revert rate within five minutes (a strong bad-output signal), resume count (a network or proxy signal) and long render frames are not visible in status transitions; they are proposed as further event names on the same TelemetryEvent shape (gck.apply_reverted, gck.resumed, gck.long_frame) for a 1.x minor.

Gotcha: runId is the join key, not the user

Telemetry events carry runId so the host can join them with the engine's server-side run log, which already knows the user under the host's own access rules. The kit never adds a user id, email or tenant id. If a host needs per-user analysis, it joins on its side, under its own privacy policy.

docs.title: 13.2 Error reporting
docs.text:
The kit has one error vocabulary, the protocol's GckErrorCode (Run protocol and client): transport failures throw GckError from @gck/client (code, retryable, status, retryAfterMs, details), and run and apply failures land in run.state.error as a GckErrorBody (an apply that returns ok: false becomes code: "conflict", a thrown apply error goes through the same conversion). Every styled component is wrapped in an error boundary that renders a compact failure state with Retry (StreamingPreview's preview boundary is the example in React SDK and UI kit). A host reports errors from the state it already has:

examples/presenton-ai-slides/src/report-errors.ts (new, host code)
import type { GckErrorBody } from "@gck/protocol";

/** Codes, flags and the run id only: the message can echo model output. */
export function reportRunError(error: GckErrorBody, runId: string | null,
                               report: (name: string, tags: Record<string, string>) => void) {
  report(`gck.${error.code}`, { runId: runId ?? "none", retryable: String(error.retryable) });
}

run.failed.message from the engine is rendered as text (never HTML) and is not forwarded to the host's error tracker unless the host opts in, because an engine message can echo model output. Render exceptions caught by a boundary are kit bugs rather than protocol errors; an onError prop for them is a proposal, not part of GckConfig 1.0. Hosts forward reports to whatever they already use (Sentry, Superset's own logging, a console in development).

docs.title: 13.3 Feature flags
What you now know
docs.text:
• The kit is a pnpm and Turborepo monorepo of ESM-only packages with types-first exports maps, sideEffects declared per package (CSS and customElements.define are side effects), React 18.3 or 19 as a peer, Tiptap 2 or 3 behind a compat module, and @apache-superset/core as an optional peer of @gck/host-superset; tsconfig lib without DOM keeps @gck/core headless.
  • Budgets (core under 15 kB, React kit under 40 kB gzipped) are enforced by size-limit in CI, and the slides renderer plus Chart.js (about 70 kB gzipped as Presenton vendors it today) load only when a slides preview mounts, through a module-scoped ESM loader instead of Presenton's global script.
  • Inside Superset the kit is a Module Federation remote that takes React, react-dom, antd and @apache-superset/core from the host with import: false, imports only the package root, reads the theme through theme.useTheme(), and maps antd tokens into GckProvider's theme prop (the --gck-* custom properties), so dark mode follows the host theme and density is one --gck-space override; non-React hosts use the <gck-generate> element, which bundles its own React inside a shadow root.
  • Streaming UIs need throttled polite announcements, focus moves only on user actions, a drag alternative and reduced motion; performance comes from frame-aligned notification batching in the artifact store, per-block subscriptions through useArtifact, virtualization and a CSP-safe worker for repair instead of Presenton's whole-string jsonrepair per chunk.
  • Model output is untrusted end to end: one SafeHtml component with DOMPurify, no model-authored script ever executed (unlike Presenton's Smart-mode chart injection), no eval under Superset's strict Talisman policy, short-lived tokens from a provider callback, origin-checked postMessage, and telemetry that the host owns and that never contains text.
  • Quality is layered: Vitest units, contract tests against JSON Schemas exported from the engine's Pydantic models, MSW replaying recorded event logs in tests and Storybook, visual and axe checks per story, fuzzed adapters, Playwright per host, and changesets with an explicit semver and deprecation policy and canary releases.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: With the engineering plan in place, Roadmap and tracker sequences the packages, hosts and quality gates from this chapter into milestones.

docs.title: Roadmap and tracker
docs.text:
Reads: the earlier Part IX chapters · Builds on: Architecture, Part VIII (AI Slides delivery plan) · Time: ~15 min

This chapter turns Part IX into a plan you can track. It covers five phases, each ending in something a user can try, with 27 work packages, effort estimates, dependencies and exit criteria. Each phase adds one new host or target, so the kit proves its "plug into any host" promise step by step instead of all at the end.

Download tracker (.csv)

docs.title: Step 1: Understand the planning assumptions
docs.text:
Assumption Value Start After the AI Slides pilot is stable, or in parallel with a separate small team (see Step 5) Team 2 frontend engineers, 1 backend engineer at about 50%, QA support in phases 2 and 3 Effort unit Ideal person-days (d), including tests and review Capacity 4 focus-days per person per week Windows Indicative week ranges relative to the start date; convert them to Friday release trains when a start date is fixed, the same way as the AI Slides release plan in Part VIII

Totals: about 104 d of frontend work, 33 d of backend work and 8 d of QA. Two frontend engineers at 4 d per week deliver the frontend share in about 13 weeks of pure work, so 19 weeks leaves room for review, integration and surprises.

docs.title: Step 2: Read the phase plan
docs.text:
Why this order:

  1. P0 first, because the protocol and core are the contract every host and target depends on. Changing them later is the most expensive change in the project.
  2. Text before Tiptap before dashboards. Text is the simplest target (no custom editor nodes, no layout), so it validates the engine and the kit with the least risk. Tiptap adds editor integration and undo. Dashboards add layout and real Superset objects.
  3. Slides last, because AI Slides already works through Part VIII. Moving it onto the kit is a refactor, not new value, and it is safest once the kit is proven on three other targets.

docs.text: Phase Exit criteria (a demo a user can run) P0 A Storybook story streams a recorded run from the mock engine through @gck/core into a preview, and can be cancelled and resumed P1 In Superset, a user writes "summarize this dashboard for leadership" and gets a Markdown component whose numbers come from data tokens resolved against bound charts (Markdown is static text, so they are frozen at snapshotAt and shown with an "as of" date, see Host integrations) P2 In a Tiptap page, /ai generates a page with a live chart node; selecting text and choosing "turn into chart" replaces the selection (transform); "Edit page" changes only the affected blocks (edit with patch); one undo reverts each of them P3 From a dashboard, "create an EMEA tab with revenue and churn" produces a new tab that uses existing charts, respects permissions and can be reverted P4 Presenton's own outline and streaming screens run on the kit with no user-visible regression; the <gck-generate> web component works in a plain HTML page; version 1.0 is published

docs.title: Step 5: Decide how to run it alongside AI Slides
docs.text:
Two workable options:

  • Sequential (recommended for a small team). Finish the AI Slides pilot, then start P0 with the same people. The Part VIII code (bindings, refresh API, harness planner) becomes the engine's data layer, and nothing is built twice.
  • Parallel. A separate pair of frontend engineers starts P0 and P1 while AI Slides continues. This works only if @gck/protocol adopts Part VIII's binding shape unchanged and one person owns the protocol across both teams.

docs.title: Part VIII · AI Slides delivery plan
docs.text:
Reads: the architect's story backlog, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts · Builds on: Part VII landing, Template v2 format · Time: ~15 min

Part VII describes a long-term, Superset-native design. Part VIII is the plan the team is actually building first. It forks Presenton, embeds it inside the Superset-based analytics platform as a feature called AI Slides, and makes every chart and metric in a generated deck a live binding to Superset data that refreshes when the deck is opened. This part takes the architect's nine stories and turns each one into an implementation guide, with architecture diagrams, the exact code changes in the Presenton fork and in the analytics backend, UI component code, tests and rollout steps.

docs.title: The nine stories
docs.text:
The backlog below is transcribed from the architect's story sheet. Each row links to the chapter that explains how to build it.

Srini, Sourav, Nitesh Story 1 2 [Presenton BE] Platform Integration: Postgres, access control, pod-ready API Moves metadata to the analytics Postgres, enforces owner, org and collaborator access with platform identity, and makes the API fit the analytics pod. Nitesh Story 2 3 [Presenton BE] Prompt library and custom templates backend Provides APIs for curated prompts and bundled templates and async generation, with custom template upload on hold pending a decision. docs.text:
flowchart LR
    U["User in browser"] --> SS["Superset web (analytics platform)"]
    SS -->|"AI Slides menu, /ai-slides/launch"| HOST["Host page with iframe and postMessage bridge (Story 5)"]
    HOST -->|"iframe /ai-slides/"| FE["Presenton FE, Next.js (Stories 4, 5, 6)"]
    FE -->|"/ai-slides/api"| BE["Presenton BE, FastAPI (Stories 1, 2, 3)"]
    HOST -->|"POST /api/v1/ai_slides/handoff"| ABE["Analytics BE: ai_slides blueprint (Story 8)"]
    BE -->|"refresh as the user"| ABE
    BE -->|"plan a deck"| H["Harness: presentation-planner skill (Story 7)"]
    H -->|"MCP tools as the user"| MCP["Superset MCP service (Story 8)"]
    ABE --> Q["Superset query engine, RBAC and RLS"]
    MCP --> Q
    BE --> PG["Analytics Postgres, schema presenton (Story 2)"]
    BE --> OBJ["Object storage for exports and images (Story 9)"]

Three ideas hold the plan together:

  1. One identity. The user is signed in to Superset only. The host page exchanges the Superset session for a short-lived signed assertion. Presenton turns that into its own session, and every data call afterwards runs as that same Superset user, so roles and row-level security apply unchanged (Story 2, Story 8).
  2. Bindings, not numbers. A chart on a slide stores a reference to a saved Superset chart plus a mapping, never typed-in values. The planner only proposes charts that Superset can refresh and the user can see (Story 7). The refresh service resolves them on open (Story 1), and the editor fills them in progressively (Story 4).
  3. Same origin. Presenton is served under /ai-slides/ on the analytics domain. That keeps cookies, Content Security Policy and API calls simple, and it is why Next.js basePath and prefix-aware routing matter so much (Story 5, Story 9).

docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/async_tasks/router.py, servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts, apache/superset: superset/config.py · Builds on: Part VIII landing · Time: ~30 min

This chapter fixes the names, tables, endpoints and payloads that all nine stories share, so that teams working in parallel build pieces that fit. It walks through the deployment topology, the identity flow, the data-binding model, the three main request flows (generate, open, export), and the decisions behind each choice. Story chapters refer back here instead of redefining these contracts.

docs.title: Step 1: Fix the deployment topology
docs.text:
The recommended default serves Presenton under a path prefix on the analytics domain, rather than on its own subdomain.

Why same-origin is the default:

  • Cookies just work. Presenton's session cookie is set with samesite="lax" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:47-55). Inside a same-site iframe a Lax cookie is sent normally. On a separate subdomain that is still same-site, but on a different registrable domain the cookie becomes third-party and needs SameSite=None; Secure, plus partitioned cookies for browsers that block third-party cookies.
  • Framing is already allowed. Superset's default TALISMAN_CONFIG content security policy sets default-src 'self' and no explicit frame-src (apache/superset: superset/config.py:3116-3160), so a same-origin iframe is permitted without changing Superset's CSP. A different origin would need frame-src added there.
  • No CORS. The browser talks to one origin, so neither Superset nor Presenton needs CORS for the embedded flow.

Gotcha: cookie path on a shared origin

Stock Presenton sets presenton_session with path="/" (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:54). On a shared origin that cookie would also travel with every Superset request. Set Path=/ai-slides in the fork. Story 2 changes both _set_login_cookie and the fastapi-users cookie transport (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:188-192).

Gotcha: base path everywhere

Presenton assumes it owns /. Its Next.js proxy rewrites /api/v1, /api/v2, /app_data and /static to FastAPI (see Next.js architecture), and generated asset URLs start with /app_data/. Every one of these must become prefix-aware. Story 5 lists each touchpoint.

docs.title: Step 2: Fix the identity contract
docs.text:
One identity, owned by Superset, flows into Presenton and back out to every data call.

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Superset host page
    participant ABE as Analytics BE ai_slides
    participant F as Presenton FE in iframe
    participant P as Presenton BE
    B->>ABE: POST /api/v1/ai_slides/handoff (Superset session, CSRF)
    ABE-->>B: assertion (aud presenton, 60 s) and data_token (aud analytics-data, 15 min)
    B->>F: postMessage ai-slides:handoff (target origin pinned)
    F->>P: POST /api/v1/platform/session with assertion and data_token
    P->>ABE: GET /api/v1/ai_slides/.well-known/jwks.json (cached)
    P->>P: verify iss, aud, exp, single-use jti, upsert user and org
    P-->>F: Set-Cookie presenton_session (HttpOnly, Secure, Lax, Path=/ai-slides)
    Note over P: data_token stored server-side, encrypted, keyed by session
    F->>B: postMessage ai-slides:ready
Token Issued by Audience Lifetime Holder Used for Superset session cookie Superset Superset Superset config Browser Calling the handoff endpoint Handoff assertion (JWT, RS256) Analytics BE presenton 60 s, single use Browser, briefly Creating a Presenton session presenton_session Presenton BE Presenton Presenton session TTL Browser cookie All Presenton API calls Data token (JWT, RS256) Analytics BE analytics-data, scopes ai_slides:refresh superset:chart:read superset:dashboard:read superset:dataset:read 15 min Presenton BE only Refresh API and harness/MCP calls as the user

Assertion claims: iss, aud, sub (Superset user id), username, email, first_name, last_name, org_id, roles, jti, iat, exp. The data token carries the same sub and username, plus scope.

Gotcha: per-user MCP needs Superset master

Superset's MCP service maps JWT claims to a Superset user (by preferred_username, username, email, then sub) and checks superset:* scopes only on master; Superset 6.1.0 runs every MCP tool as one configured user. On 6.1 the harness must use the analytics catalog and refresh endpoints instead of MCP for anything user-specific (Story 7, Story 8). That is also why the data token carries a username claim and read-only superset:* scopes.

Why a separate data token

Presenton BE must call Superset as the user long after the handoff. Storing the user's Superset session cookie would be fragile and over-privileged. A narrow token with its own audience and scope is easy to verify in Superset and to revoke by rotating keys. When it expires, the FE asks the parent page for a fresh handoff (ai-slides:handoff-request).

docs.title: Step 3: Fix the data-binding model
docs.text:
Presenton's Template v2 already has a chart element with real data fields. It has chart_type drawn from the ChartType enum (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:76-88), plus categories: list[str] and series: list[ChartSeries], where each series is {name, values: list[float]} (elements.py:176-178, elements.py:361-393). Today the language model invents those numbers. A binding replaces invention with a reference.

erDiagram
    presentations ||--o{ slides : contains
    presentations ||--o{ slide_data_bindings : has
    slides ||--o{ slide_data_bindings : has
    presentations ||--o{ presentation_collaborators : shared_with
    organizations ||--o{ presentations : owns
    slide_data_bindings {
        uuid id PK
        uuid presentation_id FK
        uuid slide_id FK
        text element_name
        text element_path
        text kind
        jsonb source
        jsonb mapping
        jsonb format
        jsonb snapshot
        timestamptz snapshot_at
        text snapshot_hash
        text status
    }

The source and mapping for one chart binding:

{
  "kind": "chart",
  "element_name": "main_chart",
  "source": {
    "type": "superset_chart",
    "chart_id": 412,
    "dashboard_id": 37,
    "viz_type": "echarts_timeseries_bar",
    "datasource": "12__table",
    "overrides": {
      "time_range": "Last quarter",
      "extra_filters": [{ "col": "region", "op": "IN", "val": ["EMEA"] }]
    },
    "row_limit": 50
  },
  "mapping": {
    "x": "order_date",
    "series": ["SUM(revenue)"],
    "series_labels": { "SUM(revenue)": "Revenue" },
    "sort": "x_asc",
    "top_n": 12
  },
  "format": { "number": ",.0f", "prefix": "$" }
}

Resolution produces an element patch that the existing renderer already understands:

{
  "categories": ["Jul", "Aug", "Sep"],
  "series": [{ "name": "Revenue", "values": [182340, 197800, 211050] }]
}

Three binding kinds cover v1:

Kind Target element Mapping Result written into chart Template v2 chart x, series, labels, sort, top-N categories, series metric Text element (a KPI) metric, optional compare Text run, formatted with format table Template v2 table columns, max_rows Table rows and header

Statuses: pending (never resolved), ok, stale (snapshot older than AI_SLIDES_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS, default 3600), error, forbidden (the viewer may not see this data).

Refreshable means resolvable

In v1, "refreshable" has one precise meaning: the source is a saved Superset chart that the analytics refresh API can execute, for the current user, with a viz_type that maps onto a Presenton ChartType. The planner (Story 7) and the catalog (Story 8) use exactly this rule.

docs.title: Analytics BE (Story 8)
Presenton BE (Stories 1, 2 and 3)
docs.text:
Method and path Story Purpose POST /api/v1/platform/session 2 Exchange the assertion for a Presenton session POST /api/v1/platform/session/refresh-data-token 2 Replace an expiring data token GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/bindings 1 List bindings with snapshot and status PUT /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/bindings/{binding_id} 1 Edit overrides or mapping (owner or editor) GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/refresh/stream 1 Refresh-on-open, server-sent events POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/refresh 1 Batch refresh, used before export GET /api/v1/ppt/prompt-library 3 List curated prompts GET /api/v1/ppt/prompt-library/{slug} 3 Prompt detail with variables schema POST /api/v1/ppt/prompt-library/{slug}/render 3 Validate variables, render the prompt GET /api/v1/ppt/templates/bundled 3 Curated built-in templates POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate-from-prompt/async 3 Async generation from a prompt, polled with GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id} (servers/fastapi/api/v1/async_tasks/router.py:15)

Refresh stream events:

Event Payload Meaning refresh_started {total} Number of bindings that will be resolved binding_loading {binding_id, slide_id} A request for this binding is in flight binding_data {binding_id, slide_id, element_name, element_patch, snapshot_at, changed} Fresh data; element_patch is merged into the slide binding_error {binding_id, code, message} Resolution failed; the snapshot stays on screen binding_stale {binding_id, snapshot_at, reason} Kept the old snapshot, for example on timeout refresh_complete {ok, errors, stale, duration_ms} All bindings settled

Wire format: like every Presenton stream (Streaming (SSE)), each frame is sent as event: response and the event name above travels in the JSON type field, for example data: {"type": "binding_data", "binding_id": "...", ...}.

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text: This chapter turns Story 1 into an implementation plan for the Presenton backend. You will run a three-day spike that picks how chart data is refreshed, then build the slide_data_bindings table (SQLModel model and Alembic migration), hook binding creation into the generation pipeline, and write the BindingRefreshService with its four endpoints. It ends with export integration, the error matrix, metrics, tests and the rollout plan.

docs.title: Step 1: The story, its owners and its acceptance criteria
docs.text:
The architect's backlog row, transcribed exactly:

# Story What it does Owners 1 [Presenton BE] Dynamic data: refresh spike, binding storage and refresh service Stores a Superset data binding for each chart or metric and refreshes values on open, after a spike picks the refresh approach. Srini, Sourav, Nitesh

Goal. Every chart, metric and table that the planner (Story 7) binds to a saved Superset chart keeps a durable link to that chart. When a deck is opened, exported or explicitly refreshed, Presenton re-runs the chart's query as the current user, maps the result into the Template v2 element, and stores the latest snapshot so the next open renders instantly.

Suggested split of work. Srini owns the spike and the refresh service, Sourav owns binding creation in the generation pipeline and export integration, Nitesh owns the migration and the contract with Story 8 (refresh API). This split is a recommendation, not part of the backlog.

Relationship to Part VII. Part VII's DataBinding (Data-bound slide model) becomes one slide_data_bindings row here, and Part VII's Binding Resolver becomes the refresh service of this chapter plus the analytics refresh API of Story 8. Native PPTX refresh in place is out of scope: Part VIII refreshes on open in the browser and bakes the latest snapshot into exports.
