docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text: This chapter is about what is running once a Presenton container has started, not how the image is built (that is Docker build and deployment). You will follow start.js from its first line to the point where it parks forever, learn exactly which process listens on which port and how readiness and shutdown work, map every directory under app_data to the code that writes it, read every nginx location block, and trace four representative requests end to end: a page load, an authenticated API call, a protected image fetch, and an MCP tool call.

docs.title: Step 1: The process tree at a glance
docs.text:
In the production image the container command is CMD ["node", "/app/start.js"] (Dockerfile:153). The development image runs CMD ["node", "/app/start.js", "--dev"] (Dockerfile.dev:93). start.js is a small supervisor: it prepares the filesystem, starts nginx as a system service, and spawns four kinds of children.

flowchart TB
  N["node /app/start.js (PID 1 supervisor)"]
  NG["nginx master + www-data workers (port 80)"]
  FA["python server.py --port 8000 (uvicorn, 127.0.0.1:8000)"]
  MCP["python mcp_server.py --port 8001 (FastMCP, 127.0.0.1:8001)"]
  NX["node servers/nextjs/server.js (127.0.0.1:3000)"]
  OL["ollama serve (only when START_OLLAMA is truthy)"]
  EX["node presentation-export/runner.mjs + Chromium (per export, spawned by FastAPI or Next.js)"]
  N -->|"service nginx start"| NG
  N -->|"spawn, watched"| FA
  N -->|"spawn, not watched"| MCP
  N -->|"spawn, watched"| NX
  N -->|"spawn, watched"| OL
  FA -->|"subprocess per API export task"| EX
  NX -->|"subprocess per UI export"| EX
Process Bind address Started at Watched by start.js? Logs nginx 0.0.0.0:80 (listen 80, nginx.conf:26) start.js:696-718 No (only the service command's exit code) /var/log/nginx/error.log (nginx.conf:4) FastAPI (uvicorn) 127.0.0.1:8000 (servers/fastapi/server.py:21-28) start.js:521-536, 601-606 Yes forwarded to container stdout/stderr MCP server (FastMCP) 127.0.0.1:8001 (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:457-465) start.js:608-620 No discarded (stdio: "ignore") Next.js 127.0.0.1:3000 start.js:538-566, 622-627 Yes forwarded Ollama (optional) Ollama's default start.js:661-670 Yes (no restart) inherited

Only port 80 is meant to be reachable from outside the container. FastAPI hard-codes host = "127.0.0.1" (servers/fastapi/server.py:21), Next.js is told -H 127.0.0.1 or HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1, and FastMCP runs on host="127.0.0.1". The Compose files also publish 1455:1455 for the Codex OAuth callback (docker-compose.yml:12), which is unrelated to the four servers above.

docs.title: Step 2: What happens before main() runs
docs.text: start.js does real work at module load time, before main() is called.

docs.title: 2.1 umask and required environment
docs.text:
process.umask(0o022) (start.js:28) makes every file and directory created by the supervisor and its children default to group/other read but not write. Then:

start.js (excerpt)
const fastapiPort = 8000;
const nextjsPort = 3000;
const appmcpPort = 8001;

const appDataDirectory = process.env.APP_DATA_DIRECTORY;
if (!appDataDirectory) {
  throw new Error("APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is required");
}

The ports are constants (start.js:46-48); there is no environment variable to change them. Both Dockerfiles set APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/app_data and TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton (Dockerfile:82-83, Dockerfile.dev:10-11).

docs.title: 2.2 Creating the app_data skeleton
docs.text:
ensureAppDataDirectories() runs at start.js:103. It creates the data root and seven asset directories with mode 0755, then tightens the three directories that hold export output:

start.js (excerpt)
const appDataDirectoryMode = 0o755;
const userConfigPath = join(appDataDirectory, "userConfig.json");
const userConfigBackupPath = `${userConfigPath}.bak`;
const userDataDir = dirname(userConfigPath);
const appDataStaticDirectories = [
  "exports",
  "images",
  "uploads",
  "fonts",
  "templates",
  "pptx-to-html",
  "pptx-to-json",
].map((name) => join(appDataDirectory, name));
// ...
const ensureAppDataDirectories = () => {
  ensureReadableDirectory(userDataDir);
  for (const dirPath of appDataStaticDirectories) {
    ensureReadableDirectory(dirPath);
  }
  for (const name of ["exports", "pptx-to-html", "pptx-to-json"]) {
    ensureReadableExportFiles(join(appDataDirectory, name));
  }
};

chmodBestEffort (start.js:73-82) swallows EPERM and EACCES, so a volume owned by another UID (the comment mentions Kubernetes/OpenShift PVCs) does not crash startup. Immediately afterwards userConfig.json and userConfig.json.bak are forced to 0600 if they exist (start.js:104-106).

ensureReadableExportFiles calls finalizeExportPermissions(dirPath, [appDataDirectory], { recursive: true, legacy: true }) from scripts/export-permissions.cjs:37-64. When the process runs as root it looks up the www-data (or nginx) group in /etc/group (scripts/export-permissions.cjs:4-16), chowns each path to that group, sets files to 0640, and for directories in legacy mode keeps the existing mode but strips the "other" bits (stat.mode & 0o7770, scripts/export-permissions.cjs:27-30). It walks upward from the export directory to the boundary root (app_data itself), so app_data, exports, pptx-to-html and pptx-to-json end up group-readable by the nginx worker user but not world-readable.

Gotcha

nginx runs its workers as user www-data (nginx.conf:1) and serves /app_data/... straight from disk with alias. If you change the nginx user, or run the container as a non-root UID without a www-data group, exported files may become unreadable to nginx and downloads fail with 403/404 from nginx even though FastAPI produced the file. The export runtime calls the same helper after each export (scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:123, servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:269-280).

docs.title: 2.3 Environment variables start.js sets for its children
Step 3: main() in order
3.1 ensurePresentationExportRuntime() (start.js:444-466)
docs.text:
Skipped when ENSURE_PRESENTATION_EXPORT_RUNTIME === "false" or when scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs is absent. Otherwise it runs node scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs --check-only. The check (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:253-286, 359-366) verifies that presentation-export/runner.mjs, node_modules/@presenton/export-core/package.json and presenton-export-version.json exist, that the installed version equals presentationExportVersion in the root package.json (v1.0.51 at this snapshot), that the sharp native runtime is valid, and that export-permissions.cjs was copied in.

  • Production: a failed check throws presentation-export runtime is missing in this container image. Rebuild the image so the runtime package is installed. (start.js:457-461). Because main() is not awaited with a catch, the unhandled rejection terminates Node and the container exits.
  • Development: it warns and runs the same script with --force, which downloads presenton-export-core-opensource-<version>.tgz from GitHub releases (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:32-33, 382-394).

docs.title: 3.2 ensureOllamaRuntime() (start.js:433-442)
docs.text: If START_OLLAMA is truthy (anything except empty, 0, false, no, off, start.js:418-426) and neither /usr/bin/ollama nor /usr/local/bin/ollama exists, it runs curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh. The production image sets START_OLLAMA=false (Dockerfile:91).

docs.title: 3.3 Dev-only steps
docs.text: With --dev (or -d, start.js:43): npm ci inside servers/nextjs (start.js:171-195), then scripts/sync-document-dependencies.cjs (start.js:225-227), which installs the LiteParse document-extraction dependencies.

docs.title: 3.4 setupUserConfigFromEnv() (start.js:490-497)
3.5 syncNginxConfigForDev() (start.js:468-479)
docs.text: In dev only, copies the bind-mounted /app/nginx.conf to /etc/nginx/nginx.conf, so nginx changes in your working tree take effect on container restart without rebuilding.

docs.title: 3.6 startNginx() (start.js:696-718)
docs.text:
Runs service nginx start. The init script daemonizes nginx and exits; the promise resolves true on exit code 0 and false otherwise. It never rejects.

Gotcha

nginx is not in the supervisor's managed set. If nginx fails to start, start.js only logs Nginx failed to start with exit code: ... and keeps running FastAPI and Next.js, so the container looks healthy while port 80 refuses connections. If nginx dies later, nothing notices.

docs.title: 3.7 startServers() (start.js:499-693)
docs.text:
Spawn order: FastAPI, MCP, Next.js, then optional Ollama. Command lines:

Child Command Working dir FastAPI python server.py --port 8000 --reload false (true in dev) servers/fastapi MCP python mcp_server.py --port 8001 servers/fastapi Next.js, production node servers/nextjs/server.js with HOSTNAME=127.0.0.1 PORT=3000 (only if server.js exists, start.js:539) servers/nextjs Next.js, dev or no standalone build node node_modules/next/dist/bin/next dev --webpack -H 127.0.0.1 -p 3000 (or start instead of dev --webpack) servers/nextjs Ollama ollama serve /

server.py simply parses --port, --reload and --log-level (default info) and calls uvicorn.run("api.main:app", host="127.0.0.1", ...) (servers/fastapi/server.py:6-28). Everything about the FastAPI app itself (lifespan, migrations, admin bootstrap, routers, middleware) is in FastAPI app and startup.

docs.title: 4.1 Readiness
4.2 Child exit and restart
Step 5: The app_data directory
docs.text:
APP_DATA_DIRECTORY (/app_data in Docker, a bind mount ./app_data:/app_data in every Compose service) is the only persistent state.

Path Mode Written by Read by userConfig.json 0600 start.js:140-168; FastAPI api/v1/auth/config.py:32-47 (auth secret, admin hash), services/provider_settings.py:85-100 (mirror) FastAPI, Next.js route handlers userConfig.json.bak 0600 start.js:129-138 start.js:126-127 fallback fastapi.db default umask SQLite default when DATABASE_URL is empty (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:57-60) FastAPI, MCP server exports/ and exports/users/<user-id>/ 0750-style dirs, 0640 files, group www-data export runtime writes to exports/ (scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:47-51), FastAPI moves into the owner folder (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:773-805) nginx /app_data/exports/ images/users/<user-id>/ 0755 generated and fetched slide images (servers/fastapi/utils/asset_directory_utils.py:23-30, 227-228) nginx /app_data/images/ uploads/users/<user-id>/ 0755 uploaded documents and files (asset_directory_utils.py:233-234); editor image uploads from the Next.js route servers/nextjs/app/api/upload-image/route.ts:46-48 nginx, document ingestion fonts/ 0755 font uploads (servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py:68-72) nginx, public templates/<template-id>/static/ 0755 bundled template assets copied on startup (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:295-307) nginx, public pptx-to-html/, pptx-to-json/ (users/<user-id>/<session>/) like exports/ PPTX conversion artifacts for custom templates (export_task_service.py:807-845) nginx with auth mem0/ (qdrant/, history.db) default chat memory (servers/fastapi/services/mem0_oss_memory.py:94-102, MEM0_DIR in Compose) FastAPI preview_slide/<n>/ default template-generation previews (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/tools.py:84-91) FastAPI assets/ default created by IconFinderService through get_writable_path("assets") as a fallback location for the icon vector store; normally empty because the bundled servers/fastapi/assets/icons-vectorstore.json is used (servers/fastapi/services/icon_finder_service.py:53-58) FastAPI

Per-user subfolders come from _owned_directory (asset_directory_utils.py:23-30): when a request has an owner (set by the auth middleware), files go under <root>/users/<owner_id>/. Files left in the root by pre-multi-user versions are "legacy" and only the admin may read them (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:106-123).

Why 0600 for userConfig.json

The file holds provider API keys, the JWT signing secret AUTH_SECRET_KEY (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/config.py:71-81) and a recovery copy of the admin password hash. The app-data mounts in nginx and FastAPI deliberately expose only the seven asset roots (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:80-82), never the root itself, so userConfig.json and fastapi.db have no HTTP path at all.

TEMP_DIRECTORY (/tmp/presenton) is not persistent; the export service puts per-owner work folders there (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:164-171).

docs.title: Step 6: The nginx routing table
docs.text:
nginx.conf has one server on port 80. Global settings: worker_connections 1024, client_max_body_size 100M (nginx.conf:7, 13), and two maps that keep X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host from an outer proxy, falling back to $scheme and $http_host (nginx.conf:16-23).

Location Upstream / target Auth Body limit Timeouts Notes / (:29) http://localhost:3000 (Next.js) none at nginx; Next.js layouts and proxy.ts 100M read 30m, connect 30m WebSocket Upgrade/Connection headers (Next dev HMR); Host $http_host keeps the port /api/v1/ (:45) http://localhost:8000 (path kept) FastAPI SessionAuthMiddleware 110M read/send/connect 30m error_page 413 = @request_entity_too_large /api/v2/ (:59) http://localhost:8000 FastAPI 100M (inherited) 30m no custom 413 body @request_entity_too_large (:71) returns 413 n/a n/a n/a body {"detail":"File size must be less than 100MB."} /mcp/ and /mcp (:77, :94) http://localhost:8001/mcp/ and /mcp bearer API key checked inside FastMCP 145M read/connect 30m forces Host: localhost:8001, forwards public host in X-Forwarded-Host /docs (:110) http://localhost:8000/docs FastAPI (protected path) 100M 30m uses $host and $scheme, not the forwarded maps /openapi.json (:120) http://localhost:8000/openapi.json FastAPI (protected path) 100M 30m same as /docs = /_auth_check (:133) http://localhost:8000/api/v1/auth/verify internal only body dropped defaults sends X-Original-URI, Cookie, Authorization /static/ (:153) alias /app/servers/fastapi/static/ none n/a n/a expires 1y, Cache-Control: public, immutable /app_data/images/, exports/, uploads/, pptx-to-html/, pptx-to-json/ alias /app_data/<root>/ auth_request /_auth_check n/a n/a disable_symlinks on, Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000 /app_data/fonts/, /app_data/templates/ alias none n/a n/a same caching; matches SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS (assets.py:17)

nginx picks the longest matching prefix, so /api/v1/... never reaches Next.js and /app_data/images/... never reaches FastAPI in Docker. There is no location for /redoc; it falls to / and Next.js answers 404.

docs.title: 6.1 The /static/ path-traversal comment
docs.text:
nginx.conf (excerpt)
    # Bundled UI static assets (logos, fonts packaged with the app) are safe to
    # serve unauthenticated; they contain no user data. The trailing slash on
    # the location pattern is required: with a bare `/static`, a request like
    # `/static../server.py` matches this block and `alias` rewrites it to
    # `/app/servers/fastapi/static/../server.py`, which nginx resolves to
    # `/app/servers/fastapi/server.py` — unauthenticated arbitrary read of any
    # file under /app the worker can stat. `/static/` constrains the match so
    # the only path that lands here is one that actually started with the
    # separator.
    location /static/ {
      alias /app/servers/fastapi/static/;

This is the classic nginx "alias traversal" misconfiguration: with location /static plus alias .../static/, nginx substitutes the matched prefix and the rest of the URI (../server.py) is appended verbatim. Ending both the location and the alias with / closes it.

Gotcha

When you add a new alias location (for example a new asset root), always end both the location prefix and the alias path with a slash, keep disable_symlinks on for user-writable roots, and add the root to PRIVATE_APP_DATA_ROOTS or SHARED_APP_DATA_ROOTS in servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:10-17. Otherwise /_auth_check returns 403 for every file in it, because _namespace_authorized rejects unknown roots (assets.py:111-112).

docs.title: Step 7: Sequence (a), a browser page load
docs.text:
Take GET /dashboard with a valid session cookie.

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant NG as nginx :80
  participant NX as Next.js :3000
  participant PX as proxy.ts
  participant L as Server layout
  participant FA as FastAPI :8000
  B->>NG: GET /dashboard (Cookie presenton_session)
  NG->>NX: location / proxy_pass, Host and X-Forwarded headers
  NX->>PX: proxy(request)
  PX-->>NX: not /api, not /app_data, not /pdf-maker so NextResponse.next()
  NX->>L: render (presentation-generator)/layout.tsx
  L->>FA: GET 127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/auth/status with the cookie
  FA-->>L: configured true, authenticated true, role
  L-->>NX: requireAppSession passes
  NX-->>NG: HTML, RSC payload
  NG-->>B: 200
  B->>NG: GET /_next/static/... (matcher excludes it from proxy.ts)
  1. nginx matches location / and forwards to localhost:3000 (nginx.conf:29-43).
  2. proxy.ts runs for every path except _next/static and favicon.ico (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:174-176). For page paths it first runs desktopRequestDenied (a no-op unless PRESENTON_ELECTRON=true, servers/nextjs/lib/desktop-auth.ts:14-15), then returns NextResponse.next() (proxy.ts:103-105).
  3. The (presentation-generator) layout calls requireAppSession() (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/layout.tsx:6-7), which fetches ${FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL}/api/v1/auth/status with the incoming cookie (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:37-58). It redirects to / when FastAPI is unreachable or no admin exists, and to /?reason=unauthorized when not signed in (serverAuth.ts:93-107).
  4. The response to /api/v1/auth/status looks like this (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:71-78):
{"configured": true, "authenticated": true, "username": "admin",
 "user_id": "6f1c2d8e-...", "role": "admin"}

Page-level guarding is covered in Settings, onboarding, auth UI.

docs.title: Step 8: Sequence (b), an authenticated API call
docs.text:
Browser code builds FastAPI URLs with getApiUrl(), which in the Docker web runtime returns a same-origin relative path such as /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all (servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:123-141, resolveBackendPathForRuntime at api.ts:88-98). So the request goes to nginx, not to Next.js.

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant NG as nginx :80
  participant MW as SessionAuthMiddleware
  participant R as Route handler
  participant DB as Database
  B->>NG: GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/all (Cookie presenton_session)
  NG->>MW: location /api/v1/ proxy_pass to 127.0.0.1:8000
  MW->>DB: SELECT count(*) FROM user
  alt no users
    MW-->>B: 428 detail Login setup is required, setup_required true
  else users exist
    MW->>DB: decode JWT cookie, load user (or verify Bearer sk-presenton- key)
    alt no principal
      MW-->>B: 401 detail Unauthorized
    else principal found
      MW->>R: set request.state and owner context vars
      R->>DB: owner-scoped query
      R-->>B: 200 JSON
    end
  end

The middleware stack, outermost first, is: the static_icon_fallback_middleware function middleware, SessionAuthMiddleware, UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware, then CORSMiddleware (Starlette runs the last-added middleware first, servers/fastapi/api/main.py:94-118). SessionAuthMiddleware.dispatch (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:55-152) does, in order:

  1. Desktop guard (desktop_request_denied), then the auth-disabled branch for Electron.
  2. Pass through OPTIONS, public auth paths, and paths that do not require auth (_requires_auth, middlewares.py:44-53: everything under /api/, /app_data/ except fonts and templates, plus /docs, /openapi.json, /redoc).
  3. 428 when the user table is empty (middlewares.py:83-94).
  4. resolve_request_principal (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/principal.py:22-57): cookie JWT first, then Authorization: Bearer <token> checked as an API key. Failure gives 401.
  5. Admin-only paths (/api/v1/admin/, Codex auth, font POST/DELETE, model listings, /api/v1/ppt/images/test) require a browser JWT from an admin, otherwise 403 Admin browser session required (middlewares.py:100-119).
  6. Store the principal on request.state, mint an internal JWT for API-key callers (used later by the exporter), set owner context variables, and call the route.

docs.title: 8.1 How proxy.ts behaves for /api paths
docs.text:
In Docker, /api/v1/* and /api/v2/* never reach Next.js because nginx routes them first. Next.js's own route handlers do reach it: servers/nextjs/app/api/ contains export-presentation, export-presentation-data/[id], read-file, runtime-config, telemetry-status, update-svg, upload-image, user-config, has-required-key and github-stars. For those, proxy.ts:138-171 applies:

Condition Result DISABLE_AUTH truthy pass through (continueRequest) OPTIONS, or path is /api/v1/auth/*, /api/telemetry-status, /api/update-svg, /api/export-presentation-data/* pass through Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... if FastAPI path, rewrite to FastAPI, else 403 API keys are only accepted by the Presenton API cookie valid per GET {FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL}/api/v1/auth/status pass through no admin configured 428 {"detail":"Login setup is required","setup_required":true} otherwise 401 {"detail":"Unauthorized"}

continueRequest rewrites /api/v1 and /api/v2 paths to the FastAPI base URL and lets other paths fall to the Next.js handler (proxy.ts:51-55). The rewrite branch matters when Next.js is reached without nginx (local next dev and Electron). getAuthStatus treats any fetch failure as {configured: true, authenticated: false} (proxy.ts:65-85), so a down FastAPI produces 401, not 428.

Gotcha

API keys are rejected by Next.js route handlers on purpose (proxy.ts:146-156). A script that calls /api/export-presentation with Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... gets 403. Use the FastAPI endpoints such as POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/{id}/export instead; see REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

docs.title: Step 9: Sequence (c), a protected image under /app_data/images
docs.text:
Generated images are stored as files and referenced in slide JSON by URL, for example /app_data/images/users/6f1c.../a1b2.png. In Docker the filesystem path and the URL path coincide because APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is /app_data.

sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant NG as nginx :80
  participant AC as location /_auth_check
  participant FA as FastAPI /api/v1/auth/verify
  participant FS as Disk /app_data/images
  B->>NG: GET /app_data/images/users/U/a1b2.png (Cookie)
  NG->>AC: auth_request subrequest
  AC->>FA: GET /api/v1/auth/verify, X-Original-URI, Cookie, Authorization, no body
  FA->>FA: resolve_request_principal
  alt no session or key
    FA-->>NG: 401
    NG-->>B: 401
  else path not owned by caller
    FA-->>NG: 403 Asset access denied
    NG-->>B: 403
  else authorized
    FA-->>NG: 200 authenticated true
    NG->>FS: alias read with disable_symlinks on
    FS-->>NG: bytes
    NG-->>B: 200 image, Cache-Control private, max-age=31536000
  end

verify_session (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:81-107) is public at the middleware level (it is in _PUBLIC_AUTH_PATHS) and does its own check. It calls is_app_data_path_authorized(original_uri, ...) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:78-103), which:

  1. Decodes the path up to 8 times until stable, failing closed on deeper nesting, and rejects NUL bytes, backslashes, empty, . and .. segments (assets.py:47-75).
  2. Allows fonts and templates for everyone; for the five private roots requires users/<caller-id>/<file> (at least three segments) or, for legacy root-level files, an admin (assets.py:106-123).
  3. Re-checks the canonical realpath target relative to the root, so a symlink cannot alias another user's folder (assets.py:89-103).

Gotcha

nginx auth_request treats only 2xx as allow and 401/403 as deny; any other status from /api/v1/auth/verify (for example a 500 while the database is locked) becomes a 500 to the browser. Broken images during heavy SQLite contention usually come from this subrequest, not from the file itself.

Outside Docker, the same URL is served by FastAPI's own _OwnerScopedStaticFiles mounts (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:20-44, mounted in servers/fastapi/api/main.py:77-82), with SessionAuthMiddleware returning 404 Asset not found for unauthorized paths (middlewares.py:138-148). The response code for "not yours" therefore differs: 403 behind nginx, 404 without it.

docs.title: Step 10: Sequence (d), an MCP client call to /mcp
docs.text:
mcp_server.py builds a FastMCP server from the checked-in OpenAPI spec servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json and exposes only a short allowlist of routes as tools (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:54-125). It proxies each tool call to FastAPI over HTTP.

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as MCP client
  participant NG as nginx :80
  participant M as FastMCP :8001
  participant V as PresentonTokenVerifier
  participant FA as FastAPI :8000
  C->>NG: POST /mcp, Authorization Bearer sk-presenton-ID.SECRET, tools/call
  NG->>M: proxy_pass /mcp, Host localhost:8001, X-Forwarded-Host public host
  M->>M: host and origin allowlist check
  M->>V: verify_token(token)
  V->>V: verify_api_key against api_keys table, mint 1 h internal JWT
  V-->>M: AccessToken with claims user_id and internal_session_token
  M->>FA: POST 127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async, Cookie presenton_session=JWT, X-Presenton-MCP-Request 1
  FA->>FA: SessionAuthMiddleware principal method jwt
  FA-->>M: AsyncTaskModel id, status pending
  M-->>C: tool result
  C->>NG: POST /mcp tools/call get_job_status
  NG->>M: proxy
  M->>FA: GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/ID
  FA-->>M: completed, data.path and data.edit_path made absolute
  M-->>C: tool result

Key code points:

  • nginx forces Host: localhost:8001 because FastMCP's DNS-rebinding guard only accepts localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:41, nginx.conf:85-87). The browser-visible host travels in X-Forwarded-Host. Allowed Origins are local origins plus PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL when set (mcp_server.py:128-140).
  • nginx deliberately does not use /_auth_check for /mcp (comment at nginx.conf:79-81): the asset ownership check would reject the non-asset path.
  • PresentonTokenVerifier.verify_token accepts only tokens starting with sk-presenton- (mcp_server.py:285-316). Browser cookies are never accepted as MCP credentials.
  • In normal operation attach_request_auth_header never forwards the long-lived API key to FastAPI (the only bearer fallback is for auth-disabled development and old tests, per its docstring). It sends the minted internal session as Cookie: presenton_session=..., adds X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, and copies X-Forwarded-Host/X-Forwarded-Proto (mcp_server.py:365-414). That header makes FastAPI turn path, edit_path and preview_url into absolute URLs (servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py:9-52).
  • The internal JWT lives for one hour (MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS, mcp_server.py:39) because the same session is reused by the exporter at the end of a long generation. Upstream reads time out after 600 s, connects after 15 s (mcp_server.py:31-34).
  • Which tools exist depends on PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE (get_mcp_route_maps, mcp_server.py:113-125). The full tool list and naming are in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

Gotcha

The MCP server reads the database directly (async_session_maker for API-key verification) but serves everything else by calling FastAPI at the hard-coded http://127.0.0.1:8000 (MCP_API_BASE_URL, mcp_server.py:31). It must run in the same network namespace as FastAPI, with the same DATABASE_URL and USER_CONFIG_PATH; splitting them into separate containers needs code changes.

docs.title: Step 11: One more hop, the export runtime calling back into the app
docs.text:
When FastAPI exports a deck, export_presentation builds a URL "{NEXT_PUBLIC_URL or http://127.0.0.1}/pdf-maker?id=..." and hands it to the export runtime (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:18-40). In Docker NEXT_PUBLIC_URL is not set, so headless Chromium loads http://127.0.0.1/pdf-maker, which is nginx on port 80, then location /, then Next.js. The caller's cookie travels two ways: the task's cookieHeader is installed as browser cookies for the page origin by the runner (scripts/run-presentation-export.mjs:43-56), and it is also appended as a #exportCookie=... URL fragment that PdfMakerPage reads (export_utils.py:35-36, servers/nextjs/app/(export)/pdf-maker/PdfMakerPage.tsx:146-152). The browser export path built by Next.js additionally sets an exportSession query parameter (servers/nextjs/lib/run-bundled-presentation-export.ts:162-165), which proxy.ts:114-136 converts into a presenton_session cookie before redirecting to the clean URL. The whole export path is the subject of PPTX and PDF export.

Gotcha

Because the exporter goes through nginx on 127.0.0.1:80 from inside the container, an nginx that failed to start (Step 3.6) breaks exports even if you were reaching the UI some other way, and a custom nginx config that drops location / or binds a different port breaks every PPTX/PDF download.

docs.title: Step 12: Electron, the same code without nginx
docs.text:
The desktop app runs the same FastAPI and Next.js with a different topology. Details are in Electron desktop app; the contrasts that matter here:

Concern Docker Electron Reverse proxy nginx on port 80 none Ports fixed 8000, 3000, 8001 first two free ports scanning upward from 40000 (findUnusedPorts, electron/app/utils/index.ts:39-65, called at electron/app/main.ts:468-470) How the browser reaches FastAPI same origin through nginx NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API=http://127.0.0.1:<port> set by setupEnv (electron/app/utils/index.ts:5-22), plus proxy.ts rewriting /app_data and /static (proxy.ts:107-112) and /api/v1, /api/v2 (continueRequest, proxy.ts:51-55) to FastAPI at request time Auth enabled; admin account required DISABLE_AUTH defaults to "true" unless ELECTRON_DISABLE_AUTH/DISABLE_AUTH says otherwise (electron/app/main.ts:150-160, 455-459); FastAPI and Next.js short-circuit to an "electron" admin Request guard none beyond auth desktop token cookie or header plus exact host and origin checks (servers/nextjs/lib/desktop-auth.ts:14-44) MCP port 8001 behind /mcp disabled when PRESENTON_ELECTRON is truthy (mcp_server.py:319-321) CORS * fallback (same origin anyway) exact NEXT_PUBLIC_URL origin with credentials (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:92-100)

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• start.js validates the export runtime, optionally installs Ollama, writes userConfig.json atomically from the environment, starts nginx as a daemon, then spawns FastAPI (8000), the MCP server (8001) and Next.js (3000), all bound to loopback.
  • Readiness is an HTTP probe of /api/v1/auth/status for FastAPI in production and log-line regexes otherwise; it only gates the banner. Any watched child exit stops the container, except clean exits in dev, which restart; nginx and MCP are not watched.
  • app_data holds userConfig.json (0600), the SQLite database, and seven asset roots with per-user users/<id>/ folders; export roots are group-owned by www-data with no world bits.
  • nginx routes /api/v1, /api/v2, /docs and /openapi.json to FastAPI, /mcp to FastMCP, serves /static/ and /app_data/* from disk, and protects five private asset roots with an auth_request to /api/v1/auth/verify.
  • proxy.ts guards Next.js's own /api handlers, rejects API keys there, and performs the rewrites that replace nginx in Electron.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: With the topology in mind, get a copy running yourself in Running it locally.

docs.title: Running it locally
docs.text: Reads: README.md, docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile.dev, start.js, scripts/user-config-env.cjs, scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs, test-local.sh, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py, servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py, servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, electron/package.json · Builds on: Runtime topology · Time: ~40 min

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text: This is the hands-on chapter. You will start Presenton from the published image, then from source with each of the four Compose services, then with FastAPI and Next.js as two plain processes on your machine, and finally as the Electron app. Along the way you will create the first administrator (both through the UI and unattended), open Swagger, mint an API key and generate a deck with curl, and run the same test suites CI runs. The chapter ends with a troubleshooting table built from error strings that actually exist in the code.

docs.title: Step 1: Run the published image
docs.text:
The quickest start, straight from README.md:328:

docker run -it --name presenton -p 5001:80 -v "./app_data:/app_data" ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:latest
  • Port 80 inside the container is nginx; nothing else is reachable from the host (see Runtime topology).
  • ./app_data on the host becomes APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/app_data (Dockerfile:82). Everything that must survive a restart lives there: userConfig.json, fastapi.db, images, exports and so on.
  • Open http://localhost:5001. With no account yet, the first screen is the account setup form (Step 4).

To preconfigure a text and image provider, pass them as environment variables (README.md:679):

docker run -it --name presenton -p 5001:80 \
  -e LLM="openai" -e OPENAI_API_KEY="******" -e IMAGE_PROVIDER="gpt-image-2" \
  -v "./app_data:/app_data" ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:latest

start.js copies the recognized variables into app_data/userConfig.json before FastAPI starts (start.js:490-497, key list in scripts/user-config-env.cjs:20-116).

Gotcha

Provider variables are authoritative only on the first boot. FastAPI's lifespan imports userConfig.json into a ProviderSettings database row the first time, and on every later start mirrors that row back over the file (servers/fastapi/services/provider_settings.py:85-127). Changing OPENAI_MODEL in your docker run command after the first boot therefore may not change anything. Use Settings in the UI, which writes the database row. Configuration precedence is detailed in Configuration and LLM providers.

docs.title: Step 2: The four Compose services
docs.text:
docker-compose.yml defines four services. They are services, not Compose profiles: there is no profiles: key in the file, so you name the service you want, for example docker compose up production. Running a bare docker compose up starts all four, which collide on the same host port.

Service Dockerfile Ports Volumes Command in container GPU production Dockerfile (multi-stage) ${PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT:-5001}:80, 1455:1455 ./app_data:/app_data, ./servers/fastapi/templates:/app/servers/fastapi/templates:ro node /app/start.js no production-gpu Dockerfile same ./app_data:/app_data only node /app/start.js 1 NVIDIA device (docker-compose.yml:136-142) development Dockerfile.dev same .:/app, named volumes for /app/node_modules, /app/document-extraction-liteparse, /app/presentation-export, ./app_data:/app_data node /app/start.js --dev no development-gpu Dockerfile.dev same same as development node /app/start.js --dev 1 NVIDIA device

Line references: production at docker-compose.yml:2-128, production-gpu at :130-262, development at :264-393, development-gpu at :395-520, named volumes at :530-534. Every service sets MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=true, PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE=${...:-both}, PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium, and forwards about a hundred provider, search, Mem0 and auth variables with empty defaults. Port 1455 exists for the Codex OAuth callback, because OpenAI redirects the browser to localhost:1455 (docker-compose.yml:11-12).

docs.title: 2.1 What the development image does differently
docs.text:
Dockerfile.dev is a single stage on python:3.11-slim-trixie (Dockerfile.dev:2). It installs nginx, Chromium (pinned to 149.0.7827.196-1~deb13u1), fonts, Tesseract and Node 22, runs the LiteParse and export-runtime sync scripts, installs FastAPI dependencies into the system interpreter with uv pip install --system (Dockerfile.dev:73-76), warms the FastEmbed caches, and ends with CMD ["node", "/app/start.js", "--dev"] (Dockerfile.dev:93).

The comment at Dockerfile.dev:68-69 explains the system-wide install: the .:/app bind mount hides any .venv you may have under servers/fastapi, so dependencies must live outside the source tree. The three named volumes do the same job for Node: they stop your host's node_modules (built for macOS, say) from shadowing the Linux ones.

With --dev, start.js (see Runtime topology) additionally:

  1. Runs npm ci in servers/nextjs (start.js:171-195). On the first start this takes several minutes.
  2. Re-syncs the export runtime with --force if the check fails, instead of exiting (start.js:456-465).
  3. Copies your working-tree nginx.conf into /etc/nginx/nginx.conf (start.js:468-479).
  4. Starts uvicorn with --reload true and next dev --webpack, and restarts either one after a clean exit (start.js:521-536, 538-566, 582-590).
docker compose up development
# edit servers/fastapi/... and uvicorn reloads; edit servers/nextjs/... and Next hot-reloads

Gotcha

Python dependencies are baked into the dev image. If you change servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml, rebuild with docker compose build development; uvicorn's reloader will not install new packages. Node dependencies in servers/nextjs are reinstalled by npm ci at every container start.

Gotcha

The host port is controlled by PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT (the port mapping), while the container receives PRESENTON_HOST_HTTP_PORT (only used by the startup banner, scripts/presenton-terminal-banner.mjs:98). The names differ by word order. The banner reads PRESENTON_HTTP_HOST_PORT first, but Compose does not pass that variable into the container, so in practice it uses PRESENTON_HOST_HTTP_PORT (scripts/presenton-terminal-banner.mjs:95-99). Both GPU services default the banner variable to 5000 (docker-compose.yml:152, docker-compose.yml:419) while mapping 5001, so their banner can print the wrong URL.

docs.title: Step 3: A minimal .env
docs.text:
Compose substitutes ${VAR:-default} from a .env file next to docker-compose.yml. A minimal working setup needs one text provider and, optionally, one image provider:

.env
LLM=openai
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
# OPENAI_MODEL defaults to gpt-4.1 when empty (servers/fastapi/constants/llm.py:4)
IMAGE_PROVIDER=pexels
PEXELS_API_KEY=...
# Optional unattended admin (Step 4.2)
AUTH_USERNAME=admin
AUTH_PASSWORD=change-this-password

start.js's config writer knows these LLM values: ollama, openai, deepseek, google, vertex, azure, bedrock, openrouter, fireworks, together, cerebras, anthropic, litellm, lmstudio, custom, codex (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:1-18). The list is applied only to the value already in userConfig.json, which is dropped when it is not in the set (sanitizeExistingConfig, scripts/user-config-env.cjs:224-230); a value coming from the environment is copied as is and is only rejected later, by FastAPI, at the first LLM call. Note that presenton (the Presenton Cloud provider) is not in this set, so a rewrite by start.js drops an LLM=presenton from the file; the database-backed provider row is mirrored back over the file when FastAPI starts (Step 1). Image providers are the ImageProvider enum: pexels, pixabay, gemini_flash, nanobanana_pro, gpt-image-2, gpt-image-1.5, comfyui, open_webui, openai_compatible (servers/fastapi/enums/image_provider.py:4-13).

If you omit IMAGE_PROVIDER, normalizeImageConfig picks one in this order (scripts/user-config-env.cjs:194-219): openai_compatible if its base URL, key and model are all set; open_webui if OPEN_WEBUI_IMAGE_URL; comfyui if COMFYUI_URL; pexels or pixabay if their keys exist; gpt-image-1.5 (quality medium) when LLM=openai with a key; gemini_flash when LLM=google with a key; otherwise it sets DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true. A legacy IMAGE_PROVIDER=dall-e-3 is rewritten to gpt-image-2 (:187-192).

docs.title: Step 4: First-run administrator
docs.text: Every /api/ route except the public /api/v1/auth/status, verify, setup, login and logout paths is behind SessionAuthMiddleware (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:30-36). Until a user exists it answers 428 {"detail":"Login setup is required","setup_required":true} (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:82-93). There are two ways to create the first account.

docs.title: 4.1 Through the UI
docs.text:
1. Open the app. The root page's AuthGate asks GET /api/v1/auth/status; when configured is false it shows setup mode (servers/nextjs/components/Auth/AuthGate.tsx:39).
  2. Submit username, password and confirmation. The client checks the two passwords match, then posts to /api/v1/auth/setup (AuthGate.tsx:199-235).
POST /api/v1/auth/setup
Content-Type: application/json

{"username": "admin", "password": "change-this-password"}
  1. setup_credentials (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:110-152) returns 409 if any user already exists, validates the body (AuthCredentialsRequest: username 3 to 128 non-whitespace characters, password 8 to 128, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/schemas.py:28-34), creates a User with is_superuser=True and admin_slot="primary", writes a recovery copy of the hash and a signing secret to userConfig.json (persist_admin_credentials, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/config.py:95-107), and responds:
{"configured": true, "authenticated": false, "username": "admin", "role": "admin"}
  1. Setup does not sign you in (authenticated: false). The UI shows "Account created" and asks you to sign in, which calls POST /api/v1/auth/login; that sets the presenton_session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 30 days, Secure only when the request or X-Forwarded-Proto is HTTPS, router.py:39-55, config.py:11-12).

docs.title: 4.2 Unattended, from environment variables
docs.text:
bootstrap_database_admin() runs in FastAPI's lifespan on every start (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:58). Its logic (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py:43-125):

State at startup Variables Result No users, AUTH_USERNAME and AUTH_PASSWORD set (no flags) creates the primary admin with that password; password must be at least 8 characters, username at least 3 No users, legacy AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH in userConfig.json no flag migrates the legacy account (pre-multi-user installs); AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD from the environment are ignored No users, legacy credentials present RESET_AUTH=true or AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true plus AUTH_PASSWORD creates the admin from the environment values instead of the legacy ones (bootstrap.py:91-106) No users, nothing set none does nothing; UI setup is required Admin exists RESET_AUTH=true or AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true plus AUTH_PASSWORD replaces password (and username if given), bumps auth_version so old sessions die, deletes all API keys, rotates the signing secret Admin exists a flag without AUTH_PASSWORD raises RuntimeError("RESET_AUTH and AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV require AUTH_PASSWORD ..."), FastAPI fails to start Users exist but none is superuser any raises User accounts exist but no bootstrap administrator is configured 
docker run -it --name presenton -p 5001:80 \
  -e AUTH_USERNAME=admin -e AUTH_PASSWORD=change-this-password \
  -v "./app_data:/app_data" ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:latest

Gotcha

Leaving RESET_AUTH=true or AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV=true in your .env rotates the admin on every container restart, which also deletes every API key (bootstrap.py:61-74). Remove the flag after one successful start, as the README advises.

Gotcha

Do not delete AUTH_* fields from app_data/userConfig.json to "reset" login. AUTH_SECRET_KEY there signs every session JWT and derives the Fernet key that encrypts stored API keys (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:39-43). Losing it invalidates sessions and makes existing keys impossible to reveal again.

docs.title: Step 5: Run FastAPI and Next.js without Docker
docs.text:
For fast iteration on one side you can run both servers directly. There is no nginx, so Next.js's proxy.ts takes over the routing role (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:43-55, 107-112).

flowchart LR
  BR["Browser at http://127.0.0.1:3000"]
  NX["next dev (port 3000) with proxy.ts"]
  FA["uv run python server.py --port 8000"]
  EXR["presentation-export/runner.mjs + Chromium"]
  DB["SQLite in APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/fastapi.db"]
  BR -->|"pages, /api/* route handlers"| NX
  NX -->|"rewrite /api/v1, /api/v2, /app_data, /static"| FA
  FA --> DB
  FA -->|"spawn per export"| EXR
  EXR -->|"loads NEXT_PUBLIC_URL/pdf-maker"| NX

docs.title: 5.1 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 exactly (requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.12", servers/fastapi/pyproject.toml:11) and uv.
  • Node 22 (the Docker images use NodeSource 22.x, Dockerfile:113-114) and npm.
  • A Chrome or Chromium for exports, pointed to by PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH (the images use /usr/bin/chromium). Whether the export package can fetch its own browser when the variable is unset is not verified here.

docs.title: 5.2 Sync the export runtime once
docs.text:
From the repository root:

npm ci
npm run sync:presentation-export      # node scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs
npm run check:presentation-export     # --check-only, prints "[presentation-export] OK (<version>)"

The sync downloads presenton-export-core-opensource-<version>.tgz for the version pinned by presentationExportVersion in package.json from github.com/presenton/presenton-export releases into presentation-export/ (scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:32-33, 155-172, 359-394). Use npm run sync:presentation-export:force to reinstall, or set EXPORT_CORE_ARCHIVE=/path/to/file.tgz to install from a local archive (:381-388). FastAPI finds the runtime at ../../presentation-export relative to servers/fastapi, or wherever EXPORT_PACKAGE_ROOT points (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:128-147).

docs.title: 5.3 Start FastAPI
docs.text:
cd servers/fastapi
uv sync
mkdir -p /tmp/presenton-dev/app_data /tmp/presenton-dev/tmp
export APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-dev/app_data
export TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-dev/tmp
export USER_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/presenton-dev/app_data/userConfig.json
export MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP=true
export NEXT_PUBLIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000
export PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH="/path/to/chrome"
uv run python server.py --port 8000 --reload true

Why each variable:

Variable Required? Reason in code APP_DATA_DIRECTORY yes lifespan calls os.makedirs(get_app_data_directory_env(), ...) and fails on None (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:55); asset mounts are only added when it is set (servers/fastapi/api/main.py:77-82); exports raise 500 without it (export_task_service.py:155-161) USER_CONFIG_PATH effectively yes the JWT secret is created and saved there; without it _save_auth_config raises ValueError("USER_CONFIG_PATH is not set") on the first login or bootstrap (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/config.py:32-35) TEMP_DIRECTORY no defaults to the system temp dir plus presenton (export_task_service.py:164-166) MIGRATE_DATABASE_ON_STARTUP no defaults to "true" when unset (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:453-454); Alembic runs only when the value is exactly true or True (servers/fastapi/migrations.py:40-42); create_db_and_tables still runs either way DATABASE_URL no defaults to sqlite:///$APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/fastapi.db, rewritten to sqlite+aiosqlite://; postgresql:// and mysql:// become asyncpg/aiomysql (servers/fastapi/utils/db_utils.py:57-67) NEXT_PUBLIC_URL yes for exports the exporter opens {NEXT_PUBLIC_URL or http://127.0.0.1}/pdf-maker (servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:18-40); without nginx on port 80 the default points nowhere. It also narrows CORS to that origin (api/main.py:92-100)

server.py accepts --port (required), --reload ("true" enables it) and --log-level (default info) and always binds 127.0.0.1 (servers/fastapi/server.py:6-28). The lifespan steps that run next are described in FastAPI app and startup.

Gotcha

update_env_with_user_config() runs on every request (UserConfigEnvUpdateMiddleware, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:23-26). When USER_CONFIG_PATH is set and the file has no LLM key, it removes LLM from os.environ (servers/fastapi/utils/user_config.py:378-383). An export LLM=openai in your shell can therefore vanish after the first request. Configure the provider through Settings, which persists it, rather than relying on shell variables.

docs.title: 5.4 Start Next.js
docs.text:
cd servers/nextjs
npm ci
export FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000
export USER_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/presenton-dev/app_data/userConfig.json
export APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-dev/app_data
export TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-dev/tmp
export NEXT_PUBLIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000
export PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH="/path/to/chrome"
npm run dev        # "next dev", serves http://localhost:3000
Variable Used by Default when unset FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL proxy.ts rewrites and auth checks, server layouts NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API, then http://127.0.0.1:8000 (proxy.ts:10-23, utils/serverAuth.ts:17-30) NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API browser and server code that needs an absolute backend origin none; leave it unset in this setup so browser calls stay same-origin and go through proxy.ts (utils/api.ts:88-98) USER_CONFIG_PATH app/api/user-config, lib/fastapi-internal.ts none APP_DATA_DIRECTORY app/api/export-presentation/*, app/api/upload-image those routes throw APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is required ... NEXT_PUBLIC_URL the browser export route builds {NEXT_PUBLIC_URL}/pdf-maker?... for the export runtime (servers/nextjs/lib/run-bundled-presentation-export.ts:159-160) http://127.0.0.1, which is nothing without nginx on port 80 PRESENTON_APP_ROOT, EXPORT_PACKAGE_ROOT where the browser export route finds presentation-export/runner.mjs the repository root two levels above servers/nextjs (run-bundled-presentation-export.ts:20-25) PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE which generation UI is offered both (see What Presenton is)

Open http://127.0.0.1:3000. A browser request to /api/v1/... hits Next.js, proxy.ts asks FastAPI /api/v1/auth/status with your cookie, then rewrites the request to http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/... (proxy.ts:138-171, 51-55). Requests to /app_data/* and /static/* are rewritten unconditionally and FastAPI's own owner-scoped static mounts enforce access (proxy.ts:110-112, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py:20-44).

Gotcha

Because each /api/v1 call in this mode costs an extra auth/status round trip from proxy.ts to FastAPI, it is slower than Docker, where nginx routes /api/v1 straight to FastAPI. Do not benchmark from this setup.

docs.title: Step 6: Electron in development
docs.text:
cd electron
npm run setup:env   # npm install, uv sync in servers/fastapi, npm install in servers/nextjs,
                    # export runtime sync, ImageMagick prep (electron/package.json:38)
npm run dev         # export runtime + bundled Chromium prep, copy templates, tsc, electron . --no-sandbox

In dev mode Electron starts FastAPI with uv run python server.py --port <port> --reload true and Next.js with npm run dev -- -H 127.0.0.1 -p <port> (electron/app/utils/servers.ts:137-143, 208-212). Ports are the first two free ones from 40000 upward, auth is disabled by default, and MCP is off. The full lifecycle is in Electron desktop app.

docs.title: Step 7: Swagger and the OpenAPI document
docs.text:
nginx proxies /docs and /openapi.json to FastAPI (nginx.conf:110-128). Both are in SessionAuthMiddleware._PROTECTED_NON_API_PATHS (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:42), so sign in through the UI first; the browser then sends presenton_session and Swagger loads. In the no-Docker setup, sign in through the UI at http://127.0.0.1:3000, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs. Browser cookies are scoped to the host name, not the port, so the presenton_session cookie set on 127.0.0.1:3000 is also sent to 127.0.0.1:8000. Use the same host name for both (localhost and 127.0.0.1 are different cookie hosts).

The MCP server does not read the live /openapi.json. It uses the checked-in servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json, regenerated by servers/fastapi/scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py. After adding or renaming an endpoint the MCP layer depends on, regenerate that file.

docs.title: Step 8: An API key and a generation with curl
docs.text: API keys are created by an admin with a browser session, then used by scripts. The full API surface is in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP; this step is the shortest working path.

docs.title: 8.1 Log in and capture the session cookie
docs.text:
curl -s -c cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"change-this-password"}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/v1/auth/login

{"configured": true, "authenticated": true, "id": "6f1c2d8e-...", "username": "admin", "role": "admin", "created_at": "..."}

The handler is login (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/router.py:155-188); the user fields come from serialize_user (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/users.py:227-233). IDs and timestamps above are placeholders. Wrong credentials give 401 Unauthorized; no account gives 428 Login setup is required.

docs.title: 8.2 Create the key
docs.text:
curl -s -b cookies.txt -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"user_id":"6f1c2d8e-...","label":"My API client","expiry_days":90}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/v1/admin/api-keys

AdminCreateApiKeyRequest requires user_id; label defaults to "API client" (1 to 120 characters) and expiry_days to 90 (1 to 365) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/schemas.py:56-59). The endpoint (servers/fastapi/api/v1/admin/router.py:60-82) returns 201 with ApiKeyCreated:

{
  "id": "0123456789abcdef",
  "user_id": "6f1c2d8e-...",
  "created_by_id": "6f1c2d8e-...",
  "label": "My API client",
  "created_at": "...",
  "expires_at": "...",
  "last_used_at": null,
  "revoked_at": null,
  "token": "sk-presenton-0123456789abcdef.<secret>"
}

The token format is sk-presenton-<16 hex id>.<secret> where the secret is secrets.token_urlsafe(40) (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:19-22, 79-104). Only a hash of the secret is used for verification, plus a Fernet-encrypted copy so an admin can reveal it again with GET /api/v1/admin/api-keys/{id}/token.

Gotcha

/api/v1/admin/* accepts only a browser JWT from an admin (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:100-119). Calling it with an API key, even an admin's, returns 403 Admin browser session required. That is why this step logs in with a cookie first.

docs.title: 8.3 Generate a deck
docs.text:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5001/api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-0123456789abcdef.<secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"content":"Introduction to Machine Learning","n_slides":5,"language":"English","template":"general","export_as":"pptx"}'

GeneratePresentationRequest (servers/fastapi/models/generate_presentation_request.py:8-46):

Field Type Default content string, required (none) slides_markdown list of strings null instructions string null tone default, casual, professional, funny, educational, sales_pitch default verbosity concise, standard, text-heavy standard web_search bool false n_slides int null (model decides) language string null (model decides) template string "general" include_table_of_contents bool false include_title_slide bool true files list of uploaded file paths null export_as pptx or pdf pptx trigger_webhook bool false

check_if_api_request_is_valid (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:2620-2681) returns 400 when content, slides_markdown and files are all empty, when n_slides is not positive or exceeds MAX_NUMBER_OF_SLIDES = 50 (servers/fastapi/constants/presentation.py:4), when slides_markdown has more than 50 items, when a table of contents is requested with fewer than 3 slides, or with Template not found. Please use a valid template. The 16 bundled names are the folder names under templates/ (civic, dynamic, editorial, executive, general, horizon, landmark, modern, momentum, mosaic, nova, pulse, signal, standard, swift, verdant).

The synchronous endpoint (presentation.py:3169-3195) blocks until export finishes and returns PresentationPathAndEditPath:

{
  "presentation_id": "d3000f96-096c-4768-b67b-e99aed029b57",
  "path": "/app_data/exports/users/6f1c2d8e-.../Introduction_to_Machine_Learning.pptx",
  "edit_path": "/presentation?id=d3000f96-096c-4768-b67b-e99aed029b57"
}

The file name is derived from the generated presentation title, so the values above are illustrative. path is the filesystem path returned by the export service after it moves the file into the owner's folder (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:449-455, 773-805); in Docker it is also the nginx URL. Download it with the same bearer key, since nginx's /_auth_check forwards Authorization (nginx.conf:141):

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-..." -o deck.pptx \
  "http://localhost:5001/app_data/exports/users/6f1c2d8e-.../Introduction_to_Machine_Learning.pptx"

For long decks use POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async, which returns an AsyncTaskModel immediately, then poll GET /api/v1/ppt/presentation/status/{id} until status is completed; data.path and data.edit_path carry the same values (presentation.py:3240-3298, completion data at :3113-3127).

Gotcha

The README example shows a path like /app_data/<id>/<name>.pptx. In this snapshot, authenticated exports land in exports/users/<owner-id>/. Always use the path the API returns rather than building it yourself.

docs.title: Step 9: Running the test suites
docs.text:
test-local.sh reproduces .github/workflows/test-all.yml and runs three checks, counting failures instead of stopping at the first one (test-local.sh:15-30, 73-83). It needs uv, npm and node on PATH (:63-68).

Check Commands (test-local.sh lines) Repository tooling npm ci && npm test && npm run sync:presentation-export && npm run check:presentation-export at the root (:32-38) FastAPI uv sync --locked --dev, then uv run --locked python -m pytest --verbose --tb=short with APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/app-data, TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/temp, DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/presenton-tests/test.db, DISABLE_ANONYMOUS_TRACKING=true, DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true (:40-50) Next.js npm ci && npm test && npm run lint && NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API=http://localhost:8000 NEXT_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:3000 npm run build && npx cypress run --component --browser electron (:52-61)

Per suite, run the same commands by hand. The root npm test runs the template converter tests and seven node --test files under scripts/ (package.json, "test" script). In servers/nextjs, npm test is plain node --test, which discovers the *.test.mjs files in servers/nextjs/tests/, and component tests live in servers/nextjs/cypress/. Electron has its own npm run test:security (electron/package.json:41). CI wiring is covered in CI, tests, security.

# just the FastAPI suite, one file
cd servers/fastapi
APP_DATA_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/app-data TEMP_DIRECTORY=/tmp/presenton-tests/temp \
DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/presenton-tests/test.db DISABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true \
uv run python -m pytest tests/integration -q

docs.title: Step 10: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Every message below is a literal string from the code.

Symptom Where it comes from Cause and fix Container exits with APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is required start.js:50-53 running start.js outside the images without the variable; set it Container exits with presentation-export runtime is missing in this container image. Rebuild the image so the runtime package is installed. start.js:457-461 production check failed; rebuild, or in a custom image run node scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs --force. ENSURE_PRESENTATION_EXPORT_RUNTIME=false skips the check but exports will then fail [presentation-export] Expected export-core X, found Y. scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs:267-271 presentationExportVersion in package.json changed; run npm run sync:presentation-export Nginx failed to start with exit code: ... but the logs continue start.js:713 nginx config error; nothing on port 80. Check /var/log/nginx/error.log Skipping startup banner: FastAPI did not respond at http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/auth/status within 60000ms start.js:358-363, 689 slow first boot (migrations, model cache) or a lifespan crash; read the FastAPI traceback above it 428 {"detail":"Login setup is required","setup_required":true} servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:86-93, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:162-167 no user yet; complete setup (Step 4) 401 {"detail":"Unauthorized"} middlewares.py:95-99, proxy.ts:168-171 missing or expired cookie, revoked or expired API key, wrong Bearer format; keys must start with sk-presenton- and have a secret of at least 32 characters (servers/fastapi/services/api_keys.py:50-61) 403 {"detail":"Admin browser session required"} middlewares.py:115-119 admin endpoint called with an API key or a non-admin account 403 {"detail":"API keys are only accepted by the Presenton API"} proxy.ts:150-155 API key sent to a Next.js /api/* route handler 409 Credentials already configured router.py:116-117 setup called twice; log in instead FastAPI fails with RESET_AUTH and AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV require AUTH_PASSWORD ... servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/bootstrap.py:56-60 recovery flag without a password 500 Invalid LLM provider. Please select one of: ... servers/fastapi/utils/llm_provider.py:47-59 LLM empty or unknown; choose a provider in Settings 400 Google API Key is not set (and similar per provider) utils/llm_provider.py:177-180 provider selected without credentials 400 Template not found. Please use a valid template. presentation.py:2677-2680 misspelled template name or a custom template ID from another user 413 {"detail":"File size must be less than 100MB."} nginx.conf:71-74 upload above the 110M /api/v1/ limit; /api/v2/ uses the 100M default without the JSON body Images or downloads 403 behind nginx, 404 without router.py:96-102, middlewares.py:138-148 the file is in another user's users/<id>/ folder or a legacy root-level file and you are not admin /mcp returns 502 MCP process not watched, logs discarded (start.js:608-620) run python mcp_server.py --port 8001 in the container to see why it died Exports hang or fail in a no-Docker setup servers/fastapi/utils/export_utils.py:18-19 NEXT_PUBLIC_URL not set, so Chromium loads http://127.0.0.1/pdf-maker on port 80 APP_DATA_DIRECTORY is required to download exported files. servers/nextjs/app/api/export-presentation/route.ts:35-38 Next.js started without APP_DATA_DIRECTORY

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• docker run -p 5001:80 -v ./app_data:/app_data ghcr.io/presenton/presenton:latest is the fastest start; Compose offers four named services (production, production-gpu, development, development-gpu), and the dev ones bind-mount the source and run start.js --dev.
  • Provider environment variables seed userConfig.json, but after the first boot the database copy wins; change providers in Settings.
  • The first admin is created either through POST /api/v1/auth/setup from the UI or by bootstrap_database_admin() from AUTH_USERNAME/AUTH_PASSWORD, with RESET_AUTH/AUTH_OVERRIDE_FROM_ENV for recovery.
  • Without Docker you need APP_DATA_DIRECTORY, USER_CONFIG_PATH and, for exports, NEXT_PUBLIC_URL on the FastAPI side, plus a synced presentation-export/; proxy.ts stands in for nginx.
  • API keys are minted by an admin browser session at POST /api/v1/admin/api-keys and sent as Authorization: Bearer sk-presenton-... to POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate or its async twin.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Now look inside the backend process you just started, beginning with FastAPI app and startup.

docs.title: FastAPI app and startup
docs.text:
Reads: servers/fastapi/server.py, servers/fastapi/api/main.py, servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py, servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/context.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/auth/assets.py, servers/fastapi/services/database.py · Builds on: Running it locally · Time: ~35 min

This chapter follows the FastAPI process from python server.py to the first request it serves. You will see every router and its full URL prefix, the /app_data and /static mounts, the CORS rule, the middleware stack in the order it really executes, each lifespan step, and the SessionAuthMiddleware decision tree. It ends with the request-scoped owner context that makes multi-user isolation automatic, and a worked example of adding an endpoint the way the codebase expects.

All paths below are relative to the repository root. Unless stated otherwise, servers/fastapi/ is the Python package root and the working directory of the process.

docs.title: Step 1: The process entry point (server.py)
docs.text:
The whole backend is started by a 29-line script, servers/fastapi/server.py. It parses three flags and hands a module path string to Uvicorn.

Flag Type Default Effect --port int required TCP port (server.py:7) --reload str "false" Only the exact string "true" enables Uvicorn auto-reload (server.py:11, server.py:20) --log-level str "info" Passed to uvicorn.run(log_level=...) (server.py:13)

The bind host is hard-coded:

servers/fastapi/server.py (excerpt)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    reload = args.reload == "true"
    host = "127.0.0.1"

    uvicorn.run(
        "api.main:app",
        host=host,
        port=args.port,
        log_level=args.log_level,
        reload=reload,
    )

FastAPI therefore only listens on loopback. In Docker, nginx is the public face and proxies /api/v1/, /api/v2/, /docs and /openapi.json to localhost:8000 (nginx.conf:45, nginx.conf:59, nginx.conf:110). Two launchers call this script:

  • start.js spawns python server.py --port 8000 --reload <isDev> with cwd set to servers/fastapi (start.js:521, start.js:532, with fastapiDir defined at start.js:33).
  • Electron runs either uv run python server.py --port <port> --reload true in development or a PyInstaller binary with --port <port> (electron/app/utils/servers.ts:139, electron/app/utils/servers.ts:143). See Electron desktop app.

Gotcha

server.py imports from api.main import app at line 3, before uvicorn.run receives the string "api.main:app". With --reload true, the Uvicorn supervisor process has therefore already executed all of api/main.py (Sentry init, directory creation, mounts) even though only the reloaded child serves requests. The lifespan (Step 8) runs only in the serving process.

The working directory matters. utils/path_helpers.py:15 resolves bundled read-only assets with os.path.join(os.getcwd(), relative_path), so static/ and assets/ are found only when the process starts inside servers/fastapi.

docs.title: Step 2: Import-time work in api/main.py
docs.text: Everything in api/main.py runs when the module is imported, before any request and before the lifespan.

docs.title: 2.1 A sandbox-safe MIME table
docs.text:
init_sandbox_safe_mimetypes() is the first statement (api/main.py:29). It re-initializes the stdlib mimetypes table with files=[], so Python never reads OS databases such as /etc/apache2/mime.types, then registers 15 explicit types (utils/mime_types.py:4). The docstring explains why: macOS App Store sandboxed builds can be denied access to those files, and Starlette's FileResponse calls mimetypes.guess_type lazily (utils/mime_types.py:23).

Extension Media type .avif, .gif, .jpeg/.jpg, .png, .svg, .webp image types (.svg is image/svg+xml) .otf, .ttf, .woff, .woff2 font/otf, font/ttf, font/woff, font/woff2 .pdf, .docx, .pptx, .xlsx application/pdf and the three OOXML types

docs.title: 2.2 Optional Sentry
docs.text:
_maybe_init_sentry() runs at api/main.py:63, still at import time.

servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt)
    traces_sample_rate = get_sentry_traces_sample_rate_env()
    send_default_pii = get_sentry_send_default_pii_env()
    try:
        parsed_sample_rate = (
            float(traces_sample_rate) if traces_sample_rate is not None else 1.0
        )
    except ValueError:
        parsed_sample_rate = 1.0

    parsed_send_default_pii = (
        send_default_pii.lower() == "true" if send_default_pii is not None else True
    )

    sentry_sdk.init(
        dsn=sentry_dsn,
        send_default_pii=parsed_send_default_pii,

Env var Getter Default when unset SENTRY_DSN get_sentry_dsn_env (utils/get_env.py:457) No Sentry at all SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE get_sentry_traces_sample_rate_env (utils/get_env.py:461) 1.0; also 1.0 if not parseable as float SENTRY_SEND_DEFAULT_PII get_sentry_send_default_pii_env (utils/get_env.py:465) True; any value other than true (case-insensitive) means False

If sentry_sdk cannot be imported, the function returns silently (api/main.py:37), because the SDK is optional in some build targets.

Gotcha

Setting only SENTRY_DSN gives you 100 percent trace sampling and send_default_pii=True. Set both companion variables explicitly in any deployment that handles real user data.

docs.title: 2.3 Creating the application
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/api/main.py (excerpt)
app = FastAPI(lifespan=app_lifespan)

There are no global exception handlers, no custom OpenAPI configuration and no root path. The only startup hook is the app_lifespan async context manager covered in Step 8.

Declaration order inside a router is part of the routing logic. GET /presentation/all is declared at presentation.py:1499, before GET /presentation/{id} at presentation.py:1551; GET /template/all (template.py:1113) precedes GET /template/{template_id} (template.py:2122).
