docs.title: 9.3 When and what is sent
docs.text:
generate_presentation_handler schedules delivery with CONCURRENT_SERVICE.run_task(None, WebhookService.send_webhook, event, payload) on both outcomes (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3133 and servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:3150). run_task wraps the call in asyncio.create_task and keeps a reference until it finishes (servers/fastapi/services/concurrent_service.py:10), so the HTTP response does not wait for delivery.

presentation.generation.completedpresentation.generation.failed 
{
  "presentation_id": "d3000f96-096c-4768-b67b-e99aed029b57",
  "path": "/app_data/exports/users/<owner-uuid>/<Deck_Title>.pptx",
  "edit_path": "/presentation?id=d3000f96-096c-4768-b67b-e99aed029b57"
}

{
  "status_code": 500,
  "detail": "Presentation generation failed"
}

The success body is response.model_dump(mode="json") and the failure body is APIErrorModel (servers/fastapi/models/api_error_model.py:5). Both are host-relative and unsigned.

docs.title: 9.4 Delivery mechanics
9.5 The mock router
docs.text: API_V1_MOCK_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/mock/router.py:9) has two GET endpoints that return a one-element list of each payload type: a PresentationPathAndEditPath with a random id, path built by absolute_fastapi_asset_url("/app_data/exports/test.pdf") and edit_path /presentation?id=123; and an APIErrorModel with 500 / Presentation generation failed. Nothing in the application calls them. Their response models are exactly the two webhook bodies, so in practice they document those schemas in the OpenAPI document and return samples you can use when building a receiver. Both handler functions are named mock_presentation_generation_completed; FastAPI registered both routes before the second definition shadowed the first name, so the generated operation ids differ only by path. The routes sit under /api/, so they require authentication like everything else.

docs.title: 10.1 Process and routing
docs.text:
mcp_server.py is a separate Python process started by start.js as python mcp_server.py --port 8001 with stdio: "ignore" (start.js:608). Its main() (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:417) exits immediately when PRESENTON_ELECTRON is truthy, otherwise serves FastMCP's HTTP transport on 127.0.0.1:<port>. nginx exposes it at /mcp and /mcp/ (nginx.conf:77 and nginx.conf:94) with:

  • client_max_body_size 145M, enough for the 100 MiB base64 upload limit (base64 inflates by a third),
  • proxy_read_timeout 30m,
  • Host localhost:8001 rewritten, because FastMCP's host check only allows localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 (MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS, servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:41), while the public host travels in X-Forwarded-Host,
  • no auth_request: the MCP server authenticates bearer keys itself.

The README describes it as an MCP 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP endpoint at /mcp.

Gotcha

Unlike FastAPI and Next.js, the MCP child process is not registered with watchManagedProcess in start.js (only an error listener is attached at start.js:618), and its output is discarded. If it crashes, nothing restarts it and nothing is logged. A failing MCP client while the web app works is the usual symptom.

docs.title: 10.2 Building tools from OpenAPI
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py (excerpt)
def create_mcp_server(
    api_client: httpx.AsyncClient | httpx2.AsyncClient,
    *,
    name: str = "Presenton",
    auth: TokenVerifier | None = None,
) -> FastMCP:
    """Create the MCP server with only the public presentation workflow exposed."""
    generation_mode = get_presentation_generation_mode()
    return FastMCP.from_openapi(
        openapi_spec=openapi_spec,
        client=api_client,
        name=name,
        auth=auth,
        route_maps=get_mcp_route_maps(generation_mode),
        mcp_names=MCP_TOOL_NAMES,
        instructions=get_mcp_instructions(generation_mode),
    )

There is no hand-written tool code. openapi_spec is openai_spec.json, loaded once at import (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:281). FastMCP.from_openapi turns each allowed operation into a tool whose input schema is the operation's parameters plus its request body properties (the upload_files tool exposes files directly, as servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_mcp_server_auth.py:312 asserts). Calling a tool makes an HTTP request through api_client, an httpx2.AsyncClient with base URL http://127.0.0.1:8000, a 600 s read timeout and a 15 s connect timeout (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:31 to servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:34).

docs.title: 10.3 Every tool
docs.text:
MCP_TOOL_NAMES (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:101) renames operation ids to friendly tool names:

Tool HTTP route Inputs (from openai_spec.json) start_standard_presentation POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate/async all GeneratePresentationRequest fields; content required start_smart_presentation POST /api/v2/ppt/presentation/generate/smart/async all GenerateSmartPresentationRequest fields; none required list_templates GET /api/v1/ppt/template/all page (int, min 1, default 1), page_size (1 to 100, default 20), default (bool or null: true = built-in only, false = user's custom only) upload_template_assets POST /api/v1/ppt/template/mcp-upload pptx (filename 1 to 255 chars, content_base64, optional original_font_name), fonts (up to 32 of the same shape); returns pptx_url, slide_image_urls, fonts start_template_generation POST /api/v1/ppt/template/async pptx_url (required), slide_image_urls (required, min 1), fonts (object), name, description, icon_type (bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin, default bold) upload_files POST /api/v1/ppt/files/mcp-upload files: 1 to 32 items of filename (1 to 255 chars) and content_base64; returns file_paths get_job_status GET /api/v1/async-tasks/status/{id} id (path)

upload_files decodes each item with strict base64 validation (400 Invalid base64 content for '<name>'), enforces 100 MiB per file and combined (413), wraps the bytes in UploadFile objects and reuses the multipart handler (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/files.py:108). It exists because MCP tools carry JSON, not multipart bodies.

Example arguments an MCP client would send to start_standard_presentation after an upload:

{
  "content": "Turn the attached report into a board update",
  "n_slides": 10,
  "template": "general",
  "files": ["/tmp/presenton/<owner>/<uuid>/q3-report.pdf"],
  "export_as": "pdf"
}

docs.title: 10.4 Mode gating with PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py (excerpt)
def get_mcp_route_maps(
    generation_mode: PresentationGenerationMode,
) -> list[RouteMap]:
    """Expose only workflows enabled by PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE."""
    route_maps: list[RouteMap] = []
    if generation_mode in {"both", "standard"}:
        route_maps.extend(MCP_STANDARD_ROUTE_MAPS)
        route_maps.extend(MCP_TEMPLATE_ROUTE_MAPS)
    if generation_mode in {"both", "smart"}:
        route_maps.extend(MCP_SMART_ROUTE_MAPS)
    route_maps.extend(MCP_SHARED_ROUTE_MAPS)
    route_maps.append(RouteMap(mcp_type=MCPType.EXCLUDE))
    return route_maps

The final catch-all EXCLUDE hides everything else: the spec has 100 operations across 93 paths, and at most 7 become tools. get_presentation_generation_mode lowercases and trims the variable and falls back to both for anything unrecognized (servers/fastapi/utils/get_env.py:24).

Mode Tools exposed both (default, or invalid) all seven standard start_standard_presentation, list_templates, upload_template_assets, start_template_generation, upload_files, get_job_status smart start_smart_presentation, upload_files, get_job_status

These sets are pinned by servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_mcp_server_auth.py:372. The server instructions text is assembled per mode too (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:143): it tells the model to copy ids and paths verbatim, never to send a client attachment id in place of base64 bytes, to start exactly one job per request, to poll every 10 to 15 seconds, to use data.path and data.edit_path on completion, and never to ask the user to paste an API key into chat.

Gotcha

PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE gates the MCP tool list and the web UI only. As docs/presentation-generation-modes.md states, it is not an authorization control: with smart set, POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate still works for any authenticated REST caller. The variable is also read once when the MCP server is built, so changing it requires restarting the MCP process.

docs.title: 10.5 The token verifier and the key-for-session exchange
docs.text:
When auth is enabled, create_mcp_auth_provider returns a PresentonTokenVerifier; with DISABLE_AUTH it returns None and the MCP endpoint is open (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:324).

servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py (excerpt)
class PresentonTokenVerifier(TokenVerifier):
    """Validate the same user-scoped API keys accepted by the REST API."""

    async def verify_token(self, token: str) -> AccessToken | None:
        if not token.startswith(API_KEY_PREFIX):
            return None
        async with async_session_maker() as session:
            verified = await verify_api_key(session, token)
            if verified is None:
                return None
            user = verified.user
            try:
                internal_session_token = await get_jwt_strategy(
                    lifetime_seconds=MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS
                ).write_token(user)
            except ValueError:
                # ...
                internal_session_token = None

The returned AccessToken carries claims u (username), role (admin or user), user_id, api_key_id and internal_session_token, a one-hour JWT (MCP_INTERNAL_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS = 60 * 60, chosen so a 10 to 20 minute generation including export does not outlive its session, per the comment at servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:35).

Then, on every outbound call to FastAPI, the httpx request hook attach_request_auth_header (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:365) rewrites the request:

sequenceDiagram
    participant Cl as MCP client
    participant Ng as nginx
    participant Mc as FastMCP on 8001
    participant Fa as FastAPI on 8000
    Cl->>Ng: POST /mcp tools/call with Authorization Bearer sk-presenton key
    Ng->>Mc: same request, Host rewritten, X-Forwarded-Host kept
    Mc->>Mc: verify_api_key against the database
    Mc->>Mc: mint 1 hour presenton_session JWT
    Mc->>Fa: POST generate/async with Cookie presenton_session and X-Presenton-MCP-Request 1
    Fa-->>Mc: AsyncTaskModel JSON
    Mc-->>Cl: tool result with task id
  1. Always set X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, and forward the client's X-Forwarded-Host (or Host) and X-Forwarded-Proto.
  2. If the outgoing request already has Authorization or Cookie, stop.
  3. If the verified token has an internal_session_token, send it as Cookie: presenton_session=<jwt>. The long-lived API key is never forwarded to FastAPI.
  4. If the token has a user_id but no session could be minted, raise RuntimeError rather than fall back to the key.
  5. Fallbacks for auth-disabled development: forward Bearer <token> or the incoming Authorization header.

FastAPI then authenticates the cookie like a browser session, which is also why the export step works without further plumbing: build_export_cookie_header copies the incoming cookie header verbatim.

docs.title: 10.6 Absolute result links
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py (excerpt)
def absolute_mcp_url(request: Request, value: str) -> str:
    """Make a host-relative MCP result link usable by client-neutral renderers."""
    if not is_mcp_request(request) or not value.startswith("/"):
        return value

    configured_origin = get_presenton_public_url()
    if configured_origin:
        return f"{configured_origin}{value}"

absolute_mcp_result_links (servers/fastapi/utils/mcp_public_urls.py:43) copies a payload and rewrites only the keys path, edit_path and preview_url, only when the request carried X-Presenton-MCP-Request: 1, and only for values starting with /. The origin is PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL when it is set to an http(s) URL; otherwise the first value of X-Forwarded-Proto (if http or https) and X-Forwarded-Host, falling back to the request's own scheme and Host. So an MCP client connected through https://slides.example.com/mcp receives https://slides.example.com/app_data/exports/... and https://slides.example.com/presentation?id=..., while REST callers keep relative links. The same function is applied in the sync v1 and v2 handlers and both status endpoints.

docs.title: 10.7 Host and origin protection
docs.text: mcp.run_async(..., host_origin_protection=True, allowed_hosts=MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS, allowed_origins=get_mcp_allowed_origins()) (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:457) enables FastMCP's DNS-rebinding guard. Allowed browser origins are http(s)://localhost:*, http(s)://127.0.0.1:*, http(s)://[::1]:*, plus the origin of PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL when set (servers/fastapi/mcp_server.py:128). Set PRESENTON_PUBLIC_URL if a browser-based MCP client on your public domain needs to connect.

docs.title: 10.8 Worked example: MCP client configuration
docs.text:
From the README, in VS Code's .vscode/mcp.json format; any Streamable HTTP client takes the same URL and header:

{
  "servers": {
    "presenton": {
      "url": "http://localhost:5001/mcp",
      "type": "http",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer sk-presenton-0123456789abcdef.REPLACE_WITH_SECRET"
      }
    }
  },
  "inputs": []
}

A typical agent session then runs upload_files (optional), list_templates (optional), start_standard_presentation, and get_job_status until status is completed, reading the absolute data.path and data.edit_path from the final result.

docs.title: Step 11: Keeping openai_spec.json in sync
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json is a committed, minified copy of the FastAPI OpenAPI document (about 144 KB, OpenAPI 3.1.0, 93 paths). It is produced by:

servers/fastapi/scripts/generate_openapi_spec.py
"""Regenerate the static OpenAPI document consumed by the MCP server."""

import json
from pathlib import Path

from api.main import app


OUTPUT_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "openai_spec.json"


def main() -> None:
    OUTPUT_PATH.write_text(
        json.dumps(app.openapi(), separators=(",", ":")),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The script does not add its parent directory to sys.path (unlike warm_fastembed_cache.py), so run it from servers/fastapi as a module, python -m scripts.generate_openapi_spec, or with PYTHONPATH=.; importing api.main executes the app's module-level setup, so the environment must be able to import the app. Several routes set explicit operation_ids (generate_smart_presentation_async, mcp_files_upload, mcp_template_upload, template_list) precisely so the MCP_TOOL_NAMES keys stay stable; the others rely on FastAPI's generated ids such as generate_presentation_async_api_v1_ppt_presentation_generate_async_post. Unit tests read the committed file to assert template-related operation ids and schemas (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_mcp_openapi_templates.py:28).

Gotcha

The MCP server never asks the live app for its schema. If you add a field to GeneratePresentationRequest or rename a route and forget to regenerate openai_spec.json, MCP clients keep seeing the old tool schema, and a renamed operation id silently drops out of MCP_TOOL_NAMES (keeping its long generated name) or out of the route maps entirely. Regenerate the file and restart the MCP process after any API change.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Programs authenticate with sk-presenton-<id>.<secret> bearer keys that act as one user; the middleware mints an internal session JWT so the export browser can render the deck as that user.
  • GeneratePresentationRequest has 14 fields with the defaults tabulated above; validation errors are 400s with fixed messages, and trigger_webhook is inert.
  • Sync and async Standard generation share generate_presentation_handler; async progress lives in an async_tasks row with only pending, completed and error, carries presentation_id from the start and path / edit_path at the end, and is failed with a 503-style error on restart.
  • Smart generation is exposed under /api/v2 with its own request model, commits the presentation first, parses its own SSE stream, and sends no webhooks.
  • Webhooks are owner-scoped, single-attempt, unsigned POSTs carrying a bearer secret, fired for every Standard generation.
  • The MCP server is FastMCP built from the committed openai_spec.json, exposing at most seven tools gated by PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE, exchanging API keys for one-hour session cookies, and returning absolute links.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Turn from how decks are requested to what they are made of: Template v2 format describes the layout JSON every Standard deck is built from.

docs.title: Template v2 format
docs.text: Reads: templates/general/template.json, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py, servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py, servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py, layouts.json · Builds on: Data model · Time: ~35 min

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text: Every slide Presenton generates is a copy of a "Template v2" layout with some values swapped out. This chapter specifies that format field by field, from the Pydantic models that validate it and from the 16 template bundles that ship in the repository. You will learn the top-level template.json keys, how layouts, components and elements nest inside a 1280 x 720 canvas, every element type and property, the decorative/name/limit flags that turn an element into a content field, and how the same data is stored in the template_v2 table. The chapter ends with the inventory of built-in templates and an explanation of the stray layouts.json file at the repository root.

docs.title: Step 1: One template, three shapes
docs.text:
A Template v2 template exists in three places during its life, and the shape changes slightly between them. Keep this map in mind; the rest of the chapter refers back to it.

flowchart LR
    A["templates/NAME/template.json plus static/ (on disk)"] -->|"import_default_templates_on_startup"| B["template_v2 row (database)"]
    P["Uploaded PPTX"] -->|"certification passes, chapter 18"| B
    B -->|"_copy_template_layout_payload"| C["presentations.layout (one copy per deck)"]
    C -->|"_template_slide_ui plus hydration"| D["slides.ui (one layout per slide)"]
Shape Where layouts merged_components Fonts, icons, thumbnail Bundle templates/<name>/template.json bare list bare list top-level fonts, icon_type, thumbnail Row template_v2 table {"layouts": [...]} {"components": [...]} inside the assets JSON column Deck presentations.layout {"layouts": [...], "icon_type", "icon_weight", "name", "template_id"} not copied presentations.fonts Slide slides.ui one layout object not copied not copied

The wrapping happens in _coerce_slide_layouts and _coerce_merged_components (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:202 and :210), which accept either a bare list or an already wrapped object. The deck copy is built by _copy_template_layout_payload (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:232). Chapter 17 walks through those transitions; this chapter is about the data itself.

docs.title: Step 2: The top-level template.json keys
docs.text:
Each bundle directory contains one template.json and a static/ folder of assets. Here is the head of the General bundle and its last two keys, verbatim (the 17,000 lines of merged_components and layouts in between are elided):

templates/general/template.json (excerpt)
{
  "id": "general",
  "name": "General",
  "description": "General template best for simple presentations, great spacing and clean layout.",
  "thumbnail": "static/thumbnail.png",
  "merged_components": [
  // ...
  "layouts": [
  // ...
  "fonts": {
    "Poppins": "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:ital,wght@0,400;0,700;1,400&display=swap"
  },
  "theme": {
    "colors": {
      "primary": "#3B82F6",
      "background": "#9333EA",
      "card": "#FFFFFF",
      "stroke": "#E5E7EB",
      "primary_text": "#111827",
      "background_text": "#FFFFFF",
      "graph_0": "#EF4444",
      // ... graph_1 to graph_9
    },
    "fonts": {
      "textFont": {
        "name": "Poppins",
        "url": "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:wght@100..900&display=swap"
      }
    }
  }
}

The keys, what validates them, and where they end up:

Key Type Required Validation at import Stored as id string no stripped; falls back to the directory name; must not contain / or \ (default_templates.py:177) template_v2.id (primary key) name string no stripped; falls back to the id (default_templates.py:189) template_v2.name description string no stripped; empty becomes null template_v2.description thumbnail string no static/... rewritten (Step 10) assets.thumbnail icon_type string no normalized to one of bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin; default bold (servers/fastapi/utils/icon_weights.py:5) assets.icon_type and assets.icon_weight merged_components list no MergedComponents Pydantic model template_v2.merged_components layouts list yes SlideLayouts Pydantic model, at least one layout template_v2.layouts fonts object no must be an object, otherwise {} assets.fonts theme object no none at import, stored if it is an object template_v2.theme components object no stored only if it is an object (no bundle uses it) template_v2.components

_load_default_template (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:113) performs exactly these steps:

servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py (excerpt)
def _load_default_template(template_dir: Path) -> TemplateV2:
    template_json_path = template_dir / "template.json"
    raw = json.loads(template_json_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if not isinstance(raw, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"Default template must be a JSON object: {template_json_path}")

    template_id = _read_template_id(raw, template_dir)
    rewritten = _rewrite_static_asset_urls(raw, template_id)

    layouts = _coerce_slide_layouts(rewritten.get("layouts"))
    merged_components = _coerce_merged_components(rewritten.get("merged_components"))
    components = rewritten.get("components")
    theme = rewritten.get("theme")
    assets = _build_assets(rewritten, template_id, layouts, merged_components)
    # ...

Gotcha: the docstring says UUIDs, the data says names

resolve_default_template_id (servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py:62) explains that bundled templates "use UUIDs as database IDs" while clients send the public directory name. In this snapshot every one of the 16 bundles sets "id" equal to its directory name ("general", "momentum", and so on), so the translation is the identity. The code path still matters: if you ship a bundle whose id is a UUID, clients can keep sending the directory name and generation resolves it.

Gotcha: the theme is not validated at import

theme is copied into the row as a raw dict. It is only validated later, as PresentationThemeData, when GET /api/v1/ppt/template/{template_id} builds its response (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:2149). That call does not catch ValidationError, so a malformed theme in a bundle surfaces as a 500 on the template detail endpoint, not at startup. The /theme endpoint is more forgiving: it logs a warning and derives a replacement (chapter 19).

docs.title: Step 3: Layouts and components
docs.text:
A layout is one slide design. A component is a reusable region of that slide. Both are plain Pydantic models in servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py (excerpt)
class Component(BaseModel):
    id: str
    description: str
    position: Position
    elements: list[SlideElement] = Field(min_length=1)

# ...

class SlideLayout(BaseModel):
    id: str
    description: str
    components: list[Component]

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _component_ids_must_be_unique(self) -> "SlideLayout":
        ids = [component.id for component in self.components]
        if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
            raise ValueError("component ids must be unique within a slide layout")
        return self


class SlideLayouts(BaseModel):
    layouts: list[SlideLayout] = Field(min_length=1)
Model Field Rule Source SlideLayout id string, unique across the template layouts.py:98, layouts.py:114 SlideLayout description string; the structure-selection LLM reads it (chapter 17) layouts.py:100 SlideLayout components list; ids unique within the layout layouts.py:101, layouts.py:103 Component id string; becomes the top-level key of the slide's content JSON layouts.py:55 Component description string layouts.py:56 Component position {x, y} on the 1280 x 720 canvas layouts.py:57 Component elements at least one element layouts.py:58 SlideLayouts layouts at least one layout layouts.py:112

There is no size on a component. The model omits it, and the repair prompt sent to the model during layout generation says so explicitly: "Each component must include position and local-coordinate elements. Do not include component size." (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py:1331). The renderer computes a component's extent from its children.

The RawSlideLayout model (layouts.py:44) is the pre-certification shape produced from a PPTX: {id, description, elements} with no components at all. Custom-template creation turns raw layouts into certified layouts (chapter 18).

Layout ids follow two conventions in the bundles. Hand-curated templates such as General use plain structural ids (title_description_image). Templates produced by the certification pipeline carry a random four-digit suffix such as center_title_agenda_grid_wave_7815, added by _with_randomized_layout_ids (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:833), which appends random.randint(1000, 9999).

Gotcha: unknown keys are silently dropped

None of the element or layout models set extra="forbid", so Pydantic ignores fields it does not know. Across the 16 bundles (layouts plus merged components), nine layouts carry a stray layout-level "elements" key (two in General, four in Modern), 126 elements (104 of them text) carry __presenton_manual_position, 22 Editorial groups carry description, 30 vectors in Editorial and Mosaic carry decorative, and two General vectors carry max_length. All of those vanish when the bundle is validated and dumped by _coerce_slide_layouts and _coerce_merged_components. That includes __presenton_manual_position, so the renderer's manual-placement exception (Step 4) never sees the flag on a built-in template row. If you add a new property to the JSON, add it to the Pydantic model too, or it will never reach the database.

docs.title: Step 4: The coordinate system and how positions nest
docs.text:
Layouts use a fixed 1280 x 720 pixel canvas (docs/template-v2.md:159; TEMPLATE_V2_HTML_WIDTH/HEIGHT at servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:153). Positions are always relative to the nearest positioned ancestor:

flowchart TD
    S["Slide canvas 1280 x 720"] --> C["Component: position is absolute on the canvas"]
    C --> E["Element: position is relative to the component"]
    E --> G["group: children positioned relative to the group"]
    E --> K["container: one child, absolute if it has a position, otherwise flowed"]
    E --> F["flex and grid: children are flowed, their positions are ignored"]
    E --> V["vector: no position, its points are in the parent coordinate space"]

The rules come from two places that must agree: the compiler that writes layouts and the renderer that reads them.

  • Component origin. When the certification compiler builds a component, it sets position to the top-left corner of the union bounds of the component's source elements, then subtracts that offset from each element (_localize_top_level_element, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py:3050, and the position assignment at :2998).
  • Components render as groups. renderItem treats any record with an elements array and no known element type as a component and renders it as a group whose children are its elements (servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:308).
  • Groups position children absolutely. renderGroup renders every child in "absolute" mode, which emits left/top from the child's position (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:839 and frameStyleFromBox at :3209).
  • Containers choose per child. renderContainer renders its single child absolutely when the child has a position, otherwise in flow mode inside a flexbox that honors alignment and padding (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:485).
  • Flex and grid flow their children. Children render in "flow" mode (position: relative, no left/top) and are laid out by the shared flow engine (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:534, :777). The one exception is a child flagged __presenton_manual_position, which the flow engine treats as manually placed (htmlFlowLayoutDeps, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:583).
  • Vectors have no position. readBox derives a vector's box from the minimum and maximum of its points (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3221, polygonBox at :3413), so the points themselves are coordinates in the parent's space. The compiler shifts vector points rather than a position when it localizes them (certified_generation.py:3061).

In Step 7 you will see the consequence: in a component placed at (672, 199.47), a divider whose points run from (0, 144) to (80, 148) is drawn at canvas coordinates (672, 343.47) to (752, 347.47).

docs.title: Step 5: The element catalog
docs.text:
Every element is a member of one discriminated union, keyed by type:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt)
SlideElement: TypeAlias = Annotated[
    Union[
        Text,
        Container,
        Image,
        TextList,
        Table,
        Vector,
        Chart,
        Infographic,
        Flex,
        Grid,
        Group,
    ],
    Field(discriminator="type"),
]

The table below lists all eleven types, which schema fields each carries, and how often each appears across the 383 layouts of the 16 bundles (counted by walking every component, including nested children).

type Model decorative name Limit fields Count in bundles text Text (elements.py:203) required required max_length, min_length 3,623 image Image (elements.py:240) required required none (is_icon required) 2,251 group Group (elements.py:611) absent required none 2,038 flex Flex (elements.py:567) absent required max_children, min_children 1,132 vector Vector (elements.py:342) absent optional none 733 container Container (elements.py:224) absent absent none 255 chart Chart (elements.py:361) required required none 113 infographic Infographic (elements.py:549) required required none 51 grid Grid (elements.py:589) absent required max_children, min_children 45 text-list TextList (elements.py:265) required required max_items, min_items, max_item_length, min_item_length 35 table Table (elements.py:302) required required max_columns, min_columns, max_rows, min_rows 7

docs.title: 5.1 Shared geometry
docs.text: Every type except vector has optional position ({x, y}, floats) and size ({width, height}, floats). Almost every type has rotation (degrees), flip_h and flip_v. The renderer turns them into one CSS transform, rotate(...) scaleX(-1) scaleY(-1) with transform-origin:center (transformStyle, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3478).

docs.title: 5.2 Style primitives
docs.text:
Model Fields Source Font size, family, color, bold, italic, underline, line_height, letter_spacing, ellipsis, opacity (all optional) elements.py:126 Alignment horizontal in left, center, right, justify; vertical in top, middle, bottom elements.py:121 Fill color (required), opacity elements.py:139 Stroke color, width (required); opacity, dash (list of floats), line_cap (butt/round/square), line_join (bevel/miter/round), start_marker, end_marker elements.py:150 StrokeMarker type in arrow, diamond, open, oval, stealth, triangle; length and width in sm, med, lg elements.py:144 Shadow color (required), blur, opacity, offset_x, offset_y elements.py:168 BorderRadius tl, tr, bl, br (all required) elements.py:161 Padding top, right, bottom, left (all required) elements.py:114

line_height is read two ways downstream: values above 2 are treated as pixels, values up to 2 as a multiple of the font size (_text_capacity_geometry, certified_generation.py:2499, and the same rule in _table_cell_typography, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:152).

docs.title: 5.3 text
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt)
class TextRun(BaseModel):
    text: str
    font: Optional[Font] = None
    # ... rejects any "type" other than None or "text"

class LatexTextRun(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["latex"]
    latex: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=4000)
    display_mode: bool = False
    font: Optional[Font] = None

# ...

class Text(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["text"]
    position: Optional[Position] = None
    size: Optional[Size] = None
    # ... rotation, flip_h, flip_v
    font: Optional[Font] = None
    alignment: Optional[Alignment] = None
    fill: Optional[Fill] = None
    stroke: Optional[Stroke] = None
    shadow: Optional[Shadow] = None
    runs: list[TextRunValue]

    # Schema
    decorative: bool
    name: str
    max_length: int
    min_length: int

A text element has an element-level font and a list of runs, each with its own optional font. The renderer merges them per run ({...font, ...run.font}, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:399), so a run only needs to carry what differs. In the bundles, runs usually repeat the full font. A run can instead be a LaTeX run ({"type": "latex", "latex": "...", "display_mode": false}, up to 4,000 characters), which the HTML renderer typesets with KaTeX (chapter 17). fill, stroke and shadow on a text element style the box, not the glyphs; a shadow becomes a CSS text-shadow (textShadowStyle, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3460).

max_length and min_length are character counts. They become maxLength/minLength in the content schema the LLM must satisfy (chapter 17). Certification computes them from geometry: characters per line times line count, multiplied by a 0.85 safety factor, never below the current text length (_estimated_text_capacity, certified_generation.py:2375, TEXT_CAPACITY_SAFETY_FACTOR at :62).

docs.title: 5.4 image
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt)
class Image(BaseModel):  # Konva Image
    type: Literal["image"]
    # ... position, size, rotation, flip_h, flip_v
    opacity: Optional[float] = None
    data: str
    fit: Optional[ImageFit] = None
    focus_x: Optional[float] = None
    focus_y: Optional[float] = None
    crop_scale: Optional[float] = None
    border_radius: Optional[BorderRadius] = None
    clip_path: Optional[str] = None
    color: Optional[str] = None

    # Schema
    decorative: bool
    name: str
    prompt: Optional[str] = None
    is_icon: bool
    icon_type: Optional[IconType] = None
Field Meaning data URL of the image. Replaceable images hold a placeholder: /static/images/replaceable_template_image.png for photos, /static/icons/placeholder.svg for icons (certified_generation.py:63). Decorative images keep their real asset URL. fit contain, cover or fill. The HTML renderer defaults to contain when it is missing (imageFit, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3980). focus_x, focus_y Percentages (0 to 100) for CSS object-position (imageFocusValue, :4008). crop_scale Zoom factor clamped to 1 to 6, applied as a CSS scale() around the focus point (imageCropScale, :3989). border_radius Per-corner radius. clip_path A CSS clip-path. Only path, polygon, circle, ellipse and inset functions pass the sanitizer (normalizeCssClipPath, :4026). color Icon tint. When color is set and is_icon is true, the renderer draws the icon as a CSS mask filled with that color (renderImage, :357). opacity Element opacity. prompt The prompt or icon query that produced the current data, written back during hydration (chapter 17). is_icon Distinguishes a searchable icon from a photo or illustration. It changes the generated content field from image_prompt to icon_query. icon_type Icon style: bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin.

docs.title: 5.5 text-list
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt)
class TextList(BaseModel):  # Konva Group
    type: Literal["text-list"]
    # ... position, size, rotation, flip_h, flip_v
    font: Optional[Font] = None
    marker: Optional[Marker] = None
    gap: Optional[float] = None
    marker_gap: Optional[float] = None
    items: list[list[TextRunValue]]

    # Schema
    decorative: bool
    name: str
    max_items: int
    min_items: int
    max_item_length: int
    min_item_length: int

items is a list of items, each item a list of runs. marker is bullet, number or none. gap is the vertical space between items in pixels and marker_gap the horizontal space between the marker and the text. The limits bound both the number of items and the characters per item.

docs.title: 5.6 table
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt)
class TableCell(BaseModel):
    color: Optional[Fill] = None
    font: Optional[Font] = None
    alignment: Optional[HorizontalAlignment] = None
    borders: Optional[TableCellBorders] = None
    runs: List[TextRunValue]


class Table(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["table"]
    # ... position, size, rotation, flip_h, flip_v
    columns: list[TableCell]
    rows: list[list[TableCell]]

    # Schema
    decorative: bool
    name: str
    max_columns: int
    min_columns: int
    max_rows: int
    min_rows: int

columns is the header row; rows are the body rows. A cell's background is its color (a Fill), and borders holds an optional Stroke per side (TableCellBorders, elements.py:287). The renderer treats row 0 as the header and bolds it unless the cell sets bold explicitly (tableCellStyle, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3559). The certification compiler insists that every body row has exactly as many cells as columns (certified_generation.py:3539).

docs.title: 5.7 vector: polygons and ellipses
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt)
class VectorCurve(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["smooth"]
    tension: Optional[float] = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=1)
    segments: Optional[int] = Field(default=16, ge=1, le=96)


class Vector(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["vector"]
    name: Optional[str] = None
    shape: Optional[VectorShape] = None
    points: list[Position] = Field(min_length=2)
    closed: Optional[bool] = None
    curve: Optional[VectorCurve] = None
    corner_radii: Optional[list[Annotated[float, Field(ge=0)]]] = None
    start_marker: Optional[VectorMarker] = None
    end_marker: Optional[VectorMarker] = None
    # ... rotation, flip_h, flip_v
    opacity: Optional[float] = None
    fill: Optional[Fill] = None
    stroke: Optional[Stroke] = None
    shadow: Optional[Shadow] = None

Vectors replace the older rectangle/line types (you will see those in layouts.json, Step 12). The fields:

  • shape is polygon (default) or ellipse. An ellipse is drawn inside the bounding box of its points, so two opposite corners are enough (renderEllipseVector, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:1019).
  • points needs at least two entries. With two points and closed unset it is an open line; with three or more it is closed unless closed is false (polygonClosed, :3403).
  • corner_radii lists one radius per vertex; the renderer rounds each corner with a quadratic curve, capping the radius at half of each adjacent edge (roundedPolygonPoints, :3307).
  • curve: {"type": "smooth"} resamples the outline as a Hermite spline; tension defaults to 0.4 in the renderer and segments to 16, clamped to 1 to 96 (curveSettings, :3336).
  • start_marker/end_marker (none, arrow, stealth, triangle, circle, square, diamond) only render on open paths. Markers can also sit on the stroke, where the PPTX names oval and open map to circle and arrow (vectorMarker, :946).
  • fill applies to closed shapes only. An open path without a stroke color is drawn in black (renderPolygon, :863).

Vectors have no decorative flag and no content schema: they are always fixed artwork.

docs.title: 5.8 chart
docs.text:
Chart (elements.py:361) carries the chart type, the data, and its styling:

Group Fields Type chart_type: bar, horizontal_bar, line, area, pie, donut, stacked_bar, horizontal_stacked_bar, scatter, radar, polar_area (ChartType, elements.py:76) Data categories (list of strings), series (list of {name, values}), source Text title, x_axis_title, y_axis_title Colors colors (palette in renderer order), title_color, legend_color, text_color, axis_color, grid_color Toggles x_axis, y_axis, x_axis_grid, y_axis_grid, legend, legend_position (left/right/top/bottom), data_labels (base/mid/top/outside)

Three validators run on every chart. Pie and donut charts keep only their first series (elements.py:395). A legacy boolean data_labels: true becomes "top" and false becomes null (:405). An explicit size smaller than 80 x 60 pixels is rejected (:418).

docs.title: 5.9 infographic
docs.text:
servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py (excerpt)
InfographicData = Annotated[
    Union[
        ProgressBarInfographicData,
        GaugeInfographicData,
        StructuralInfographicData,
    ],
    Field(discriminator="type"),
]


class Infographic(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["infographic"]
    # ... position, size, rotation, flip_h, flip_v
    data: InfographicData

    # Design
    colors: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    text_color: Optional[str] = None

    # Schema
    decorative: bool
    name: str

InfographicType (elements.py:427) enumerates 27 kinds. Two are metrics with a strict shape (extra="forbid"): progress_bar and gauge, each {type, min_value, max_value, value} with max_value > min_value (elements.py:464, :479). The other 25 (gantt, timeline, roadmap, milestone_timeline, staircase, supply_chain, stair_step_blocks, maturity_model, pillar_framework, transformation_hub, diagonal_circles, risk_matrix, chevron_process, radial_cycle, conversion_funnel, vertical_funnel, pyramid, segmented_wheel, customer_journey, before_after, impact_effort_matrix, comparison_matrix, org_chart, decision_tree, mind_map) are "structural": the model allows extra keys and normalizes them through normalize_infographic_data in servers/fastapi/utils/infographic_catalog.py (elements.py:523). For metrics, colors[0] is the track and colors[1] the filled value (infographicBaseColor/infographicHighlightColor, template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3037). In the bundles the 51 infographics are 26 gauges, 19 progress bars, two timelines, two vertical funnels, one maturity model and one staircase.

docs.title: 5.10 container
docs.text: Container (elements.py:224) is a styled box around exactly one optional child: fill, stroke, border_radius, shadow, padding and alignment. It has no name and no decorative, so it is pure layout; any content lives in its child.

docs.title: 5.11 flex, grid and group: flexible and repeated regions
docs.text:
These three types are how a template expresses "this region holds a variable number of items".

Type Layout fields Schema fields Behavior flex direction (row/column, required), wrap, align_items, justify_content (flex-start, flex-end, center, stretch), gap, column_gap, row_gap, children name, max_children, min_children One-dimensional flow. grid columns (required), rows, gap, column_gap, row_gap, align_items, justify_items, children name, max_children, min_children Two-dimensional flow. group children name Free placement; children keep absolute positions.

When all children of a flex or grid expose the same editable fields, the content schema turns the region into an array whose length is bounded by min_children and max_children (chapter 17). A group whose children repeat becomes an array bounded by half to all of its items. The certification compiler sets min_children to max(1, (n + 1) // 2) for a repeated region of n items and to n for a fixed one, with max_children = n (certified_generation.py:3301).

docs.title: Step 6: The schema flags
docs.text:
Three kinds of fields decide whether an element is content or decoration.

decorative is the switch. Only elements with decorative: false whose type is one of text, image, text-list, table, chart or infographic become fields in the content schema (CONTENT_TYPES and _is_editable_element, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:15 and :53). Everything else is copied untouched into every slide. In the bundles, 3,584 of 3,623 text elements and 607 of 2,251 images are editable; all charts, tables, text lists and infographics are editable.

name is the field's key in the content JSON. Names are lowercase snake case; the semantic certification pass enforces ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and at most 80 characters (SemanticElementAnnotation.name, layouts.py:128). For flex, grid and group, the name becomes the key of the nested object or array.

Limit pairs (min_length/max_length, min_items/max_items, min_item_length/max_item_length, min_columns/max_columns, min_rows/max_rows, min_children/max_children) bound the generated content. Certification refuses negative limits and a minimum above its maximum (_certify_element_tree, certified_generation.py:3531).

Gotcha: the min-equals-half rule is defined but not enforced

elements.py opens with _validate_min_max, which raises unless a minimum equals half of its maximum, rounded up (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:13). Nothing calls it. The "half rounded up" convention is applied by the generators instead (for example (len(columns) + 1) // 2 for tables at certified_generation.py:1513), and the bundles do not follow it everywhere: the General title has min_length: 8, max_length: 25. Do not rely on the relation when you read or hand-edit templates.

docs.title: Step 8: merged_components
docs.text:
merged_components is a catalog of interchangeable component variants collected from all layouts:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py (excerpt)
class MergedComponent(BaseModel):
    id: str
    description: str
    variants: list[Component] = Field(min_length=1)


class MergedComponents(BaseModel):
    components: list[MergedComponent]

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _component_ids_must_be_unique(self) -> "MergedComponents":
        ids = [component.id for component in self.components]
        if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
            raise ValueError("merged component ids must be unique")
        return self

Each entry groups full Component objects (with position and elements) that can stand in for one another. In General, the first group, background_canvas, holds the white full-slide rectangles from several layouts as separate variants. The catalog is produced by an LLM clustering pass plus a structural de-duplication step during custom-template creation (chapter 18).

The generation pipeline never reads merged_components. It is consumed by three side features: prompted layout generation passes up to eight matching groups to the model as reusable components (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py:726), the chat assistant turns them into insertable block candidates (servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:2905), and the template editor offers them as insertable blocks (chapter 18).

Gotcha: variants are copies, not references

A variant is a full copy of a component, not a pointer into layouts. Editing a layout does not update its variant, and scripts/convert-presentation-template.mjs exists precisely to push edited slide UIs back into both layouts and the matching variants by deep equality (chapter 18). If you hand-edit a bundle, edit both places.

docs.title: Step 9: The fonts and theme blocks
docs.text:
fonts maps a display family name to a URL: {"Montserrat Semi-Bold": "static/Montserrat SemiBold.ttf", ...}. A URL is either a bundle-relative static/... font file or a Google Fonts CSS URL. The bundles mix both: Civic ships six local font files, General only a Google Fonts URL for Poppins. Template fonts are stored as assets.fonts and later copied into presentations.fonts.

theme has the shape of PresentationThemeData (servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py:32): a colors object with exactly 16 roles (primary, background, card, stroke, background_text, primary_text, graph_0 to graph_9) and fonts.textFont: {name, url}. The theme is a semantic summary of the template's palette; layouts do not reference it, every element carries literal colors.

Gotcha: Google Fonts URLs in bundles are never fetched

A test asserts that runtime frontend code never loads fonts.googleapis.com (servers/nextjs/local-font-loading-validation.test.mjs:26). The browser-side font loader ignores any URL that is not a font file and maps the family name to the vendored copy in servers/nextjs/public/vendor/fonts instead. A Google Fonts URL in a bundle is therefore only a hint; if the family is missing from the vendored catalog, the text falls back to another font. Chapter 19 covers the font pipeline.

docs.title: Step 10: From bundle to row
docs.text:
import_default_templates_on_startup (walked through in chapter 17) turns each bundle into a TemplateV2 row. The columns, from servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py:16:

Column Type Built-in bundle value Custom template value id string PK, default uuid4() bundle id UUID owner_id UUID FK to user.id, nullable, cascade delete null creating user name, description string from bundle from request or PPTX file name raw_layouts JSON null PPTX-to-JSON output, {"layouts": [...]} components JSON null (unused) null merged_components JSON {"components": [...]} from clustering layouts JSON {"layouts": [...]} certified layouts theme JSON bundle theme generated theme assets JSON see below see chapter 18 is_default bool true false created_at, updated_at timestamptz set on insert / update same

Two rewrites happen before validation:

servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py (excerpt)
def _rewrite_static_asset_url(value: str, template_id: str) -> str:
    if not value.startswith("static/"):
        return value

    relative = PurePosixPath(value)
    if relative.is_absolute() or ".." in relative.parts:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid default template static asset path: {value}")
    return f"/app_data/templates/{template_id}/{relative.as_posix()}"

Every string anywhere in the JSON that starts with static/ (image data, thumbnail, font URLs, even theme.fonts.textFont.url) is rewritten to /app_data/templates/<id>/static/..., and the bundle's static/ folder is copied to $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/templates/<id>/static (default_templates.py:295). Strings that start with /static/ (with a leading slash), such as the image placeholder, are left alone because they are FastAPI's own static files.

_build_assets (default_templates.py:220) then assembles:

{
  "template_id": "general",
  "icon_type": "bold",
  "icon_weight": "bold",
  "fonts": {"Poppins": "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:ital,wght@0,400;0,700;1,400&display=swap"},
  "images": ["/static/images/replaceable_template_image.png", "/app_data/templates/general/static/image2-ec1c92dee7a3.png"],
  "thumbnail": "/app_data/templates/general/static/thumbnail.png"
}

The images list holds every distinct image data value found in layouts and merged_components (_collect_image_urls, default_templates.py:267); the two values shown are the first two real entries, and the full list for General has 18.

Directory and id Name Layouts Merged groups Icon type Theme text font Static files civic Civic 29 38 regular Montserrat 87 dynamic Dynamic 32 40 bold (absent) Montserrat 23 editorial Editorial 24 9 thin DM Sans Bold 116 executive Executive 32 47 bold (absent) Montserrat Bold 20 general General 12 15 bold (absent) Poppins 17 horizon Horizon 28 29 regular Poppins 84 landmark Landmark 27 17 regular Poppins 123 modern Modern 10 19 bold Montserrat 1 momentum Momentum 28 27 bold (absent) Lato 33 mosaic Mosaic 34 67 regular Montserrat 108 nova Nova 28 26 regular Poppins 102 pulse Pulse 28 20 regular Inter 1 114 signal Signal 24 20 regular Inter 1 98 standard Standard 11 19 bold Playfair Display 3 swift Swift 9 20 bold Inter 3 verdant Verdant 27 31 regular DM Sans 70 Total 383 444

Gotcha: bundles are authoritative and read-only

Built-in rows are overwritten from disk on every start, their static folder is deleted and recopied, and rows for bundles that no longer exist are deleted along with their assets (default_templates.py:142, :154, :305). The API refuses to edit or delete them with 403 Built-in templates are read-only (_require_private_template, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:2170). To change a built-in template, edit its bundle and restart.

docs.title: Step 12: layouts.json at the repository root
docs.text:
The repository root contains a 252 KB layouts.json. Its shape is a doubly wrapped layout list, {"layouts": {"layouts": [...]}}, holding 14 layouts with ids such as business_proposal_cover_layout, content_index_slide and slide_14_component_layout. It predates the current element union:

Feature in layouts.json Current format rectangle (46 elements) and line (3) types replaced by vector size on components not part of Component chart fields data, color, label_color, show_values replaced by categories, series, colors, text_color, data_labels image URLs such as http://127.0.0.1:8000/app_data/pptx-to-json/<session>/images/... bundle-relative static/... paths

A search of the whole repository (excluding node_modules and this tutorial) finds no file that reads or references layouts.json: no Python module, no Next.js code, no script, no test, no Dockerfile. It was added in the commit "feat: template v2 rendering issues fix and adds ui in slide model to save the layout edits" and looks like a development artifact from an earlier PPTX conversion. It would not validate against SlideLayouts today, because rectangle and line are not members of the SlideElement union. Treat it as a historical sample, not as a reference.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• A template is a list of layouts; a layout is a list of components with canvas positions; a component is a list of elements whose positions are local to it, on a fixed 1280 x 720 canvas.
  • There are eleven element types. Six of them (text, image, text-list, table, chart, infographic) can be content; flex, grid and group define fixed or repeatable regions; vector and container are always structure.
  • decorative: false plus a name turns an element into a schema field, and the min/max pairs bound what the LLM may write.
  • Bundles store layouts and merged components as bare lists, static/ paths and loose top-level keys; the database row wraps the lists and moves fonts, icon type and thumbnail into assets.
  • Unknown JSON keys are dropped on import, the theme is unvalidated until it is served, and built-in templates are rewritten from disk at every start.
  • layouts.json at the repository root uses an obsolete element vocabulary and has no consumers.
