docs.title: From template to schema to slide
docs.text: Reads: servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py, servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/content.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py, servers/fastapi/utils/ppt_utils.py, servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx · Builds on: Template v2 format · Time: ~45 min

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
This chapter follows one layout through its whole life: imported from a bundle at startup, stored as a row, turned into a JSON Schema the LLM has to fill, chosen for a slide, filled with generated content, hydrated back into a renderable layout tree, and finally drawn as HTML in the browser. You will see the schema builder's rules for every element type (including repeated regions and the length limits), the exact hydration algorithm that writes content back into elements, and every branch of the HTML renderer. A worked example runs a real General layout through the real schema builder and hydrator.

flowchart TD
    A["templates/NAME/template.json"] -->|"Step 1: startup import"| B["template_v2 row"]
    B -->|"Step 3: copy layouts"| C["presentations.layout payload"]
    C -->|"Step 4: get_template_schema"| D["SlideLayoutModel list with json_schema"]
    D -->|"Step 5: structure selection LLM"| E["one layout index per outline slide"]
    E -->|"Step 6: slide content LLM"| F["slides.content JSON"]
    F -->|"Step 8: process_slides adds image_url"| G["content with asset URLs"]
    C -->|"_template_slide_ui"| H["slides.ui = deep copy of the chosen layout"]
    G --> I["Step 9: _apply_template_content_to_ui"]
    H --> I
    I --> J["hydrated slides.ui"]
    J -->|"Step 10: templateV2UiToHtmlFragment"| K["HTML preview"]

docs.title: Step 1: Importing the built-in templates at startup
docs.text:
The FastAPI lifespan calls import_default_templates_on_startup() after migrations, admin bootstrap and the cleanup of interrupted tasks (servers/fastapi/api/lifespan.py:64). The function is short enough to read in full:

servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py (excerpt)
async def import_default_templates_on_startup(
    templates_root: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    root = templates_root or _default_templates_root()
    if not root.is_dir():
        LOGGER.info("Default templates directory not found: %s", root)
        return

    template_dirs = [
        path
        for path in sorted(root.iterdir())
        if path.is_dir() and (path / "template.json").is_file()
    ]
    # ...
    async with async_session_maker() as session:
        imported_template_ids: set[str] = set()
        for template_dir in template_dirs:
            template = _load_default_template(template_dir)
            imported_template_ids.add(template.id)
            existing = await session.get(TemplateV2, template.id)

            _copy_default_template_static_assets(template_dir, template.id)
            if existing:
                _update_template_from_default(existing, template)
                session.add(existing)
                # ...
            else:
                session.add(template)
                # ...
            await session.commit()

        await _remove_stale_default_templates(session, imported_template_ids)

Step by step:

  1. Find the bundles. The root is Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "templates" (default_templates.py:58), which resolves to the repository-level templates/ directory. Every subdirectory with a template.json is a bundle, processed in alphabetical order.
  2. Load and validate. _load_default_template reads the JSON, rewrites static/... strings to /app_data/templates/<id>/static/..., validates layouts through SlideLayouts and merged_components through MergedComponents (dropping unknown keys), and assembles assets (chapter 16, Step 10). The row is built with raw_layouts=None and is_default=True (default_templates.py:128).
  3. Copy static assets. _copy_default_template_static_assets deletes $APP_DATA_DIRECTORY/templates/<id>/static and copies the bundle's static/ folder in its place. It raises RuntimeError("APP_DATA_DIRECTORY must be set to import default templates") if the variable is missing (default_templates.py:295).
  4. Upsert. An existing row has every content column overwritten (_update_template_from_default, default_templates.py:142); otherwise the new row is inserted. Each template is committed on its own.
  5. Remove stale defaults. Any is_default row whose id was not seen in this run is deleted, and its templates/<id> asset directory removed (default_templates.py:154, :310).

Built-in rows have owner_id = NULL, because no user context exists during startup. They are still visible to everyone: the session-level loader criteria for TemplateV2 admit rows that belong to the current owner or rows with owner_id IS NULL AND is_default IS TRUE (servers/fastapi/services/database.py:87). User-created templates are stamped with the creator's id on flush (services/database.py:100). Chapter 25 covers the ownership model.

Gotcha: one broken bundle stops the server

The loop has no try/except. A template.json that fails SlideLayouts validation, a static/../ path, or an id containing a slash raises out of the lifespan, and FastAPI does not start. The unit tests test_bundled_general_template_json_matches_template_v2_shapes and test_new_bundled_templates_load_with_layouts_and_assets (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_default_templates.py:363, :382) exist to catch this before release; run them after editing a bundle.

docs.title: Step 2: The row that comes out
docs.text:
After the import, a template is a template_v2 row (servers/fastapi/models/sql/template_v2.py:16). The columns that matter for generation are:

Column Used for id lookup key; also written into every slide's layout_group layouts {"layouts": [...]}; the source of both the schemas and the slide UIs assets.fonts copied to presentations.fonts assets.icon_type the icon weight used when searching icons for this deck theme wrapped and copied to presentations.theme on the API path (chapter 19) raw_layouts, merged_components not used by generation

Clients name templates either by id or, for built-ins, by directory name. resolve_default_template_id maps a directory name to the id stored in its template.json, after rejecting ., .. and any name containing / or \ (default_templates.py:62).

docs.title: Step 3: Resolving a template for a deck
docs.text:
Two endpoints resolve a template into a layout payload. The UI path, POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/prepare, uses _resolve_prepare_layout (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1448), which strips an optional custom- prefix and looks the id up directly, returning 404 Template layout not found on a miss. The API path, POST /api/v1/ppt/presentation/generate, uses _resolve_generation_layout (presentation.py:262), which also accepts bundled directory names and answers 503 with "Restart the service to import bundled templates." when a bundle exists on disk but its row is missing.

Both end in _copy_template_layout_payload:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
def _copy_template_layout_payload(
    template: TemplateV2,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    layout_payload = copy.deepcopy(template.layouts)
    if not isinstance(layout_payload, dict):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Template layout JSON must be an object",
        )

    icon_type = _template_icon_type(template, layout_payload)
    layout_payload["icon_type"] = icon_type
    layout_payload["icon_weight"] = icon_type
    layout_payload["name"] = _template_reference(template.id)
    layout_payload["template_id"] = template.id
    return layout_payload

This payload is stored in presentations.layout. From here on the deck is independent of the template row's layouts: later edits to the template do not change existing decks. _template_icon_type checks assets, then the payload, then layouts, and keeps the first value that is not the default bold (presentation.py:250).

docs.title: Step 4: Layouts become SlideLayoutModels
docs.text:
The LLM never sees layout JSON. It sees one JSON Schema per layout, carried by two small models:

servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py (excerpt)
class SlideLayoutModel(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    json_schema: dict


class PresentationLayoutModel(BaseModel):
    name: str
    ordered: bool = Field(default=False)
    icon_type: str = Field(default=DEFAULT_ICON_TYPE)
    icon_weight: str = Field(default=DEFAULT_ICON_TYPE)
    slides: List[SlideLayoutModel]

_build_template_layout_model (presentation.py:410) produces them:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
    try:
        template_schema = get_template_schema(layout_payload)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=f"Invalid template layout JSON: {exc}",
        ) from exc
    # ...
    for index, schema_layout in enumerate(template_schema["layouts"]):
        # ...
        layout_id = (
            schema_layout.get("layout_id")
            or source_layout.get("id")
            or f"layout_{index + 1}"
        )
        layout_schema = schema_layout.get("schema")
        if not isinstance(layout_schema, dict):
            layout_schema = {
                "title": str(layout_id),
                "description": source_layout.get("description"),
            }

        slides.append(
            SlideLayoutModel(
                id=str(layout_id),
                name=source_layout.get("name") or layout_schema.get("title"),
                description=source_layout.get("description")
                or layout_schema.get("description"),
                json_schema=layout_schema,
            )
        )

ordered is always False for templates (presentation.py:467), so an LLM always chooses the layout for each slide. A layout with no editable elements still gets a model, with a stub schema containing only title and description; the content call for such a slide is skipped (Step 6). The same builder runs again when a prepared deck is streamed (_get_presentation_stream_layout, presentation.py:1435), so schemas are always regenerated from the stored payload rather than cached.

docs.title: Step 5: The schema builder
docs.text:
get_template_schema (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:257) returns {"source_file", "layout_count", "layouts": [{"slide", "layout_id", "schema"}]}. Each layout schema is assembled by _template_layout_schema (schema.py:585), one property per component that has at least one editable field:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py (excerpt)
    schema = None
    if properties:
        schema = {
            "$schema": JSON_SCHEMA_URI,
            "type": "object",
            "title": layout.get("id") or f"slide_{slide_index}",
            "description": layout.get("description"),
            "additionalProperties": False,
            "properties": properties,
            "required": required,
        }

    return {
        "slide": slide_index,
        "layout_id": layout.get("id"),
        "schema": schema,
    }

docs.title: 5.1 Component keys
docs.text: Each component's schema comes from get_component_schema (schema.py:192). The key under which it is placed is the component id. When the same id occurs more than once in a layout, the keys become id_0, id_1, and so on (_template_component_key, schema.py:671); the hydrator computes the same keys with _template_component_content_keys (presentation.py:538) so the two stay in sync. Within a component, a second field with the same name becomes name_2, then name_3 (_component_add_schema_property, schema.py:877).

docs.title: 5.2 Which elements become fields
docs.text:
_component_schema_nodes_for_element (schema.py:762) walks the element tree:

  • An element whose type is in CONTENT_TYPES (text, image, text-list, table, chart, infographic), whose decorative is exactly False, and which has a non-empty name, becomes a leaf field.
  • A container passes through to its child. If the container itself has no name, the child's fields are lifted to the parent level.
  • A flex, grid or group with a name becomes either an array (if its children repeat, Step 5.4) or a nested object. Without a name, its children's fields are lifted.
  • Everything else (vector, decorative elements, unnamed leaves) contributes nothing.

docs.title: 5.3 Leaf field schemas
docs.text:
_component_content_field_schema (schema.py:1200) maps each leaf type:

Element Field schema Constraint source text {"type": "string", "minLength", "maxLength"} min_length, max_length image, is_icon: false {"type": "object", "properties": {"image_prompt": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["image_prompt"]} none image, is_icon: true same with icon_query none text-list {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "minLength", "maxLength"}, "minItems", "maxItems"} min_items, max_items, min_item_length, max_item_length table {"columns": [string...], "rows": [[string...]...]} object min/max_columns, min/max_rows, plus computed text limits chart {"chart_type", "title"?, "categories", "series"} object fixed caps (below) infographic {"data": {...}} object, per infographic type per type (below)

Every leaf also gets a human title (main_visual_image becomes Main Visual Image), x-element-type and x-element-path, and image fields get a description ("Prompt for the replacement image."). Those annotations are then removed for the layout schema: _strip_component_schema_metadata deletes every $schema, title, description, x-element-type and x-element-path keyword while preserving property names (COMPONENT_SCHEMA_METADATA_KEYS, schema.py:40, and schema.py:647).

Table text limits. Table cells have no stored character limits, so _table_text_limits (schema.py:57) estimates them from geometry:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py (excerpt)
    cell_width = max(
        1.0,
        width / column_count - 2 * TABLE_CELL_HORIZONTAL_PADDING,
    )
    cell_height = max(
        1.0,
        height / (row_count + 1) - 2 * TABLE_CELL_VERTICAL_PADDING,
    )

With TABLE_CELL_HORIZONTAL_PADDING = 12, TABLE_CELL_VERTICAL_PADDING = 6, a glyph width of 0.58 x font size (0.62 when bold) plus letter spacing, a line height of 1.2 x size unless the font says otherwise, and a 14 px default font (schema.py:47 to :50, :128). The maximum is floor(chars_per_line x lines x 0.85), but never less than the longest existing cell; the minimum is 1 if every existing cell has text, otherwise 0 (schema.py:106).

Chart fields. _chart_content_schema (schema.py:1490) always requires chart_type (enum of 12 values: area, bar, bubble, donut, horizontal_bar, horizontal_stacked_bar, line, pie, polar_area, radar, scatter, stacked_bar), categories (at most 24 strings) and series (at most 12 objects {name, values} with at most 24 numbers). title is included only if the layout's chart already has a non-empty title.

Infographic fields. _infographic_content_schema (schema.py:1448) produces {"data": {"type": {"const": "<type>"}, ...}}. Progress bars and gauges require min_value, max_value and value. Gantt charts require columns and rows with {name, start: {column, offset}, end: {...}} spans. Comparison matrices require criteria and items with values. All other types require an items array of {heading, description, label, focus, icon: {url, color}}, with extra required fields for some kinds (id/parent_id for org charts and decision trees, value plus at most 8 items for funnels, labels for before/after and impact/effort matrices). An infographic whose type is not in the catalog falls back to oneOf progress bar or gauge.

Gotcha: the schema offers bubble, the model does not

CHART_TYPE_VALUES in the schema builder includes bubble (schema.py:23), and the hydrator accepts it (presentation.py:1378), but the Pydantic ChartType enum has no bubble (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:76). A generated slide can therefore carry "chart_type": "bubble" in slides.ui, which the HTML renderer draws, but the same chart would fail validation if that UI were ever saved back as a template layout.

docs.title: 5.4 Repeated regions and their limits
docs.text:
When the children of a named flex, grid or group expose identical editable fields, the region becomes a JSON array (_component_repeated_children_schema_result, schema.py:898). The algorithm:

  1. Compute the field nodes of every child. If any child has no editable fields, the region is not repeated.
  2. With fewer than two children, repeat only if max_children is larger than the child count (_can_expand_repeated_children, schema.py:561). This is how a grid with one sample child can become an array of up to eight.
  3. Try three name-normalization strategies in order: numeric strips an index token such as _1 from names (card_1_heading and card_2_heading both become card_heading), none compares names as they are, and prefix strips the first underscore-separated token. The first strategy under which every child's item schema is identical wins.
  4. If none matches but every child is a single wrapper with matching root names, flatten the wrappers to their leaf fields and try again. The comment at schema.py:935 explains why: a leading divider can add an extra wrapper around every item after the first.
  5. Bound the array. For flex and grid, minItems/maxItems are the element's min_children/max_children. For a group, they are item_count // 2 and item_count (_component_repeated_item_limits, schema.py:1038).

A component whose top-level elements are all groups that repeat is collapsed into a single array field, named after the first group with its index token removed (_component_repeated_top_level_group_node, schema.py:822). The Civic layout side_badges_with_comparison_rows_6038, for example, has two category_badge groups and produces:

"side_category_badges": {
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "category_badge": {
      "type": "array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "maxItems": 2,
      "items": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "properties": {
          "category_label": {"type": "string", "minLength": 5, "maxLength": 15}
        },
        "required": ["category_label"]
      }
    }
  },
  "required": ["category_badge"]
}

Gotcha: n // 2 for groups, (n + 1) // 2 elsewhere

Groups use floor division for their minimum (item_count // 2), so three repeated groups allow a single item. Certification sets min_children for flex and grid to max(1, (n + 1) // 2). The two rules differ by one for odd counts; do not assume they are interchangeable when you hand-edit limits.

docs.title: Step 6: Two LLM calls read the schemas
docs.text: The schema is used twice during generation. Both prompts are covered in depth in Prompts and schemas; here is what each sees of the template.

docs.title: 6.1 Structure selection: which layout for which slide
docs.text:
generate_presentation_structure (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_presentation_structure.py:157) sends PresentationLayoutModel.to_string():

servers/fastapi/templates/presentation_layout.py (excerpt)
    def to_string(self, with_schema: bool = False) -> str:
        message = "## Presentation Layout\n\n"
        for index, slide in enumerate(self.slides):
            message += f"### Slide Layout: {index}\n"
            message += f"- Name: {slide.name or slide.json_schema.get('title')}\n"
            message += f"- Description: {slide.description}\n"
            if with_schema:
                try:
                    schema_text = json.dumps(slide.json_schema, ensure_ascii=False)
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    schema_text = str(slide.json_schema)
                message += f"- Schema: {schema_text}\n"
            message += "\n"
        return message

For the General template the first entries read:

## Presentation Layout

### Slide Layout: 0
- Name: title_intro
- Description: A clean split presentation layout with a large rounded image card and a structured text panel with attribution card.

### Slide Layout: 1
- Name: title_description_image
- Description: A clean split presentation layout with a large rounded visual card on the left and stacked headline copy on the right.

In the normal flow only names and descriptions are sent, in the user message ahead of the outline (generate_presentation_structure.py:127). When the user supplied slide-by-slide Markdown, the layouts go into the system prompt with full schemas (to_string(with_schema=True), generate_presentation_structure.py:151). That is why layout descriptions matter so much: in the normal flow they are the only thing the selector knows about a layout. The answer is a list of layout indexes. The two paths repair it differently. The prepare path pads a short list and replaces any index outside 0..layout_count-1 with a random valid one (_normalize_presentation_structure, presentation.py:384). The API path truncates the list to the outline count and replaces only indexes at or above the layout count (presentation.py:2904); its branch for appending missing indexes tests index >= total_outlines inside range(total_outlines) and so never runs, which means a short list is not padded there.

When a table of contents is requested, select_toc_or_list_slide_layout_index (servers/fastapi/utils/ppt_utils.py:59) searches layout ids, names, descriptions and schema titles with case-insensitive regexes: first table of contents, agenda, contents, outline, index, toc; then bullet list, numbered list, list. The first matching layout index is inserted once per required table-of-contents slide, at position 1 when there is a title slide and at position 0 otherwise (_insert_toc_layouts, presentation.py:361). No TOC is inserted when no layout matches.

docs.title: 6.2 Slide content: filling the schema
docs.text:
For each slide, get_slide_content_from_type_and_outline (servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py:229) prepares the chosen layout's schema:

servers/fastapi/utils/llm_calls/generate_slide_content.py (excerpt)
def _prepare_response_schema(json_schema: Optional[dict]) -> Optional[dict]:
    if not isinstance(json_schema, dict):
        return None

    response_schema = remove_fields_from_schema(json_schema, ASSET_ONLY_FIELDS)
    if not _schema_has_content_fields(response_schema):
        return None
    # ...
    response_schema = add_field_in_schema(
        response_schema,
        {
            "__speaker_note__": {
                "type": "string",
                "minLength": 100,
                "maxLength": 500,
                "description": "Speaker note for the slide",
            }
        },
        True,
    )
    return ensure_array_schemas_have_items(response_schema)

ASSET_ONLY_FIELDS is ["__image_url__", "__icon_url__"] (generate_slide_content.py:86). A layout without content fields returns {} immediately, with no LLM call. The schema is sent both as the structured-output response format (strict=True) and inline in the system prompt ("Follow this response schema exactly: ..."), and the response is validated against it with retries.

docs.title: Step 7: Worked example, part 1: layout to schema
docs.text:
Take the title_description_image layout printed in full in chapter 16, Step 7. Running get_template_schema on it produces this layout schema (output of the real function, reformatted):

get_template_schema output for title_description_image
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "type": "object",
  "title": "title_description_image",
  "description": "A clean split presentation layout with a large rounded visual card on the left and stacked headline copy on the right.",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "left_visual_card": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "main_visual_image": {
          "type": "object",
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "properties": {"image_prompt": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["image_prompt"]
        }
      },
      "required": ["main_visual_image"]
    },
    "right_text_stack": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "primary_heading": {"type": "string", "minLength": 8, "maxLength": 25},
        "supporting_paragraph": {"type": "string", "minLength": 105, "maxLength": 274}
      },
      "required": ["primary_heading", "supporting_paragraph"]
    }
  },
  "required": ["left_visual_card", "right_text_stack"]
}

Note what is missing: slide_background contributes nothing (a vector only), and neither the accent bar nor any style information appears. The LLM fills three values: one image prompt and two strings.

A response that satisfies the prepared schema looks like this (an illustrative sample, not captured from a model):

Sample slide content returned by the LLM
{
  "left_visual_card": {
    "main_visual_image": {
      "image_prompt": "Analyst team reviewing a revenue dashboard on a large monitor"
    }
  },
  "right_text_stack": {
    "primary_heading": "Q3 Revenue Review",
    "supporting_paragraph": "Revenue grew **18% year over year**, driven by enterprise renewals and a faster sales cycle in EMEA. Margins held steady while support costs fell for the second straight quarter."
  },
  "__speaker_note__": "Open with the headline number, then explain the two drivers: enterprise renewals and the shorter EMEA sales cycle. Close by noting that support costs declined again."
}

The system prompt tells the model to "Strictly use markdown to emphasize important points" (generate_slide_content.py:120), which is why **18% year over year** appears; the hydrator turns it into a bold run.

docs.title: Step 8: Creating the slide row and fetching assets
docs.text:
On the API path the slides are built in batches (presentation.py:3013):

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
                slide = SlideModel(
                    presentation=presentation_id,
                    layout_group=layout_model.name,
                    layout=slide_layout.id,
                    index=i,
                    speaker_note=slide_content.get("__speaker_note__"),
                    content=slide_content,
                    ui=_template_slide_ui(layout_payload, slide_layout.id),
                )

layout_group is the template id (from the payload name), layout the layout id, content the raw LLM JSON, and ui a deep copy of the chosen layout found by id in the deck payload (_template_slide_ui, presentation.py:490).

Asset fetching then runs concurrently with the next batch's LLM calls (process_slide_and_fetch_assets, covered in Images, icons, web search). For template slides it writes the result next to the prompt in content, under image_url or icon_url (_asset_url_key, servers/fastapi/utils/process_slides.py:110). Before generating images, image_target_sizes_from_template runs the hydrator once on a copy with unique marker URLs to learn each image slot's pixel size, so images can be generated at the right aspect ratio (process_slides.py:35). After this step the example content contains:

"main_visual_image": {
  "image_prompt": "Analyst team reviewing a revenue dashboard on a large monitor",
  "image_url": "/app_data/images/5f1c0b7e-revenue.png"
}

(The file name is illustrative.) Only after all asset tasks finish does the pipeline hydrate every slide (presentation.py:3084) and commit.

docs.title: Step 9: Hydration, content back into the layout
docs.text: Hydration is _apply_template_content_to_ui(ui, content) (presentation.py:575). It is called from _hydrate_template_slide_ui on the API path, from the streaming path for every slide it emits (presentation.py:2396, :2431, :2455, :2487), and from the edit and derive endpoints (presentation.py:3325, :3376).

docs.title: 9.1 Top level
9.2 Matching an element to its value
docs.text:
_apply_template_content_to_element (presentation.py:626) looks up the element's name in the current content object. _template_content_name_candidates (presentation.py:743) tries three keys in order: the name itself, the name with a _<digits> token removed (metric_2_value becomes metric_value), and that result with its first underscore-separated prefix removed (metric_value becomes value). For the second and later occurrences of the same name in one scope, it first tries name_2, name_3 and so on, mirroring the schema builder's de-duplication (_template_repeated_content_keys_for_name, presentation.py:851).

A value is applied only if the element has decorative: False, a name, a found value, and a type in GENERATED_VALUE_ELEMENT_TYPES (text, math, image, text-list, table, chart, infographic; presentation.py:503). Otherwise the element is copied as is, and containers, flex, grid and group elements recurse into their children with the nested content object.

When an array item is applied to a repeated child (direct_value=True) and the item is not wrapped in the child's name, the item itself is the value. The comment at presentation.py:674 gives the example: three repeated image children are emitted as [{"image_prompt": ..., "image_url": ...}, ...], not as [{"gallery_photo": {...}}, ...].

docs.title: 9.3 Expanding and contracting repeated regions
docs.text:
For a flex, grid or group whose value is a list, _apply_template_content_to_children builds one child per item (presentation.py:758). The template child used for item i comes from repeated_child_source_index:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/content.py (excerpt)
def repeated_child_source_index(
    index: int,
    *,
    template_count: int,
    content_count: int,
    center_when_reduced: bool,
) -> int:
    """Return the template child used for a repeated content item."""
    if center_when_reduced and content_count < template_count:
        start = (template_count - content_count) // 2
        return start + index
    return min(index, template_count - 1)
  • More items than template children: extra items reuse the last child. _repeated_child_for_index deep-copies it, removes __presenton_manual_position, and renumbers index tokens in every nested name to the new position (_normalize_repeated_names, presentation.py:813, which rewrites _\d+ to _<index+1>).
  • Fewer items, flex or grid: the first n children are used and the flow engine re-spaces them.
  • Fewer items, group or top-level groups: center_when_reduced is true, so the middle n children are used. Their absolute positions are kept, which centers the remaining items within the original spread.

Running the real hydrator on the Momentum layout center_title_agenda_grid_wave_7815, whose grid (min_children: 1, max_children: 8, columns: 4) holds a single sample child, with three agenda items produces three copies of that child:

grid name=grid_items_elements_with_descrtipiton_title  min_children=1 max_children=8 columns=4 rows=2
  group name=agenda_items
    vector
    text name=agenda_item_label        '01'
    text name=agenda_item_description  'Market overview'
  group name=agenda_items
    vector
    text name=agenda_item_label        '02'
    text name=agenda_item_description  'Product roadmap'
  group name=agenda_items
    vector
    text name=agenda_item_label        '03'
    text name=agenda_item_description  'Hiring plan'

Gotcha: expansion copies geometry verbatim

A copied child keeps the source child's position and size. Inside flex and grid that is harmless because the flow engine places children. Inside a free-form group, a copy beyond the template count lands exactly on top of the last child. The schema prevents this for groups by capping maxItems at the number of template groups, but if you raise max_children on a hand-edited group, expect overlapping items.

docs.title: 9.4 Writing each value type
docs.text:
_apply_template_content_value (presentation.py:865) dispatches by element type:

Type Function What it does text _apply_template_text_content (:946) Accepts a string, a number, or {"text": ...}. Builds new runs from the first existing run's style. Inline Markdown **x**/__x__ becomes {"bold": true} and *x*/_x_ becomes {"italic": true}; when any emphasis is present, bold and italic are removed from the base run so plain segments inherit the element font. Strings with <latex>...</latex> tags or an unbalanced leading ** go through replace_text_runs instead (:1163). Adjacent runs with identical style are merged. An empty string leaves the element unchanged. image _apply_template_image_content (:965) Takes the URL from image_url, icon_url, __image_url__, __icon_url__ or url, in that order, and writes it to data. Writes the prompt (image_prompt or icon_query first, depending on is_icon) to prompt. Sets fit: "cover" unless the element is an icon, already cover, has a clip_path, or the URL is an SVG (_normalize_generated_image_fit, servers/fastapi/services/chat/slide_ui_helpers.py:412). No URL means no change. text-list _apply_template_text_list_content (:1007) Replaces items with one run list per non-empty string, each styled like the existing item at the same index. table _apply_template_table_content (:1047) Rebuilds columns and rows to the generated lengths. Extra cells copy the last template cell's style; missing template cells fall back to built-in defaults (GENERATED_TABLE_TEXT_FONT: Sniglet, 12 px, #082314; fill #F8F4E9; stroke #D8D3C4, presentation.py:512). Each cell's text is cut to 80 characters (_read_template_table_text, :1319). chart _apply_template_chart_content (:1367) Copies chart_type (if in the allowed set), title, categories, series, colors, axis, grid and legend colors, axis titles, source, boolean axis and grid toggles, and data_labels, accepting both snake_case and camelCase keys. Removes stale data_labels_color and grid. infographic _apply_template_infographic_content (:884) Strips inline Markdown from every string in data (infographic_markdown_to_plain_text, content.py:27), keeps the template's data.type, merges the rest over the existing data, and copies colors if given. math _apply_template_math_content (:913) Writes latex, stripping $$...$$ or \[...\] delimiters and capping at 4,000 characters. No Pydantic element has this type; it only matters for legacy UIs.

Gotcha: table cells are silently truncated to 80 characters

The schema may allow longer cell text (its limit comes from geometry, Step 5.3), but hydration keeps only the first 80 characters of every cell. If you build templates with wide, text-heavy tables, raise both limits together.

docs.title: Step 10: Worked example, part 2: the hydrated slide
docs.text:
Feeding the sample content (with the image_url added in Step 8) to _apply_template_content_to_ui changes exactly three elements of the layout. The rest of the output is identical to the input layout.

Hydrated slides.ui, changed elements only (real hydrator output)
// left_visual_card, element 1
{
  "type": "image",
  // ... position, size, rotation, border_radius unchanged
  "data": "/app_data/images/5f1c0b7e-revenue.png",
  "fit": "cover",
  "decorative": false,
  "name": "main_visual_image",
  "is_icon": false,
  "prompt": "Analyst team reviewing a revenue dashboard on a large monitor"
}
// right_text_stack, element 0: runs replaced, element font unchanged
"runs": [
  {
    "text": "Q3 Revenue Review",
    "font": {"size": 60, "family": "Poppins", "color": "#111827", "bold": true, "italic": false, "line_height": 0.8}
  }
]
// right_text_stack, element 2: Markdown emphasis became three runs
"runs": [
  {"text": "Revenue grew ",
   "font": {"size": 18, "family": "Poppins", "color": "#4B5563", "line_height": 1.24}},
  {"text": "18% year over year",
   "font": {"size": 18, "family": "Poppins", "color": "#4B5563", "line_height": 1.24, "bold": true}},
  {"text": ", driven by enterprise renewals and a faster sales cycle in EMEA. Margins held steady while support costs fell for the second straight quarter.",
   "font": {"size": 18, "family": "Poppins", "color": "#4B5563", "line_height": 1.24}}
]

Observe that the plain runs lost their "bold": false, "italic": false keys. They still render as regular text because the renderer merges each run over the element-level font, which keeps bold: false (servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:399). slides.content keeps the raw LLM JSON (with image_url) and slides.ui the hydrated tree; the editor and exporters render ui.

docs.title: Step 11: The HTML renderer
docs.text: The Next.js app has two renderers for the same ui tree: a Konva canvas renderer used by the slide editor (Slide editor) and a pure string renderer, servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts, used for previews and thumbnails. This step documents the string renderer.

docs.title: 11.1 Entry points and payload
11.2 Dispatch and z-order
11.3 Element by element
docs.text:
Type Rendering text A div at the element's box with display:flex, align-items from alignment.vertical (top/middle/bottom to flex-start/center/flex-end), justify-content and text-align from alignment.horizontal, element font on the box, and one span per run with the merged run font. Line height defaults to 1.1 when the font has none (renderText, :391). Residual Markdown in run text is rendered through the editor's normalizeRawTextMarkdownElement. LaTeX runs become KaTeX MathML spans (renderTextRunHtml, :3877; renderMathHtml, servers/nextjs/lib/math.ts:25, which caps LaTeX at 4,000 characters). text-list ul (or ol for number) with 24 px left padding. When marker_gap is set, native markers are hidden and each item becomes a two-column grid of a literal • or N. and the text, separated by marker_gap px; gap becomes margin-top between items (renderTextList, :415). table A CSS grid of equal columns and equal rows over the element box. Row 0 is columns; header cells are bold unless a cell font sets bold. Cells get padding:4px 6px, overflow:hidden, borders from borders per side or a 1 px #D1D5DB stroke, and a base font of Arial 18 px #111827 with line height 1.15 unless the table sets font (renderTable, :454; tableBaseFont, :3548). image An img with object-fit from fit (default contain) and object-position from focus_x/focus_y. With crop_scale or clip_path, the image is wrapped in a clipping div. An icon with a color becomes a div filled with that color and masked by the icon file (renderImage, :352). vector An absolutely positioned div sized to the points' bounding box, containing an SVG polygon or polyline (points translated to the box origin) with preserveAspectRatio="none", rounded corners, smoothed curves, dashes, caps, joins and SVG marker definitions for arrowheads (renderPolygon, :847). Ellipses become one SVG ellipse (:1019). Shadows are not drawn for vectors by this renderer. chart A canvas carrying the whole Chart.js configuration in a data-chart-config attribute (renderChart, :1074). chartConfig (:2261) maps kinds to Chart.js types (donut to doughnut, area to a filled line, polar_area to polarArea, horizontal kinds to bar with indexAxis: "y"), shows the legend automatically for pie-like or multi-series charts, sizes fonts from the chart height (clamp(height x 0.033, 9, 18) for labels), disables tooltips and animation, and configures chartjs-plugin-datalabels from data_labels. Charts are drawn later by the browser (Step 11.5). infographic Gauges draw a 120 x 72 SVG arc; progress bars draw a pill track with a value bar and, when the box is at least 28 px tall, a right-aligned value label (:1238, :1271). The 23 structural kinds listed in FIXED_INFOGRAPHIC_RENDERERS draw at a fixed design size (for example 720 x 260 for timeline, 560 x 520 for radial_cycle) and are scaled uniformly and centered into the element box (FIXED_INFOGRAPHIC_RENDERERS, :1096; renderScaledInfographic, :1163). Org charts and decision trees use 720 x 360. container A styled div (fill, border, radius, shadow, padding) that centers or aligns its child with flexbox. Overflow is hidden only when explicitly requested, when the child image has a clip path, or when a positioned child image overflows the box (containerOverflowStyle, :500). flex A flexbox with direction, wrap, gap, align_items (default stretch) and justify_content (default flex-start). Child sizes come from the shared flow engine, layoutFlowChildren in servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/layout/flowLayout.ts:69, the same code the Konva editor uses. The box grows if its children need more room than its declared size (flexFrameStyle, :678). grid A CSS grid with columns equal tracks (fixed pixel tracks when the grid has a width) and, when rows is set, at least that many rows (renderGrid, :777). group A div sized to its declared size or to its children's extent, with absolutely positioned children (renderGroup, :839).

Gotcha: no auto-shrink, overflow is visible

Nothing in this renderer measures text and reduces the font size. Text boxes use overflow:visible;white-space:pre-wrap;overflow-wrap:anywhere (textOverflowStyle, :3612), so text that exceeds its box spills out below it. The only protection against overflow is upstream: max_length limits in the schema, which certification derives from the box geometry with a 0.85 safety factor. If you shrink a text box in a template without lowering max_length, generated slides will overflow. The flow engine does measure text, but only to size auto-width children inside flex (intrinsicTextMainSize, flowLayout.ts:549; covered by servers/nextjs/tests/flow-layout-text-sizing.test.mjs).

docs.title: 11.4 Scaling the slide into the page
docs.text:
TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx:218) always renders the slide at its native 1280 x 720 and scales it with a CSS transform. A ResizeObserver tracks the container width, and the natural scale is:

TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx (excerpt)
  const naturalScale = fixedSize
    ? 1
    : containerWidth
      ? Math.min((containerWidth / TEMPLATE_V2_HTML_WIDTH) * 0.98, 1)
      : 0;

so previews never upscale beyond 100% and leave a 2% margin. With fitBounds, the component instead zooms to a sub-rectangle of the slide, with default padding of 8% horizontally and 10% vertically (:376). The slide is hidden (opacity: 0) until a scale is known, which avoids a flash at the wrong size. The markup is injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML and pointer-events: none.

docs.title: 11.5 Drawing the charts
docs.text: After the HTML is in the DOM, a layout effect finds every canvas[data-presenton-chart], loads the vendored Chart.js runtime (/vendor/chart-4.5.1.umd.min.js and /vendor/chartjs-plugin-datalabels-2.2.0.min.js, servers/nextjs/lib/chart-browser.ts:1), parses the configuration, re-attaches the function-valued options that JSON cannot carry (axis tick formatters, per-bar border radii, data label formatters), and constructs each chart with animation disabled (TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview.tsx:271). Progress is published on window.__PRESENTON_JSON_CHARTS__ as {status: "pending" | "ready" | "error", pending, rendered}, which lets an automated browser wait for charts before taking a screenshot.

docs.title: 11.6 Where the HTML preview is used
docs.text: TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview is imported by the template editor's thumbnail strip, the presentation's new-slide picker, the insert palette, the presentation actions menu, the chat panel and its widgets, and both copies of the blank-slide prompt overlay (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/template-preview/components/editor/ThumbnailStrip.tsx:19, presentation/components/NewSlide.tsx:18, InsertPalettePreview.tsx:18, PresentationActions.tsx:95, Chat.tsx:49, chat/chat-widgets.tsx:5, components/V1ContentRender.tsx:11 and _shared/TemplateV2PromptOverlay.tsx:6). The main editing surface does not use it; it draws slides with Konva.

docs.title: Step 12: Themes in rendering
docs.text: The renderer has no notion of a theme: every color it emits is a literal from the element JSON, and it never reads presentations.theme or CSS variables. Theme roles (primary, card, graph_0 to graph_9 and so on) are applied when the editor inserts new elements, through servers/nextjs/lib/template-theme.ts and components/slide-editor/insert/insert-elements.ts; the presentation page also writes them as CSS variables. Themes and fonts traces all of that.

docs.title: Step 13: V1ContentRender, V1SelectEdit and the v1 legacy path
docs.text:
Despite their names, the "V1" components are part of the current Template v2 stack.

  • V1ContentRender (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/V1ContentRender.tsx:159) is the slide body used by the presentation page. It renders TemplateV2KonvaSlide, the Konva editor surface, for every slide, using the slide's ui or, for blank slides, BLANK_TEMPLATE_V2_LAYOUT. It wraps the surface in an error boundary and, in edit mode, can overlay TemplateV2PromptOverlay, a prompt box that previews the layout through TemplateV2HtmlSlidePreview at a scale of 0.085 and dispatches a PRESENTON_BLANK_SLIDE_PROMPT_EVENT window event when submitted.
  • V1SelectEdit (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/components/V1SelectEdit.tsx) exports HtmlSelectionEditor, a hover-and-select overlay that would send complete_code, section_code, edit_prompt and slide_id to an "edit selection HTML" API. The API call and the state update are commented out (V1SelectEdit.tsx:569), and no file imports the component. It is dead code from the HTML-template era.
  • v1 decks are rejected outright. When a presentation's version is v1-standard, usePresentationData shows "Unsupported presentation" and redirects to the dashboard (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts:33). New decks are created with version=V2_STANDARD (presentation.py:2944).

Gotcha: two renderers must agree

The Konva editor and the HTML preview are separate implementations of the same format. They share the flow engine (flowLayout.ts) and the text-run normalization, but everything else (vector rounding, table cells, infographic drawings) is written twice. Tests such as template-v2-json-to-html-metadata.test.mjs ("allocates unsized flex children like the Konva renderer") and template-v2-renderer-fields.test.mjs pin the two together. When you add an element property, implement it in both renderers and in both exporters (PPTX and PDF export).

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Bundles are re-imported, re-validated and re-copied on every start; a single invalid bundle prevents startup, and built-in rows are shared through owner_id IS NULL AND is_default.
  • A deck stores a private copy of the template's layouts; schemas are rebuilt from that copy whenever generation or streaming needs them.
  • The schema builder emits one object per component, one field per non-decorative named content element, arrays for repeated flex/grid/group regions with bounded lengths, and geometry-derived limits for tables.
  • The structure selector sees only layout names and descriptions (plus schemas in the slides-Markdown flow); the content generator sees the schema plus a required 100 to 500 character speaker note.
  • Hydration deep-copies the layout, matches values by name with suffix and prefix fallbacks, expands or contracts repeated children (centering reductions for groups), converts Markdown emphasis to runs, writes image URLs with cover fit, and truncates table cells to 80 characters.
  • The HTML renderer paints in array order at 1280 x 720, never shrinks text, draws charts with Chart.js after mount, and ignores themes.

docs.title: Custom templates from PPTX
docs.text: Reads: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py, servers/fastapi/templates/fonts_and_slides_preview.py, servers/fastapi/templates/pptx_font_utils.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/hooks/useTemplateCreation.ts, scripts/convert-template.mjs · Builds on: From template to schema to slide · Time: ~50 min

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
This chapter follows a user's .pptx file from the upload dropzone to a persisted, certified TemplateV2 row. You will see the font check and font replacement pass, how slide preview images are rendered, the four vision passes that turn raw PPTX elements into editable layouts (and every fallback when a pass fails), how reusable components are clustered and a semantic theme is derived, and every route in the template API. The chapter ends with the template studio and editor in Next.js and the two Node scripts that turn a stored template into a bundled templates/<id>/template.json.

flowchart TD
    U["Browser: /custom-template"] --> FC["POST /api/v1/ppt/fonts/check"]
    FC --> FP["POST /api/v1/ppt/template/fonts-upload-and-slides-preview"]
    FP --> EX1["Export runtime: pptx-to-json"]
    EX1 --> EX2["Export runtime: json-to-images (Chromium)"]
    EX2 --> PRE["slide_image_urls + modified_pptx_url + fonts"]
    PRE --> ASYNC["POST /api/v1/ppt/template/async"]
    ASYNC --> TASK["async_task row, BackgroundTasks"]
    TASK --> PREP["_prepare_template_source: pptx-to-json again"]
    PREP --> GEN["generate_slide_layout per slide, up to 10 threads"]
    GEN --> VP["Pass 1: visual data"]
    VP --> SP["Pass 2: semantic manifest"]
    SP --> FL["Pass 3: flexible regions"]
    FL --> TC["Pass 4: text capacity"]
    TC --> CMP["Compile and certify"]
    CMP --> MERGE["merge_similar_components"]
    CMP --> THEME["generate_template_theme"]
    MERGE --> ROW["TemplateV2 row"]
    THEME --> ROW

docs.title: Step 1: The two creation workflows and the API surface
docs.text:
Everything lives under TEMPLATE_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/template", tags=["Templates"]) (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:96), mounted inside API_V1_PPT_ROUTER (prefix /api/v1/ppt, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:22, include at :39). The font routes are a separate router, FONTS_ROUTER = APIRouter(prefix="/fonts") (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py:18), included at servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/router.py:25.

There are two ways to turn preview images plus a PPTX into a template:

  1. One-shot asynchronous creation. POST /template/async stores an async_task row and runs _run_create_template_task as a FastAPI background task. It certifies every slide in parallel, clusters components, derives a theme and inserts one TemplateV2 row at the end. The template studio's Generate Template button uses this route, and so does the MCP tool flow.
  2. Incremental creation. POST /template/init stores a row with raw_layouts and no layouts. The client then calls POST /template/layouts/create per slide, saves each result with PATCH /template/{id}/layouts, and finally calls POST /template/generate-blocks to cluster components and derive a theme. This is wired into the useTemplateCreation hook and is also what the template editor uses to "reconstruct" a single slide.
Method and path Handler Request Response GET /template/all list_templates (template.py:1118) query page (default 1), page_size (default 20, max 100), default (optional bool) TemplateListResponse {items, total, page, page_size} POST /template/fonts-upload-and-slides-preview upload_template_fonts_and_slides_preview (:1193) multipart: pptx_file, font_files[], original_font_names[], google_font_original_names[], google_font_replacement_names[], google_font_names[], google_font_urls[] FontsUploadAndSlidesPreviewResponse {slide_image_urls, pptx_url, modified_pptx_url, fonts} POST /template/mcp-upload upload_template_assets_for_mcp (:1220) JSON {pptx: {filename, content_base64}, fonts: [{filename, content_base64, original_font_name}]} {pptx_url, slide_image_urls, fonts} POST /template/init init_template (:1277), status 201 InitTemplateRequest the new template id as a bare JSON string POST /template/async create_template (:1574), status 201 CreateTemplateRequest (same fields as init) AsyncTaskModel POST /template/async/{task_id}/retry retry_create_template (:1626), status 202 none AsyncTaskModel POST /template/layouts/generate generate_template_layout_from_prompt (:1700) {template_id or id, prompt} {layout, response} POST /template/layouts/create create_template_slide_layouts (:1789) {template_id or id, index or indices, generation_options?} {layouts: [{index, layout}]} POST /template/generate-blocks generate_template_blocks (:1874) {template_id or id} TemplateResponse PATCH /template/{template_id}/layouts patch_template_slide_layout (:1929) {index, layout} or {layouts: [{index, layout}]} TemplateResponse PATCH /template/{template_id} update_template_metadata (:1976) UpdateTemplateMetadataRequest TemplateResponse GET /template/{template_id}/theme get_template_theme (:2093) none {template_id, theme} GET /template/{template_id} get_template (:2127) none TemplateResponse DELETE /template/{template_id} delete_template (:2158), status 204 none Every mutating route except creation calls _require_private_template (template.py:2170), which raises 403 "Built-in templates are read-only" when is_default is true.

Gotcha

GET /template/{template_id}/theme must be registered before GET /template/{template_id}, otherwise FastAPI would match theme as a template id. The order in the file is deliberate and pinned by test_get_template_theme_route_is_registered_before_template_detail_get (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_template_api.py:1127).

docs.title: Step 2: Choose the file in the browser
docs.text:
The studio page is servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/page.tsx. It redirects to /dashboard when PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE normalizes to smart (page.tsx:8), because smart-mode decks do not use templates (see Smart mode). Otherwise it renders CustomTemplatePage.

File selection goes through useFileUpload (custom-template/hooks/useFileUpload.ts). The only client-side checks are the extension and size:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/hooks/useFileUpload.ts (excerpt)
    const lowerName = file.name.toLowerCase();
    const isPptx = lowerName.endsWith(".pptx");
    if (!isPptx) {
      notify.error("Invalid file", "Please select a valid PPTX file.");
      return;
    }

    const maxSize = 100 * 1024 * 1024;
    if (file.size > maxSize) {
      notify.error("File too large", "File size must be less than 100MB.");
      return;
    }

When the page mounts it also calls showTemplateV2ModelWarningIfNeeded(llmConfig) (CustomTemplatePage.tsx:1296). That helper (custom-template/utils/templateModelWarning.ts) shows a persistent toast unless the configured text model is on a hard-coded allow list: the presenton provider, OpenAI families such as gpt-5, gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, gpt-4-turbo, or any claude- model containing opus or sonnet. Dismissal is remembered in localStorage under presenton.nonSotaTemplateToastDismissed. This is only a warning; nothing blocks a weaker model.

Model requirements

docs/template-v2.md is explicit that template creation sends each slide screenshot to the configured text LLM, so that model must accept image input and structured JSON output. Template creation requests up to 16,000 completion tokens (TEMPLATE_GENERATION_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS = 16000, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py:61, and SLIDE_LAYOUT_GENERATION_MAX_TOKENS = 16000, template.py:101). Configuring an image-generation provider does not help. Generating a deck from an existing template does not need vision. Provider configuration is covered in Configuration and LLM providers.

docs.title: Step 3: Check the fonts in the PPTX
docs.text:
checkFonts in useTemplateCreation.ts:135 posts the file as pptx_file to POST /api/v1/ppt/fonts/check. The route is registered without a decorator, as a call on the router:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py (excerpt)
FONTS_ROUTER.post("/check", response_model=FontCheckResponse)(
    check_fonts_in_pptx_handler
)

check_fonts_in_pptx_handler (servers/fastapi/templates/fonts_and_slides_preview.py:1160) does the following, in order:

  1. Rejects anything not ending in .pptx with 400 "Invalid file type. Expected PPTX file".
  2. Rejects uploads of 100 MB or more with 413 (MAX_FONT_CHECK_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024, :150; the check is size >= MAX, :1040).
  3. Writes the bytes to a temporary presentation.pptx and validates the ZIP package (_validate_pptx_package, :1045): testzip() must pass, and [Content_Types].xml, ppt/presentation.xml and at least one ppt/slides/slide*.xml must exist, otherwise 400 "The uploaded PowerPoint file is corrupted or unsupported.".
  4. Extracts every font family and the variants actually used (extract_used_font_variants_from_pptx, servers/fastapi/templates/pptx_font_utils.py:366). Variants are one of regular, bold, italic, bold_italic, derived by _font_style_variant (pptx_font_utils.py:330) from the b and i attributes on run properties plus the family name itself. Theme references such as +mj-lt are resolved to the theme's major/minor fonts (_resolve_theme_typeface, :193).
  5. Calls get_available_and_unavailable_fonts_for_pptx (pptx_font_utils.py:813). For every family/variant it first looks for a matching embedded font (ppt/fonts/*.fntdata), then the packaged catalog through get_static_font_url (:177). Anything left is unavailable.
  6. For unavailable fonts, looks in the global font_uploads table (get_font_uploads_for_names_by_variant, servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py:406). A previously uploaded file whose variant matches moves the entry into available_fonts with its /app_data/fonts/... URL.

A response looks like this (one entry per family and variant; name is the display name built by _font_info_entry, fonts_and_slides_preview.py:874):

{
  "available_fonts": [
    {"name": "Montserrat Regular", "url": "/vendor/fonts/sans_serif/montserrat/Montserrat[wght].ttf",
     "original_name": "Montserrat", "family_name": "Montserrat",
     "variant": "regular", "variants": ["regular"]}
  ],
  "unavailable_fonts": [
    {"name": "Brand Sans Bold", "url": null, "original_name": "BrandSans-Bold",
     "family_name": "Brand Sans", "variant": "bold", "variants": ["bold"]}
  ]
}

Gotcha

Embedded fonts are reported as available with a fake URL. The code literally stores "https://example.com/just-a-placeholder-url.ttf" for embedded matches (pptx_font_utils.py:860, inside get_available_and_unavailable_fonts_for_pptx), because at check time nothing has been extracted yet. The real URL only appears after the next step extracts and persists the embedded file. Do not render or cache the URL from /fonts/check for embedded fonts.

The "packaged catalog" is servers/fastapi/templates/assets/fonts.json: a JSON array of 95 {font_name, font_url} objects whose URLs point at /vendor/fonts/<category>/<dir>/<file> (files that ship in the Next.js public/ folder). It is loaded once with @lru_cache(maxsize=1) by get_static_font_catalog (pptx_font_utils.py:162) and keyed by normalize_font_family_name(family).casefold(). Normalization (:130) turns _ and - into spaces, splits camelCase, and strips trailing weight/style tokens, so Montserrat-SemiBold and MontserratSemiBold both normalize to Montserrat. Themes and fonts covers the catalog from the frontend side.

docs.title: Step 4: Replace fonts and render slide previews
docs.text:
If any font is missing, the studio shows a picker per missing font. The user can upload a font file or pick a fallback from the local catalog LOCAL_FONT_OPTIONS (CustomTemplatePage.tsx:1199); a default fallback is pre-selected by preferredFallbackFont (:208), which tries the font's family_name and original_name against the catalog and otherwise takes the first catalog entry. When every font is covered, fontUploadAndPreview (useTemplateCreation.ts:259) posts multipart form data to POST /api/v1/ppt/template/fonts-upload-and-slides-preview:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/hooks/useTemplateCreation.ts (excerpt)
            uploadedFonts.forEach(font => {
                formData.append("font_files", font.file);
                formData.append("original_font_names", font.fontName);
            });
            Object.entries(googleFontReplacementsByOriginalName).forEach(
                ([originalFontName, googleFont]) => {
                    formData.append("google_font_original_names", originalFontName);
                    formData.append("google_font_replacement_names", googleFont.fontName);
                    formData.append("google_font_urls", googleFont.fontUrl);
                }
            );

Gotcha

The google_font_* form fields no longer carry Google Fonts. The values the studio sends are local catalog fonts (fontUrl: selectedFont.sourceUrl, a /vendor/fonts/... path, CustomTemplatePage.tsx:1267). The backend helpers that once called Google are now stubs that consult the packaged catalog (get_google_font_file_urls, check_google_font_availability, pptx_font_utils.py:258 and :264). The field names are kept for API compatibility.

The route forwards to upload_fonts_and_preview_handler (fonts_and_slides_preview.py:1304, via the thin wrapper in servers/fastapi/templates/preview.py). Its steps:

  1. Validate the pairs. font_files and original_font_names must both be present and equal in length (400 otherwise). _selected_google_font_maps (:76) applies the same rule to the replacement names and URLs and returns selected_fonts {replacement_name: url} plus replacements {original_name: replacement_name}.
  2. Save, validate and trim the PPTX. The file is written to a temp dir, validated as in Step 3, then _trim_pptx_to_max_slides (:1086) removes slides beyond the cap. The cap is MAX_TEMPLATE_PREVIEW_SLIDES = 50 (:149; _resolve_template_preview_slide_cap, :1069). Trimming edits ppt/presentation.xml, its .rels, and [Content_Types].xml directly, and writes <stem>-first-50.pptx.
  3. Create a session directory. session_id = uuid.uuid4() and the directory <uploads>/template-previews/<session_id> (_get_template_preview_session_dir, :676).
  4. Fix fonts in the PPTX (upload_fonts_and_fix_fonts_in_pptx, :1503):
    • Extract embedded .fntdata fonts, convert EOT to TTF when needed, and copy them to <app_data>/fonts/embedded/<random uuid>/<name>.ttf (_prepare_embedded_fonts, :1826).
    • Save uploaded font files with the 10 MB limit (read_upload_with_size_limit, servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py:148), read their name tables with fontTools (get_font_details), and build font_mapping {original: actual} and font_variant_mapping {original: {variant: actual}} (_save_uploaded_fonts_to_temp, :1769).
    • Add the catalog replacements to the same maps (_add_google_font_replacements_to_mapping, :1468). Uploaded files win over catalog picks for the same original name.
    • For fonts still not replaced, reuse previously uploaded fonts from font_uploads when every required variant is covered.
    • Rewrite font names inside the PPTX XML with replace_fonts_in_pptx (pptx_font_utils.py:1069) into a file named by _build_modified_pptx_filename. If there is no mapping at all, the original file is used unchanged.
    • Persist uploaded fonts permanently with persist_font_file (font_uploads.py:321), which copies the file to <app_data>/fonts/<stem>_<8 hex>.<ext> and inserts a font_uploads row.
  5. Collect font URLs for the response (_build_upload_preview_font_urls, :1246): embedded fonts, uploaded fonts, and every remaining family that resolves in the packaged catalog. The catalog replacement URLs from step 1 are merged last (fonts.update(selected_google_fonts)).
  6. Render previews (create_slide_previews, :1712, which calls render_pptx_slides_to_images, :775).
  7. Persist the modified PPTX into the session directory (upload_presentations, :1751) and convert every local path to a URL with _public_urls_for_local_paths (:1924), which produces /app_data/<relative path> URLs through absolute_fastapi_asset_url.

Gotcha

replace_fonts_in_pptx documents itself as "Replace fonts in a PPTX file using python-pptx", but its python-pptx loop only runs when both font_mapping and font_variant_mapping are empty. The only caller skips the call in that case (fonts_and_slides_preview.py:1672: if font_mapping: ... else: modified_pptx_path = pptx_path), so in practice every rewrite goes through the raw XML path _replace_fonts_in_pptx_xml (pptx_font_utils.py:1038). Edit that function, not the python-pptx branch.

docs.title: How previews are rendered (and who converts PPTX to JSON)
docs.text:
Python does not parse slide geometry. Both the conversion and the rendering are tasks for the Node export runtime, a runner.mjs resolved from EXPORT_PACKAGE_ROOT or a sibling presentation-export directory (servers/fastapi/services/export_task_service.py:129 to :151) and spawned as a child process with LITEPARSE_NODE_BINARY (default node, :124). The runtime is synced into the image at build time (both Dockerfile and Dockerfile.dev run node scripts/sync-presentation-export.cjs --force); its internals are covered in PPTX and PDF export.

render_pptx_slides_to_images makes two runtime calls:

servers/fastapi/templates/fonts_and_slides_preview.py (excerpt)
    pptx_document = await EXPORT_TASK_SERVICE.convert_pptx_to_json(modified_pptx_path)
    if not pptx_document.layouts:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="PPTX-to-JSON returned no slides")

    slide_layouts = pptx_document.layouts
    if max_slides:
        slide_layouts = slide_layouts[:max_slides]

    width, height = await asyncio.to_thread(
        _preview_dimensions_from_pptx,
        modified_pptx_path,
    )
    # ...
    rendered = await EXPORT_TASK_SERVICE.render_jsons_to_images(
        data=slide_layouts,
        width=width,
        height=height,
        fonts=fonts or None,
    )

convert_pptx_to_json (export_task_service.py:687) sends {"type": "pptx-to-json", "pptx_path": ...} and returns PptxToJsonDocument {layouts: list[dict]} (:101). render_jsons_to_images (:580) sends {"type": "json-to-images", "jsons": [...], "width", "height", "fonts"} and expects exactly one PNG path per slide; a count mismatch is a 500 (fonts_and_slides_preview.py:836). The preview width is always 1280 and the height follows the PPTX aspect ratio (_preview_dimensions_from_document, :165): the code comment explains that the export runtime normalizes PPTX-to-JSON coordinates to a 1280px-wide canvas, so a 1707x960 deck is captured at 1280x720.

The previews are therefore a rendering of the parsed JSON, not of PowerPoint itself. That is intentional: the vision passes later compare the JSON against these pixels, so both views agree on fonts and geometry.

Each preview is copied to <session_dir>/slide_<n>.png (create_slide_previews, :1741). The response:

{
  "slide_image_urls": [
    "http://localhost:8000/app_data/uploads/template-previews/3f1c.../slide_1.png",
    "http://localhost:8000/app_data/uploads/template-previews/3f1c.../slide_2.png"
  ],
  "pptx_url": "http://localhost:8000/app_data/uploads/template-previews/3f1c.../deck-modified.pptx",
  "modified_pptx_url": "http://localhost:8000/app_data/uploads/template-previews/3f1c.../deck-modified.pptx",
  "fonts": {
    "Brand Sans": "http://localhost:8000/app_data/fonts/BrandSans_1a2b3c4d.ttf",
    "Montserrat": "/vendor/fonts/sans_serif/montserrat/Montserrat[wght].ttf"
  }
}

The exact host prefix depends on absolute_fastapi_asset_url; the modified PPTX filename comes from _build_modified_pptx_filename (:1033).

Note

_build_slide_preview_html (:692) builds a full HTML document with Tailwind, Chart.js and the datalabels plugin. It is still covered by unit tests (servers/fastapi/tests/test_pptx_font_utils.py:719) but no production code path calls it anymore; previews come from the JSON renderer only.

docs.title: The MCP variant
docs.text: MCP clients cannot send multipart bodies, so POST /template/mcp-upload (template.py:1220) accepts base64. Each file is decoded with base64.b64decode(..., validate=True) (_decode_mcp_upload, :211); the PPTX may be up to 100 MiB, each font up to 10 MiB, and the combined decoded size is capped at MCP_TEMPLATE_UPLOAD_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 100 * 1024 * 1024 (:102), with a pre-check on the encoded length in McpTemplateUploadRequest.validate_combined_upload_size (:181). The decoded bytes are wrapped in UploadFile objects and passed to the same upload_fonts_and_slides_preview_handler. MCP tooling in general is covered in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

docs.title: Step 5: Start creation
docs.text:
From the preview step, the Generate Template button opens a name/description modal and then calls handleCreateTemplate (CustomTemplatePage.tsx:1446):

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/custom-template/CustomTemplatePage.tsx (excerpt)
        await TemplateService.createTemplate({
          pptx_url: state.previewData.modified_pptx_url,
          slide_image_urls: state.previewData.slide_image_urls,
          fonts: {
            ...state.previewData.fonts,
            ...selectedLocalFontAssets,
          },
          name,
          description: description || null,
        });
        // ...
        router.push("/templates?tab=custom");

TemplateService.createTemplate (app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/template.ts:205) posts that body to /api/v1/ppt/template/async. The request model is:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py (excerpt)
class InitTemplateRequest(BaseModel):
    pptx_url: str = Field(
        min_length=1,
        # ...
    )
    slide_image_urls: list[str] = Field(
        min_length=1,
        # ...
    )
    fonts: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    name: Optional[str] = None
    description: Optional[str] = None
    icon_type: Optional[IconType] = DEFAULT_ICON_TYPE
    generation_options: LayoutGenerationOptions = Field(
        default_factory=LayoutGenerationOptions
    )

LayoutGenerationOptions (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/layouts.py:34) is extra="forbid", strict=True with three booleans, all default true: text_growth, visual_replacement, flexible_grouping. The semantic pass always runs.

create_template (template.py:1574) then:

  1. Resolves pptx_url to a file with resolve_app_path_to_filesystem. A URL that is not a file inside Presenton's own app-data (for example a host application's attachment id) is rejected with 400 before any task is stored (:1581).
  2. Pre-allocates template_id = str(uuid.uuid4()). The template row does not exist yet; the id is reserved in the task data so retries reuse it.
  3. Inserts an AsyncTaskModel with type="template.create", status=PENDING, message="Queued for template creation", and payload equal to the request (with generation_options included only if the caller sent it, _explicit_template_generation_options, :558).
  4. Sets task.data with _template_task_progress_data (:396).
  5. Schedules _run_create_template_task(task.id, get_current_owner_id()) on BackgroundTasks and returns the task.

The progress object stored in task.data and returned by the async-task API has this exact shape:

{
  "async_task_id": "6f0c...",
  "template_v2_id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "attempt": 1,
  "created_layouts": 3,
  "remaining_layouts": 9,
  "slide_layout_statuses": [
    {"index": 0, "status": "completed"},
    {"index": 1, "status": "pending"}
  ],
  "name": "Quarterly Review",
  "thumbnail": "http://localhost:8000/app_data/uploads/template-previews/.../slide_1.png"
}

thumbnail is the first non-empty slide image URL (_template_request_thumbnail, :444); name falls back to the PPTX filename without extension via _derive_template_name (:455), and finally to "Untitled template".

Gotcha

The background task runs in the same process as the API, through Starlette's BackgroundTasks. There is no queue or worker: if the process restarts mid-creation, the task stays pending forever and the template row is never written. Recovery is the retry route, which only accepts tasks in ERROR state (Step 9). The async-task table itself is described in REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP.

docs.title: Step 6: Prepare the template source in the background
docs.text:
_run_create_template_task (template.py:1482) restores the owner context (set_current_owner_id(owner_id), set_current_owner_is_admin(False); see Auth and multi-user), opens its own session from async_session_maker, re-validates task.payload as a CreateTemplateRequest, sets message="Creating template" and then "Generating slide layouts", and calls _create_template_with_task_progress (:1403).

That function begins with _prepare_template_source (:925), shared with init:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py (excerpt)
    pptx_json = await EXPORT_TASK_SERVICE.convert_pptx_to_json(pptx_path)
    try:
        raw_layouts = RawSlideLayouts.model_validate(
            pptx_json.model_dump(mode="json")
        )
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # ...
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=500,
            detail="PPTX-to-JSON export produced invalid slide layout JSON",
        ) from exc
    # ...
    if len(raw_layouts.layouts) > len(request.slide_image_urls):
        # ...
        raw_layouts = RawSlideLayouts(
            layouts=raw_layouts.layouts[: len(request.slide_image_urls)]
        )
    elif len(request.slide_image_urls) > len(raw_layouts.layouts):
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail="Exactly one slide image is required for each slide layout",
        )

The PPTX is converted a second time (the preview step's JSON is not reused). The result validates into RawSlideLayouts, a list of RawSlideLayout {id, description, elements} (layouts.py:44); the element models are the Template v2 element union described in Template v2 format. Extra slides beyond the preview count are dropped silently, because the preview step may have trimmed the deck to 50 slides; extra preview images are an error. The function returns (pptx_path, raw_layouts, raw_layouts_json, fonts) where fonts is the request's font map cleaned by _coerce_font_map (:863, keeps only non-empty string keys and values).

A first progress commit with zero completed layouts follows (_commit_template_task_progress, :664).

docs.title: Step 7: Certify every slide (four vision passes)
docs.text:
_generate_slide_layouts_with_task_progress (template.py:709) is the async driver. It requires one image per raw slide, creates a ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=min(MAX_PARALLEL_SLIDE_LAYOUTS, slide_count)) with MAX_PARALLEL_SLIDE_LAYOUTS = 10 (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/generation.py:47), and submits one generate_slide_layout per slide with max_tokens=SLIDE_LAYOUT_GENERATION_MAX_TOKENS. Each submission runs inside copy_context().run so context variables such as the current owner survive the thread hop. As each future completes (asyncio.as_completed), the slide index is added to completed_layout_indices and progress is committed immediately, which is how the UI can show per-slide ticks. If any slide raises, the remaining tasks are cancelled and the error propagates.

templates.v2.generation.generate_slide_layout (generation.py:612) is a thin public wrapper over certified_generation.generate_slide_layout (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py:3651). That is the core of the chapter.

flowchart TD
    S["RawSlideLayout + slide PNG"] --> V{"visual_replacement and candidates?"}
    V -- yes --> VP["Pass 1: VisualDataReplacementPlan"]
    V -- no --> SM
    VP -- "fails" --> SM["Pass 2: SemanticSlideManifest"]
    VP -- "ok: apply replacements" --> SM
    SM -- "fails" --> FB["_fallback_slide_layout"]
    SM -- ok --> F{"flexible_grouping?"}
    F -- yes --> FP["Pass 3: FlexibleSlidePlan"]
    F -- no --> T
    FP --> T{"text_growth?"}
    T -- yes --> TP["Pass 4: TextCapacityPlan"]
    T -- no --> C
    TP --> C["Compile: up to 4 attempts"]
    C -- "all fail" --> FB
    C -- ok --> R["_replace_content_image_urls"]
    FB --> R
    R --> OUT["Certified SlideLayout"]

Every pass uses the same machinery, _generate_structured_with_provider_fallback (certified_generation.py:4305): a system prompt, a user message containing the slide image (as raw bytes when the URL resolves to a local file, _openai_image_part, :4194) and a JSON payload, a JSON Schema response format with strict=False, Pydantic validation of the parsed JSON, and an extra_validator that checks semantic rules against the source. On any exception it appends the bad response and a repair prompt and tries again:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt)
    response_schema = _llm_output_json_schema(output_model)
    effective_max_tokens = max_tokens or TEMPLATE_GENERATION_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS
    attempts_per_provider = max(1, validation_retries)
    last_error: Exception | None = None

    for provider in providers or _template_structured_providers():

With DEFAULT_VALIDATION_RETRIES = 5 (:59) that is five attempts in total per pass, not five retries after a first try. _template_structured_providers (:4204) returns a single provider built from the configured client and model (get_client(config=get_llm_config()), get_model()), resolved through the public generation module so tests and integrations can monkeypatch it. Gemini models get a special visual-data schema and an extra table-encoding instruction (_response_schema_for_model, :4257; _messages_for_structured_provider, :4271).

docs.title: Pass 1: visual data detection
docs.text:
Only when options.visual_replacement is true. _visual_data_generation_payload (:1076) sends the source layout id/description, every top-level element with its source_index (with decorative stripped), and visual_region_candidates: every container, group or non-icon image element at least 24x12 px, found recursively through child and children (_visual_data_region_candidates_in_element, :1105). Each candidate carries a path such as elements.3.children.1, its bounds, and a content preview.

The model returns a VisualDataReplacementPlan (layouts.py:497): a list of replacements discriminated by kind (chart, infographic, table, text-list; layouts.py:173, :390, :432, :449). Each names a primary path, the extra top-level consumed_paths it absorbs, typed data, and (except for text lists) new bounds. The intent, per DETECT_VISUAL_DATA_REGIONS_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:180), is to turn a chart that the PPTX stored as a picture or as a pile of shapes into a real editable chart element. _apply_visual_data_replacement_plan (:1291) swaps the elements in. If the pass fails for any reason the exception is logged and the source regions are kept.

docs.title: Pass 2: semantic manifest (the only mandatory pass)
docs.text:
_semantic_generation_payload (:1555) sends:

{
  "source_layout": {"id": "slide_4", "description": "..."},
  "available_font_families": ["Brand Sans", "Montserrat"],
  "indexed_elements": [{"source_index": 0, "element": {"type": "vector", "...": "..."}}],
  "editable_candidates": [
    {"path": "elements.2", "type": "text", "current_name": null, "content_preview": "Quarterly results"}
  ]
}

Candidates are all text, image, text-list, table, chart and supported infographic elements at any depth (_SEMANTIC_ELEMENT_TYPES, :1054). The system prompt GENERATE_SLIDE_LAYOUT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:111) is long and opinionated.
