Its key rules: partition the elements into the smallest useful reusable components; keep a repeated collection (cards, steps, metrics) together in one component; mark replaceable content decorative=false and scaffolding (backgrounds, logos, frames, connectors, rings) decorative=true; name fields in generic snake_case from structure, never from sample content; set is_icon, an icon color and an icon_type (bold, duotone, fill, light, regular, thin) on every image annotation.

The reply is a SemanticSlideManifest (layouts.py:575): id (snake_case, at most 80 chars), description (10 to 300 chars), components with element_indices, and one annotation per candidate path. _validate_semantic_manifest (:1640) enforces, among other things:

  • every source index is assigned to exactly one component, in ascending order within each component;
  • repeated_items must be null in this pass;
  • annotation paths equal the candidate paths exactly (it reports missing= and extra= lists in the error so the repair prompt can fix them);
  • only image annotations may carry is_icon; icon annotations must carry color and icon_type;
  • charts, infographics, tables and text lists can never be decorative.

If this pass fails after five attempts, the slide does not fail. generate_slide_layout logs "semantic pass failed; using fidelity-preserving fallback" and returns _fallback_slide_layout (:3874). _fallback_semantic_manifest (:3593) puts every element into one component called slide_content, makes all text, charts, tables, lists and infographics editable, keeps images' existing decorative flag, and derives safe identifiers from the element names.

docs.title: Pass 3: flexible regions
docs.text:
Only when options.flexible_grouping is true. The payload is the manifest plus indexed elements (_flexible_generation_payload, :1729). The model returns a FlexibleSlidePlan (layouts.py:696, whose regions are FlexibleRegionPlan objects, layouts.py:663): at most one region per component, each a tree of flow nodes with mode row, column, grid or group and at least two items, each item either a list of source indices (a leaf) or a nested flow_id. _validate_flexible_plan (:2512) checks geometry: repeated items must be structurally equivalent (_region_items_are_structurally_equivalent, :2649), must not overlap, and regular repeats must have regular spacing (_validate_regular_repeat_geometry, :2814). Failure leaves FlexibleSlidePlan(regions=[]).

When compiled (_compile_flow_node, :3088), a flow becomes a flex, grid or group element. A repeatable flow gets elastic limits, which is what lets generation produce three cards from a four-card source:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt)
    min_children = max(1, (len(children) + 1) // 2) if repeatable else len(children)
    base: dict[str, Any] = {
        "type": "group" if mode == "group" else "grid" if mode == "grid" else "flex",
        "name": flow.name,
        "position": {"x": 0.0, "y": 0.0},
        "size": {
            "width": node_bounds["width"],
            "height": round(compiled_height, 2),
        },
        "children": children,
    }
    if mode != "group":
        base["min_children"] = min_children
        base["max_children"] = len(children)

So a repeated region with 4 source items accepts 2 to 4 items, and one with 5 accepts 3 to 5. How the schema builder exposes these limits to the content LLM is covered in From template to schema to slide.

docs.title: Pass 4: text capacity
docs.text:
Only when options.text_growth is true. The payload adds editable_text_boxes (the non-decorative text elements with their paths, _text_capacity_generation_payload, :1746). The model returns TextCapacityAdjustment items (layouts.py:716) per path: left_characters and right_characters (0 to 200), top_lines and bottom_lines (0 to 12), and a horizontal and vertical alignment. It never returns pixels; the compiler converts characters and lines into geometry and refuses growth that would collide with other content.

Independently of the LLM, every editable text box gets geometry-derived length limits (_normalize_existing_text_box_limits, :2391). The estimate is deliberately crude:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt)
def _estimated_text_capacity(element: dict[str, Any], *, max_lines: int) -> int:
    capacity_units = _estimated_text_capacity_units(
        element,
        max_lines=max_lines,
    )
    current_text = "".join(
        str(run.get("text") or run.get("latex") or "")
        for run in element.get("runs", [])
        if isinstance(run, dict)
    )
    return max(
        len(current_text),
        math.floor(capacity_units * TEXT_CAPACITY_SAFETY_FACTOR),
    )

Capacity units are floor(width / char_width) * line_count, where a character is 0.58 x font_size wide (0.62 when bold) plus letter spacing (_estimated_text_character_width, :2449), the font size defaults to 18 and the line height to 1.2 x font_size (_text_capacity_geometry, :2483), and the line count is capped at 12. The safety factor is TEXT_CAPACITY_SAFETY_FACTOR = 0.85 (:62). max_length is only ever raised, never lowered, and never set below the length of the sample text.

docs.title: Compile and certify
docs.text:
The four plans are fed to _compile_semantic_layout (:2895) with a fallback ladder:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt)
    compile_attempts = [
        (flexible_plan, text_capacity_plan),
        (flexible_plan, TextCapacityPlan(adjustments=[])),
        (FlexibleSlidePlan(regions=[]), text_capacity_plan),
        (FlexibleSlidePlan(regions=[]), TextCapacityPlan(adjustments=[])),
    ]

Duplicate combinations are skipped by a JSON signature. The compiler deep-copies the source elements, writes each annotation's name, decorative, is_icon, color and icon_type onto the element at its path, marks unsupported infographics decorative, applies text limits and growth, and then builds components. Two details matter when you modify it:

  • Component positions are the bounding box of their elements on the 1280x720 canvas, and element positions are rewritten to be local to that box (_localize_top_level_element, :3050).
  • Components are sorted by their lowest source index, not by the model's order. The code comment explains why: the model may return components in reading order, which could lift a full-slide background above the title and hide it.

_certify_compiled_layout (:3491) then rejects the result if any component is empty, any number is non-finite, any size is not positive, any min_* exceeds its max_* (_SCHEMA_LIMIT_PAIRS, :1066), a table row length differs from its column count, a chart series length differs from its categories, a flex/grid child count falls outside min_children..max_children, a grid's columns x rows cannot hold its children, or a component has editable elements but get_component_schema returns no schema. If all four attempts fail, the fidelity-preserving fallback is compiled instead.

docs.title: Placeholders for editable images and icons
docs.text:
The last step on every path is _replace_content_image_urls (:3886), which walks every element with _replace_content_image_url_in_element (:3902):

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/certified_generation.py (excerpt)
    if isinstance(element, SlideImageElement) and element.decorative is False:
        if not replace_visuals:
            element.decorative = True
        elif element.is_icon:
            element.data = CONTENT_ICON_PLACEHOLDER_URL
        else:
            element.data = CONTENT_IMAGE_PLACEHOLDER_URL
            element.fit = ImageFit.COVER

Editable photos become /static/images/replaceable_template_image.png with fit: cover; editable icons become /static/icons/placeholder.svg. Decorative images keep their original /app_data/... URL. With visual_replacement=false, editable images are instead frozen as decorative.

Gotcha

generate_slide_layout never raises for LLM quality problems: semantic failure and compile failure both fall back to a one-component "preserve everything" layout. A template full of slide_content components with generic field names is the visible symptom of a weak or non-vision model. Check the logs for semantic pass failed before debugging the renderer.

After all slides finish, _ensure_unique_async_slide_layout_ids (template.py:686) suffixes duplicate ids with _<n>, and _with_randomized_layout_ids (:833) appends a random _1000 to _9999 suffix to every layout id, so a certified title_with_image_cards becomes, for example, title_with_image_cards_4821.

docs.title: Step 8: Cluster components and derive the theme, then persist
docs.text: Two jobs run concurrently with asyncio.gather (template.py:1447), each in its own single-thread executor (_run_template_generation_thread, :809).

docs.title: Merged components
docs.text:
merge_similar_components (certified_generation.py:550) flattens every component of every layout into one indexed list and sends compact summaries (_component_clustering_summary, :600: id, description, position, content bounds, the flattened element type hierarchy, and the editable JSON schema) to the LLM with CLUSTER_SIMILAR_COMPONENTS_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:445). The reply is a SimilarComponentsList of index groups; _validate_similarity_groups (:623) rejects out-of-range or repeated indices. _build_merged_components (:642) turns each group into a MergedComponent {id, description, variants} (layouts.py:81), and every component not in a group becomes its own singleton.

A deterministic pass then runs: _deduplicate_merged_components (:670) computes a structural signature for every variant (_component_duplicate_signature, :740) and unions groups that share a signature. The signature ignores names and min/max limits (_IGNORED_DUPLICATE_SCHEMA_KEYS, :79), ignores replaceable content values (text runs, list items, image data, chart data; _CONTENT_VALUE_KEYS_BY_ELEMENT_TYPE, :94), and snaps positions and sizes to a grid relative to the component size (_DUPLICATE_POSITION_GRID_UNITS = 5, :78).

If clustering raises a ValidationError or ValueError, _merge_generated_components (template.py:626) stores an empty MergedComponents(components=[]) and creation continues. Merged components feed the editor's insert palette and the prompted-layout generator (Step 10).

docs.title: Semantic theme
docs.text: generate_template_theme (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py:246) profiles every color and font in the certified layouts (build_theme_profile, :145), asks the LLM to assign roles by profile id (select_theme_roles_with_llm, :261, 2 retries, 2,000 max tokens), falls back to select_theme_roles_deterministically (:305) on any error, and materializes a PresentationThemeData (materialize_theme, :357). If even that raises, _generate_generated_theme (template.py:649) stores theme=None. The profile, the role rules and the contrast repair are explained in Themes and fonts.

docs.title: The row
docs.text:
_build_created_template (template.py:1320) assembles the TemplateV2 row with the pre-allocated id:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py (excerpt)
    return TemplateV2(
        id=template_id or str(uuid.uuid4()),
        name=(request.name or "").strip() or _derive_template_name(
            request.pptx_url, pptx_path
        ),
        description=request.description,
        raw_layouts=raw_layouts_json,
        merged_components=merged_components.model_dump(
            mode="json", exclude_none=True
        ),
        layouts=generated_layouts.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True),
        theme=(
            generated_theme.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
            if generated_theme is not None
            else None
        ),
        assets={
            **_explicit_template_generation_options(request),
            "icon_type": icon_type,
            "icon_weight": icon_type,
            "fonts": available_fonts,
            "slide_image_urls": request.slide_image_urls,
            "images": _collect_image_urls_from_layouts(raw_layouts_json),
        },
    )

icon_type is the most common icon_type across all certified icon images (_most_common_icon_type_in_layouts, :520), falling back to the request's icon_type. assets.images lists every distinct image.data URL found in the raw layouts. raw_layouts is kept so a single slide can be re-certified later without re-uploading the PPTX. The column layout of template_v2 is described in Template v2 format.

On success the task becomes COMPLETED with message="Template creation completed". On any exception it becomes ERROR with message="Template creation failed" and error set to an APIErrorModel dump; non-HTTP exceptions are reduced to a generic 500 "Template creation failed" so internal messages do not leak.

docs.title: Step 9: Track progress and retry
docs.text:
The template library polls. useTemplateSummaries({ includeProcessingTemplateTasks: true }) (app/(presentation-generator)/hooks/useTemplateSummaries.ts) loads default and custom templates with two GET /template/all?page_size=100&default=... calls, plus GET /api/v1/async-tasks?type=template.create&order_by=created_at&order=desc&limit=50&offset=0&created_at=<one hour ago> (services/api/template.ts:219). It keeps tasks whose status is pending or error and re-polls every 30 seconds (setInterval(..., 30000)), refreshing the template list whenever a pending task was seen. The panel ((dashboard)/templates/components/TemplatePanel.tsx:69) offers a retry button whose handler calls the hook's retryTemplateTask, which in turn calls TemplateService.retryTemplateCreateTask (useTemplateSummaries.ts:194).

retry_create_template (template.py:1626) only accepts a task that exists (404), has type template.create (400), is in ERROR (409), still has a dict payload (409), and whose reserved template_v2_id does not already exist as a row (409 "Template has already been created"). It resets the same task to PENDING, increments attempt, and schedules the same background function. The whole PPTX is processed again from scratch.

Gotcha

GET /template/all filters out any template whose layouts is empty (if layout_count == 0: continue, template.py:1164), and paginates in Python after loading every row. A row created by init stays invisible in the library until at least one layout is patched in. The frontend applies the same rule again in filterTemplatesWithLayouts.

docs.title: Step 10: The incremental routes
docs.text:
These routes exist for the per-slide flow, for the editor, and for API users who want control.

POST /template/init (template.py:1277) runs _prepare_template_source and immediately inserts a row with layouts=None and assets {pptx_url, icon_type, icon_weight, fonts, slide_image_urls, images, layout_indexes: []}. It returns the id as a JSON string.

POST /template/layouts/create (:1789) accepts index or indices (never both; at most MAX_PARALLEL_SLIDE_LAYOUTS = 10, unique, non-negative; CreateTemplateLayoutsRequest._validate_indices, :241). It loads raw_layouts, checks each index is in range and has a stored slide image, merges saved and override generation options (_template_generation_options, :564), and runs _generate_indexed_slide_layouts (:1071) in a thread. It returns {layouts: [{index, layout}]} but does not save anything.

PATCH /template/{id}/layouts (:1929) saves. It serializes concurrent patches to the same template with a per-template asyncio.Lock (_get_template_layout_patch_lock, :916) so out-of-order saves from parallel slide generations cannot overwrite each other. _merge_template_layout_items (:1031) keys existing layouts by their original slide index (stored in assets.layout_indexes), inserts or replaces the patched ones, sorts by index, and re-validates SlideLayouts. Duplicate layout ids are rejected by the SlideLayouts validator (test test_patch_template_slide_layout_rejects_duplicate_layout_ids, test_template_api.py:1633).

POST /template/generate-blocks (:1874) runs the Step 8 clustering and theme jobs on the saved layouts and stores merged_components and, if non-null, theme.

POST /template/layouts/generate (:1700) creates a brand-new layout from a text prompt. generate_prompted_slide_layout (generation.py:631) ranks existing layouts and merged components by how many prompt words (longer than two characters) appear in their ids and descriptions, sends at most 4 reference layouts and 8 reusable components (PROMPTED_LAYOUT_MAX_REFERENCE_LAYOUTS, PROMPTED_LAYOUT_MAX_REUSABLE_COMPONENTS, :114), trims the context to 160,000 characters, and asks for one SlideLayout under GENERATE_PROMPTED_TEMPLATE_LAYOUT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (:88). The extra validator requires a snake_case id matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{2,79}$ that is not already used, at least one component, and at least one decorative=false element. Images marked editable get the standard placeholders. The result is a draft returned to the caller; the editor must save it.

PATCH /template/{id} (:1976) updates only the fields present in the body (model_fields_set): name (blank is 400), description, merged_components (validated), layouts (validated, layout_indexes recomputed, icon_type re-derived), theme, thumbnail (stored in assets.thumbnail; blank removes it), fonts (stored in assets.fonts), icon_type. An id in the body must match the path (400). A body with nothing to update returns the template without writing.

The preview tool that production does not use

templates/v2/tools.py defines PreviewSlideTool, an LLM tool named previewSlide that renders a candidate SlideLayout to a 1280x720 PNG through the export runtime's render_json_to_image and saves debug artifacts to <app_data>/preview_slide/<slide>/<n>.json|png. _generate_preview_candidate (generation.py:852) implements a loop that lets the model call it at most twice (MAX_PREVIEW_SLIDE_CALLS = 2). In this snapshot that loop is exercised only by unit tests (servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_templates_v2_generation.py:141); certified generation uses structured responses only, which matches the "Tool calling: Optional" row in docs/template-v2.md.

docs.title: Step 11: The template editor
docs.text:
After creation, the library links to /template-preview?templateV2Id=<id> (TemplatePanel.tsx:59). TemplatePreviewClient.tsx loads the template with GET /template/{id} (TemplateService.getTemplateDetails, services/api/template.ts:142, which strips an optional template-v2- prefix from the id) and the theme with GET /template/{id}/theme (TemplatePreviewClient.tsx:236). Editing is allowed only when !template.is_default (canEditTemplate, :275).

What can be edited, and how it is saved:

Action Where Backend call Move, resize, restyle elements on the Konva canvas handlePreviewLayoutChange (:405) none until Save Edit layout id and description handleLayoutMetadataChange (:451) none until Save Edit a schema field's sample value, its min/max constraint, or toggle decorative handleSchemaFieldChange (:493), handleSchemaConstraintChange (:512), handleSchemaDecorationChange (:529) none until Save Preview content density (fill text and repeated arrays to min or max) applyContentDensity none (preview only) Duplicate a layout duplicateActiveLayout (id suffixed -copy) none until Save Generate a new slide from a prompt TemplatePreviewClient.tsx:648 POST /template/layouts/generate Re-certify the active slide from the original PPTX reconstructActiveLayout (:783) POST /template/layouts/create Save saveTemplate (:1046) PATCH /template/{id} with the full template, edited layouts and layout_count Delete :1139 DELETE /template/{id}

Before saving, the editor dispatches COMMIT_TEMPLATE_V2_INLINE_TEXT_EVENT and waits one tick so an open inline text editor flushes its pending change (:1064). buildTemplateSavePayload (template-preview/components/editor/templatePreviewUtils.ts:1179) clones the loaded template record and replaces layouts, name, id and layout_count. Every TemplateService write invalidates the 5-minute theme cache for that template (invalidateTemplateTheme). The Konva canvas and inline text editing are the same components the slide editor uses; see Slide editor.

Gotcha

The studio also contains a second, per-slide creation path in useTemplateCreation.ts (generateTemplateV2, :446): init, then one layouts/create call per slide (TEMPLATE_V2_LAYOUT_BATCH_SIZE = 1, awaited sequentially), a PATCH .../layouts after each, then generate-blocks. In this snapshot CustomTemplatePage destructures only retrySlide from that part of the hook, so the button path is the async route. If you wire initTemplateCreation back in, remember that it processes slides one at a time and never benefits from the ten-thread pool.

docs.title: Step 12: Turning a stored template into a bundled template
docs.text: Two Node scripts turn a stored template into the bundle format that the 16 built-in templates under templates/<id>/template.json use. Both are pure file transformations; neither talks to the API.

docs.title: scripts/convert-template.mjs
docs.text:
node scripts/convert-template.mjs <input.json> [--output <path>] [--app-data <dir>] converts a template JSON (for example a GET /template/{id} response saved to disk) into the bundle format:

  1. buildTargetShape (scripts/convert-template.mjs:81) keeps exactly id, name, description, thumbnail, merged_components, layouts, fonts (TOP_LEVEL_KEYS, :17). layouts and merged_components may be arrays or wrapped objects ({layouts: [...]}, {components: [...]}) and are unwrapped. id falls back to the output directory name; thumbnail falls back to the first assets.slide_image_urls entry; fonts comes from assets.fonts or fonts.
  2. replaceEditableImages (:116) rewrites every non-decorative image's data to the icon or image placeholder, exactly like Step 7.
  3. planAssets (:206) finds every string that points into app-data (/app_data/... URLs, app_data/... paths, or absolute paths under the app-data root) or into a sibling static/ folder, verifies each file exists, and plans a copy into <output dir>/static/. The thumbnail is renamed thumbnail.<ext>; name collisions get a 12-character SHA-256 suffix. Every planned path is checked with assertInside so a crafted path cannot escape the root.
  4. rewriteStrings (:257) replaces those strings with static/<name>, the files are copied, stale files in static/ are deleted (cleanStaticDirectory, :268), and the JSON is written with two-space indentation.

At startup, default_templates.py rewrites static/... back to /app_data/templates/<id>/static/... and copies the folder into app-data; see From template to schema to slide.

docs.title: scripts/convert-presentation-template.mjs
docs.text:
node scripts/convert-presentation-template.mjs <presentation.json> [--output] [--app-data] [--id] [--name] [--description] [--thumbnail] starts from a presentation detail response instead. This lets a designer tweak slides in the normal editor and fold those edits back into the template. buildTemplateFromPresentation (scripts/convert-presentation-template.mjs:133):

  1. Reads the presentation's layout (the copied template payload), its merged_components, and its slides.
  2. Collects each slide's edited ui tree keyed by its layout id; two slides with conflicting edits of the same layout are an error.
  3. For each edited layout, finds every original component in the original merged catalog by deep equality (findVariant, :80; exactly one match required), replaces that variant with the edited component, marks removed components, and appends components that were added in the editor as new singleton groups.
  4. Verifies every final component is present in the final catalog, then hands the result to convertTemplateData for asset packaging.

The scripts are covered by scripts/convert-template.test.mjs and scripts/convert-presentation-template.test.mjs.

Gotcha

TOP_LEVEL_KEYS in convert-template.mjs does not include theme, yet every bundled template.json in this snapshot has a theme block. Running the converter on a template drops its theme; you have to add it back by hand (or extend buildTargetShape) before committing a bundle, otherwise get_template_theme will derive a deterministic theme at first request.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• The studio does three requests: POST /fonts/check, POST /template/fonts-upload-and-slides-preview (font fixing, PPTX-to-JSON and Chromium previews in the Node export runtime, capped at 50 slides), and POST /template/async, which runs creation as an in-process background task with per-slide progress in async_task.data.
  • Each slide is certified by up to four schema-validated vision passes (visual data, semantic manifest, flexible regions, text capacity), each with five total attempts, followed by a four-step compile ladder and a fidelity-preserving fallback, all with up to 10 slides in parallel.
  • Text limits come from a character-width heuristic with a 0.85 safety factor; repeatable flows accept from half to all of their source items.
  • Component clustering and the semantic theme run in parallel after certification; both degrade gracefully (empty catalog, deterministic or no theme).
  • Incremental routes (init, layouts/create, PATCH .../layouts, generate-blocks, layouts/generate) let the editor re-certify or invent single slides, and built-in templates are read-only.
  • convert-template.mjs and convert-presentation-template.mjs package stored templates and edited decks into templates/<id>/template.json plus static/ assets.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Themes and fonts to see how the theme derived here and the font maps collected here are stored, overridden and applied in the browser.

docs.title: Themes and fonts
docs.text: Reads: servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py, servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py, servers/fastapi/templates/pptx_font_utils.py, servers/nextjs/lib/template-theme.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/applyPresentationThemeDom.ts, servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/local-fonts.ts, nginx.conf · Builds on: Custom templates from PPTX · Time: ~35 min

docs.title: What you will learn
docs.text:
A Presenton "theme" is a small JSON object with sixteen color roles and one text font, and a "font map" is a dictionary from family name to font file URL. This chapter specifies both, shows how a theme is derived from a template's layouts, where themes and fonts are stored on templates and presentations and which one wins, how the browser loads fonts and applies the theme, and where fonts live on disk and on the wire. It also explains the one surprising fact that governs everything else: template slides carry literal colors and font families, so the theme mostly affects newly inserted content, not existing slides.

flowchart LR
    TJ["templates/id/template.json: theme + fonts"] --> IMP["import at startup"]
    PPTX["custom PPTX"] --> GEN["generate_template_theme"]
    IMP --> TV2["template_v2.theme, template_v2.assets.fonts"]
    GEN --> TV2
    TV2 --> API["GET /template/id/theme"]
    TV2 --> PRES["presentations.fonts (always), presentations.theme (API generate only)"]
    API --> FE["usePresentationData: fetched ?? stored ?? default"]
    PRES --> FE
    FE --> CSS["CSS variables + font-family on the slides wrapper"]
    FE --> INS["Insert palette: themed new elements"]
    PRES --> FL["useFontLoader: inject @font-face"]

docs.title: Step 1: The theme data model
docs.text:
The backend contract is four Pydantic models in servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py:

servers/fastapi/models/theme_data.py (excerpt)
class PresentationThemeColors(BaseModel):
    primary: str
    background: str
    card: str
    stroke: str
    background_text: str
    primary_text: str
    graph_0: str
    graph_1: str
    # ... graph_2 to graph_8
    graph_9: str


class PresentationThemeTextFont(BaseModel):
    name: str
    url: str


class PresentationThemeFonts(BaseModel):
    textFont: PresentationThemeTextFont


class PresentationThemeData(BaseModel):
    colors: PresentationThemeColors
    fonts: PresentationThemeFonts
Role Meaning (from THEME_ROLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py:131) CSS variable set by the frontend background a large, frequently repeated surface color --background-color primary the dominant branded or accent color, not a neutral background --primary-color card a secondary surface --card-color stroke a subtle structural or border color --stroke background_text text color that contrasts with background --background-text primary_text text color that contrasts with primary --primary-text graph_0 to graph_9 distinct chart and accent colors, in order --graph-0 to --graph-9 fonts.textFont {name, url} the dominant readable font font-family, --heading-font-family, --body-font-family

Note the camelCase textFont inside an otherwise snake_case model; the frontend reads exactly that key. Every built-in template.json carries a theme block in this shape. For example, templates/momentum/template.json has primary: "#213EBB", background: "#F6F7FC", primary_text: "#FFFFFF", background_text: "#000000" and textFont: {"name": "Lato", "url": "static/Lato Regular.ttf"}.

The TypeScript mirror is TemplateTheme in servers/nextjs/lib/template-theme.ts: a flat record of the same sixteen keys (TEMPLATE_THEME_COLOR_KEYS, lib/template-theme.ts:1) plus an optional fonts.textFont. The frontend flattens colors into the top level.

docs.title: Step 2: Where themes and fonts are stored
docs.text:
Column Type Written by Shape template_v2.theme JSON default template import, template creation, generate-blocks, PATCH /template/{id}, lazy derivation in GET /template/{id}/theme PresentationThemeData dump template_v2.assets.fonts inside JSON assets default template import (_build_assets, servers/fastapi/templates/default_templates.py), template creation, PATCH /template/{id} with fonts {family: url} presentations.fonts JSON (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:74) POST /presentation/create/blank (when a template id is given), prepare, generate, and the stream endpoint as a fallback (presentation.py:2027) {family: url} copied from the template presentations.theme JSON (servers/fastapi/models/sql/presentation.py:73) only the API generate path a wrapper around the template theme (below) font_uploads table (servers/fastapi/models/sql/font_upload.py) POST /fonts/upload, template font uploads, disk backfill one row per font file

The migrations are servers/fastapi/alembic/versions/e4c7a9b2d6f1_add_theme_to_template_v2.py, f42ad4074449_add_theme_column_to_presentations.py (an idempotent _has_column guard; 82abdbc476a7 has the same title), 9b2d1c4e5f6a_add_fonts_column_to_presentations.py and 5d7e9a1b2c3f_add_font_uploads.py. The schema as a whole is covered in Data model.

docs.title: How a presentation gets its fonts and theme
docs.text:
When a presentation is created from a template, the backend copies the template's font map, never a mutable reference:

servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py (excerpt)
def _extract_template_fonts_from_assets(assets: Any) -> Optional[dict[str, str]]:
    if not isinstance(assets, dict):
        return None
    return _coerce_presentation_font_map(assets.get("fonts"))

_coerce_presentation_font_map (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:322) keeps only non-empty string names and URLs and returns None for an empty map. The UI flow sets presentation.fonts = template_fonts in prepare_presentation (presentation.py:1919); blank presentations get them at creation (:1810); the API generate_presentation_handler sets both fonts=template_fonts and theme=template_theme (:2957 to :2958).

The API path's theme is not the raw template theme but a wrapper built by template_theme_for_presentation (servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py:405):

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py (excerpt)
    if not isinstance(theme, dict):
        return None
    return {
        "name": f"{template_name} Theme",
        "description": template_description or "Theme generated from the template",
        "data": json.loads(json.dumps(theme)),
        "source": "template",
        "template_id": template_id,
    }

During streaming, the backend also emits the font map as an SSE event {"type": "fonts", "fonts": {...}} (presentation.py:1953, :2037), which usePresentationStreaming.ts:407 merges into the Redux presentation. See Streaming (SSE).

Gotcha

There is no API that changes a presentation's theme. PATCH /api/v1/ppt/presentation/update (presentation.py:2527) accepts only id, n_slides, title and slides; a theme key in the body is ignored. servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_presentation_template_theme_updates.py pins this: updates with {"theme": None} or a new theme leave the stored theme unchanged. The chat assistant reads the theme (get_template_theme in servers/fastapi/services/chat/memory_layer.py:1265, documented as "without offering theme customization") but cannot write it.

docs.title: Step 3: Deriving a theme from layouts
docs.text: When a custom template is created (see Custom templates from PPTX), or when GET /template/{id}/theme finds no valid stored theme, the backend derives one in three stages.

docs.title: Stage 1: profile
docs.text:
build_theme_profile(layouts, available_fonts) (theme.py:145) walks every element of every layout with _collect_element_profile (:431) and records per-color statistics in _ColorStats (:91):

Source in the element JSON Counted as fill fill (with normalized area = width x height / (1280 x 720), clamped to 1) stroke stroke color (icon tint) fill font.color, and font.color inside runs, items, columns, rows text table cell color fills inside columns and rows fill colors[] infographic for infographic elements, else chart title_color, legend_color, text_color text axis_color, grid_color stroke

Every text color is also paired with the nearest enclosing fill (the "effective background"); text with no enclosing fill is paired with the slide's largest fill. Fonts are counted by family (case-insensitive) with an average size (_record_font, :590).

Colors are then clustered: sorted by an importance score, and any color within RGB Euclidean distance 8 of an existing cluster is merged into it (NEAR_COLOR_DISTANCE = 8.0, :30; _cluster_colors, :638). The importance score is:

servers/fastapi/templates/v2/theme.py (excerpt)
    @property
    def importance(self) -> float:
        return (
            self.fill_area * 12
            + self.fill_count
            + self.text_count * 1.5
            + self.stroke_count * 0.75
            + self.chart_count * 2
            + self.infographic_count * 2
            + len(self.slides)
        )

The profile keeps at most 14 colors (ids c0..c13), 8 foreground/background pairs with their WCAG contrast ratio, and 5 fonts (ids f0..f4) (MAX_PROFILE_COLORS, MAX_PROFILE_PAIRS, MAX_PROFILE_FONTS, :27 to :29). Fonts that appear in the template's font map but not in the layouts are added with a usage count of zero, and each profile font carries its URL from the map when one exists (_build_profile_fonts, :604). If the layouts contain no colors at all, the profile is seeded with #FFFFFF, #111111, #2563EB and #E5E7EB.

docs.title: Stage 2: role selection
docs.text:
generate_template_theme (:246) first asks the LLM. select_theme_roles_with_llm (:261) sends the profile with font URLs removed, compact JSON, and requires a ThemeRoleSelection (:77) whose values are profile ids only. Its validator rejects unknown ids; it uses 2 validation retries and 2,000 max tokens. On any exception it falls back to select_theme_roles_deterministically (:305):

  • background: max by (fill_area, slide_count, fill_count, -saturation).
  • primary: among the rest, max by (chart_count + infographic_count, saturation, fill_count, slide_count).
  • card: max by (fill_area, fill_count, -saturation).
  • stroke: max by (stroke_count, fill_count).
  • graph_colors: the rest sorted by chart usage, then saturation, first 10.
  • background_text and primary_text: _best_text_candidate (:664), the most-used text color with contrast at least 4.5 against the surface.
  • text_font: the most-used profile font.

_derive_template_theme in the template endpoint (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/template.py:882) skips the LLM entirely and always uses the deterministic selector.

docs.title: Stage 3: materialize
docs.text:
materialize_theme (:357) turns ids back into hex colors and repairs them:

  • Text colors with contrast below 4.5 are replaced by the best observed text color that passes, or else by black or white, whichever contrasts more (_repair_text_color, :680).
  • A card within RGB distance 10 of background becomes a background variant shifted by 0.06 lightness; a stroke within 12 becomes a 0.14 variant (_surface_variant, :723).
  • Graph colors are de-duplicated, primary is appended, and the list is padded to exactly 10 by rotating the primary hue in steps of 0.137 with lightness clamped to 0.25..0.78 (_complete_graph_colors, :698).
  • With no font, the text font defaults to {"name": "Inter", "url": ""}.

servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_template_theme.py covers clustering of near colors (:117), contrast repair and graph completion (:136), that the LLM receives only the compact profile (:163), and the fallback path (:197).

docs.title: Step 4: Serving the template theme
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/ppt/template/{template_id}/theme (template.py:2093) returns {"template_id": ..., "theme": PresentationThemeData | null}. If the stored theme is missing or fails validation, it derives one deterministically and writes it back to the row before responding (:2112 to :2117). A GET with a side effect is unusual; it means old templates acquire a theme the first time anyone opens them.

On the frontend, TemplateService.getTemplateTheme (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/template.ts:153) caches results per template id for TEMPLATE_THEME_CACHE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000 (:10), de-duplicates concurrent requests, caches a 404 as "no theme" (old decks can outlive their template), and does not cache other failures so they can be retried. Every write through TemplateService invalidates the cache entry. These behaviors are tested in servers/nextjs/tests/template-theme-infographics.test.mjs (:119, :176, :197).

docs.title: Step 5: Normalizing any theme payload in the browser
docs.text:
The frontend receives themes in at least four shapes: the API response {template_id, theme: {colors, fonts}}, a bare {colors, fonts}, the presentation wrapper {name, data: {colors, fonts}, source, template_id}, and legacy flat {primary, background, ...}. normalizeTemplateTheme (lib/template-theme.ts) accepts all of them:

servers/nextjs/lib/template-theme.ts (excerpt)
export function normalizeTemplateTheme(value: unknown): TemplateTheme | null {
  const root = asRecord(value);
  if (!root) return null;
  const data = asRecord(root.data);
  const nestedTheme = asRecord(root.theme) ?? asRecord(data?.theme);
  const colors =
    asRecord(nestedTheme?.colors) ??
    asRecord(root.colors) ??
    asRecord(data?.colors) ??
    nestedTheme ??
    data ??
    root;

  if (
    !TEMPLATE_THEME_COLOR_KEYS.some(
      (key) => normalizedHex(colors[key]) != null,
    )
  ) {
    return null;
  }
  // ...
}

Each key must match ^#?[0-9a-f]{6}$ (six-digit hex only, no rgb(), no alpha) and is lower-cased; missing or invalid keys fall back to DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_THEME (primary: "#4a6ebd", background: "#ffffff", and so on). A text font is kept only when both name and url are non-empty. The Redux reducer setPresentationData runs every incoming theme through this function (servers/nextjs/store/slices/presentationGeneration.ts:135).

There is also a pure-frontend fallback, resolveTemplateTheme (lib/template-theme.ts), used by the template editor (TemplatePreviewClient.tsx:159). If the template has no explicit theme it scans the layouts' JSON keys for hex values, classifies them by key path (font, text_color, title_color, legend_color as text; stroke, axis_color, grid_color as stroke; chart, infographic, colors as graph; everything else as fill), and picks roles with simple weights and a 4.5 contrast rule. It is a cousin of the Python deterministic selector, not a copy, so the two can disagree.

docs.title: Step 6: Which theme wins when a deck opens
docs.text:
usePresentationData.fetchUserSlides (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts:27) decides:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/hooks/usePresentationData.ts (excerpt)
        const templateId = resolveTemplateIdFromPresentation(normalizedData);
        const responseTheme = normalizeTemplateTheme(normalizedData.theme);
        const fetchedTheme = templateId
          ? await TemplateService.getTemplateTheme(templateId)
          : null;
        const theme = fetchedTheme ?? responseTheme ?? DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_THEME;

resolveTemplateIdFromPresentation (lib/template-theme.ts) looks at template_id, then design_v2_id, then the first slide's layout_group, then presentation.layout, ignoring the placeholder values no, blank and template-v2.

So the precedence is: the template's current theme, then the presentation's stored theme, then the built-in default. The presentation's font map is loaded separately and in full (useFontLoader(normalizedData.fonts), :67), and the theme's text font is loaded on top (:71). Finally the theme is applied to #presentation-slides-wrapper (:74).

Gotcha

Because the live template theme wins, editing a template's theme (with PATCH /template/{id}) restyles the theme-driven parts of every presentation made from it the next time they load (after the 5-minute client cache expires). The stored presentations.theme is only a fallback for decks whose template was deleted. If you need per-deck theme snapshots, the precedence in usePresentationData.ts:52 is the line to change.

Gotcha

The PDF/export renderer page does not follow the same precedence. PdfMakerPage.tsx loads presentation.fonts (:184) and applies only the stored presentation.theme (:186 to :191), wrapped in a try/catch so theme errors cannot block export. Decks created through the UI have theme = null (only the API generate path stores one), so their export page applies no theme variables at all. Whether that changes pixels depends on Step 7. The export pipeline itself is in PPTX and PDF export.

docs.title: Step 7: What applying a theme actually does
docs.text:
applyPresentationThemeToElement(element, theme) (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/applyPresentationThemeDom.ts:38) normalizes the theme and sets sixteen CSS custom properties as inline styles on the given element. If there is a text font, it loads it and sets three more properties:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/presentation/utils/applyPresentationThemeDom.ts (excerpt)
  const textFont = normalizedTheme.fonts?.textFont;
  if (!textFont) return;
  useFontLoader({ [textFont.name]: textFont.url });
  element.style.setProperty("font-family", `"${textFont.name}"`);
  element.style.setProperty("--heading-font-family", `"${textFont.name}"`);
  element.style.setProperty("--body-font-family", `"${textFont.name}"`);

It is called for the editor wrapper (usePresentationData.ts:74, and again in a useLayoutEffect in PresentationPage.tsx:506 because leaving present mode remounts the tree and loses inline styles), for present mode (PresentationMode.tsx:270), and for export (PdfMakerPage.tsx:188). clearPresentationThemeFromElement (:24) removes the same properties; the outline page clears them with its own copy of the list (outline/hooks/usePresentationGeneration.ts:66).

Now the important part. The Template v2 HTML renderer writes literal styles. fontStyle in servers/nextjs/lib/template-v2-json-to-html.ts:3491 emits color: from the element's font.color (default #111827) and font-family: from font.family when present, and the slide root sets font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:298). The renderer contains no var(--...) references at all. The Konva editor surface likewise reads colors and families from the element JSON. Consequences:

  • An existing template slide looks the same whatever theme is applied: its colors come from its own elements.
  • The inherited font-family on the wrapper reaches only HTML that does not set its own family. Template text elements imported from PPTX almost always carry font.family, and the slide root resets to Arial anyway.
  • The CSS variables exist for other UI that might read them, but a search of app/, components/ and lib/ finds no var(...) reference to any of the sixteen color variables or to --heading-font-family and --body-font-family.

Where the theme does matter is new content. The editor's insert palette passes resolvePresentationTheme(presentationData) (PresentationActions.tsx:2121) into createTextInsertElements and the other creators, which run applyTemplateThemeToElement (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/insert/insert-elements.ts, around :3212):

Inserted element Theme roles applied text, text-list font.color = background_text, font.family = textFont.name on the element and every run table header cells: fill primary, text primary_text; body cells: fill background, text background_text chart color = graph_0, colors = graph_0..graph_9, axis and grid stroke, title and legend background_text, data point colors cycle through the graph colors infographic card_color = card, background_text_color = background_text, icon tint primary_text; meters (progress bar, gauge) use [card, primary], others [background, graph..., card, stroke] vector fill.color = primary when a fill exists, stroke.color = stroke when a stroke exists image icons get color = primary; photos are unchanged container fill card, stroke stroke, and the child is themed recursively; flex, grid and group theme their children

These rules are tested in servers/nextjs/tests/template-theme-infographics.test.mjs (:66, :82).

Gotcha

If you expect "change theme, slides recolor", you will be surprised: that is not how Template v2 works. Recoloring existing slides would require rewriting element colors in slides.ui (or teaching the renderer to resolve role references), and neither exists in this snapshot. For a Superset-style product where a brand theme must apply to generated slides, plan for role references in the slide model from the start; see Data-bound slide model.

docs.title: Step 8: The font catalog
docs.text:
Presenton ships its fonts. There are two catalogs that must stay in sync:

  • Backend: servers/fastapi/templates/assets/fonts.json, a JSON array of 95 {"font_name", "font_url"} entries, for example {"font_name": "Anton", "font_url": "/vendor/fonts/display/anton/Anton-Regular.ttf"}. It is read through importlib.resources (get_static_font_catalog, servers/fastapi/templates/pptx_font_utils.py:162), so it must be packaged into the wheel; the production Dockerfile:22 asserts at build time that the catalog is non-empty, and servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_font_catalog_packaging.py checks it loads outside the source tree.
  • Frontend: LOCAL_FONT_OPTIONS in servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/text/local-fonts.ts:70, 95 entries built with font(family, category, dir, file, italicFile?) for variable fonts and staticFont(family, category, dir, files[]) for families with one file per weight. Weights are inferred from file names (fontWeightFromFileName, :58). One extra application font, Syne, is added outside the catalog (APPLICATION_FONT_OPTIONS, :174), and inter variable is aliased to Inter.

The files themselves live in servers/nextjs/public/vendor/fonts/<category>/<dir>/ with categories display, handwritten, monospace, sans_serif, script, serif, slab_serif. servers/nextjs/local-font-loading-validation.test.mjs asserts exactly 95 catalog entries and 320 font files, and that runtime code under app/, components/ and lib/ never references fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com or next/font/google.

next.config.mjs:18 adds one response header rule: /vendor/fonts/:path* gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, because "Sandboxed community previews load public fonts from an opaque origin". servers/nextjs/tests/font-cors.test.mjs asserts this is the only wildcard CORS rule and that it never sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials.

Gotcha

Built-in templates still contain Google Fonts URLs. templates/general/template.json maps "Poppins" to https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Poppins:... in both fonts and theme.fonts.textFont.url. Nothing downloads it: the frontend parser only accepts URLs ending in a font file extension (isFontAssetUrl, local-fonts.ts:391), so the stylesheet URL is discarded and the family name Poppins is matched against the local catalog instead. A custom family that is not in the catalog and only has a CSS URL will silently fall back to the browser default.

docs.title: Step 9: Loading fonts in the browser
docs.text:
The public entry point is a plain function with a hook-like name:

servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/hooks/useFontLoad.tsx
import {
  ensureTemplateFontLoaded,
  localFontOptionsFromUnknown,
} from "@/components/slide-editor/text/local-fonts";

export const useFontLoader = (fonts: Record<string, string>) => {
  localFontOptionsFromUnknown(fonts).forEach((font) => {
    void ensureTemplateFontLoaded(font);
  });
};

hooks/useFontLoader.tsx only re-exports it. Despite the use prefix it uses no React state and is safe to call from event handlers and non-component code, which is exactly how applyPresentationThemeToElement calls it.

localFontOptionsFromUnknown (local-fonts.ts:249) is a tolerant parser that walks any value (a font map, a list of {family, url} objects, CSS text, nested structures) and produces LocalFontOption records:

  • A family -> url pair is accepted only when the URL is a data:font/ URI or ends in .eot, .otf, .ttf, .woff or .woff2 (isFontAssetUrl, :391).
  • If the family is in the local catalog and the URL starts with /vendor/fonts/, the full catalog option (with all its faces) is used.
  • Otherwise a single-face option is created. Weight is read from an explicit weight field, else 100 900 for variable files whose name contains [wght], else inferred from the filename; style is italic when the family or URL contains "italic". Aliases strip trailing weight words, so Lato Bold also registers as Lato (fontFamilyAliases, :431).
  • Bare family names, and font-family: declarations inside CSS strings, are resolved against the catalog.

ensureFontOptionLoaded (:558) injects one <style data-local-font-family="..."> per family into document.head with @font-face rules from renderLocalFontFaceCss (:482), using font-display: swap and a format() hint derived from the extension. A template-provided font is allowed to replace a catalog font's style tag, but not the other way round (data-font-source is template or vendor). It then waits for 400 16px "<family>" and 700 16px "<family>" through document.fonts.load, with a 3-second timeout after which it resolves anyway (waitForFontDescriptorsLoaded, :522). Concurrent waits for the same descriptor set share one promise.

The Konva editor needs fonts loaded before it measures text, so useFontLoadState (servers/nextjs/components/slide-editor/surface/fontLoading.ts:25) collects font descriptors from every element, run, list item and table cell of a slide, triggers ensureLocalFontsForDescriptors (skipping system families such as Arial, Helvetica, Georgia and the generic families, SYSTEM_FONT_FAMILY_KEYS, local-fonts.ts:181) and ensureTemplateFontsForDescriptors, and bumps a revision counter when they are ready so the canvas re-measures. The editor surface is covered in Slide editor.

The HTML renderer embeds fonts differently: renderFontAssetTags (template-v2-json-to-html.ts:301) runs the same parser over the font map passed in and inlines the resulting @font-face CSS in a <style> tag inside the generated HTML, so a standalone HTML slide carries its own font declarations.

Gotcha

Font descriptor parsing is a security boundary because family names come from user PPTX files. fontFamilyFromFontDescriptor (local-fonts.ts:615) uses an anchored regex (^[^"]*"((?:\\.|[^"\\])*)"\s*$) so a malformed name with thousands of escaped quotes cannot trigger catastrophic backtracking. servers/nextjs/tests/font-descriptor-security.test.mjs runs adversarial descriptors in a child process with a 2-second timeout and checks that quoted, escaped and Unicode family names (Font "quoted", Path\Face, 日本語 Font) still load. Keep that regex anchored if you touch it.

docs.title: Step 10: Uploading and serving font files
The font upload API
docs.text:
FONTS_ROUTER (servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/fonts.py:18) is mounted at /api/v1/ppt/fonts:

Method and path Purpose Response POST /fonts/upload multipart font_file; validates, stores, indexes {success, font_name, font_url, font_path, message} GET /fonts/list all uploads with metadata {success, fonts: [{id, filename, font_name, original_name, font_url, font_path, font_type, file_size, family_name, subfamily_name, full_name, postscript_name, normalized_family_name, weight_class, width_class, format}], message} GET /fonts/uploaded compact list {fonts: [{id, name, url}]} POST /fonts/check PPTX font availability (see Custom templates from PPTX) FontCheckResponse DELETE /fonts/delete/{filename} delete by stored filename or by row UUID {success, message}

In the files read for this chapter, the Next.js app calls only /fonts/check; the other routes are available to API and MCP clients (they appear in servers/fastapi/openai_spec.json).

persist_upload_file (servers/fastapi/utils/font_uploads.py:346) implements the upload:

  1. safe_font_filename keeps only the basename and replaces slashes (:126).
  2. The extension must be one of .eot, .fntdata, .otf, .ttc, .ttf, .woff, .woff2 (ALLOWED_FONT_EXTENSIONS, :24), else 400.
  3. The target name is <stem>_<8 hex chars><ext>, to avoid collisions, inside <APP_DATA_DIRECTORY>/fonts/ (default /tmp/presenton/fonts, get_fonts_directory, :68).
  4. The body is read in 64 KiB chunks and rejected with 413 as soon as it passes MAX_FONT_UPLOAD_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024 (:35, read_upload_with_size_limit, :148); only then is it written to the target path.
  5. fontTools parses the name table (get_font_details); a parse error is a 400 and the written file is deleted (remove_font_file_quietly).
  6. A font_uploads row is flushed, refreshed and only then committed, so a refresh failure cannot leave a committed row without a file (_persist_built_font_upload, :304).

_font_display_name (fonts.py:41) prefers family_name, then full_name, then the normalized family, then the filename stem. _font_original_name (:50) strips the 8-character suffix back off for display.

Variants for matching are computed by get_font_upload_variant (font_uploads.py:75): weight class 700 is bold, 400 is regular, and any other weight class is unsupported and ignored by matching; without a weight class, tokens like bold or gras in the metadata decide, and medium or black (with no bold token) make the file unsupported. Because the check is a substring match on the compacted metadata, semibold, demibold and extrabold all contain bold and are therefore classified as bold, not unsupported.

Every listing, deletion and match first calls backfill_font_uploads_from_disk (:265), which indexes any font file sitting in the fonts directory without a row. Dropping a .ttf into <app_data>/fonts/ is therefore enough to make it available.

Gotcha

font_uploads has no owner_id column (compare template_v2.owner_id). Uploaded fonts are shared across all users of an instance: any user's /fonts/list shows them, /fonts/check will report another user's upload as available, and any user can delete any font by filename. This is consistent with how the files are served (below), but it matters for multi-tenant deployments; see Auth and multi-user.

docs.title: Serving /app_data/fonts/ without authentication
docs.text:
Font URLs are built by _font_path_to_url (font_uploads.py:173) as /app_data/<path relative to app data> through absolute_fastapi_asset_url. In Docker, nginx serves app-data directly with alias, and most locations are gated by auth_request /_auth_check, a subrequest to /api/v1/auth/verify (nginx.conf:133). Two are not:

nginx.conf (excerpt)
    location /app_data/fonts/ {
      alias /app_data/fonts/;
      disable_symlinks on;
      expires 1y;
      add_header Cache-Control "private, max-age=31536000";
    }

    location /app_data/templates/ {
      alias /app_data/templates/;
      disable_symlinks on;
      expires 1y;
      add_header Cache-Control "private, max-age=31536000";
    }

FastAPI's own SessionAuthMiddleware mirrors this with _PUBLIC_APP_DATA_PREFIXES = ("/app_data/fonts/", "/app_data/templates/") (servers/fastapi/api/middlewares.py:38), and servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_session_auth_middleware.py:14 (named test_only_shared_app_data_asset_prefixes_do_not_require_auth) asserts that /app_data/fonts/embedded/font.ttf and /app_data/templates/default/thumbnail.png are public while images, uploads and conversion outputs under /app_data/pptx-to-html/... are not.

The code does not state the reason in a comment. What it does show is that these are the two shared asset trees: fonts are not owner-scoped (above), and /app_data/templates/<id>/static/ holds bundled template assets such as static/Lato Regular.ttf from templates/momentum, which default_templates.py rewrites to /app_data/templates/momentum/static/Lato Regular.ttf and which every user's presentation references. Fonts are also fetched by @font-face and by headless renderers, where attaching session credentials is less straightforward than for page requests. Treat both directories as public: never write user-private files there.

docs.title: Step 11: Fonts in Docker and at export
docs.text:
The production image installs only Noto fonts system-wide and then deletes everything else:

Dockerfile (excerpt)
# Remove any non-Noto fonts that may have been installed as dependencies.
RUN find /usr/share/fonts -type f ! -iname 'Noto*' -delete \
    && find /usr/share/fonts -type d -empty -delete \
    && fc-cache -fsv

The apt package list includes fonts-liberation alongside the Noto packages (Dockerfile:98), but the cleanup removes Liberation too. Chromium inside the container therefore resolves Arial, Helvetica and sans-serif through fontconfig to a Noto face. Any text whose family is not supplied as a web font (through the presentation font map, the theme text font, or the inlined @font-face CSS) renders in Noto in screenshots, previews and PDF exports, while the same deck in a desktop browser renders in the real Arial. The Template v2 renderer's root font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif is exactly such a case. Dockerfile.dev:43 does the same.

How the export runtime receives and embeds fonts (the font map passed to json-to-images and to the PPTX writer, and PPTX font embedding) is covered in PPTX and PDF export. Template creation previews pass fonts the same way, as shown in Custom templates from PPTX.

Gotcha

A missing font never fails loudly. Backend catalog misses fall through to "unavailable" only at /fonts/check time; the frontend parser silently drops unusable URLs; waitForFontDescriptorsLoaded resolves after 3 seconds even if nothing loaded; and Docker falls back to Noto. When a slide "looks wrong" in export but right in the editor, compare the presentation's fonts map against what the export page actually injected before suspecting layout code.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• A theme is sixteen hex color roles plus one textFont {name, url} (PresentationThemeData), stored on template_v2.theme; presentations store a font map always and a wrapped theme only when created through the API generate path.
  • Custom template themes come from a color/font profile of the certified layouts, role selection by LLM with a deterministic fallback, and contrast and graph-color repair; GET /template/{id}/theme derives and persists a theme lazily.
  • In the editor the live template theme beats the stored presentation theme; the export page applies only the stored one.
  • Applying a theme sets CSS variables and a wrapper font, but Template v2 slides use literal colors and families, so the theme mainly styles newly inserted elements and chart palettes.
  • Fonts come from a 95-family local catalog mirrored in fonts.json and local-fonts.ts, plus uploaded or embedded files under the shared, unauthenticated /app_data/fonts/; no remote font service is used at runtime, and Docker falls back to Noto for anything else.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Next.js architecture to see how the frontend that loads these themes and fonts is organized.

docs.title: Next.js architecture
docs.text:
Reads: servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs, servers/nextjs/proxy.ts, servers/nextjs/app/layout.tsx, servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx, servers/nextjs/store/store.ts, servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts, servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/services/api/ · Builds on: Runtime topology · Time: ~40 min

This chapter takes the Next.js server apart layer by layer: how it is built, how URLs map to route files, which layouts run on the server and which components run in the browser, how the proxy.ts request hook gates and rewrites traffic to FastAPI, how the browser decides which origin to call, what lives in the Redux store, and which function calls which backend endpoint. By the end you should be able to open any file under servers/nextjs and know where it sits in the request path. All paths below are relative to the repository root; inside prose, servers/nextjs/ is abbreviated where the context is obvious.

docs.title: Step 1: The build configuration
docs.text:
Everything starts in servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs. The file is short, but each option has a deployment consequence.

servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs (excerpt)
const nextjsRoot = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const isElectronBuild = process.env.PRESENTON_ELECTRON_BUILD === "true";
const isElectronRuntime = process.env.PRESENTON_ELECTRON === "true";

const nextConfig = {
  reactStrictMode: false,
  distDir: ".next-build",
  output: "standalone",
  turbopack: {
    root: nextjsRoot,
  },
  async headers() {
    return [
      {
        source: "/vendor/fonts/:path*",
        // Sandboxed community previews load public fonts from an opaque origin.
        headers: [{ key: "Access-Control-Allow-Origin", value: "*" }],
      },
    ];
  },
  // ...
  images: {
    // ...
    unoptimized: isElectronBuild || isElectronRuntime,
Option Value Where Why it matters reactStrictMode false servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:9 Effects are not double-invoked in development, so the many useEffect-driven EventSource streams open once. distDir .next-build servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:10 Build output does not go to the default .next folder. Any Dockerfile, Electron packager or script that copies the build must look for .next-build. output standalone servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:11 Next.js emits a self-contained server.js plus a pruned node_modules, which is what the Docker image and the Electron bundle run (see Docker build and deployment). turbopack.root directory of the config file servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:12-14 Pins Turbopack's workspace root to servers/nextjs instead of letting it walk up to the monorepo root. headers() Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on /vendor/fonts/:path* servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:15-23 Community previews render in a sandboxed (opaque-origin) frame and still need the bundled fonts. allowedDevOrigins 127.0.0.1, localhost servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:24-31 Only spread in when NODE_ENV !== "production". images.unoptimized true when PRESENTON_ELECTRON_BUILD or PRESENTON_ELECTRON is "true" servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:37 The packaged desktop app lives in a read-only directory, and the image optimizer writes into <distDir>/cache. images.remotePatterns nine HTTPS hosts servers/nextjs/next.config.mjs:38-75 Only these hosts can be used with next/image: an R2 bucket, two pptgen-public S3 hosts, img.icons8.com, present-for-me.s3.amazonaws.com, a Supabase project host, images.unsplash.com, picsum.photos and unsplash.com.

The dependency versions that shape the rest of this chapter come from servers/nextjs/package.json: next 16.4.1, react 19.2.6, @reduxjs/toolkit ^2.2.8, react-redux ^9.1.2, konva ^10.3.0 with react-konva ^19.2.4, Tiptap 3.30.5, @dnd-kit/core ^6.3.1, mixpanel-browser ^2.67.0, and tailwindcss ^3.4.1 for the build-time stylesheet. The scripts block is minimal: dev, build, start, lint (eslint .) and test (node --test).

Gotcha

Two Tailwind versions coexist. The application chrome is compiled at build time with Tailwind 3 (servers/nextjs/tailwind.config.ts), but Smart-mode slides are LLM-generated HTML that uses arbitrary Tailwind classes, so a browser build of Tailwind 4.3.3 is served from /vendor/tailwindcss-browser-4.3.3.js (servers/nextjs/lib/tailwind-browser.ts:1-3) and scoped with @scope ([data-tailwind-runtime-scope]) (servers/nextjs/lib/tailwind-browser.ts:5-11). If you upgrade one, do not assume the other follows.

docs.title: Step 2: The route map
docs.text:
The App Router directory servers/nextjs/app uses three route groups. A route group is a folder whose name is wrapped in parentheses: it organizes files and can carry its own layout.tsx, but it does not appear in the URL.

flowchart TD
  ROOT["app/layout.tsx (server): html, Providers, MixpanelInitializer, TailwindBrowserRuntime, Toaster"]
  HOME["app/page.tsx (async server): AuthGate or ConfigurationInitializer + Home"]
  PG["(presentation-generator)/layout.tsx (async server): requireAppSession + ConfigurationInitializer"]
  DASH["(dashboard)/layout.tsx (server): DashboardSidebar + children"]
  EXP["(export) group: no layout"]
  D1["/dashboard"]
  D2["/settings"]
  D3["/admin"]
  D4["/community"]
  D5["/templates"]
  P1["/upload"]
  P2["/documents-preview"]
  P3["/outline"]
  P4["/presentation"]
  P5["/custom-template"]
  P6["/template-preview"]
  X1["/pdf-maker"]
  ROOT --> HOME
  ROOT --> PG
  ROOT --> EXP
  PG --> DASH
  DASH --> D1
  DASH --> D2
  DASH --> D3
  DASH --> D4
  DASH --> D5
  PG --> P1
  PG --> P2
  PG --> P3
  PG --> P4
  PG --> P5
  PG --> P6
  EXP --> X1

Every page, its file, and whether the page file is a server or a client component:

URL Page file (under servers/nextjs/app/) Page kind Guards and notes / page.tsx async server Auth disabled or signed in: renders ConfigurationInitializer around Home (onboarding). Otherwise renders AuthGate (servers/nextjs/app/page.tsx:7-25). /dashboard (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx server, renders client DashboardPage Has loading.tsx. /settings (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx async server Calls getServerAuthStatus() and renders SettingPage for admins, UserAccountSettings for everyone else (.../settings/page.tsx:11-17). /admin (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/admin/page.tsx async server requireAdminSession() (.../admin/page.tsx:8-11). /community (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/community/page.tsx server, dynamic = "force-dynamic" notFound() when PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED is a disabled value (.../community/page.tsx:7-19). /templates (presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/templates/page.tsx server Redirects to /dashboard when PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE normalizes to smart. /upload (presentation-generator)/upload/page.tsx server Reads PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE and PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED on the server and passes them as props to the client UploadPage (.../upload/page.tsx:46-66). /documents-preview (presentation-generator)/documents-preview/page.tsx server wrapper Renders the client DocumentPreviewPage. /outline (presentation-generator)/outline/page.tsx server (exports metadata) Renders the client OutlinePage. /presentation (presentation-generator)/presentation/page.tsx client ('use client') Reads ?id; shows "No presentation id found" without it. /custom-template (presentation-generator)/custom-template/page.tsx server, force-dynamic Redirects to /dashboard in smart-only mode. Covered in Custom templates from PPTX. /template-preview (presentation-generator)/template-preview/page.tsx server with Suspense Redirects to /dashboard in smart-only mode. /pdf-maker (export)/pdf-maker/page.tsx client The headless export renderer, covered in PPTX and PDF export.

PRESENTATION_GENERATION_MODE is normalized by normalizePresentationGenerationMode() to one of standard, smart or both, defaulting to both for anything else (servers/nextjs/utils/presentationGenerationMode.ts:4-21). PRESENTON_COMMUNITY_ENABLED is parsed by isCommunityEnabled(): empty or missing means enabled, and only 0, false, no, off (case-insensitive) disable it (servers/nextjs/utils/community.ts:1-5).

The dashboard group's layout renders a fixed 114 px sidebar and the page beside it (servers/nextjs/app/(presentation-generator)/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:6-23). DashboardSidebar shows Dashboard, a Templates link (hidden in smart-only mode), Community (hidden when disabled), Settings, and an external Help link to https://docs.presenton.ai/help (.../Components/DashboardSidebar.tsx:52-123). The defaultNavItems array also lists a "Smart" entry keyed designs, but no link renders for it.

Gotcha

/pdf-maker lives in the (export) group, which has no layout.tsx. It therefore does not get requireAppSession() or ConfigurationInitializer; its authentication comes from the exportSession cookie handoff in proxy.ts (Step 6). ConfigurationInitializer still contains /pdf-maker checks (servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:56, :206, :300), which are inert for that route today because it never wraps it.

docs.title: Step 3: The root layout and the client provider shell
docs.text:
servers/nextjs/app/layout.tsx is a server component. It exports static metadata (title, Open Graph and Twitter cards pointing at https://presenton.ai) and renders the document shell:

servers/nextjs/app/layout.tsx (excerpt)
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body className="antialiased">
        <Providers>
          <MixpanelInitializer>

            {children}

          </MixpanelInitializer>
        </Providers>
        <TailwindBrowserRuntime />
        <Toaster position="top-center" />
      </body>
    </html>
  );

Four client components hang off it.

docs.title: 3.1 Providers
docs.text: servers/nextjs/app/providers.tsx:7-12 is the only place the Redux store is attached to React: it wraps children in react-redux's Provider store={store} and mounts ChatGptAuthRedirectHandler as a sibling. Because the store is a module-level singleton (servers/nextjs/store/store.ts:7-14), some non-component code (for example syncStoreAfterCodexSignOut() in servers/nextjs/utils/storeHelpers.ts:376-392) imports store directly and dispatches without React.

docs.title: 3.2 ChatGptAuthRedirectHandler
docs.text:
This component renders nothing. It listens on window for the custom event presenton:chatgpt-auth-required (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:5, listener at servers/nextjs/app/ChatGptAuthRedirectHandler.tsx:50). Any code that detects an expired ChatGPT (Codex OAuth) session calls requestChatGptReauth(), which tracks Codex Reauth Required and dispatches the event (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:86-106). The handler then:

  1. Guards against re-entry with handlingRef and releases the guard after 2 seconds (.../ChatGptAuthRedirectHandler.tsx:22-23, :45-47).
  2. Shows an 8 second error toast with id chatgpt-auth-required (:25-30).
  3. Calls logoutChatGptAuth(), which posts to /api/v1/ppt/codex/auth/logout and then clears the Codex fields in Redux (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:108-127).
  4. Navigates to /settings?chatgpt=reauth, using replace if already on /settings (:38-43).

Detection is centralized in ApiResponseHandler.handleResponse() (Step 9) and in the two SSE hooks, which call isChatGptAuthRequiredMessage() on error events. A response counts as "ChatGPT auth required" if it carries the header x-presenton-auth-action: codex-reauth, or if it is a 401/403 whose message contains CHATGPT_AUTH_REQUIRED:, chatgpt authentication, chatgpt session or codex oauth (servers/nextjs/utils/chatgptAuth.ts:54-84).

docs.title: 3.3 MixpanelInitializer
docs.text: servers/nextjs/app/MixpanelInitializer.tsx:7-20 calls initMixpanel() once and tracks a Page View event with { url: pathname } on every pathname change. Whether anything is actually sent depends on /api/telemetry-status; the full mechanism is in Settings, onboarding, auth UI.

docs.title: 3.4 TailwindBrowserRuntime and Toaster
docs.text: servers/nextjs/components/runtime/TailwindBrowserRuntime.tsx:25-58 injects a <style type="text/tailwindcss"> block and the browser Tailwind script with strategy="afterInteractive". On /pdf-maker it renders nothing; on / it defers loading until some component dispatches presenton:tailwind-runtime-request, which useTailwindRuntimeReady() does on mount (:60-76). Once the script loads it fires presenton:tailwind-runtime-ready exactly once per page lifetime (:17-23). Toaster is the Sonner wrapper in servers/nextjs/components/ui/sonner.tsx; the rest of the app calls it through notify.error/success/info/warning/loading(title, description, options) plus notify.dismiss(id) (servers/nextjs/components/ui/sonner.tsx:44-56).

docs.title: Step 4: Server-side session gating in layouts
docs.text:
Page protection happens in server components, not in proxy.ts. The proxy comment states this explicitly (servers/nextjs/proxy.ts:5-9). The helpers are in servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts.

getServerAuthStatus() (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:37-88) reads the incoming cookie header with headers() and calls FastAPI GET {base}/api/v1/auth/status with cache: "no-store", where base is FAST_API_INTERNAL_URL, else NEXT_PUBLIC_FAST_API, else http://127.0.0.1:8000 (:17-30). It returns:

servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts (excerpt)
export type AuthStatus = {
  configured: boolean;
  authenticated: boolean;
  username: string | null;
  user_id: string | null;
  available: boolean;
  role: "admin" | "user" | null;
};

available is false when the backend could not be reached or answered non-2xx. When DISABLE_AUTH is truthy (1, true, yes, on, checked by isAuthDisabled() in servers/nextjs/utils/auth.ts:1-20), it short-circuits to an authenticated admin named electron.

Two guards are built on it:

Guard Used by Not available Not configured Not authenticated Wrong role requireAppSession() (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:94-108) (presentation-generator)/layout.tsx:7 redirect / redirect / redirect /?reason=unauthorized not checked requireAdminSession() (servers/nextjs/utils/serverAuth.ts:110-121) /admin page redirect /?reason=unauthorized not distinguished redirect /?reason=unauthorized redirect /dashboard

The root page (servers/nextjs/app/page.tsx:7-26) is the only entry that is not behind requireAppSession(): it renders AuthGate for setup and sign-in, which turns the ?reason=unauthorized query into a toast. Because the guard lives in the (presentation-generator) layout, an unknown URL still produces the normal 404 page instead of a login redirect; the layout only executes for routes that exist under it.

Gotcha

The server guard only proves that a session cookie is valid. The browser-side role used by the UI comes from a second call to the same endpoint inside ConfigurationInitializer (Step 5). Until that resolves, state.userConfig.role is null, and components such as Home (servers/nextjs/components/Home.tsx:19-27) and SettingPage treat null as "not admin".

docs.title: Step 5: ConfigurationInitializer, the client bootstrap
docs.text:
servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx wraps both the root page and every (presentation-generator) route. It is a client component that holds the page behind a full-screen "Loading Presenton..." screen until it has established three facts: the backend is reachable, who the user is, and whether a usable text provider is configured.

flowchart TD
  A["mount: fetchUserConfigState()"] --> B{"route starts with /pdf-maker?"}
  B -- "yes" --> Z["stop loading"]
  B -- "no" --> C["assertBackendReachable(): GET /api/v1/auth/status must be JSON"]
  C -- "fails" --> E1["toast Cannot reach backend, stop loading"]
  C -- "ok" --> D["GET /api/v1/auth/status, read role"]
  D -- "no role" --> E2["setUserRole(null), setLLMConfig({}), toast"]
  D -- "admin" --> F["GET /api/user-config (unredacted), normalizeLLMConfig, setLLMConfig"]
  D -- "user" --> G["GET /api/runtime-config (redacted), setLLMConfig"]
  F --> H{"LLM is presenton?"}
  H -- "yes" --> I["GET /api/v1/auth/presenton/status, need linked"]
  H -- "no" --> J{"hasValidLLMConfig?"}
  I --> J
  J -- "valid, ollama" --> K["check model is pulled, else push /"]
  J -- "valid, route is /" --> L["push /upload"]
  J -- "invalid, not / or /settings" --> M["push / (onboarding)"]
  G --> N{"runtime.configured?"}
  N -- "no" --> E3["toast Instance not configured"]
  N -- "yes, route is /" --> L

The key code paths:

  1. Reachability. assertBackendReachable() (servers/nextjs/utils/api.ts:155-179) fetches getApiUrl("/api/v1/auth/status") with credentials: "include" and throws BackendConnectionError unless the response is 2xx, has a JSON content type, and parses to a non-array object. The JSON check exists because a same-origin Next.js 404 or 500 is HTML and must not be mistaken for a healthy backend.
  2. Role. role becomes "admin" or "user" only if authenticated is true (servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:226-249).
  3. Admin config. Admins load /api/user-config, which proxies FastAPI's GET /api/v1/admin/provider-settings with real secrets (Step 10). Validity is computed client-side with hasValidLLMConfig() plus, for LLM === "presenton", a linked Presenton Cloud account (:251-299). An Ollama selection additionally calls isOllamaModelAvailable() and bounces to / if the model is not pulled (:305-328).
  4. User config. Regular users load /api/runtime-config, whose secrets are redacted to __configured__, so validity comes from the server-computed configured flag rather than client validation (:344-379).
  5. Routing. A valid config on / pushes /upload; an invalid admin config on any route other than / or /settings pushes / (where Home shows onboarding). Navigation completion is detected by polling window.location.pathname every 500 ms in setLoadingToFalseAfterNavigatingTo() (:191-203).
  6. Splash timing. The loading screen stays up for at least PRESENTON_SPLASH_MIN_DURATION_MS (3000 ms, servers/nextjs/components/ui/presenton-splash-loader.tsx:11) even if everything resolves faster (servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:178-189, :382-384).

A second effect re-validates on every navigation once role is known (:75-176), skipping /, /settings* and /pdf-maker*. It re-fetches /api/user-config (admin) or /api/runtime-config (user) with cache: "no-store" and re-dispatches setLLMConfig. If the config is no longer valid it shows a "Provider setup required" warning toast and, for admins only, calls router.replace('/') (:113-125). For Presenton Cloud it re-checks GET /api/v1/auth/presenton/status; if the cloud link is gone it blanks LLM in Redux and sends the user to / (:127-147).

Gotcha

fetchUserConfigState() runs once per mount of ConfigurationInitializer with an empty dependency list (servers/nextjs/app/ConfigurationInitializer.tsx:68-73). Because the component sits in the (presentation-generator) layout, client-side navigation between pages under that layout does not remount it, so the full bootstrap does not re-run; only the lighter revalidation effect does. A hard reload is what re-runs the bootstrap.
