The superset-extensions CLI (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py) has six commands: init scaffolds a project, validate checks extension.json against ExtensionConfig and npm at least 10.8.2, update bumps metadata, build (:554) runs npm run build and copies backend files matched by [tool.apache_superset_extensions.build] include (copy_backend_files, :225), bundle (:587) zips dist/ into {name}-{version}.supx by default (:612), so with name docgen the default file is docgen-1.0.0.supx; the canonical databound-docgen-<version>.supx is produced with superset-extensions bundle --output databound-docgen-1.0.0.supx, and dev (:634) watches and rebuilds into dist/ for use with LOCAL_EXTENSIONS.

build_manifest (:149) derives two identifiers you cannot choose freely:

  • the backend entrypoint <publisher_snake>.<name_snake>.entrypoint, so for publisher databound and name docgen it is databound.docgen.entrypoint;
  • the Module Federation name <camel(publisher)>_<camel(name)>, here databound_docgen.

The extension id is computed as f"{publisher}.{name}" (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/types.py:38-84), here databound.docgen. The accepted bundle layout is manifest.json, frontend/dist/<file> and backend/src/<module path>.py; anything else raises "Unexpected file in bundle". 6.1.0 accepted only flat files under frontend/dist; master allows nested paths [M*].

extension/extension.json (Data-Bound Documents)
{
  "publisher": "databound",
  "name": "docgen",
  "displayName": "Data-Bound Documents",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "description": "Prompt and template driven decks, documents, pages and briefs bound to live Superset data",
  "dependencies": [],
  "permissions": []
}

Gotcha: a .supx cannot install dependencies

Only files matched by include are copied, and the host imports only from the in-memory bundle. [project] dependencies in the backend pyproject.toml are installed by nothing. python-pptx, python-docx, an HTTP client and every other library must be preinstalled in the web, worker and MCP images. This is why Data-Bound Documents is a "thin .supx, fat wheel" design: the superset-databound-docs wheel holds the engine and the bundle holds only the Superset wiring.

Gotcha: dependencies and permissions are not enforced

A grep of master finds no consumer of the manifest's dependencies or permissions lists. Authorization must come from FAB permissions on the extension's API classes and MCP tools.

docs.title: 1.3 The injection mechanism
docs.text:
Every public function or class in superset_core is a stub that raises NotImplementedError until the host overwrites the module attribute in initialize_core_api_dependencies() (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:318-333) and initialize_core_mcp_dependencies() (apache/superset: superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py:375). Two consequences:

  • Import superset_core decorators inside the extension's modules, which are imported after injection. A library imported earlier (for example from superset_config.py) would bind the stubs.
  • Models and DAOs are replaced by the host's: superset_core.common.models.Chart becomes superset.models.slice.Slice, Dataset becomes SqlaTable, Dashboard becomes superset.models.dashboard.Dashboard (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:82-125). Host DAOs apply access base filters evaluated against the current Flask user (apache/superset: superset/daos/chart.py:47, superset/daos/dashboard.py:505, superset/daos/dataset.py:80).

docs.title: 1.4 Backend contribution types
1.5 Extension context and storage [M]
docs.text:
superset_core.extensions.context.get_context() returns .extension (the manifest) and .storage.ephemeral / .storage.persistent (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/context.py:52-119). Persistent storage is a table extension_storage with 1 MB values and a 100 MB quota per extension.

Gotcha: backend context appears to exist only during import

The host sets the extension ContextVar in one place, around eager_import(entrypoint) (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:686). Storage accessors resolve the extension id from that variable on every call (apache/superset: superset/extensions/storage/utils.py:84-97) and raise when it is unset. Inside a REST handler, an MCP tool or a GTF task body, get_context() therefore appears to fail (inferred from source, not exercised). Data-Bound Documents captures EXTENSION_ID = "databound.docgen" as a constant at import and keeps its own dbd_ tables instead of extension storage.

docs.title: 1.6 Frontend: @apache-superset/core namespaces
docs.text:
The npm package is mostly type stubs; the host assigns real implementations to window.superset in ExtensionsStartup (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/extensions/ExtensionsStartup.tsx:56-67). Namespaces exported from src/index.ts include authentication, commands, menus, views, sqlLab, editors, extensions, theme, translation, components, plus master-only chat, navigation and storage.

Namespace Key signatures (under superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/) Availability authentication getCSRFToken(): Promise<string \| undefined> (authentication/index.ts:43) [6.1] commands registerCommand({id, title, icon?, description?}, callback): Disposable (commands/index.ts:63), executeCommand(id, ...rest) [6.1] views registerView(view: {id, name, description?}, location: string, component: ComponentType): Disposable (views/index.ts:73-77) [M*]: 6.1 took a provider function () => <X/> menus registerMenuItem({view, command, description?}, location, group: 'primary' \| 'secondary' \| 'context') (menus/index.ts:83-87) [6.1] sqlLab getCurrentTab() returns {id, title, databaseId, catalog, schema, getEditor(), panels} (sqlLab/index.ts:290); executeQuery(...); events onDidQueryRun, onDidQueryStop, onDidQueryFail, onDidQuerySuccess [6.1] navigation getPage(): Page (navigation/index.ts:65) with Page one of 'dashboard', 'dashboard_list', 'explore', 'chart_list', 'sqllab', 'query_history', 'saved_queries', 'dataset', 'dataset_list', 'home'; onDidChangePage (:81) [M] chat registerChat(chat: {id, name, description?}, trigger: ComponentType, panel: ComponentType): Disposable (chat/index.ts:76-80), plus open, close, setDisplayMode('floating' \| 'panel') [M]

The success event payload carries remoteId, the backend Query id (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/sqlLab/index.ts:214), alongside executedSql and result. That id is what the SQL Lab panel sends to the backend, which reloads and re-checks the row rather than trusting the browser's copy of the SQL.

docs.title: 1.7 Frontend contribution areas the host actually renders
docs.text:
This is the most consequential limitation in the whole landscape. The only view locations the host defines are SQL Lab's:

apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/SqlLab/contributions.ts:40-50
export const ViewLocations = {
  sqllab: {
    leftSidebar: 'sqllab.leftSidebar',
    rightSidebar: 'sqllab.rightSidebar',
    panels: 'sqllab.panels',
    editor: 'sqllab.editor',
    statusBar: 'sqllab.statusBar',
    results: 'sqllab.results',
    queryHistory: 'sqllab.queryHistory',
  },
} as const;
Location Rendered by Kind Props Availability sqllab.leftSidebar SqlLab/components/TableExploreTree/index.tsx:441-442 menu none [6.1] sqllab.rightSidebar SqlLab/components/AppLayout/index.tsx:101, 141 view none [6.1] sqllab.panels SqlLab/components/SouthPane/index.tsx:110, 225, 244 view and menu none [6.1] sqllab.editor SqlLab/components/SqlEditorTopBar/index.tsx:45-46 menu none [6.1] sqllab.statusBar SqlLab/components/StatusBar/index.tsx:41, 47 view none [6.1] sqllab.results SqlLab/components/ResultSet/index.tsx:493-494 menu none [6.1] sqllab.queryHistory SqlLab/components/QueryHistory/index.tsx:125 menu none [6.1] chat (singleton) ChatFloatingHost, ChatPanelHost in App.tsx:248-264 trigger and panel none [M]

Views render with no props at all: resolveView(id) wraps the component in an ErrorBoundary and passes nothing (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/core/views/index.ts:87-97), and toolbar menus call commands.executeCommand(command.id) with no arguments (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/components/PanelToolbar/index.tsx:59, 85). A view registered at any other string, for example dashboard.header, is stored but never displayed.

The dashboard and Explore hooks people often cite (dashboard.nav.right, dashboard.slice.header.menu [M], explore.chart.header) belong to a different, older mechanism: the build-time UI-override registry in @superset-ui/core (apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-ui-core/src/ui-overrides/types.ts:249-286). It is a module-local singleton inside the host bundle, and @superset-ui/core is not a federated shared module, so a .supx remote cannot reach it. Only deployments that build their own Superset frontend can fill those keys.

What Data-Bound Documents does about it:

Need Master 6.1 fallback Entry point on dashboards and Explore chat.registerChat with id databound.docgen.chat, plus navigation.getPage() and URL parsing for the dashboard id, native_filters_key or slice_id Standalone Studio page GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/studio?dashboard=... (its own non-federated bundle with its own React) and the SQL Lab panel's dashboard picker Entry point in SQL Lab view databound.docgen.panel at sqllab.panels, menu items at sqllab.results and sqllab.editor same, with a provider function for registerView Dashboard button for custom builds optional databound-docs-ui-overrides package filling dashboard.nav.right and dashboard.slice.header.menu same, minus dashboard.slice.header.menu extension/frontend/src/index.tsx (skeleton, both versions)
import React from 'react';
import { commands, menus, sqlLab, views } from '@apache-superset/core';
import { SqlLabDocumentsPanel } from './studio/SqlLabDocumentsPanel';
import { openStudio, setLastSqlResult } from './studio/state';

const ID = 'databound.docgen';
const IS_MASTER_API = typeof (window as any).superset?.navigation?.getPage === 'function';

views.registerView(
  { id: `${ID}.panel`, name: 'Documents', description: 'Generate data-bound documents' },
  'sqllab.panels',
  // 6.1 expects a provider function, master expects the component itself
  (IS_MASTER_API ? SqlLabDocumentsPanel : () => <SqlLabDocumentsPanel />) as any,
);

commands.registerCommand(
  { id: `${ID}.generateFromResults`, title: 'Generate brief from results' },
  () => openStudio({ source: 'sqllab' }),
);
menus.registerMenuItem({ view: `${ID}.panel`, command: `${ID}.generateFromResults` },
  'sqllab.results', 'primary');

sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess(e => {
  const tab = sqlLab.getCurrentTab();
  setLastSqlResult({ queryId: e.remoteId, databaseId: tab?.databaseId,
                     catalog: tab?.catalog ?? null, schema: tab?.schema ?? null });
});

Gotcha: two webpack configurations

6.1.0 maps @apache-superset/core to window.superset through webpack externals, while master injects a per-extension copy through the Module Federation share scope (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/extensions/ExtensionsLoader.ts:214-244). An extension built with the 6.1 template needs a webpack change to run on master. Data-Bound Documents builds two bundles from one source and checks the match in superset dbd doctor.

Gotcha: no SupersetClient and no app root helper

@superset-ui/core is not shared with remotes, so an extension calls its own backend with fetch(url, {credentials: 'same-origin', headers: {'X-CSRFToken': await authentication.getCSRFToken()}}). The loader's makeUrl is internal; on subdirectory deployments the extension must derive the application root itself, for example from its own remote entry URL under /api/v1/extensions/<publisher>/<name>/.

Frontend extensions are loaded only by App.tsx. Nothing under superset-frontend/src/embedded/ references ExtensionsStartup, so extensions do not load in embedded dashboards [6.1].

docs.title: Step 2: The Global Task Framework (GTF)
docs.text: GTF is Superset's engine for long-running work, behind GLOBAL_TASK_FRAMEWORK (default False, apache/superset: superset/config.py:909). Data-Bound Documents runs every generation, refresh, render and trigger run as a GTF task.

docs.title: 2.1 Public API
docs.text:
apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/decorators.py:32-37
def task(
    name: str | None = None,
    scope: TaskScope = TaskScope.PRIVATE,
    timeout: int | None = None,
    subscription_policy: "TaskSubscriptionPolicy | None" = None,
) -> Callable[[Callable[P, R]], "TaskWrapper[P]"]:
  • TaskWrapper.__call__(*args, **kwargs) runs synchronously; TaskWrapper.schedule(*args, options: TaskOptions | None = None, **kwargs) enqueues and returns a PENDING task. The function's return value is discarded; output goes to the task payload.
  • get_context() returns a TaskContext inside a running task, with update_task(progress=None, payload=None) ([6.1]; the keyword immediate= is [M]), on_abort(handler), on_cleanup(handler) and, on master, get_dependency_payloads().
  • TaskScope: PRIVATE (default, per user), SHARED (dedup across users, requires a task_key), SYSTEM (admin only). TaskStatus: PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS, FAILURE, ABORTING, ABORTED, TIMED_OUT (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:30-51).
  • TaskOptions(task_key, task_name, timeout) on 6.1; master adds depends_on for DAGs (types.py:138-193) [M*].
  • progress accepts a float 0 to 1, an integer count, or a (current, total) tuple. On master, payload merges into the existing payload; the 6.1.0 docs said each call replaced it, so write the full payload each time to be portable.

docs.title: 2.2 What happens on .schedule()
docs.text:
1. TaskManager.submit_task(...) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/manager.py:518-611) creates or joins a task row under a distributed lock, keyed by type, scope and task_key.
  2. Only for a new row, it enqueues the single generic Celery task: execute_task.delay(task_uuid=str(task.uuid), task_type=task_type, args=args, kwargs=kwargs) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/manager.py:582).
  3. The Celery task tasks.execute (apache/superset: superset/tasks/scheduler.py:396-512) loads the row, builds a TaskContext, starts the timeout timer, looks up the executor in TaskRegistry (:584) and runs it inside use_context(ctx) (:595).

Two design choices follow directly. First, task_key = sha256(user_id, template@version, canonical(context), prompt, parameters) makes a double click join the same job. Second, because every GTF task travels as tasks.execute with the GTF type in the task_type keyword, a Celery router function can send Data-Bound Documents work to its own databound_docs queue without any Superset change (behavior on 6.1 is a prototype gate in Roadmap).

Gotcha: GTF does not switch users

TaskContext.__init__ (apache/superset: superset/tasks/context.py:60-125) does not set g.user. Superset's own GTF task passes user_id and guest_token as arguments and wraps its body in with override_user(_resolve_user(user_id, guest_token), force=False): (apache/superset: superset/tasks/async_queries.py:165-175, 273-297). A generation task that skips this runs DAO filters, permission checks and RLS without the requester.

Gotcha: positional @task arguments break

The stub's first positional parameter is name, but the host implementation's first positional parameter is func (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:57-79). Always use keywords: @task(name="generate_document", scope=TaskScope.PRIVATE, timeout=900). The host also rejects task functions with parameters named ctx or options (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:165-173).

backend/src/databound/docgen/tasks.py (skeleton)
from superset_core.tasks.decorators import get_context, task
from superset_core.tasks.types import TaskScope


@task(name="generate_document", scope=TaskScope.PRIVATE, timeout=900)
def generate_document(job_id: str, user_id: int) -> None:
    from superset.extensions import security_manager      # internal, via the Superset Adapter
    from superset.utils.core import override_user

    ctx = get_context()
    cancelled = {"flag": False}

    @ctx.on_abort
    def _abort() -> None:
        cancelled["flag"] = True                         # checked between LLM calls and queries

    user = security_manager.get_user_by_id(user_id)
    if user is None or not user.is_active:
        raise PermissionError("Requesting user no longer exists or is inactive")
    with override_user(user, force=False):
        ctx.update_task(progress=(1, 8), payload={"stage": "digest", "job_id": job_id})
        ...  # digest, outline, layout, register, resolve, write, verify, render

docs.title: 2.3 REST surface and UI
docs.text:
TaskRestApi (resource_name = "task", class_permission_name = "Task") is registered only when the flag is on at startup (apache/superset: superset/initialization/__init__.py:342-345; class at apache/superset: superset/tasks/api.py:60-95):

Route Method Availability /api/v1/task/ (rison q), /_info, /related/<col> GET [6.1] /api/v1/task/<task_uuid> GET [6.1] /api/v1/task/<task_uuid>/status GET [6.1] /api/v1/task/status_changes?cursor=&task_type= GET [M] /api/v1/task/<task_uuid>/cancel POST [6.1]

The Task List UI under Manage shows and cancels DBD jobs for free. Abort is cooperative: registering on_abort makes the task abortable and starts polling every TASK_ABORT_POLLING_DEFAULT_INTERVAL = 10 seconds, or uses Redis pub/sub when DISTRIBUTED_COORDINATION_CONFIG is set. Master adds heartbeats (GTF_TASK_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 15) and orphan reaping.

GTF has no scheduler

GTF runs work now, or after prerequisites on master. It has no cron, no run_at and no retry policy (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/tasks/types.py:143-150 lists them as future work). Recurring work needs a Celery beat entry in the operator's CELERY_CONFIG.beat_schedule, which no superset_core API can add. Data-Bound Documents ships one beat task, databound_docs.trigger_tick, documented as a required configuration line.

docs.title: Step 3: The built-in MCP service
docs.text: superset mcp run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5008 (apache/superset: superset/cli/mcp.py:28-41) starts a FastMCP server inside a Flask app context. It is an optional extra: fastmcp>=3.1.0,<4.0 in 6.1.0, fastmcp>=4.1.0,<5.0 on master (apache/superset: pyproject.toml:202-203). Master ships 79 tools; 6.1.0 shipped 24.

docs.title: 3.1 Data and discovery tools relevant to generation
docs.text: Tool Purpose Availability get_dashboard_info dashboard metadata, accepts permalink_key and filter_state [6.1] ([M*]) get_dashboard_layout tabs, tab tree, charts, native filters, filter state, permalink key [M] get_dashboard_data compact, filter-aware summary across up to 15 charts (max_charts 1 to 30, fetch_row_limit = 100, sample_rows = 10) [M] get_chart_info, get_chart_data chart metadata; data that prefers the saved query_context and runs ChartDataCommand [6.1] ([M*]) get_chart_preview ASCII, table, Vega-Lite, URL, and on master PNG [6.1] get_dataset_info, list_datasets dataset columns and metrics [6.1] query_dataset metrics plus columns query through QueryContext and ChartDataCommand (row_limit 1 to 50,000) [M] execute_sql raise_for_access(..., force_dataset_match=True) then database.execute (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/sql_lab/tool/execute_sql.py:189-236); tagged mutate [6.1] ([M*]) generate_chart, generate_dashboard create charts and dashboards [6.1] list_reports, get_report_info, list_tasks, get_task_info reports and GTF tasks [M]

docs.title: 3.2 Identity: the main 6.1 versus master difference
docs.text:
• Master. get_user_from_request() (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:889-950) resolves, in order: a JWT bearer mapped to a username by MCP_USER_RESOLVER (default prefers preferred_username, then username, email, sub; apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:937-967); a FAB API key (sst_ prefix); MCP_DEV_USERNAME; then g.user from external middleware. A JWT that resolves to no user fails closed.
  • 6.1.0. Only g.user (set by external middleware) and then MCP_DEV_USERNAME are consulted. MCP_AUTH_ENABLED and MCP_JWT_* authenticate the transport, but every call still runs as the dev user unless middleware sets g.user.

RBAC: with MCP_RBAC_ENABLED = True (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:150), check_tool_permission verifies can_<method> on <class_permission_name> before a tool runs (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:397-440). An extension tool declared with class_permission_name="DataBoundDocs" gets the same check; the method defaults to write when the tags contain mutate, else read.

Gotcha: never call MCP tool functions in-process from a worker

Without a request context, _setup_user_context pops g.user (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/auth.py:1107-1121), and MCP_DEV_USERNAME outranks g.user in resolution. A worker that imports and calls a tool function directly can end up running as the dev user. Data-Bound Documents calls MCP only over the transport with a short-lived per-user JWT (master, agent planner only), and its own data path never touches MCP.

Gotcha: MCP responses are capped

Master caps responses at 50,000 bytes (MCP_RESPONSE_SIZE_CONFIG, apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:499-512); 6.1.0 used a 25,000-token estimate. That is enough for planning and far too small to carry a deck's data. Final numbers always come from the Binding Resolver.

On 6.1, the design therefore uses only the pipeline and template planners, and DBD's own MCP tools refuse to mutate or read data when the resolved user is the configured dev user unless DATABOUND_DOCS["MCP_ALLOW_DEV_USER"] (a Data-Bound Documents setting, not a Superset one) is set for development.

docs.title: Step 4: The chart data API and the query context
4.1 Endpoints
docs.text:
Route Handler Purpose Availability POST /api/v1/chart/data ChartDataRestApi.data run a client-built QueryContext [6.1] ([M*] async semantics) GET /api/v1/chart/<pk>/data/ ChartDataRestApi.get_data (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:97) run the chart's stored query_context; ?format=, ?type=, ?force= [6.1]; ?filters_dashboard_id= [M] GET /api/v1/chart/data/<cache_key> data_from_cache async result after a 202 6.1 only; removed on master POST /api/v1/datasource/<type>/<id>/query DatasourceRestApi.query (apache/superset: superset/datasource/api.py:790) headless metrics and dimensions query, names validated against saved metrics [M] POST /api/v1/dashboard/<pk>/export_xlsx/ DashboardRestApi.export_xlsx (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/api.py:1867) every chart's data, filter-aware, into XLSX [M]

GET /api/v1/chart/<pk>/data/ returns 400 "Chart has no query context saved. Please save the chart again." when the chart has none (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:180). On master, ?filters_dashboard_id=<int> merges the dashboard's saved default native filters in scope for that chart (:191-219) and adds a dashboard_filters object to the response listing each filter's id, name, status (applied, not_applied, not_applied_uses_default_to_first_item_prequery) and column.

docs.title: 4.2 The QueryContext payload
docs.text:
ChartDataQueryContextSchema (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1677-1770) has, on 6.1.0, exactly datasource, queries, custom_cache_timeout, force, result_type, result_format and form_data. Master adds force_nonce, async_mode and tab_id. A dataset-source binding in Data-Bound Documents compiles to a payload like this:

QueryContext for 'revenue by month, last quarter, EMEA' (6.1 compatible)
{
  "datasource": {"id": 7, "type": "table"},
  "queries": [{
    "columns": [{"columnType": "BASE_AXIS", "sqlExpression": "order_date", "label": "order_date",
                 "expressionType": "SQL", "timeGrain": "P1M"}],
    "metrics": ["revenue"],
    "filters": [
      {"col": "region", "op": "IN", "val": ["EMEA"]},
      {"col": "order_date", "op": "TEMPORAL_RANGE", "val": "Last quarter"}
    ],
    "orderby": [["revenue", false]],
    "row_limit": 100,
    "time_offsets": ["1 year ago"],
    "series_limit": 0,
    "post_processing": [],
    "extras": {"time_grain_sqla": "P1M"}
  }],
  "form_data": {"datasource": "7__table", "viz_type": "table"},
  "result_type": "full",
  "result_format": "json"
}

QueryObject fields the design relies on (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1388-1675): columns (with the BASE_AXIS adhoc column for temporal x), metrics (saved metric names or SIMPLE adhoc metrics), filters (ChartDataFilterSchema; operators include ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, LIKE, ILIKE, IN, NOT IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, TEMPORAL_RANGE), extras, orderby, row_limit, series_limit, time_offsets and post_processing. Registered post-processing operations (apache/superset: superset/utils/pandas_postprocessing/__init__.py:49-67) include aggregate, boxplot, compare, contribution, cum, diff, histogram, pivot, rank, rename, resample, rolling, select, sort and flatten. Keeping a chart's own post_processing list means shares, pivots and cumulative sums are computed server-side exactly as the dashboard computes them.

result_type values (apache/superset: superset/common/chart_data.py:20-48) are columns, full, query, results, samples, timegrains, post_processed and drill_detail. query returns compiled SQL without running it, which is useful for an optional SQL appendix; post_processed applies the table and pivot shaping the frontend would apply. result_format is csv, json, xlsx, and on master arrow.

docs.title: 4.3 The response
docs.text: Each entry of result (or of ChartDataCommand(...).run()["queries"] in-process) carries colnames, coltypes (GenericDataType: NUMERIC=0, STRING=1, TEMPORAL=2, BOOLEAN=3, MULTI_VALUE=4 [M]), data (records; temporal values as epoch milliseconds), rowcount, applied_filters, rejected_filters, cache_key, cached_dttm, queried_dttm, is_cached, query, status, error, detected_currency, from_dttm and to_dttm (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1807-1940). Every one of these feeds a Provenance field in the Document Spec: "data as of", "filter not applied to this chart", "Top 10 of 47", currency resolution.

docs.title: 4.4 Caching, limits and the async hazard
docs.text:
• Cache. Results are cached in the data cache, NullCache by default (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1532). force: true bypasses it. The cache key includes RLS through get_rls_cache_key (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304), so two users with different RLS never share rows.
  • Limits. ROW_LIMIT = 50000 (apache/superset: superset/config.py:186) is the default when row_limit is 0 or null, and SQL_MAX_ROW = 100000 (:1853) is the hard cap. A slide wants 1 to 500 aggregated rows, so every binding sets an explicit row_limit.
  • Async on 6.1.0. With GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES on, every cacheable JSON request to the chart data endpoint returns 202, and the follow-up requires the async JWT cookie; a bearer-token client gets 401. On master, async is opt-in per request through async_mode.

Gotcha: do not call the chart data HTTP endpoint from a worker

On 6.1 with GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES, a server-to-server call can get 202 and then 401. Alerts and Reports work around this by logging an executor in with cookies and calling the endpoint over HTTP. Data-Bound Documents instead calls the same command in-process, which has no transport, no cookie and no credential.

docs.title: 4.5 In-process execution: ChartDataCommand
docs.text:
The command the endpoint wraps is ChartDataCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:36). Its validate() calls self._query_context.raise_for_access() before validating queries (:107-108), so a caller-supplied filter is never rendered for a resource the user cannot read. Master's dashboard Excel export is the reference implementation of "every chart on a dashboard, with live filters, as the user": it stamps form_data, applies the filter context, sets g.form_data = json_body so Jinja macros such as filter_values work (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:225), loads the schema and runs the command (:191-232) [M].

databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py (excerpt)
def run_query_context(json_body: dict) -> dict:
    from flask import g
    from superset.charts.schemas import ChartDataQueryContextSchema
    from superset.commands.chart.data.get_data_command import ChartDataCommand

    g.form_data = json_body                      # as the Excel export does
    query_context = ChartDataQueryContextSchema().load(json_body)
    command = ChartDataCommand(query_context)
    command.validate()                           # raise_for_access first
    return command.run()                         # {"queries": [...]} for result_type "full"

ChartDataCommand, ChartDataQueryContextSchema and override_user are internal Superset APIs: superset_core exposes no chart-data API. All of them live in one module, the Superset Adapter, with contract tests per Superset version. A public run_chart_query in superset_core is the first item of the upstream SIP in Roadmap.

docs.title: 4.6 Stored query_context versus form_data
docs.text:
A chart (Slice) stores params (the Explore form data) and query_context (a full QueryContext). The query context is produced client-side by each viz plugin's buildQuery and saved when the chart is saved in Explore, so old, imported or API-created charts can have none. Explore backfills it when a user with write access opens the chart (apache/superset: superset-frontend/src/explore/components/ExploreChartPanel/index.tsx:235-254).

Master adds a server-side rebuild, build_query_context_from_form_data(form_data, datasource, viz_type=None) (apache/superset: superset/common/form_data_query_context.py:1801), with explicit adapters for tables, every ECharts timeseries type, pie, big number, pivot, histogram, box plot, waterfall, gantt, treemap, sunburst, bubble and maps, and a generic top-N fallback [M]. It is absent from the 6.1.0 tree.

Situation Master 6.1 fallback Chart has a saved query context use it (follow: live reloads it each run) same Chart has none rebuild from params with a provenance warning rebuilt_from_form_data binding status error with the remediation "Chart has no saved query context: open and save it in Explore", mirroring apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:180

Gotcha: the stored query context is a snapshot of params

If someone edits params through the API without re-saving in Explore, query_context can drift from params. The dashboard renders from query_context, so the design prefers it and treats params only as a fallback.

docs.title: Step 5: Dashboards, native filters and permalinks
5.1 Endpoints and structures
docs.text:
Dashboard endpoints [6.1] include GET /api/v1/dashboard/<id_or_slug> (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/api.py:738), /datasets (:831), /tabs (:919), /charts (:981) and /<id_or_slug>/embedded (:3235-3362). The /datasets response returns, per dataset, columns, metrics, verbose_map, column_formats, main_dttm_col and currency_code_column: everything a renderer needs for labels and formats in one call.

position_json is a flat dict of components, each {type, id, children, parents, meta}, with types ROOT, GRID, HEADER, ROW, COLUMN, CHART, MARKDOWN, TABS, TAB, DIVIDER and DYNAMIC. Grid width is 12 columns. CHART.meta holds chartId, width, height and sliceNameOverride; MARKDOWN.meta.code holds author narrative. The Data Digest walks this tree depth-first in layout order (master has get_charts_in_layout_order at apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/layout.py:69-84, which DBD ports for 6.1), turning tabs into section hints and Markdown into context, treated as untrusted data.

json_metadata (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/schemas.py:200-235) contains native_filter_configuration, chart_configuration (cross-filter scoping), color_scheme, label_colors, shared_label_colors, map_label_colors, color_scheme_domain and cross_filters_enabled. One native filter entry looks like this (shape from superset-frontend/packages/superset-ui-core/src/query/types/Dashboard.ts:70-93):

native_filter_configuration entry (illustrative values)
{
  "id": "NATIVE_FILTER-region",
  "name": "Region",
  "filterType": "filter_select",
  "targets": [{"datasetId": 7, "column": {"name": "region"}}],
  "scope": {"rootPath": ["ROOT_ID"], "excluded": [104]},
  "chartsInScope": [101, 102, 103],
  "cascadeParentIds": [],
  "defaultDataMask": {"extraFormData": {"filters": [{"col": "region", "op": "IN", "val": ["EMEA"]}]},
                      "filterState": {"value": ["EMEA"]}},
  "controlValues": {"multiSelect": true, "defaultToFirstItem": false},
  "requiredFirst": false,
  "type": "NATIVE_FILTER",
  "description": ""
}

docs.title: 5.2 The extra_form_data contract
docs.text:
Native filters publish a data mask {extraFormData, filterState, ownState}. Server-side constants define how extraFormData merges into a query (apache/superset: superset/constants.py:209-234): append keys adhoc_filters, filters, interactive_groupby, interactive_highlight, interactive_drilldown, custom_form_data; override keys granularity_sqla (mapped to granularity), time_column, time_grain, time_range, time_grain_sqla; extra override keys relative_start and relative_end.

Function Works on Location Availability merge_extra_form_data(form_data) form data, before buildQuery apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1184-1260 [6.1] get_dashboard_filter_context(dashboard_id, chart_id, *, active_data_mask=None) -> DashboardFilterContext loads filters, checks dashboard access, computes scope, resolves values from the live mask or the saved defaults apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:272 (dataclass at :60) [M] apply_dashboard_filter_context(query_context, extra_form_data) an already-built query context apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:365 [M]

On 6.1 Data-Bound Documents uses its own port, databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61. It reads native_filter_configuration, uses chartsInScope when present and otherwise scope.rootPath and scope.excluded, takes each value from the permalink's data mask or from defaultDataMask, appends filters with isExtra: true, and overrides the time keys. It deliberately does not implement cascading parents, requiredFirst or defaultToFirstItem pre-queries; a binding affected by one records a rejected filter with reason unsupported_on_6.1 instead of guessing.

docs.title: 5.3 Live filter state and permalinks
docs.text:
Source API Value Availability Filter state (short-lived, per tab) POST /api/v1/dashboard/<pk>/filter_state, GET/PUT/DELETE .../filter_state/<key> (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/filter_state/api.py:54-296) {"value": "<JSON string of the data mask>"} [6.1] Dashboard permalink (durable) POST /api/v1/dashboard/<pk>/permalink (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/permalink/api.py:48), GET /api/v1/dashboard/permalink/<key> (:182) body DashboardPermalinkState; response 201 {key, url} [6.1] Permalink page GET /superset/dashboard/p/<key>/ (apache/superset: superset/views/core.py:634) opens the dashboard with that state [6.1] Explore permalink and unsaved form data /api/v1/explore/permalink, /api/v1/explore/form_data form data [6.1] apache/superset: superset/dashboards/permalink/types.py:21-34 (excerpt)
class DashboardPermalinkState(TypedDict, total=False):
    dataMask: Optional[dict[str, Any]]
    activeTabs: Optional[list[str]]
    anchor: Optional[str]
    # ...
    urlParams: Optional[list[Sequence[str]]]
    chartStates: Optional[dict[str, Any]]


class DashboardPermalinkValue(TypedDict):
    dashboardId: str
    state: DashboardPermalinkState

Context Capture reads the native_filters_key from the dashboard URL, resolves it with GetFilterStateCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/filter_state/get.py:30), and writes a permalink with CreateDashboardPermalinkCommand(dashboard_id, state) (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/permalink/create.py:45), which is get-or-create: the same dashboard, state and user return the same key. The permalink key is stored in DashboardContext.permalink_key, so a refresh reproduces the selection long after the filter-state cache entry expires. chartStates is also present in the 6.1.0 tag's DashboardPermalinkState (checked against the tag source; 6.1.0 types urlParams as list[tuple[str, str]]). The design does not depend on it.

docs.title: Step 6: Datasets, metrics and semantic layers
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/dataset/<id_or_uuid> [6.1] returns main_dttm_col, currency_code_column, template_params, and per column column_name, verbose_name, type, type_generic, is_dttm, groupby, filterable, advanced_data_type, description; per metric metric_name, verbose_name, expression, d3format, currency ({symbol, symbolPosition}), description and warning_text (apache/superset: superset/datasets/api.py:331-420).

These fields drive three parts of the design:

  • The Binding Registry accepts a planner proposal only if every metric is a saved metric of the dataset (or a SIMPLE aggregate over a numeric column) and every dimension is a column with groupby = True; temporal dimensions must have is_dttm.
  • Formatting follows Superset's precedence: the metric's d3format and currency, then the chart's y_axis_format, number_format or currency_format, then SMART_NUMBER. AUTO currency resolves from the result's detected_currency.
  • Data exposure policies use advanced_data_type and column names to default PII columns to "never shown to the LLM".

GET /api/v1/dataset/<id_or_uuid>/related_objects (apache/superset: superset/datasets/api.py:1351) lists the charts and dashboards using a dataset, which helps fan out "this dataset changed" events. On master, the headless POST /api/v1/datasource/<type>/<id>/query (DatasourceQuerySchema, apache/superset: superset/datasource/schemas.py:165-260) accepts metrics, dimensions, filters, time_range, time_column, time_grain, limit and order and validates names against saved definitions; it is the cleanest "semantic" contract and is what the dataset binding source mirrors in a 6.1-compatible QueryObject. Semantic layers (@semantic_layer, SemanticView.get_table(...), apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/semantic_layers/view.py:131-214) are master only and behind SEMANTIC_LAYERS (apache/superset: superset/config.py:776); they back the semantic source kind in v2.

docs.title: Step 7: SQL Lab and Database.execute
docs.text:
Path What it checks Availability Role in the design POST /api/v1/sqllab/execute/ (apache/superset: superset/sqllab/api.py:546) DML gating, raise_for_access(..., force_dataset_match=True) on master [6.1] not used: CSRF applies, results are not cached by chart semantics, raw SQL is a large attack surface Database.execute(sql, QueryOptions) and execute_async (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/common/models.py:87-171) Jinja, SQL_QUERY_MUTATOR, disallowed functions and tables, DML only if allow_dml, RLS by AST rewrite, SQL_MAX_ROW, caching [6.1] opt-in sql bindings only get_sqlglot_dialect(database) (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/queries/query.py:38-48) dialect lookup [6.1] SELECT-only parse of opt-in SQL

QueryOptions fields are catalog, schema, limit, timeout_seconds, template_params, cache: CacheOptions(timeout, force_refresh) and dry_run; QueryResult carries status, statements (each with data as a DataFrame, row_count, truncated), query_id and is_cached (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/queries/types.py:49-130).

Gotcha: Database.execute does not check datasource access

A grep of superset/sql/execution/ finds no raise_for_access or can_access call. The executor applies RLS but does not itself check that the user may query the referenced tables (inferred from source). Data-Bound Documents therefore parses opt-in SQL with sqlglot, rejects anything that is not a single SELECT, and calls security_manager.raise_for_access(database=..., sql=..., catalog=..., schema=..., force_dataset_match=True) before Database.execute, mirroring MCP execute_sql.

docs.title: Step 8: Security: RBAC, RLS, guest tokens and JWT
8.1 Permissions and access checks
docs.text:
• FAB permissions. @api registers the API class and its permission view immediately (appbuilder._add_permission), so class_permission_name = "DataBoundDocs" with method_permission_name produces can_read, can_generate, can_write, can_refresh, can_schedule, can_manage_templates, can_share_snapshot and can_admin on the DataBoundDocs view, assignable to roles in the normal Security UI.
  • Object access. raise_for_access(dashboard=None, chart=None, database=None, datasource=None, query=None, query_context=None, table=None, sql=None, catalog=None, schema=None, template_params=None, force_dataset_match=False, ...) (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:5199) raises SupersetSecurityException on denial; can_access_datasource (:2673) is the boolean form. Chart data is gated by dataset-level access, so a user can render a chart in a document exactly when they could see it in Superset.
  • Access-filtered DAOs. Host DAOs apply ChartFilter, DashboardAccessFilter and DatasourceFilter for the current user, so listing candidates for the digest never reveals objects the user cannot see.

docs.title: 8.2 How RLS is applied
docs.text:
get_rls_filters(table) (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6110) returns the RowLevelSecurityFilter rows for the current user's subjects (master: users, roles and groups; 6.1.0: roles only). REGULAR filters apply to matching subjects; BASE filters apply to everyone except them; filters sharing a group_key are ORed and different groups are ANDed. SqlaTable.get_sqla_row_level_filters(...) (apache/superset: superset/connectors/sqla/models.py:1171) injects them as SQL predicates while the query is built, and clauses are Jinja-rendered as the executing user. Guest RLS rules from a guest token are added for guests.

The design consequence is simple and strict: any path that ends in ChartDataCommand with the right g.user gets RLS automatically, and the framework never opens its own connection to an analytics database. Its only job is to make g.user correct, which it does with override_user(user, force=False) (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1633).

docs.title: 8.3 Ways to act as a user
Step 9: Theming, color schemes and number formats
docs.text:
• Theme tokens. THEME_DEFAULT (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1313, built from _THEME_DEFAULT_BASE at :1264) is an Ant Design token dict with colorPrimary = "#2893B3", colorSuccess, colorError, fontFamily = "Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif", brandLogoUrl and brandAppName. Themes are managed at /api/v1/theme/ (apache/superset: superset/themes/api.py:106) and a dashboard references one through its theme field ({id, theme_name, json_data}), present in 6.1.0. The renderers map these tokens onto PPTX and DOCX accents, positive and negative colors and fonts, unless the template's theme.lock is set.
  • Color schemes. Categorical and sequential schemes are frontend registries; custom ones come from EXTRA_CATEGORICAL_COLOR_SCHEMES (apache/superset: superset/config.py:1228) and EXTRA_SEQUENTIAL_COLOR_SCHEMES (:1385). No REST API returns palette hex lists, so the wheel carries a copy generated at build time from superset-frontend and merges the EXTRA_* lists at runtime. A dashboard's label_colors and map_label_colors take precedence, so "Classic Cars" keeps its dashboard color in the deck.
  • Number formats. Charts store d3-format strings (y_axis_format, number_format, currency_format), with special ids SMART_NUMBER and SMART_NUMBER_SIGNED. Master ships a Python port, format_number_with_config (apache/superset: superset/utils/number_format.py:166) [M], which reproduces browser output for text; Data-Bound Documents vendors it for 6.1. Chart axes and embedded workbooks instead get a deterministic d3-to-Excel mapping, so values stay numeric and editable.

docs.title: Step 10: The embedded SDK
docs.text:
The embedded SDK (npm @superset-ui/embedded-sdk, source in superset-embedded-sdk/, version 0.4.0 on master) mounts a dashboard in a host page's iframe with embedDashboard({id, supersetDomain, mountPoint, fetchGuestToken, dashboardUiConfig, ...}) and returns an EmbeddedDashboard handle (apache/superset: superset-embedded-sdk/src/index.ts:159-191). On master the handle exposes getScrollSize(), unmount(), getDashboardPermalink(anchor), getActiveTabs(), getDataMask(), observeDataMask(cb), setDataMask(mask), getChartStates(), getChartDataPayloads({chartId?}), setThemeConfig(config) and setThemeMode(mode). The SDK source at the 6.1.0 tag has all of these except setDataMask, which is master only [M]; which npm release is paired with a given 6.1 deployment is not verified here. Embedding requires the EMBEDDED_SUPERSET flag (apache/superset: superset/config.py:991) and guest tokens.

Two facts limit its role. Extensions do not load inside embedded dashboards (Step 1.7), so Document Studio cannot appear there. And a guest is not the real user, so "generate as me" is not an embedded use case. The SDK matters for v2: a host application can call getDataMask() or getDashboardPermalink() to capture context, then call the DBD REST API with a guest token to open a live page, which resolves as the guest under the token's RLS. getChartDataPayloads hands back data the browser already has; the design does not use it, because numbers must come from a server-side resolution with provenance.

docs.title: 11.1 How it works
docs.text:
Three tables back the feature (apache/superset: superset/reports/models.py): report_schedule (ReportSchedule, :132, with type, crontab, timezone, report_format defaulting to PNG, sql, chart_id, dashboard_id, validator_type, validator_config_json, last_value, extra), report_recipient (type, recipient_config_json) and report_execution_log (value, value_row_json, state, error_message, timestamps). The flow:

  1. Celery beat fires reports.scheduler every minute (apache/superset: superset/config.py:2095-2096).
  2. scheduler (apache/superset: superset/tasks/scheduler.py:92-131) returns unless ALERT_REPORTS is on, then, for each active schedule and each cron tick in the window computed by cron_schedule_window(triggered_at, cron, timezone) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/cron_util.py:74), enqueues reports.execute.
  3. AsyncExecuteReportScheduleCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/report/execute.py:2668) runs ReportScheduleStateMachine (:2625). Alerts run their SQL condition first (apache/superset: superset/commands/report/alert.py:69); only a triggered alert proceeds.
  4. _get_notification_content() (apache/superset: superset/commands/report/execute.py:1649) produces content per format, and a notification plugin per recipient type delivers it. Each phase writes a log row, readable at /api/v1/report/<pk>/log/.
report_format Produced by Raster or data Dashboards Availability PNG headless browser screenshot of Explore or each dashboard tab (execute.py:1096) raster yes [6.1] PDF build_pdf_from_screenshots over those PNGs (execute.py:1239-1256) raster PDF yes [6.1] CSV saved query_context POSTed to the chart data endpoint over HTTP with executor cookies (execute.py:1338, 1382) data no (charts only) [6.1] XLSX same path data no [M] TEXT DataFrame rendered with to_html for email or to_markdown for Slack (execute.py:1502) data no [6.1] NONE link only, alerts only none n/a [M]

docs.title: 11.2 Why its screenshot pipeline is not what we want
docs.text:
The PDF path is literally a stack of images:

apache/superset: superset/utils/pdf.py:30-41
def build_pdf_from_screenshots(snapshots: list[bytes]) -> bytes:
    images = []

    for snap in snapshots:
        img = Image.open(BytesIO(snap))
        if img.mode == "RGBA":
            img = img.convert("RGB")
        images.append(img)
    logger.info("building pdf")
    try:
        new_pdf = BytesIO()
        images[0].save(new_pdf, "PDF", save_all=True, append_images=images[1:])

The reasons the pipeline is built this way are also the reasons it cannot serve native output:

  1. Rendering exists only in the browser. Each viz plugin's buildQuery makes the query and its transformProps makes the ECharts or D3 configuration; the Python backend returns DataFrames and has no renderer.
  2. Dashboards have no server-side composition. Native filters are applied in the browser, so dashboards can be delivered only as PNG or PDF; tabular formats are guarded by self._report_schedule.chart and ... (execute.py:1675-1677).
  3. Even query construction leans on the browser. For charts without a saved query context, the CSV and TEXT paths take a screenshot only to make the frontend persist one (_update_query_context, execute.py:1586).
  4. The browser machinery is heavy and fragile. Master carries 1,434 lines in superset/utils/webdriver.py and 1,870 in superset/utils/screenshot_utils.py, with readiness heuristics (_wait_for_charts_ready, webdriver.py:580) and tiled capture for large dashboards. 6.1.0 defaults to Selenium with Firefox; master removed Selenium and requires Playwright with Chromium (apache/superset: UPDATING.md:1621-1638).
  5. Identity is the executor's. Data formats run as the user chosen by ALERT_REPORTS_EXECUTORS (default [ExecutorType.EDITOR] on master, apache/superset: superset/config.py:2838; [ExecutorType.OWNER] in 6.1.0) [M*], logged in through machine auth cookies (apache/superset: superset/utils/machine_auth.py:97-100), not as each recipient.

Beyond that, the content carrier cannot hold a deck: NotificationContent (apache/superset: superset/reports/notifications/base.py:26-42) has fields for CSV, XLSX [M], PDF, screenshots, text and a DataFrame, and the recipient types are a closed enum:

apache/superset: superset/reports/models.py:67-71
class ReportRecipientType(StrEnum):
    EMAIL = "Email"
    SLACK = "Slack"
    SLACKV2 = "SlackV2"
    WEBHOOK = "Webhook"

Adding a "Generator" recipient type is a core change, listed as an upstream follow-up rather than a dependency.

docs.title: 11.3 What we reuse: the webhook, the schedule and the log
docs.text:
The Webhook recipient (feature flag ALERT_REPORT_WEBHOOK, apache/superset: superset/config.py:848) turns an Alert into a data-condition trigger, the only "data changed" signal Superset has. It posts JSON to recipient_config_json["target"]:

Webhook body (keys from apache/superset: superset/reports/notifications/webhook.py:84-105)
{
  "name": "Hourly orders below threshold",
  "header": {
    "notification_format": "TEXT",
    "notification_type": "Alert",
    "notification_source": "chart",
    "chart_id": 101,
    "dashboard_id": null
  },
  "text": null,
  "description": "",
  "url": "https://superset.example.com/explore/?slice_id=101"
}
Aspect 6.1.0 Master HTTPS only ALERT_REPORTS_WEBHOOK_HTTPS_ONLY = True same (apache/superset: superset/config.py:2916) Internal hosts allowed blocked unless ALERT_REPORTS_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_INTERNAL_HOSTS = True (:2929); SSRF-safe requester, no redirects Retries exponential backoff, 5 tries on 5xx and 429 same plus max_time=120 Signature or auth header none none TEXT format no files no files; text is set only on failure, to a generic "contact the report owner" message (webhook.py:93-99)

Gotcha: the webhook payload is a signal, not data

It carries no user identity, no execution id, no alert value, and no data for TEXT reports. Its notification_format and notification_source values differ between the 6.1 docs example ("JSON", "Alert") and the code (the schedule's report_format; chart or dashboard). The DBD hook therefore authenticates the call by an unguessable token in the URL path, cross-checks chart_id and dashboard_id against its own trigger record, ignores text and notification_format, runs as the trigger's stored run-as user, and reads the alert's value from /api/v1/report/<pk>/log/ in-process when it writes an alert brief.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• A .supx extension can deliver a REST API, GTF tasks and MCP tools on 6.1, but its UI can appear only in SQL Lab; the dashboard-visible chat slot is master only, so 6.1 needs a standalone Studio page.
  • GTF is the job engine for every generation, but it neither switches users nor schedules; the task body must use override_user, and recurring work needs a beat entry.
  • The data primitive is the chart query context executed by ChartDataCommand in-process, which applies raise_for_access and RLS and reproduces dashboard numbers; the filter-context and form-data helpers that make it easy are master only.
  • Permalinks, not filter-state keys, are the durable capture of a dashboard's filter selection.
  • MCP is useful for planning on master but is capped and, on 6.1, runs as the dev user; it never carries document data.
  • Alerts and Reports are screenshot-based by construction, yet their webhook recipient, schedule math and execution log are reusable as triggers.

docs.title: Target architecture
docs.text:
Reads: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py, superset/tasks/manager.py, superset/tasks/scheduler.py, superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py, superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py, superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py · Builds on: Superset landscape (6.1) · Time: ~40 min

This chapter lays out the final architecture of Superset Data-Bound Documents (prose name: Data-Bound Documents; identifiers: dbd, databound). You will see every component and what it is responsible for, which Superset process each one runs in, how a request travels through the system for each kind of trigger, and which Superset APIs it depends on, with their 6.1.0 and master availability. The chapter closes with a component-by-component mapping to Presenton (what is reused, extended or replaced), the technology choices and why they were made, and a summary of the decision log that produced this design.

Availability tags used throughout Part VII:

Tag Meaning [6.1] Present in the 6.1.0 tag (May 2026, the latest stable release) and on master [M] Present only on master (cabd8d4, 2026-11-02). Expected in 7.0, but that mapping is UNVERIFIED [M*] Present in 6.1.0 but changed on master

docs.title: Step 1: The interpretation this architecture serves
docs.text:
The request was for "a common framework" that gives Apache Superset the workflow Presenton gives PowerPoint: write a prompt, pick a template, get a finished artifact. The same flow should produce documents, text and pages, run on the fly and on events, use dynamic data, and never use screenshots. This design adopts the following reading of that request, and every component below exists to satisfy one part of it.

Build one common, output-agnostic generation framework that turns three inputs into four kinds of output:

  • Inputs: a prompt, a chosen template, and a Superset data context. The data context is any of: a dashboard with its live native-filter state, saved charts, datasets with their saved metrics, a semantic view [M], or a SQL Lab query.
  • Outputs:
    • (a) PowerPoint decks (PPTX);
    • (b) documents (DOCX, PDF, Markdown);
    • (c) text (narratives, executive summaries, emails, Slack posts, alert briefs);
    • (d) web pages (interactive HTML reports and, in v2, generated Superset dashboards).
  • Triggers: on demand (a button or chat message in Superset, a REST call, an MCP tool call) or by events (cron schedules, Superset Alerts firing a webhook, data freshness changes, chart or dashboard definition changes, external webhooks).

Three data rules are non-negotiable:

  1. Every chart, table, KPI and number comes from a live Superset query executed with the requesting user's permissions and row-level security (RLS). Scheduled runs use an explicitly recorded run-as user.
  2. Data elements are rendered natively: editable PPTX and DOCX charts with an embedded workbook, real tables, real text runs, vector SVG on the web. No Superset UI page is ever captured as pixels.
  3. Every artifact is re-runnable. A refresh re-executes the queries and replaces the data in place.

The design keeps Presenton's stage shape (outline, layout structure, schema-constrained content, hydration, export; see Standard generation pipeline) but changes one thing at its core. Presenton asks the LLM for chart categories and series[].values (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534) and copies them into the slide (presenton: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1367-1432). In Data-Bound Documents the LLM never produces a number. It picks bindings from menus Superset has validated and writes prose that cites facts by token. Numbers enter an artifact only through deterministic code.

docs.title: Step 2: Seven design principles
docs.text:
Each principle rules out a whole family of alternative designs. When you modify the system, check your change against this list first.

  1. Superset is the data plane. All data access goes through ChartDataCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:36), or through Database.execute for the narrow SQL case, inside a Superset process with g.user set to the right user. The framework never opens its own connection to an analytics database and never calls Superset's chart-data HTTP endpoint from a worker.
  2. The agent proposes, the engine disposes. The LLM outputs structure, binding choices from validated menus, and prose with tokens. Every number, label and chart series is produced by deterministic code.
  3. A binding exists only if the Binding Registry accepted it. The LLM can name only ids the registry issued, as JSON Schema enums, so it cannot invent a query.
  4. One spec, many renderers. The same DocumentSpec renders to a deck, a document, a page and a text brief.
  5. Thin .supx, fat wheel. A .supx bundle carries only the extension's own .py files and cannot install dependencies (apache/superset: superset-extensions-cli/src/superset_extensions_cli/cli.py:225-275). The framework therefore ships as a preinstalled wheel plus a small extension that holds only the Superset wiring.
  6. One version-sniffing Superset Adapter. Every import of non-public Superset code lives in one module, databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py, which detects capabilities at import time.
  7. Fail closed, render honestly. A forbidden or failed binding becomes a visible placeholder and removes the narrative that depends on it. Nothing ever falls back to a picture of a chart.

Gotcha: why not call /api/v1/chart/data from the worker

It looks simpler to have a worker call Superset's REST chart-data endpoint with a token. On 6.1 with GLOBAL_ASYNC_QUERIES on, that endpoint answers JSON requests with 202 and then requires the async JWT cookie, returning 401 without it. A bearer-token worker cannot read the data. Alerts and Reports work around this by logging the executor in with machine-auth cookies, which is exactly the "executor's data, not the recipient's" model this design avoids. In-process ChartDataCommand under override_user has neither problem.

docs.text:
The framework has sixteen named components. The table gives each one's single responsibility, where it runs and where its code lives. The sub-steps after the table group them by the job they do.

Component Responsibility Runs in Package or module Document Spec (DocumentSpec) Output-agnostic, data-bound description of one immutable document version everywhere databound_docs.spec Context Capture Turns "what the user is looking at" into ids plus a durable dashboard permalink browser, web extension frontend plus the POST /documents handler Data Digest Deterministic, token-budgeted summary of the context that the LLM is allowed to see worker databound_docs.planner.digest Planner (pipeline, agent, template) Decides sections, layouts and which bindings fill which slots worker (GTF task) databound_docs.planner Superset Adapter The only module that imports Superset internals; version-sniffed at import web, worker, MCP databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py Binding Registry The only way a binding enters a document: validates names, access, shape and limits, assigns b_* ids worker, web, MCP databound_docs.binder.registry Binding Resolver Runs every DataBinding in-process through ChartDataCommand as the right user and records provenance worker, web (live pages), MCP databound_docs.binder plus the Superset Adapter Fact Engine Derives facts (totals, changes, ranks, labels) from resolved rows with pure functions everywhere databound_docs.facts Narrative Writer One schema-constrained LLM call per section; writes text with fact tokens only worker databound_docs.planner.writer Narrative Verifier Deterministic checks on tokens, numerals, entities, direction and length, plus a repair loop worker, web databound_docs.planner.verify Renderers PPTX Renderer, DOCX Renderer, HTML Renderer, PDF Printer, Text Renderer: resolved spec to native files worker (PDF optionally in a sidecar) databound_docs.render DrawingML Chart Writer Writes raw c:chartSpace XML for charts python-pptx cannot create (combo, emulations) worker databound_docs.render.drawingml Template Registry Versioned templates with data slots, PPTX and DOCX masters, importer web, worker databound_docs.templates plus table dbd_template Trigger Service Schedules, alert webhooks, freshness sentinels, definition-change listeners, external webhooks beat, worker, web databound_docs.triggers plus the extension Document Studio Chat panel [M], SQL Lab panel [6.1], standalone Studio page, live page viewer browser extension frontend DBD Extension (databound.docgen) REST API, GTF tasks, MCP tools, frontend contributions web, worker, MCP databound-docgen-<version>.supx

docs.title: 3.1 Data plane: Context Capture, Superset Adapter, Binding Registry, Binding Resolver
docs.text:
These four components are the reason the framework can promise "live data with the user's permissions".

  • Context Capture runs synchronously in POST /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/documents. It checks can_generate on DataBoundDocs, loads each dashboard through the access-filtered DAO, and calls security_manager.raise_for_access(dashboard=...). If the request carries a short-lived native_filters_key, it reads the data mask with GetFilterStateCommand (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/filter_state/get.py:30) and converts it into a durable permalink with CreateDashboardPermalinkCommand(dashboard_id, state) (apache/superset: superset/commands/dashboard/permalink/create.py:45). The result is a DataContext that can be replayed months later.
  • Superset Adapter (databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py) is the only module that imports Superset internals: ChartDataCommand, ChartDataQueryContextSchema, override_user (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1633), the filter-context helpers, the form_data rebuild, the permalink and filter-state commands, and the guest-token helpers. It sniffs capabilities at import time and exposes a stable internal interface (as_user, run_query_context, apply_dashboard_filters, chart_query_context). Building the Superset extension walks through the file.
  • Binding Registry is called by every planner strategy, by chat edits and by MCP. It loads the chart or dataset through access-filtered DAOs, re-checks can_access_datasource, verifies that every metric is a saved metric (or a simple aggregate over a real numeric column) and every dimension a groupby=True column, caps row_limit, and only then issues an id b_<slug>.
  • Binding Resolver compiles each binding into a query context JSON, applies the filter merge (dashboard filters, binding filters, parameters, time overrides), sets g.form_data, loads it through ChartDataQueryContextSchema, calls ChartDataCommand(qc).validate() (which runs raise_for_access first, apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:107-108) and .run(). It then shapes rows and fills a Provenance record. Data-bound slide model specifies every field.

The resolver follows the same recipe as master's dashboard Excel export, which replays each chart's saved query context as the requesting user with live dashboard filters:

apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:200-231 (excerpt)
    json_body = dict(json_body)
    # Export full JSON results, regardless of saved values.
    json_body["result_format"] = ChartDataResultFormat.JSON
    json_body["result_type"] = ChartDataResultType.FULL
    json_body.pop("force", None)
    # ...
    form_data = dict(json_body.get("form_data") or {})
    form_data["dashboardId"] = dashboard_id
    # ...
    form_data["slice_id"] = chart.id
    json_body["form_data"] = form_data

    filter_context = get_dashboard_filter_context(
        dashboard_id=dashboard_id,
        chart_id=chart.id,
        active_data_mask=active_data_mask,
    )
    if filter_context.extra_form_data:
        apply_dashboard_filter_context(json_body, filter_context.extra_form_data)

    # Jinja macros read the query context from ``g.form_data``.
    g.form_data = json_body

    query_context = ChartDataQueryContextSchema().load(json_body)
    command = ChartDataCommand(query_context)
    command.validate()
    result = command.run()

That module is [M]. On 6.1 the Superset Adapter falls back to DBD's own port of the native-filter scope logic, databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61, which returns an object with the same extra_form_data and filters contract, so call sites do not branch.

docs.title: 3.2 Language plane: Data Digest, Planner, Narrative Writer, Narrative Verifier
docs.text:
These components are the only ones that talk to an LLM, and each one is fenced so that the LLM cannot affect numbers.

  • Data Digest builds everything the LLM may see: dashboard inventory in layout order, chart and dataset metadata, and profiles (not rows) of each candidate binding, formatted and labeled with candidate fact ids. It is bounded by DATA_POLICY.max_digest_tokens (default 12,000) and an exposure level (metadata_only, aggregates by default, samples). The digest preview endpoint POST /context/digest returns exactly this JSON so a user can see "what the AI will see".
  • Planner has three strategies that all produce the same Plan object whose bindings are always registry ids:
Strategy Availability How it plans pipeline (default) [6.1], [M] Fixed stages with strict JSON schemas: outline, deterministic layout fit (with an optional LLM tie-break), section writing. Binding proposals are enums in the outline schema agent (opt-in) [M] only Tool-calling loop over a read-only MCP allowlist, ending in submit_plan. Needs per-user MCP identity, which 6.1 lacks template (no LLM) [6.1], [M] The template declares fixed bindings and deterministic sentences. For air-gapped or regulated deployments and scheduled briefs
  • Narrative Writer makes one call per section. It receives the section intent, the text fields with character budgets, and a FACTS table restricted to that section. It never receives rows. Its response schema has a regex that forbids digits, %, $ and braces except inside valid tokens.
  • Narrative Verifier is deterministic: token validity, no literal numbers or number words, no literal category names (the entity scan), direction words that agree with the sign of the cited change fact, superlatives only next to rank facts, and length. Violations go back to the writer at most twice, then the field is replaced by a deterministic sentence and marked fallback.

All LLM calls go through call_structured() on an LLMProvider protocol (openai_compatible, anthropic, bedrock, vertex). Roles (planner, writer, verifier) map to profiles in DATABOUND_DOCS["LLM"], and allowed_hosts restricts egress. Generation flow gives every prompt and schema.

docs.title: 3.3 Output plane: Renderers and the DrawingML Chart Writer
docs.text:
Every renderer reads a resolved DocumentSpec version and its BindingResult rows. None of them re-queries unless asked to refresh, and none of them loads a Superset UI page.

Renderer Library What it produces PPTX Renderer python-pptx 1.0.2 (MIT) Native charts with an embedded XlsxWriter workbook, native tables, KPI groups, token runs, speaker notes, the /customXml/dbd-manifest.json part. Refresh through Chart.replace_data DrawingML Chart Writer lxml over python-pptx's OPC layer Combo charts (c:barChart plus c:lineChart on a secondary axis) and emulations (waterfall, funnel, bullet) DOCX Renderer python-docx 1.2.0 (MIT) Styled paragraphs, native tables, DrawingML chart parts (prototype gate G5) or vector SVG from rows HTML Renderer Jinja templates, ECharts (live pages), vl-convert-python (static SVG) Live pages that resolve as the viewer, static HTML with embedded JSON snapshots PDF Printer Playwright Chromium page.pdf() on a local file (or a printer sidecar, or WeasyPrint) Vector PDF printed from DBD's own static HTML, network disabled Text Renderer plain Python Markdown, plain text, email HTML, Slack mrkdwn, alert briefs

Native rendering, no screenshots covers each renderer in detail, including the d3-to-Excel number format mapping and the viz_type matrix.

docs.title: 3.4 Lifecycle plane: Template Registry, Trigger Service, Document Studio, DBD Extension
docs.text:
• Template Registry stores immutable template versions in dbd_template: JSON layouts derived from Presenton Template v2 with data slots, plus optional PPTX and DOCX masters in object storage. Masters are imported deterministically from shape names such as slot:chart:trend (no vision model). Built-ins ship in the wheel: tpl_exec_review, tpl_dashboard_walkthrough, tpl_analytical_report, tpl_interactive_report, tpl_kpi_brief, tpl_weekly_email, alert_brief.
  • Trigger Service covers the five trigger types cron, alert_webhook, freshness, definition_change and external_webhook. GTF has no cron, so a plain Celery beat task databound_docs.trigger_tick runs every minute and schedules run_trigger GTF tasks with a deduplicating task_key. Scheduling and live refresh has the details.
  • Document Studio is the UI. On master it lives in the global chat slot (chat.registerChat, apache/superset: superset-frontend/packages/superset-core/src/chat/index.ts:76-80), which is visible on dashboards and Explore. On 6.1 it is a SQL Lab panel at sqllab.panels plus a standalone Studio page served by the extension.
  • DBD Extension (databound.docgen) is the wiring: the @api REST class DataBoundDocsApi, the GTF @task functions, the guarded @tool and @prompt registrations, and the frontend contributions.

Gotcha: there is no dashboard or Explore contribution area

The new extension framework renders contributed views only in SQL Lab, plus the global chat slot on master. The legacy keys dashboard.nav.right, dashboard.slice.header.menu and explore.chart.header live in a module-local registry inside the host bundle that a .supx cannot reach. Data-Bound Documents covers the gap with the chat slot [M], the Studio page and SQL Lab panel [6.1], and an optional databound-docs-ui-overrides npm package for deployments that build their own Superset frontend. Upstream slots are proposed in the Roadmap.

docs.title: Step 4: Packaging, thin bundle and fat wheel
docs.text:
A .supx is a zip of manifest.json, frontend/dist/<file> and backend/src/<module>.py. Superset imports the backend files from memory through InMemoryFinder; nothing installs [project] dependencies. python-pptx, python-docx, an HTTP client and the renderers therefore cannot ride in the bundle. The framework ships as two artifacts built from one repository: the superset-databound-docs wheel, preinstalled in the web, worker and MCP images, and the databound-docgen-<version>.supx bundle, dropped into EXTENSIONS_PATH.

The repository has three top-level folders: core/ (the wheel, package databound_docs with spec, planner, binder, facts, format, render, templates, triggers, compat, llm, storage and db), extension/ (built with the superset-extensions CLI, backend modules entrypoint.py, api.py, tasks.py, tools.py, triggers.py and superset_adapter.py under databound/docgen/), and the optional ui-overrides/ npm package. Building the Superset extension walks through every file.

The identifiers follow from publisher: "databound" and name: "docgen":

Identifier Value Derived by Extension id databound.docgen publisher.name (apache/superset: superset-core/src/superset_core/extensions/types.py:38-84) Backend entrypoint databound.docgen.entrypoint the CLI build_manifest Module Federation name databound_docgen the CLI REST base path /extensions/databound/docgen/v1 @api(resource_name="v1") in extension context (apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:189-207) GTF task types extensions.databound.docgen.<task> host task decorator prefixing (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:147-160) MCP tool names extensions.databound.docgen.<tool> host tool registration (apache/superset: superset/core/mcp/core_mcp_injection.py:123-142) Bundle file databound-docgen-<version>.supx superset-extensions bundle

The core package databound_docs must not import Superset at module top level. That rule keeps the Fact Engine, the Narrative Verifier, the renderers and the spec testable without a Superset install, and it keeps the stub-binding problem away: superset_core decorators must be imported after the host has injected its implementations, which happens before the extension entrypoint is imported.

Gotcha: two frontend bundles from one source

6.1 maps @apache-superset/core to window.superset through webpack externals, while master injects it through the Module Federation share scope. views.registerView also takes a provider function on 6.1 and a component on master [M*]. The repository builds databound-docgen-1.0.0-superset6.1.supx and databound-docgen-1.0.0-superset7.supx, and superset dbd doctor checks that the installed variant matches the host.

Gotcha: @tool can take the whole extension down

If fastmcp is not installed in a process, Superset skips MCP injection and the @tool stub raises NotImplementedError at import. Because the extension entrypoint imports everything, that would make the REST API disappear too. The entrypoint wraps from databound.docgen import tools in try/except (ImportError, NotImplementedError).

    W2["celery worker -Q databound_docs (DBD pool)"] --> Redis
    W2 --> PG
    W2 --> S3["Object storage (S3, GCS, Azure, FS, or EXPORT_STORAGE on M)"]
    W2 --> LLM["LLM endpoint"]
    W2 --> DWH["Analytics databases"]
    Beat["celery beat (databound_docs.trigger_tick)"] --> Redis
    McpS --> PG
    McpS --> DWH

docs.title: 5.1 Configuration
docs.text:
All configuration lives in superset_config.py. Feature flags must be on in every process, because Superset registers APIs and imports extensions from the flag value at startup.

superset_config.py (Data-Bound Documents section)
from celery.schedules import crontab
from databound_docs.celery_routing import route_dbd_tasks  # router function, see 5.2

FEATURE_FLAGS = {
    **FEATURE_FLAGS,
    "ENABLE_EXTENSIONS": True,        # [6.1] load .supx bundles in every process
    "GLOBAL_TASK_FRAMEWORK": True,    # [6.1] @task, /api/v1/task, Task List UI
    "ALERT_REPORTS": True,            # only for alert_webhook triggers
    "ALERT_REPORT_WEBHOOK": True,     # only for alert_webhook triggers
}
EXTENSIONS_PATH = "/app/extensions"  # holds databound-docgen-1.0.0.supx

class CeleryConfig:  # extend the deployment's existing CeleryConfig
    # ... existing broker, imports, beat entries ...
    task_routes = [route_dbd_tasks]   # DBD GTF tasks to the databound_docs queue
    beat_schedule = {
        # ... existing entries (reports.scheduler, reports.prune_log) ...
        "databound_docs.trigger_tick": {
            "task": "databound_docs.trigger_tick",
            "schedule": crontab(minute="*"),
        },
    }
CELERY_CONFIG = CeleryConfig

DATABOUND_DOCS = {
    "STORAGE": {"backend": "s3", "bucket": "superset-dbd", "prefix": "dbd/"},
    "LLM": {
        "profiles": {
            "default": {"provider": "openai_compatible", "base_url": "http://vllm:8000/v1",
                        "model": "your-model-id", "api_key_env": "DBD_LLM_KEY"},
        },
        "roles": {"planner": "default", "writer": "default", "verifier": "default"},
        "allowed_hosts": ["vllm"],
    },
    "PLANNER_STRATEGY": "pipeline",       # "pipeline" (default) or "agent" (master only)
    "DATA_POLICY": {"default_exposure": "aggregates", "max_digest_tokens": 12000,
                    "label_masking": False},
    "PDF_ENGINE": "playwright",           # "playwright", "printer_sidecar", "weasyprint", "off"
    "MAX_BINDINGS_PER_DOC": 60,
    "MAX_ROWS_PER_BINDING": 5000,
    "ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS": False,
    "CHAT_SLOT": True,                    # master only; set False if another chat extension is used
    "MCP_ALLOW_DEV_USER": False,          # refuse mutate tools when MCP resolves the dev user
}

DATABOUND_DOCS is read at call time from current_app.config, never at import time, so a library imported by superset_config.py itself does not freeze stale values.

docs.title: 5.2 Isolating long jobs on their own queue
docs.text:
GTF enqueues every task through one generic Celery task, tasks.execute (apache/superset: superset/tasks/scheduler.py:396), passing the GTF type as a keyword:

apache/superset: superset/tasks/manager.py:582 (call shape)
execute_task.delay(task_uuid=str(task.uuid), task_type=task_type, args=args, kwargs=kwargs)

Celery accepts router functions in task_routes, so DBD can route on that keyword without any change to Superset:

databound_docs/celery_routing.py
DBD_PREFIX = "extensions.databound.docgen."


def route_dbd_tasks(name, args, kwargs, options, task=None, **kw):
    if name == "tasks.execute" and str((kwargs or {}).get("task_type", "")).startswith(DBD_PREFIX):
        return {"queue": "databound_docs"}
    if name == "databound_docs.trigger_tick":
        return {"queue": "databound_docs"}
    return None   # fall through to the deployment's other routes

Operators run at least one worker with -Q databound_docs and keep the default queue for reports, thumbnails and other GTF work. A 90-second LLM job then cannot starve a thumbnail. Whether the router sees task_type identically on 6.1 is covered by prototype gate G8; the fallback is a concurrency semaphore in the metadata database.

docs.title: 5.3 Image build and install
docs.text:
1. Install superset-databound-docs, python-pptx==1.0.2, python-docx==1.2.0, httpx, vl-convert-python, jsonschema and, optionally, playwright into the web, worker and MCP images.
  2. Copy the .supx into EXTENSIONS_PATH.
  3. Run superset dbd db-upgrade (DBD's own Alembic environment, version table dbd_alembic_version).
  4. Restart every process. Extension discovery happens only at startup.
  5. Run superset dbd doctor. It checks flags per process, installed packages, the beat entry and router, storage write access, the bundle variant, DATA_CACHE_CONFIG (warning on NullCache), and that MCP_DEV_USERNAME is unset when the agent strategy is used.

docs.title: Step 6: Request paths
docs.text: Five request paths cover every trigger. All of them converge on the same Binding Resolver call under a well-defined identity.

docs.title: 6.1 On-demand deck from a filtered dashboard
docs.text:
This is the headline flow. The web request does only the synchronous part (access checks, filter capture, row inserts) and returns 202 in well under a second; everything else runs in one GTF task.

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User browser
    participant A as DBD REST API (web)
    participant AD as Superset Adapter
    participant T as GTF TaskManager
