    participant W as Worker (databound_docs queue)
    participant L as LLM
    participant O as Object storage
    U->>A: POST /documents with prompt, template, dashboard and native_filters_key
    A->>AD: check dashboard access, read filter state, create permalink
    A->>A: insert dbd_document v0 and dbd_job
    A->>T: generate_document.schedule(job_id, user_id) with task_key
    A-->>U: 202 with document_id, job_id, task_uuid
    U->>A: GET /jobs/id/events?after=0 (long poll)
    T->>W: tasks.execute routed to databound_docs
    W->>W: override_user(requester)
    W->>AD: profile candidates (ChartDataCommand, small limits)
    W->>L: outline over the Data Digest
    W->>W: deterministic layout fit and Binding Registry checks
    W->>AD: resolve bindings, Fact Engine computes facts
    W->>L: section text with fact tokens
    W->>W: Narrative Verifier, repair or fallback
    W->>O: write preview HTML and PPTX
    W->>A: append events (section.ready, artifact.ready)
    A-->>U: events, then download link

Three details make this path robust:

  • Deduplication. task_key = sha256(user_id, template_id@version, canonical(context), prompt, parameters), so a double click joins the same GTF task instead of starting a second one.
  • Identity. GTF does not switch the executing user. The task receives user_id as an argument and wraps its body in override_user(user, force=False), the pattern of Superset's own execute_chart_query (apache/superset: superset/tasks/async_queries.py:165-175).
  • Events. Fine-grained events (outline.ready, binding.resolved, section.ready, artifact.ready) go to dbd_job_event and are served by long poll (GET /jobs/<id>/events?after=<seq>&wait=25). Coarse progress is mirrored into GTF with get_context().update_task(progress=(i, n), payload=...), so the built-in Task List shows it too.

Gotcha: GTF runs your task as nobody in particular

TaskContext.__init__ (apache/superset: superset/tasks/context.py:60) records the task UUID, abort and cleanup handlers and the timeout timer, and neither it nor the tasks.execute executor sets g.user. Superset's own async chart-data task says so in its docstring: "The GTF executor does not impersonate on its own" (apache/superset: superset/tasks/async_queries.py:165-175). If a task body forgets override_user, DAO base filters, raise_for_access and RLS evaluate without the requester. Depending on configuration that either fails every query or, worse, runs with a broader identity. The as_user helper in the Superset Adapter is the only sanctioned way in, and it refuses an inactive or missing user.

docs.title: 6.2 Synchronous text brief
docs.text: kind: "text" with options.sync: true (and the MCP tool dbd_brief) runs steps 2 to 10 inline in the web request within a 20-second budget. If the budget runs out, the call falls back to the asynchronous path and returns 202. This is the "text on the fly" answer: a one-paragraph KPI brief from a dashboard needs one digest, one writer call and a handful of cached queries.

docs.title: 6.3 Live page opened by a viewer
docs.text:
A page document is never a static file by default. The HTML shell loads a standalone bundle that calls GET /documents/<id>/render-model?live=1, and the server re-resolves every live binding as the viewer, under the viewer's own session.

sequenceDiagram
    participant V as Viewer browser
    participant A as DBD REST API (web)
    participant AD as Superset Adapter
    V->>A: GET /pages/document_id
    A-->>V: HTML shell plus dbd-page bundle
    V->>A: GET /documents/id/render-model?live=1
    A->>AD: resolve live bindings as g.user (the viewer)
    A->>A: recompute facts, compare RLS fingerprint with narrative
    A-->>V: sections with shaped rows, facts, provenance
    V->>V: ECharts draws charts client-side

If the viewer's RLS fingerprint differs from the one the narrative was written under, tokens still re-resolve to the viewer's values, claim lint re-runs against the viewer's facts, and a failing narrative is replaced by deterministic sentences with a "Summary written for different data" notice. Because LLM prose holds no literal numbers or category names, the stored text itself leaks nothing. Security, RLS, auth explains the rule.

docs.title: 6.4 Scheduled or alert-triggered refresh
docs.text:
Events do not get a human identity, so every trigger row carries run_as_fk, and DBD re-validates that user before each run.

sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Celery beat
    participant S as Superset Alert (webhook recipient)
    participant H as DBD hook route (web)
    participant T as GTF TaskManager
    participant W as Worker (databound_docs queue)
    B->>W: databound_docs.trigger_tick every minute
    W->>T: run_trigger.schedule with task_key trigger_id and scheduled_for
    S->>H: POST /hooks/token when the alert condition fires
    H->>H: constant-time token check, cross-check chart_id and dashboard_id
    H->>T: run_trigger.schedule
    T->>W: tasks.execute
    W->>W: validate run_as user is active and still has access
    W->>W: override_user(run_as), resolve live bindings
    W->>W: skip if every data_hash is unchanged
    W->>W: facts, narrative policy, replace_data in place
    W->>W: new version, deliver by email, Slack, webhook or library

The alert route uses Superset's own Alerts and Reports scheduler purely as a data-condition detector. The alert should use report_format = TEXT on a chart-scoped alert (6.1) or NONE (master), so Superset takes no screenshot for nothing. The webhook payload is unsigned and carries no identity or data, so DBD treats it as a signal only.

docs.title: 6.5 External agent through MCP
docs.text:
An external agent (or Superset's own chat surface) can drive the same framework through dbd_* tools registered with superset_core.mcp.decorators.tool and class_permission_name="DataBoundDocs".

sequenceDiagram
    participant G as External agent
    participant M as superset mcp run
    participant R as Binding Registry
    participant T as GTF TaskManager
    G->>M: dbd_list_templates, then get_dashboard_info
    M->>M: mcp_auth_hook resolves the user and sets g.user
    G->>M: dbd_propose_binding with a DataBinding
    M->>R: register, preview at most 10 rows and default facts
    G->>M: dbd_generate_document with CreateDocumentRequest
    M->>T: generate_document.schedule as the resolved user
    G->>M: dbd_get_job until completed

MCP responses carry ids, statuses, display strings and at most 10 preview rows, which respects master's 50 KB response cap (apache/superset: superset/mcp_service/mcp_config.py:499-512; 6.1.0 instead caps responses at an estimated 25,000 tokens). The full data for an artifact is always fetched by the worker's own Binding Resolver, never moved through MCP.

Gotcha: MCP on 6.1 is a single shared identity

On 6.1, get_user_from_request() checks only g.user (set by external middleware) and then MCP_DEV_USERNAME (6.1.0 tag, superset/mcp_service/auth.py:176-230). There is no JWT-claims-to-user mapping, so every call runs as the dev user unless your deployment adds middleware. DBD's mutate and data tools refuse to run when the resolved user is the configured dev user, unless MCP_ALLOW_DEV_USER is true. Per-user MCP (MCP_USER_RESOLVER, API keys) is [M], which is also why the agent planner is master only.

docs.title: Step 7: The Superset API surface it rides on
docs.text:
Every arrow into Superset in the diagrams above maps to one row here. "Internal" means the call lives in the Superset Adapter and is covered by per-version contract tests.

Need API or extension point Availability Public or internal Fallback when missing REST endpoints superset_core.rest_api.api.RestApi, superset_core.rest_api.decorators.api [6.1] public none needed Long jobs, progress, cancel superset_core.tasks.decorators.task, get_context().update_task, on_abort, TaskOptions(task_key, task_name, timeout) [6.1] basic; depends_on, update_task(immediate=), heartbeats, /status_changes [M] public 6.1: sequential resolution in one task, status polling Agent and external tools superset_core.mcp.decorators.tool, prompt [6.1]; per-user identity [M] public 6.1: pipeline only; mutate tools refused for the dev user Models and access-filtered DAOs superset_core.common.models, superset_core.common.daos (host-replaced, apache/superset: superset/core/api/core_api_injection.py:37-125) [6.1] public none needed SQL with RLS Database.execute(sql, QueryOptions) [6.1] public; no datasource access check, so DBD adds raise_for_access none needed Chart data as a user ChartDataQueryContextSchema, ChartDataCommand [6.1] internal none; contract tests User switching superset.utils.core.override_user(user, force=...) [6.1] internal none Native filters into chart queries get_dashboard_filter_context(dashboard_id, chart_id, *, active_data_mask=None), apply_dashboard_filter_context(query_context, extra_form_data) (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:272, 365) [M] internal 6.1: databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61 form_data to query context build_query_context_from_form_data(form_data, datasource, viz_type=None) (apache/superset: superset/common/form_data_query_context.py:1801) [M] internal 6.1: require a saved query_context Filter state and permalinks GetFilterStateCommand, CreateDashboardPermalinkCommand, GetDashboardPermalinkCommand, DashboardPermalinkState (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/permalink/types.py:21) [6.1] (chartStates UNVERIFIED on 6.1) internal; also public REST browser-side REST calls Text number formatting identical to the browser format_number_with_config (apache/superset: superset/utils/number_format.py:166) [M] internal vendored copy in databound_docs.format.d3 Guest users get_guest_user_from_token(token: GuestToken), parse_jwt_guest_token(raw) [M] verified, 6.1 UNVERIFIED internal guest features are v2 only SQL Lab UI views.registerView, menus.registerMenuItem, commands.registerCommand, sqlLab.getCurrentTab, sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess [6.1] (registerView signature [M*]) public none needed Dashboard and Explore entry chat.registerChat, navigation.getPage, navigation.onDidChangePage [M] public 6.1: Studio page and SQL Lab panel Frontend CSRF authentication.getCSRFToken() [6.1] public none needed Data-condition events Alerts and Reports webhook recipient [6.1]; SSRF guard [M] public feature none needed Schedule window math cron_schedule_window(triggered_at, cron, timezone) (apache/superset: superset/tasks/cron_util.py:74) [6.1] internal vendored copy Definition-change signal SQLAlchemy after_update listeners (as in apache/superset: superset/models/slice.py:624) [6.1] SQLAlchemy public, unsupported as an extension practice (UNVERIFIED) compare changed_on at refresh Email delivery send_email_smtp (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:939) [6.1] internal DBD's own SMTP client

The version sniffing that makes the "Fallback" column work is two lines at the top of the adapter:

databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py (excerpt)
HAS_FILTER_CONTEXT = importlib.util.find_spec(
    "superset.charts.data.dashboard_filter_context") is not None    # [M]
HAS_FORM_DATA_REBUILD = importlib.util.find_spec(
    "superset.common.form_data_query_context") is not None          # [M]

GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/capabilities reports these flags (filter_context_helper, form_data_rebuild, chat, gtf_dag, sse, pdf_engine, docx_charts, agent_planner) to the frontend, so the Studio shows only what the host can do.

Gotcha: the extension RestApi is CSRF-exempt by inheritance

RestApi subclasses FAB's BaseApi directly, not Superset's BaseSupersetApiMixin, and FAB declares csrf_exempt = True. A cookie-authenticated, state-changing endpoint must set csrf_exempt = False explicitly, which DataBoundDocsApi does. The frontend always sends X-CSRFToken from authentication.getCSRFToken().

docs.title: Step 8: State, storage and the job lifecycle
8.1 Where state lives
docs.text: Kind of state Store Why there Templates, documents, immutable versions, binding results (provenance), artifacts index, jobs, events, triggers, shares, data policy, audit dbd_* tables in the Superset metadata database (or DATABOUND_DOCS["DATABASE_URI"]) Extension persistent storage [M] is capped at 1 MB per value and appears usable only at import time, so DBD owns its tables with a separate Alembic version table dbd_alembic_version PPTX, DOCX, PDF, HTML binaries object storage at dbd/<document_id>/<version>/<artifact_id>.<ext> Binaries do not belong in the metadata DB. On master, an adapter over EXPORT_STORAGE is available Chart data Superset's DATA_CACHE_CONFIG, keyed by Superset's own cache_key, which includes RLS (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304-6313) Profiling and resolution then share cache hits with the dashboard, per user Data Digest Superset CACHE_CONFIG, 10 minutes Repeat generations from the same context are cheap Per-user UI preferences extension persistent storage [M] the one use that fits its limits

docs.title: 8.2 Job state machine
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> queued
    queued --> digest: worker picks the GTF task
    digest --> planning
    planning --> needs_input: clarification
    needs_input --> planning: continue_generation
    planning --> resolving
    resolving --> writing
    writing --> verifying
    verifying --> writing: repair
    verifying --> rendering
    rendering --> succeeded
    rendering --> partially_succeeded: some formats failed
    digest --> failed
    planning --> failed
    resolving --> failed: no binding resolved
    queued --> cancelled
    planning --> cancelled
    resolving --> cancelled
    writing --> cancelled
    succeeded --> [*]
    partially_succeeded --> [*]
    failed --> [*]
    cancelled --> [*]

dbd_job.status mirrors the GTF statuses (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, SUCCESS, FAILURE, ABORTED, TIMED_OUT) and adds needs_input and partially_succeeded. dbd_job.task_uuid is the authoritative link to the GTF row. A single failed binding never fails a job: its element shows "data unavailable" and the job completes with warnings. Clarification never blocks a worker: the task persists its state, ends with payload {"status": "needs_input"}, and the user's answer schedules continue_generation.

docs.title: 8.3 GTF tasks at a glance
docs.text:
Task (type extensions.databound.docgen.*) Scope Timeout Arguments generate_document PRIVATE 900 s job_id, user_id continue_generation PRIVATE 900 s job_id, user_id regenerate_sections PRIVATE 600 s job_id, user_id, section_ids refresh_document PRIVATE 600 s document_id, user_id, narrative, mode, force render_artifact PRIVATE 300 s document_id, version, fmt, user_id run_trigger SYSTEM 900 s trigger_id, scheduled_for, event resolve_binding [M] PRIVATE 120 s job_id, binding_id, user_id (DAG fan-out with depends_on)

Gotcha: @task positional arguments and reserved names

The superset_core stub's first positional parameter is name, but the host implementation's first positional parameter is func. @task("generate_document") passes a string as the function. Always use keywords: @task(name="generate_document", scope=TaskScope.PRIVATE, timeout=900). The host also rejects task functions with parameters named ctx or options (apache/superset: superset/tasks/decorators.py:165-173).

docs.title: Step 9: How it maps to Presenton
docs.text:
Presenton is Apache-2.0, and Data-Bound Documents ports selected parts of it into its own Apache-2.0 repository with NOTICE attribution. Presenton-derived code never enters apache/superset itself. The table maps each Presenton component, as covered in Part I, to its fate here.

Presenton component Fate What changes Presenton chapter Template v2 element model (elements.py) Extend Keeps geometry and styling on the 1280 x 720 canvas. Adds a data_slot object on chart, table and text, and a new kpi element. Chart data fields are never filled by the LLM Template v2 format Schema builder (extract_slide_schema_from_layout, _component_content_field_schema) Extend Text fields keep minLength/maxLength budgets. Bound slots emit only enums of binding or fact ids. x-element-path stays for hydration From template to schema to slide Structured retries (generate_structured_with_schema_retries) Reuse (ported) Becomes call_structured(), with regex and budget checks and audit accounting Prompts and schemas Outline, structure and content calls Reuse the stage shape, replace prompts and schemas Outline over a Data Digest with binding enums; deterministic layout fit with an LLM tie-break; per-section writing with fact tokens Standard generation pipeline SSE envelope and safe_sse_stream Reuse (ported) Same event:/data: wire format, new event types. Long poll is the default transport Streaming (SSE) Hydrator dispatch (_apply_template_content_value) Extend Same dispatch pattern; bound chart, table and KPI handlers fill from BindingResult rows instead of LLM output From template to schema to slide Custom templates from PPTX Replace The importer reads shape names (slot:chart:trend) with python-pptx; no vision model and no @presenton/export-core Custom templates from PPTX Themes and fonts Extend Theme comes from the template, or from the dashboard's label_colors, color scheme and theme tokens Themes and fonts Export pipeline (@presenton/export-core, Puppeteer) Replace License unknown, distributed outside npm, browser DOM measurement. Replaced by python-pptx, python-docx, DrawingML, vector HTML and a network-isolated PDF print PPTX and PDF export Next.js editor and Chart.js preview Replace Document Studio is a Superset extension UI with ECharts and a binding inspector; data cells are read-only Slide editor Smart mode (LLM-written HTML) Do not use Free-form HTML cannot guarantee data provenance Smart mode REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP Replace with Superset equivalents FAB @api routes, GTF tasks, superset_core MCP tools REST API, async tasks, webhooks, MCP Auth and multi-user Replace Superset session, FAB permissions on DataBoundDocs, override_user, RLS Auth and multi-user Data model (presentations, slides with content and ui) Replace Immutable dbd_document_version.spec plus dbd_binding_result provenance Data model Docker topology (FastAPI, Next.js, export service) Replace No new service; DBD runs inside Superset's processes Runtime topology

The single most important difference is in the schema builder. Presenton's _chart_content_schema (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534) asks the model for chart_type, categories and series[{name, values}]. The Data-Bound Documents builder emits, for the same slot, only {"binding": {"enum": [...]}}, a choice among registry ids. Data-bound slide model shows the full builder.

docs.title: Step 10: Technology choices and why
docs.text:
Decision area Choice Alternatives considered Why Where generation runs In-process: Superset extension plus a preinstalled wheel Presenton-derived sidecar with its own database and a credential broker; MCP-first agent service Zero credential handling, works with every auth type including SSO, numbers identical to the dashboard, no new infrastructure. The sidecar needed a non-FAB auth path and standing delegations Data execution ChartDataCommand under override_user REST chart-data calls; raw SQL; MCP get_chart_data RBAC through raise_for_access, RLS through get_sqla_row_level_filters (apache/superset: superset/connectors/sqla/models.py:1171), RLS-aware caching. REST breaks on 6.1 with GAQ; MCP caps responses at 50 KB Long-running work GTF @task on a dedicated Celery queue Raw Celery tasks; threads in gunicorn Dedup by task_key, cancel, Task List UI, status REST [6.1]; Celery router isolates load Event scheduling Own dbd_trigger table plus one beat entry Reuse Alerts and Reports schedules for everything Full control of run-as identity and parameter roll-forward. Alerts are still used as data-condition detectors through webhooks PPTX python-pptx 1.0.2 plus a DrawingML Chart Writer pptxgenjs in a Node sidecar Python, already near Superset's stack (XlsxWriter is a Superset dependency), opens existing files and refreshes with replace_data. Combo charts are written as raw c:chartSpace DOCX python-docx 1.2.0 plus a shared DrawingML chart part (gate G5), vector SVG fallback LibreOffice conversion; pandoc Native editable charts with one chart builder for both Office formats Static SVG from rows Vega-Lite through vl-convert-python ECharts SSR in Node; matplotlib No Node in MVP; BSD-3 Rust wheel. ECharts SSR is an optional v2 sidecar for visual parity Live pages Standalone non-federated bundle with React and ECharts, served by the extension Module Federation remote outside the SPA A federated remote cannot run outside the SPA without the host's share scope PDF Chromium page.pdf() on DBD's own local HTML, network off Superset's build_pdf_from_screenshots; WeasyPrint Vector text and paths, no auth cookies, no readiness heuristics. WeasyPrint is allowed but its SVG fidelity is UNVERIFIED (gate G7) Text formatting Vendored format_number_with_config (d3-format port) A Node formatter Same strings the browser shows; the module is [M], so DBD vendors it for 6.1 Events transport Long poll by default, SSE when workers are async SSE only; websockets Long poll works with every gunicorn worker class; an SSE stream holds a sync worker LLM access LLMProvider protocol with strict structured output where supported One vendor SDK Self-hosted (vLLM, Ollama) and hosted models; role-based profiles Metadata storage Own dbd_ tables with a separate Alembic version table Extension persistent storage Storage values are capped at 1 MB and the backend accessor appears to work only at import time

All runtime dependencies are ASF Category A licenses: python-pptx (MIT), python-docx (MIT), XlsxWriter (BSD), vl-convert (BSD-3), ECharts (Apache-2.0), Playwright (Apache-2.0). LibreOffice (MPL-2.0, Category B) is an optional operator-installed engine only.

docs.title: Step 11: Decision log summary
docs.text:
The blueprint was chosen by scoring three competing designs: D-A (extension-native), D-B (a Presenton-derived sidecar) and D-C (agentic and MCP-first). D-A won on 6.1 feasibility, security and operational simplicity (63 of 80 points, against 62 for D-C and 61 for D-B), and the final design grafts in the strongest ideas of the other two. The full log has 27 entries; this summary groups them.

Theme Decisions Origin Skeleton In-process extension plus a preinstalled wheel, no sidecar (1). No credential broker, grants or delegations (19). No polling proxy task that holds a Celery slot (20) D-A; D-B parts rejected Naming "Superset Data-Bound Documents", extension databound.docgen, prefix dbd; publisher is not apache because this is not an ASF artifact (2) new Number trust Binding Registry as the only entry point for bindings (3). Label tokens (.label, .abs), entity scan and deterministic fallback sentences (5). audience_rls_fingerprint and the viewer rule on live pages (6). args_json string for fact requests, because strict modes reject open objects (11) D-C, D-B Planning pipeline by default, agent opt-in on master, plus a no-LLM template strategy (4). Bipartite slot matcher with scoring, LLM only for ties (10). Clarification through job.needs_input and chat refinement through JSON Patch (24) D-A, D-B, D-C Templates Template-fill mode (replace_data on designer charts) and a python-pptx importer instead of @presenton/export-core (8). Shape-name slot convention for masters (9) D-A, D-B, D-C Refresh Guarded token-run rewrite: a run is rewritten only if its text is unchanged, so user edits in PowerPoint survive (7) D-B Superset integration fixes Celery router on task_type to the databound_docs queue (12). Standalone non-federated bundle for Studio and live pages (13). Two frontend bundles plus a doctor check (14). Guest identity passes a parsed GuestToken (15). build_query_context_from_form_data with an explicit datasource argument (16). g.form_data set to the whole body (17). MCP never called in-process from workers, MCP_DEV_USERNAME must be unset (18). 6.1 filter port limited to chartsInScope, scope and defaults, with explicit unsupported_on_6.1 rejections (21) new, verified against source Rendering Vega-Lite through vl-convert-python for SVG from rows in MVP, ECharts SSR later (22). Long poll by default, SSE only with async workers (23). No-screenshot guarantee through import-linter plus a no-raster CI test (26) D-A, D-C Content Alert briefs from report execution logs, optional label masking (25) D-B Storage Own dbd_ tables with a separate Alembic version table (27) D-A, D-C

The blueprint is also candid about its weakest points, and you should keep them in mind when you extend it: it still rides on internal Superset APIs (contained by the Superset Adapter and contract tests until a public chart-data API exists upstream); 6.1 is a second-class experience with no dashboard button; token-only prose constrains style; per-viewer RLS and author-written prose fit together imperfectly; and several native-format pieces sit behind prototype gates G1 to G7. The Roadmap lists each gate with its fallback.

docs.title: What you now know
docs.text:
• Data-Bound Documents is one framework with sixteen named components across four planes (data, language, output, lifecycle), all running inside Superset's own web, worker, beat and MCP processes.
  • It ships as a thin databound-docgen-<version>.supx for the wiring and a fat superset-databound-docs wheel for everything else, with all Superset internals behind one version-sniffing Superset Adapter.
  • Every request path, whether a button, a synchronous brief, a live page, a schedule, an alert or an MCP call, ends in the same Binding Resolver call under an explicit identity: the requester, the viewer or the recorded run-as user.
  • GTF provides deduplicated, cancellable jobs on 6.1; a Celery router on task_type isolates them on the databound_docs queue; master adds the chat slot, per-user MCP, the filter-context helper and DAG fan-out.
  • Presenton contributes its template model, schema builder, retries, stage shape and SSE envelope, while its export pipeline, editor and smart mode are replaced, because they let numbers pass through the LLM or through a browser.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Continue with Data-bound slide model, which specifies the Document Spec and every DataBinding field that these components pass between them.

docs.title: Data-bound slide model
docs.text:
Reads: superset/charts/schemas.py, superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py, superset/utils/core.py, superset/dashboards/permalink/types.py, superset/security/manager.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py, servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py, servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py · Builds on: Target architecture · Time: ~45 min

This chapter specifies the Document Spec, the data model every Data-Bound Documents component reads and writes, and its heart, the DataBinding. You will see every Pydantic model and field, how each binding source compiles into a real Superset query context, how dashboard filters, binding filters and parameters merge, how rows are shaped and formatted, what "live" and "snapshot" mean, and what provenance is recorded per resolution. Then the chapter shows how Presenton's Template v2 is extended with data slots, and how the schema builder exposes bindings to the LLM as enums instead of asking it for numbers. It ends with a complete three-slide deck, first as stored and then after resolution.

The models below live in databound_docs.spec (the wheel). They are normative: the JSON Schema published at GET /extensions/databound/docgen/v1/schema/document-spec is DocumentSpec.model_json_schema(), and the Studio's TypeScript types are generated from it at frontend build time.

docs.title: Step 1: From "the LLM fills the chart" to "the LLM picks a binding"
docs.text:
In Presenton a chart element is a box plus data. The Chart model carries categories: Optional[list[str]] and series: Optional[list[ChartSeries]], where ChartSeries is only a name and a list of floats:

presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:176-178
class ChartSeries(BaseModel):
    name: str
    values: list[float]

The schema builder asks the LLM to produce those lists (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:1490-1534), and the hydrator copies them into the element:

presenton: servers/fastapi/api/v1/ppt/endpoints/presentation.py:1395-1398
    if isinstance(value.get("categories"), list) and value["categories"]:
        updated["categories"] = value["categories"]
    if isinstance(value.get("series"), list) and value["series"]:
        updated["series"] = value["series"]

There is no number format, no x values, no provenance and no way to refresh. From template to schema to slide walks through that path. Data-Bound Documents splits the same responsibility into seven concepts, so that numbers have exactly one way in:

Concept What it is Who creates it Document One generated thing of kind deck, document, page or text; every change creates an immutable version the API, the Planner, edits, refreshes DataBinding A governed, re-runnable query plus instructions for shaping its rows only the Binding Registry Fact A deterministic scalar, label or list derived from one binding's resolved rows the Fact Engine Token The only way prose refers to data, for example {{f:f_rev}} the Narrative Writer, templates, users Element What a section shows: chart, table, kpi, text, narrative, image, link the Planner and templates Data slot A template-side placeholder that declares which element types and data shapes it accepts template authors and the importer Provenance As whom, when and how each binding was resolved, with which filters, cache state and RLS context the Binding Resolver

The LLM touches only three of these, and only by choosing ids: it picks candidate or binding ids for slots, asks for facts by operation, and writes text containing tokens. A chart's series values, a table's cells and a KPI's number come from the Binding Resolver and the Fact Engine.

flowchart LR
    T["Template layout with data slots"] --> SB["Schema builder"]
    BR["Binding Registry (issues b_ ids)"] --> SB
    SB -->|"enums of ids, text budgets"| LLM["LLM"]
    LLM -->|"slot choices, tokens"| SPEC["DocumentSpec version"]
    SPEC --> RES["Binding Resolver (ChartDataCommand as user)"]
    RES --> FE["Fact Engine"]
    FE --> RM["Resolved render model"]
    RES --> RM
    RM --> R["Renderers"]

docs.title: Step 2: The Document Spec envelope
docs.text:
All models inherit from a base with extra="forbid", so an unknown field is a validation error instead of silently dropped data (Presenton's own ChartSeries drops unknown keys, see presenton: servers/fastapi/tests/unit/test_pptx_json_element_metadata.py:79-103).

databound_docs/spec/models.py (envelope)
SPEC_VERSION = "dbd/1.0"
BindingId = Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^b_[a-z0-9_]{1,48}$")]
FactId = Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^f_[a-z0-9_]{1,48}$")]
ParamRef = Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^\$param\.[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$")]


class _M(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")


class DocumentSpec(_M):
    spec_version: Literal["dbd/1.0"] = SPEC_VERSION
    id: str
    version: int
    kind: Literal["deck", "document", "page", "text"]
    title: str                                  # tokens allowed
    language: str = "en"
    template: TemplateRef
    theme: ThemeSpec = ThemeSpec()
    parameters: dict[str, Parameter] = {}
    context: DataContext
    bindings: list[DataBinding]
    facts: list[Fact] = []
    sections: list[Section]
    generation: GenerationInfo
    provenance: DocumentProvenance
    refresh_policy: RefreshPolicy = RefreshPolicy()
Field Type Meaning spec_version "dbd/1.0" The binder accepts the current and the previous major version id str ULID with prefix doc_ version int Immutable version number; each accepted edit, refresh or parameter change adds one kind deck, document, page, text Selects the default renderer and the template family title str User text from the request form; tokens allowed ({{p:region}}) language str Output language; also selects the Verifier's number-word and direction lexicons template TemplateRef {id, version} Pinned template version; templates are immutable per version theme ThemeSpec Brand and colors (below) parameters dict[str, Parameter] Typed document parameters, referenced as $param.<name> context DataContext The captured data context (Step 3) bindings list[DataBinding] Every query the document runs (Step 4) facts list[Fact] Every number or label prose can cite (Step 11) sections list[Section] Ordered slides, document sections or page blocks (Step 12) generation GenerationInfo Prompt, prompt hash, planner strategy, LLM roles, prompt set version, trigger provenance DocumentProvenance Owner, creation time, parent version, reason, Superset and DBD versions refresh_policy RefreshPolicy What happens to narratives on refresh

The smaller envelope types are plain records:

Type Fields TemplateRef id, version ThemeSpec source (template, dashboard, system), dashboard_id, color_scheme, label_colors, palette, primary, positive, negative, font_family, logo_asset, lock (template brand wins except label colors) GenerationInfo prompt, prompt_hash, language, tone, planner_strategy (pipeline, agent, template), llm (role to profile and model), prompt_set_version, trigger (ui, api, mcp, cron, alert_webhook, freshness, definition_change, external_webhook), trigger_ref DocumentProvenance owner_user_id, created_at, parent_version, reason (generate, chat_edit, manual_edit, refresh, param_change), superset_version, dbd_version RefreshPolicy narrative (keep, retoken, regenerate_on_drift default, regenerate), drift_rules (default sign_flip, rank_change_top3, abs_change_pct>10), skip_if_unchanged (default true), on_open (pages only, default true)

ThemeSpec with source: "dashboard" is filled from the dashboard's json_metadata (label_colors, shared_label_colors, map_label_colors, color_scheme) and its theme tokens (colorPrimary, colorSuccess, colorError, fontFamily, brandLogoUrl). label_colors always wins, so "Classic Cars" keeps its dashboard color in the deck. Native rendering, no screenshots has the full color mapping.

docs.title: Step 3: Parameters and the data context
3.1 Parameters
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (parameters)
class Parameter(_M):
    type: Literal["time_range", "time_grain", "string", "string_list", "number", "boolean"]
    value: Any = None
    default: Any = None
    label: str | None = None
    native_filter_id: str | None = None        # overrides this dashboard native filter

A parameter is a named, typed value that bindings reference with $param.<name> in filters[].val, time_range, time_grain and parameters. Parameters do three jobs:

  1. Reuse. One "Period" parameter drives every binding's time range.
  2. Roll-forward. A scheduled refresh can set time_range to "Last week" without touching any binding.
  3. Native filter override. With native_filter_id set, the parameter's value replaces that native filter's captured value for every binding the filter is in scope for. A live page renders such parameters as controls, and changing one re-resolves bindings without calling the LLM.

time_range values use Superset's own grammar ("Last quarter", "2026-07-01 : 2026-10-01", "No filter"), so Superset resolves them and reports the result as from_dttm/to_dttm.

docs.title: 3.2 The data context
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (context)
class DashboardContext(_M):
    dashboard_id: int
    dashboard_uuid: str | None = None
    permalink_key: str | None = None            # durable capture of the data mask
    native_filters_key: str | None = None       # short-lived key seen at capture time
    active_tabs: list[str] = []
    data_mask_hash: str | None = None
    filter_mode: Literal["captured", "defaults", "none"] = "captured"


class SqlLabContext(_M):
    database_id: int
    catalog: str | None = None
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="schema")
    saved_query_id: int | None = None
    query_id: int | None = None                 # sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess remoteId


class DataContext(_M):
    dashboard: DashboardContext | None = None
    chart_ids: list[int] = []
    dataset_ids: list[int] = []
    sqllab: SqlLabContext | None = None
    captured_at: datetime | None = None
    captured_by_user_id: int | None = None
    locale: str = "en-US"
    timezone: str = "UTC"
Field Source at capture time Used for dashboard.permalink_key CreateDashboardPermalinkCommand(dashboard_id, state={"dataMask": ..., "activeTabs": ...}), or reused from a /superset/dashboard/p/<key>/ URL Reading state.dataMask at every resolution; the DashboardPermalinkState type has dataMask, activeTabs, anchor, urlParams, chartStates (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/permalink/types.py:21-30; chartStates is UNVERIFIED on 6.1) dashboard.native_filters_key the dashboard URL Audit only; it expires dashboard.data_mask_hash sha256 of the canonical data mask Detecting that two documents share a filter selection dashboard.filter_mode the request captured uses the permalink; defaults follows the dashboard's current defaultDataMask; none ignores native filters chart_ids, dataset_ids the request or the Studio picker Candidates and proposal targets in the Data Digest sqllab.query_id remoteId from sqlLab.onDidQuerySuccess Reloaded and ownership-checked on the server; usable only as a sql binding when ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS is on locale, timezone the user's settings Formatting and the {{m:<binding_id>.as_of}} token

Gotcha: filter state keys expire, permalinks do not

A native_filters_key points at dashboard filter state stored in a cache with a TTL. A refresh three months later would find nothing. Context Capture therefore converts it into a permalink immediately and stores permalink_key; native_filters_key is kept only for audit. Switch a document to filter_mode: "defaults" when it should follow future edits to the dashboard's default filters instead of a frozen selection.

docs.title: Step 4: DataBinding, field by field
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (DataBinding)
class DataBinding(_M):
    id: BindingId
    title: str | None = None
    source: Source
    dashboard_filters: DashboardFilterUse | None = None
    filters: list[FilterClause] = []
    time_range: str | ParamRef | None = None    # Superset grammar: "Last quarter", "a : b"
    time_grain: str | ParamRef | None = None
    parameters: dict[str, Any | ParamRef] = {}  # Jinja template_params
    post_processing: list[PostProcessingStep] | None = None  # None = keep the source's
    row_limit: int = Field(default=100, ge=1, le=5000)
    shape: Shape
    format: Format = Format()
    mode: Literal["live", "snapshot"] = "live"
    cache_ttl: int | None = None                # passed as custom_cache_timeout
    created_by: Literal["context", "template", "planner", "user"] = "context"
Field Meaning Maps to in the Superset query context id b_ plus up to 48 lowercase characters, issued by the Binding Registry not sent; used in shape names (dbd:chart:<element_id>:<binding_id>), HTML data-dbd-binding, the manifest title Human label shown in the binding inspector and alt text not sent source Discriminated union on kind: chart, dataset, semantic [M], sql (Step 5) datasource plus the base queries dashboard_filters Whether and which native filters apply (Step 6) queries[].filters entries with isExtra: true, time overrides filters Extra filter clauses for this binding appended to queries[].filters time_range Time window override, literal or $param.* rewrites the TEMPORAL_RANGE filter time_grain Grain override (ISO 8601 duration such as P1M) extras.time_grain_sqla and the BASE_AXIS column's timeGrain parameters Jinja template_params for virtual datasets and SQL form_data values that Jinja macros read through g.form_data post_processing Server-side pandas steps; None keeps the source's own list queries[].post_processing row_limit 1 to 5,000, default 100; further capped by the registry queries[].row_limit (minimum of the saved value and this one for chart sources) shape How rows become a chart, table or scalar (Step 7) not sent; applied after the query format Per-column formats (Step 8) not sent mode live re-queries on every resolution; snapshot stores rows and never re-queries controls whether dbd_binding_result.rows is written and read cache_ttl Seconds custom_cache_timeout created_by Who introduced the binding: context (an existing chart), template, planner (a proposal), user audit and UI badges

Gotcha: row_limit counts long-form rows, before pivoting

For a timeseries chart grouped by a dimension, Superset applies row_limit to the SQL result (one row per month and product line), and the pivot post-processing runs on that limited frame. A limit of 50 on twelve months by seven product lines (84 rows) silently drops data before the pivot. Chart-shaped bindings need row_limit >= periods x series; the Binding Resolver reports truncated: true when rowcount equals the limit, and the slot assignment check refuses such a binding for a hero chart.

docs.title: Step 5: Binding sources and how each resolves to a Superset query
docs.text:
Every source kind ends in the same three calls inside the Superset Adapter, under override_user:

databound/docgen/superset_adapter.py (run_query_context)
def run_query_context(json_body: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from superset.charts.schemas import ChartDataQueryContextSchema
    from superset.commands.chart.data.get_data_command import ChartDataCommand
    g.form_data = json_body                    # Jinja macros read it (workbook.py:226)
    qc = ChartDataQueryContextSchema().load(json_body)
    command = ChartDataCommand(qc)
    command.validate()                         # raise_for_access before execution
    return command.run()

ChartDataCommand.validate() is a one-liner that checks access before anything else runs:

apache/superset: superset/commands/chart/data/get_data_command.py:107-108
    def validate(self) -> None:
        self._query_context.raise_for_access()

What differs between source kinds is how the json_body is built.

Source When it is used Execution path Availability chart Default for anything the user already built Reload or pin the saved query context, stamp ids, merge filters, ChartDataCommand [6.1] with a saved query context; [M] adds a form_data rebuild dataset New visuals the planner proposes ("top countries by revenue") A QueryObject built from validated saved metrics and columns, ChartDataCommand [6.1] semantic Deployments with semantic layers SemanticView.get_table(...) [M] behind SEMANTIC_LAYERS sql Power users with a saved query, or template-admin SQL SELECT-only check, raise_for_access(..., force_dataset_match=True), Database.execute [6.1], disabled by default

The LLM may choose chart bindings and propose dataset bindings through enums. It may never write SQL or adhoc SQL expressions.

docs.title: 5.1 Chart sources
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (ChartSource)
class ChartSource(_M):
    kind: Literal["chart"] = "chart"
    chart_id: int
    chart_uuid: str | None = None
    query_index: int = 0                        # mixed_timeseries has 2 queries
    follow: Literal["live", "pinned"] = "live"  # live: reload chart.query_context each run
    query_context_snapshot: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    query_context_hash: str | None = None
    viz_type: str | None = None

Resolution, step by step:

  1. Load the chart through the access-filtered chart DAO (base filter ChartFilter), so a chart the user cannot see is a 404, not a leak.
  2. Get the query context.
    • follow: "live" loads Slice.query_context, the JSON that the viz plugin's buildQuery produced when the chart was last saved in Explore. Numbers are then identical to the dashboard.
    • follow: "pinned" uses query_context_snapshot. When the live context's hash differs from query_context_hash, the resolver records definition_changed and the Studio offers "update to the new chart definition".
    • If query_context is null: on [M] the adapter calls build_query_context_from_form_data(form_data, {"id": ..., "type": ...}, viz_type) (apache/superset: superset/common/form_data_query_context.py:1801-1805) and adds the provenance warning rebuilt_from_form_data. On [6.1] the binding resolves with status error and the remediation "Chart has no saved query context: open and save it in Explore", the same condition Superset's own endpoint reports (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/api.py:170-182).
  3. Stamp ids. Set form_data.dashboardId and form_data.slice_id, as the Excel export does for guest authorization (apache/superset: superset/dashboards/excel_export/workbook.py:205-214).
  4. Merge filters in the order of Step 6.
  5. Force the result shape. result_type = "full", result_format = "json", and pop force unless this is a forced refresh.
  6. Execute with run_query_context, then read result["queries"][query_index].

Here is what a saved query context for an echarts_timeseries_bar chart typically looks like, and what the resolver changes. The saved part is illustrative: it is the shape the ECharts timeseries buildQuery saves, and exact keys vary by plugin version.

Chart 102: saved query_context (illustrative excerpt)
{
  "datasource": {"id": 7, "type": "table"},
  "force": false,
  "queries": [{
    "filters": [{"col": "order_date", "op": "TEMPORAL_RANGE", "val": "No filter"}],
    "extras": {"having": "", "where": ""},
    "columns": [{"columnType": "BASE_AXIS", "sqlExpression": "order_date", "label": "order_date",
                 "expressionType": "SQL", "timeGrain": "P1M"}, "product_line"],
    "metrics": ["revenue"],
    "orderby": [["revenue", false]],
    "row_limit": 10000,
    "series_columns": ["product_line"],
    "post_processing": [
      {"operation": "pivot", "options": {"index": ["order_date"], "columns": ["product_line"],
                                         "aggregates": {"revenue": {"operator": "mean"}},
                                         "drop_missing_columns": false}},
      {"operation": "rename", "options": {"columns": {"revenue": null}, "level": 0, "inplace": true}},
      {"operation": "flatten"}
    ]
  }],
  "form_data": {"datasource": "7__table", "viz_type": "echarts_timeseries_bar", "slice_id": 102},
  "result_format": "json",
  "result_type": "full"
}
Chart 102: json_body sent to ChartDataCommand for binding b_rev_by_month (changed keys only)
{
  "queries": [{
    "filters": [
      {"col": "order_date", "op": "TEMPORAL_RANGE", "val": "2026-07-01 : 2026-10-01"},
      {"col": "region", "op": "IN", "val": ["EMEA"], "isExtra": true}
    ],
    "row_limit": 500
  }],
  "form_data": {"datasource": "7__table", "viz_type": "echarts_timeseries_bar",
                "slice_id": 102, "dashboardId": 12},
  "result_format": "json",
  "result_type": "full"
}

The pivot and flatten steps stay, so the result arrives wide, one column per product line, exactly as the dashboard renders it.

docs.title: 5.2 Dataset sources
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (DatasetSource)
class SimpleMetric(_M):
    expressionType: Literal["SIMPLE"] = "SIMPLE"
    column: str
    aggregate: Literal["SUM", "AVG", "COUNT", "COUNT_DISTINCT", "MIN", "MAX"]
    label: str


class DatasetSource(_M):
    kind: Literal["dataset"] = "dataset"
    dataset_id: int
    dataset_uuid: str | None = None
    metrics: list[Union[str, SimpleMetric]]     # saved metric names preferred
    dimensions: list[str] = []                  # validated column names (groupby=True)
    time_column: str | None = None
    time_grain: str | None = None               # ISO 8601 duration, e.g. "P1M"
    time_offsets: list[str] = []                # e.g. ["1 year ago"]
    orderby: list[tuple[str, bool]] = []        # (metric_or_column, ascending)
    series_limit: int | None = None

There is deliberately no SqlMetric. A planner proposal can name only saved metrics (governed definitions, with their d3format and currency) or a SimpleMetric over an existing numeric column. The Binding Registry rejects anything else before an id is issued.

The compiler is 6.1-compatible and lives in the wheel. A temporal dimension becomes an adhoc BASE_AXIS column, the same pattern the ECharts plugins use:

databound_docs/binder/dataset_query.py (excerpt)
def build_dataset_query_context(b: DataBinding) -> dict:
    src = b.source
    cols: list = []
    for dim in src.dimensions:
        if dim == src.time_column:
            cols.append({"columnType": "BASE_AXIS", "sqlExpression": dim, "label": dim,
                         "expressionType": "SQL", "timeGrain": src.time_grain})
        else:
            cols.append(dim)
    filters = [f.model_dump() for f in b.filters]
    if b.time_range and src.time_column:
        filters.append({"col": src.time_column, "op": "TEMPORAL_RANGE", "val": b.time_range})
    metrics = [m if isinstance(m, str) else
               {"expressionType": "SIMPLE", "column": {"column_name": m.column},
                "aggregate": m.aggregate, "label": m.label} for m in src.metrics]
    query = {
        "columns": cols, "metrics": metrics, "filters": filters,
        "orderby": [[m, asc] for m, asc in src.orderby], "row_limit": b.row_limit,
        "time_offsets": src.time_offsets, "series_limit": src.series_limit or 0,
        "post_processing": [p.model_dump() for p in (b.post_processing or [])],
        "extras": {"time_grain_sqla": src.time_grain} if src.time_grain else {},
    }
    return {"datasource": {"id": src.dataset_id, "type": "table"}, "queries": [query],
            "form_data": {"datasource": f"{src.dataset_id}__table", "viz_type": "table"},
            "result_type": "full", "result_format": "json"}

$param.* references are substituted before compilation (Step 6), so the compiler only ever sees literal values. When the shape has series_by, the compiler adds pivot and flatten steps that mirror the ECharts timeseries buildQuery, so a proposed "revenue by month by product line" arrives in the same wide form as a saved chart.

The fields map one to one onto ChartDataQueryObjectSchema (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1388-1675): columns, metrics, filters (ChartDataFilterSchema, with op restricted to FilterOperator values), orderby, row_limit, series_limit, time_offsets, post_processing and extras.time_grain_sqla.

Gotcha: time_offsets columns are renamed, and need a time column

Superset names comparison columns <metric>__<offset>, for example revenue__1 year ago. Facts and shapes must reference that exact name. The example deck below uses time_offsets on a query with a time_column but no temporal dimension (columns: []). On master, processing_time_offsets handles that case explicitly: with no join keys it falls back to a temporary join key and returns one joined row (apache/superset: superset/models/helpers.py:3604-3613, :3794). Whether the 6.1.0 code path does the same is UNVERIFIED and covered by the binding contract tests. If that test fails on 6.1, the fallback is to add order_date as a BASE_AXIS dimension at the period's grain (P3M), so the comparison has a temporal column to join on, and to read row 0.

docs.title: 5.3 Semantic sources [M]
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (SemanticSource)
class SemanticSource(_M):                       # [M], SEMANTIC_LAYERS flag
    kind: Literal["semantic"] = "semantic"
    view_id: str
    metrics: list[str]
    dimensions: list[str] = []
    time_grain: str | None = None

On master with SEMANTIC_LAYERS on, the resolver calls the semantic view's get_table(...) through the host registry. The superset_core.semantic_layers package is absent from the 6.1.0 tag, so on 6.1 the registry refuses this kind with unsupported_on_6.1.

docs.title: 5.4 SQL sources
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (SqlSource)
class SqlSource(_M):                            # opt-in, never proposed by the LLM
    kind: Literal["sql"] = "sql"
    database_id: int
    saved_query_id: int | None = None
    template_sql_ref: str | None = None         # admin-authored SQL stored in a template
    catalog: str | None = None
    schema_: str | None = Field(default=None, alias="schema")

SQL bindings exist only when ALLOW_SQL_BINDINGS is true, and only from a saved query the user can access, a SQL Lab query the user owns, or SQL a template admin (can_manage_templates) wrote. The resolver renders Jinja with the document parameters, parses with get_sqlglot_dialect(database) and rejects anything but a single SELECT, calls security_manager.raise_for_access(database=..., sql=..., catalog=..., schema=..., force_dataset_match=True) (because Database.execute performs no datasource access check of its own), and then runs Database.execute(sql, QueryOptions(limit=..., timeout_seconds=60, cache=CacheOptions(...))). RLS applies; chart semantics (saved metrics, formats) do not. Security, RLS, auth covers the checks.

docs.title: 5.5 Previewing a binding from the Studio
docs.text:
The binding inspector and the MCP tool dbd_propose_binding both validate a draft through the same registry call. The REST side is an ordinary superset_core API method:

backend/src/databound/docgen/api.py (bindings preview, excerpt)
from flask import g, request
from flask_appbuilder.api import expose, permission_name, protect, safe
from superset_core.rest_api.api import RestApi
from superset_core.rest_api.decorators import api

from databound_docs.binder.registry import BindingRegistry
from databound_docs.spec.models import DataBinding
from databound.docgen import superset_adapter as sa


@api(id="dbd_api", name="Data-Bound Documents API", resource_name="v1")
class DataBoundDocsApi(RestApi):
    class_permission_name = "DataBoundDocs"
    csrf_exempt = False

    @expose("/bindings/preview", methods=("POST",))
    @protect()
    @safe
    @permission_name("generate")
    def preview_binding(self):
        draft = DataBinding.model_validate(request.get_json(force=True))
        registry = BindingRegistry(adapter=sa, user=g.user)       # request user, no override
        registered = registry.register(job_id=None, draft=draft)  # raises on bad names or access
        result = registry.resolver.resolve(registered, row_limit=20)
        return self.response(200, result={
            "status": result.status, "shape": registered.shape.kind,
            "rowcount": result.rowcount, "preview_rows": result.rows[:20],
            "default_facts": [f.model_dump() for f in registry.default_facts(registered, result)],
        })

And the Studio calls it with plain fetch, because SupersetClient is not shared with extension remotes:

extension/frontend/src/studio/bindings.ts
import { authentication } from '@apache-superset/core';
import type { DataBinding } from '../generated/document-spec';   // generated from the JSON Schema
import { BASE } from './api';

export async function previewBinding(binding: DataBinding) {
  const csrf = await authentication.getCSRFToken();
  const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/bindings/preview`, {
    method: 'POST',
    credentials: 'same-origin',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(csrf ? { 'X-CSRFToken': csrf } : {}) },
    body: JSON.stringify(binding),
  });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${res.status} ${await res.text()}`);
  return (await res.json()).result as {
    status: 'ok' | 'empty' | 'error' | 'forbidden' | 'truncated';
    shape: string; rowcount: number; preview_rows: Record<string, unknown>[];
  };
}

docs.title: Step 6: Filters and parameters
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (filters)
class FilterClause(_M):
    col: str
    op: Literal["==", "!=", ">", "<", ">=", "<=", "IN", "NOT IN", "LIKE", "ILIKE",
                "IS NULL", "IS NOT NULL", "TEMPORAL_RANGE"]
    val: Any | ParamRef = None


class DashboardFilterUse(_M):
    apply: bool = True
    dashboard_id: int | None = None             # defaults to context.dashboard
    include: list[str] | None = None            # native filter ids, None = all in scope
    exclude: list[str] = []

FilterClause is a strict subset of Superset's ChartDataFilterSchema (apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1156): the same col, op and val, with op limited to scalar FilterOperator values (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:329). NOT LIKE, NOT ILIKE, IS TRUE and IS FALSE are left out of v1, and the array operators (CONTAINS_ANY, CONTAINS_ALL, IS_EMPTY, LENGTH_*), which accompany the master-only MULTI_VALUE column type, are not offered.

docs.title: 6.1 Merge order
docs.text:
Filters are applied in this order, and later steps win:

  1. The source's own filters. For chart sources, the adhoc filters inside the saved query context.
  2. Dashboard native filters, when dashboard_filters.apply is true.
    • [M]: fc = get_dashboard_filter_context(dashboard_id=..., chart_id=..., active_data_mask=data_mask), then apply_dashboard_filter_context(json_body, fc.extra_form_data) when it is not empty (apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:272, 365). fc.to_dict()["filters"] goes into Provenance.dashboard_filters.
    • [6.1]: databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61 reads json_metadata.native_filter_configuration. For chart sources it uses chartsInScope when present, else scope.rootPath and scope.excluded; for dataset sources it uses targets[].datasetId. It takes each value from the permalink dataMask or from defaultDataMask, appends filters with isExtra: true, and overrides time_range, time_grain_sqla, granularity_sqla and relative_start/relative_end, mirroring the EXTRA_FORM_DATA_* constants (apache/superset: superset/constants.py:209-234).
  3. The binding's filters.
  4. Parameter values. $param.* references are substituted, and Parameter.native_filter_id overrides that native filter's value.
  5. time_range and time_grain overrides, which rewrite the TEMPORAL_RANGE filter with the same semantics as merge_extra_form_data (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:1184-1260).
flowchart TD
    A["1. Source filters (saved adhoc filters)"] --> B["2. Dashboard native filters from permalink dataMask"]
    B --> C["3. Binding filters"]
    C --> D["4. Parameter substitution and native filter overrides"]
    D --> E["5. time_range and time_grain overrides"]
    E --> F["json_body for ChartDataCommand"]
    B -.->|"master"| M["get_dashboard_filter_context and apply_dashboard_filter_context"]
    B -.->|"6.1"| P["databound_docs.compat.filter_scope_61"]

Both branches return an object with the same contract as master's dataclass, so call sites never branch:

apache/superset: superset/charts/data/dashboard_filter_context.py:59-75
@dataclass
class DashboardFilterContext:
    extra_form_data: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    filters: list[DashboardFilterInfo] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "filters": [
                {
                    "id": f.id,
                    "name": f.name,
                    "status": f.status.value,
                    **({"column": f.column} if f.column else {}),
                }
                for f in self.filters
            ],
        }

Gotcha: the 6.1 port refuses to guess

The 6.1 port does not implement cascading parents, requiredFirst or defaultToFirstItem pre-queries. When an in-scope filter uses one of these, the binding resolves with that filter at its captured explicit value, or skips it with a rejected_filters entry {"reason": "unsupported_on_6.1"} that the provenance footer shows. It never invents a value. The binding contract tests assert that the 6.1 port and the master helper produce identical query contexts for filter_select, filter_range, filter_time and filter_timegrain.

Gotcha: dataset proposals honor dashboard filters only when targeted

A planner proposal over dataset 7 gets the dashboard's native filters only if dataset 7 is a target of those filters (targets[].datasetId). A proposal over a dataset no filter targets runs unfiltered by the dashboard selection, and the provenance footer says so. If the prompt says "for EMEA", put the region into a parameter with a binding filter, as the example deck does.

docs.title: 7.1 Post-processing runs in Superset
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (post-processing)
class PostProcessingStep(_M):
    operation: Literal["aggregate", "pivot", "rolling", "cum", "contribution", "sort",
                       "rename", "resample", "diff", "compare", "flatten", "select", "rank"]
    options: dict[str, Any] = {}

These are Superset's own pandas operations (apache/superset: superset/utils/pandas_postprocessing/__init__.py:49-67), executed server-side inside ChartDataCommand. Shares, cumulative sums and rolling averages are therefore computed by Superset, so the deck and the dashboard agree. prophet, boxplot, histogram and the geo operations are not offered to proposals; chart sources keep whatever their saved query context contains.

Gotcha: contribution is computed over the returned rows

Post-processing runs on the result frame after row_limit is applied in SQL. In a single-query context, a contribution step on a top-10 query computes each row's share of the top 10, not of the whole region. Superset can do better: when the same query context also carries a totals query (metrics, no columns, no post_processing), ensure_totals_available runs it without a row limit and injects contribution_totals into every contribution step, so shares are of the true total (apache/superset: superset/common/query_context_processor.py:99-136, :709-740; ensure_totals_available is also present in the 6.1.0 tag). The Binding Resolver therefore appends such a metrics-only totals query to any dataset binding with a contribution step (a refinement not shown in the build_dataset_query_context excerpt above) and reads the binding's rows from queries[0]. The example deck would be safe either way, because its region has eight countries and rowcount stays below the limit; without a totals query and with truncated: true, a share fact must be labeled "share of the listed countries".

docs.title: 7.2 Shape: from rows to a renderable structure
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (Shape)
class Shape(_M):
    kind: Literal["scalar", "series", "xy", "xyz", "table", "pivot"]
    x: str | None = None                        # category or temporal column
    series: list[str] | Literal["*"] = "*"      # value columns after pivot
    series_by: str | None = None                # long-form dimension to pivot on
    size: str | None = None                     # xyz only
    columns: list[str] = []                     # table display order
    top_n: int | None = None
    others_label: str | None = "Other"
kind Required result Feeds Check that fails loudly scalar one row, numeric value columns KPI groups, facts exactly one row with a numeric value series one x column plus numeric series columns category charts (column, bar, line, area, pie) one x column and at least one numeric series xy numeric x and y per series scatter numeric x and y xyz x, y, size bubble three numeric columns table any columns native tables, ranked lists listed columns exist pivot post-processed pivot tables with merged headers header levels present

The resolver's shaping pass, in order:

  1. Convert temporal values (Superset serializes them as epoch milliseconds) to timezone-aware datetime in the document timezone. Date categories produce a date axis in python-pptx.
  2. Apply top_n: keep the N largest series (or categories) by total and fold the rest into one column named others_label.
  3. Compute the reserved virtual columns __row_total (row sum across series) and __row_index (0-based position after sorting). Facts can reference them, for example argmax over __row_total, or a where of {"__row_index_lt": 3}.
  4. Enforce the target slot's series, categories and rows ranges (Step 13).

docs.title: Step 8: Formatting
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (formats)
class ColumnFormat(_M):
    d3: str | None = None                       # "$,.2f", ".1%", "SMART_NUMBER"
    currency: dict[str, str] | None = None      # {"symbol": "USD", "symbolPosition": "prefix"}
    time: str | None = None                     # d3-time-format or "smart_date"
    excel: str | None = None                    # derived for chart caches and axes
    label: str | None = None                    # display label (verbose_name)
    null_text: str = "n/a"


class Format(_M):
    columns: dict[str, ColumnFormat] = {}       # "*" applies to all value columns
    locale: str | None = None

Resolution follows Superset's own precedence:

  1. DataBinding.format.columns[col] (then "*" for value columns).
  2. The dataset metric's d3format and currency.
  3. The chart form_data keys y_axis_format, number_format and currency_format.
  4. SMART_NUMBER.

A currency with symbol AUTO resolves from the result's detected_currency. The resolved format is then consumed in two different ways, and the distinction matters:

Consumer Uses Why Fact displays, table cells, KPI values, token text d3 through the vendored format_number_with_config(d3_format, currency, value) (apache/superset: superset/utils/number_format.py:166, [M]; vendored for 6.1) The same strings a user sees in the browser Chart caches, axes, data labels, the embedded workbook excel, derived deterministically from d3 (for example ,.0f gives #,##0, .1% gives 0.0%) The workbook keeps raw numbers, so "Edit Data" in PowerPoint shows real values

label comes from the column's verbose_name or the metric's verbose_name unless the binding overrides it. The full d3-to-Excel table is in Native rendering, no screenshots.

docs.title: Step 9: Live, snapshot, live-follow and pinned
docs.text:
Two independent switches control how "dynamic" a binding is. mode decides whether data is re-queried; follow (chart sources only) decides whether the query definition is re-read.

follow: "live" (chart definition re-read) follow: "pinned" (definition frozen) mode: "live" (data re-queried) Default. Edits to the chart in Explore and new data both flow into the next refresh New data flows in, but the query is the one captured at generation time; definition changes raise a flag mode: "snapshot" (rows stored) Rows frozen in dbd_binding_result.rows; a definition change is reported but not applied Fully frozen: what was sent is what is shown, forever

Live pages re-resolve live bindings as the viewer on every open. Refresh in place re-resolves as the run-as user and rewrites the existing PPTX or DOCX. Snapshot shares require can_share_snapshot, because they carry the author's data. Scheduling and live refresh covers the refresh algorithm.

docs.title: Step 10: Results and provenance
docs.text:
Every resolution produces a BindingResult, stored in dbd_binding_result and passed to the Fact Engine and the renderers.

databound_docs/spec/models.py (results)
class Provenance(_M):
    resolved_at: datetime
    executed_as_user_id: int | None             # None for guests
    executed_as_kind: Literal["user", "run_as", "guest"]
    rls_fingerprint: str                        # hash of RLS clauses applied
    superset_version: str
    adapter_path: Literal["chart_data_command", "database_execute", "semantic_view"]
    query_hash: str                             # sha256 of canonical query context, no force
    data_hash: str                              # sha256 of canonical rows
    cache_key: str | None = None
    is_cached: bool | None = None
    queried_dttm: str | None = None
    applied_filters: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    rejected_filters: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    dashboard_filters: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    from_dttm: int | None = None
    to_dttm: int | None = None
    detected_currency: str | None = None
    row_limit: int
    truncated: bool = False


class BindingResult(_M):
    binding_id: BindingId
    status: Literal["ok", "empty", "error", "forbidden", "truncated"]
    colnames: list[str] = []
    coltypes: list[int] = []                    # GenericDataType ints
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    rowcount: int = 0
    error: str | None = None
    provenance: Provenance | None = None

Most provenance fields are copied straight from Superset's chart-data response (ChartDataResponseResult, apache/superset: superset/charts/schemas.py:1807-1940); the rest are computed by DBD:

Field Origin cache_key, is_cached, queried_dttm, applied_filters, rejected_filters, from_dttm, to_dttm, detected_currency the query result returned by ChartDataCommand.run() coltypes GenericDataType ints: NUMERIC=0, STRING=1, TEMPORAL=2, BOOLEAN=3, MULTI_VALUE=4 [M] (apache/superset: superset/utils/core.py:251-260) dashboard_filters fc.to_dict()["filters"] on master, or the 6.1 port's equivalent query_hash sha256 of the canonical query JSON without force (sorted keys, no nonces) data_hash sha256 of canonical rows; equal hashes let a refresh emit refresh.unchanged and skip a new version rls_fingerprint hash of the RLS clauses applied to the executing user, from the same inputs as get_rls_cache_key (apache/superset: superset/security/manager.py:6304-6313) executed_as_* the as_user context: the requester, the trigger's run-as user, or a parsed guest token (v2) truncated rowcount == row_limit

Status mapping: SupersetSecurityException becomes forbidden (the element renders "You do not have access to this data" and every narrative citing its facts is removed); other errors become error and the element uses its fallback; zero rows is empty; a hit limit is truncated. Rows are persisted only for mode: "snapshot" or when an audit policy requires it; refreshes add rows and never overwrite them. Each artifact references (document_id, version, binding_result_ids), so "what data was in the file we sent on Monday" is always answerable.

Provenance is also stamped into every output: a visible footer ("Data as of 2 Nov 2026 09:14 UTC. Filters: Region = EMEA."), PPTX shape names and alt text, the /customXml/dbd-manifest.json part, HTML data-dbd-binding, data-dbd-query-hash and data-dbd-as-of attributes.

docs.title: 11.1 Facts
docs.text:
databound_docs/spec/models.py (facts)
FactOp = Literal["value", "label_at", "sum", "mean", "min", "max", "count", "first", "last",
                 "abs_change", "pct_change", "share", "rank_of", "argmax", "argmin",
                 "top_k", "count_where", "period_label", "as_of"]


class Fact(_M):
    id: FactId
    binding_id: BindingId
    op: FactOp
    args: dict[str, Any] = {}   # {"column": "revenue", "baseline_column": "revenue__1 year ago"}
    format: ColumnFormat | None = None
    description: str | None = None              # plain-language, shown to the writer
    value: Any = None                           # filled by the Fact Engine
    label: str | None = None                    # argmax, argmin, rank_of, label_at
    display: str | None = None                  # formatted value
    sign: Literal[-1, 0, 1] | None = None       # changes only

A fact is a definition plus a computed value. The stored spec holds the definition (id, binding_id, op, args, format, description); value, label, display and sign are filled by the Fact Engine at every resolution with pure functions over the shaped rows, so a refresh recomputes them without the LLM.

Op Args Value value, label_at column, row or where a cell value or label sum, mean, min, max, count column, optional where aggregate over rows first, last column first or last point in x order abs_change, pct_change column, baseline_column or vs (prev, first, a time_offsets column) delta, with sign set share column, label value divided by the column total rank_of column, label 1-based rank argmax, argmin column, label_column label plus its value top_k column, k list of label and value pairs count_where where number of matching rows period_label none resolved from_dttm to to_dttm as text as_of none queried_dttm

docs.title: 11.2 Token grammar
docs.text:
Token Resolves to Example rendering {{f:<fact_id>}} the fact's display $2.91M {{f:<fact_id>.label}} the fact's label France {{f:<fact_id>.abs}} the absolute value of a change fact, formatted 8.4% (for "fell by" phrasing) {{p:<param>}} a parameter's display value EMEA {{m:<binding_id>.as_of}} the binding's queried_dttm in the document timezone 2 Nov 2026 09:14

Each token renders as its own run: an a:r in PPTX, a w:r in DOCX, a <span data-dbd-fact="f_rev"> in HTML. That is what makes in-place refresh possible: the manifest records every token run, and a refresh rewrites a run only if its text still equals what DBD last wrote. Category names are tokens too (.label), because a label visible to the author may be invisible to another viewer under RLS; the Narrative Verifier's entity scan rejects literal category names in LLM prose.

docs.title: Step 12: Elements and sections
docs.text:
A Section has id, layout_id, title (tokens allowed), intent, elements and speaker_notes (tokens allowed). Every element inherits id and slot from a small base class _El; the slot is the data slot name the element fills. The element union, discriminated on type:

type Data fields Notes chart binding_id, native (column, bar, line, area, pie, doughnut, scatter, bubble, radar, combo, waterfall, funnel, histogram, step, sparkline, heat_table, svg), grouping (clustered, stacked, percent), title, legend, data_labels, secondary_series (combo only), colors, fallback (table, omit, link) native must be in the slot's native list; fallback applies when the binding fails or the viz is tier 3 table binding_id, columns, max_rows, overflow (truncate, continue, appendix), totals_row, heat_column cells are formatted strings; numeric cells right-aligned kpi value_fact, label, comparison_fact, comparison_label, sparkline_binding the delta color follows the comparison fact's sign text text, role (title, subtitle, heading, body, caption, footer), pinned_note template or user text; may hold tokens and literal digits; pinned_note marks a value a user typed by hand ("edited, not live") narrative purpose, fact_ids, max_chars (default 600), form (paragraph, bullets, headline), text, status (pending, verified, fallback, flagged, user_edited), verify_report, audience_rls_fingerprint LLM prose with tokens only; verified before it ships; user_edited text is never regenerated automatically image asset_ref, alt template assets only, never a capture link label, target (dashboard, chart, explore, page, url), ref links come from templates or bindings, never from LLM output

docs.title: Step 13: Extending Presenton Template v2 with data slots
docs.text: Templates keep Presenton's Template v2 element model for geometry and styling: the discriminated union SlideElement of Text, Container, Image, TextList, Table, Vector, Chart, Infographic, Flex, Grid and Group (presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/models/elements.py:624-640), every element positioned on the fixed 1280 x 720 canvas. On a 16:9 slide that is 9,525 EMU per template unit. Template v2 format documents the base format. Data-Bound Documents makes two additions.

docs.title: 13.1 The data_slot attribute
docs.text:
A data_slot object is added to chart, table and text elements:

databound_docs/templates/slots.py
class DataSlot(_M):
    name: str                                    # "trend", "kpi_1", "takeaway"
    accepts: list[Literal["chart", "table", "kpi", "narrative", "sparkline"]]
    shapes: list[Literal["scalar", "series", "xy", "xyz", "table", "pivot"]] = []
    x_kind: list[Literal["temporal", "categorical", "numeric"]] = []
    series: tuple[int, int] = (1, 8)             # inclusive range
    categories: tuple[int, int] = (1, 24)
    rows: tuple[int, int] = (1, 12)              # tables
    max_chars: int | None = None                 # narratives, from box geometry
    native: list[str] = []                       # allowed ChartElement.native values
    aspect: Literal["wide", "square", "tall"] = "wide"
    optional: bool = False
Field Meaning Checked against name Slot id within the layout; becomes element.slot unique per layout accepts Element types this slot can show the candidate's kind shapes Allowed Shape.kind values the profiled shape x_kind Allowed x axis kinds the x column's GenericDataType series, categories Inclusive count ranges profiled counts; categorical overflow is allowed when top_n can fold into "Other" rows Inclusive row range for tables rowcount and max_rows max_chars Narrative budget the rendered length with tokens replaced by their displays native Allowed native chart types the viz mapping for the candidate's viz_type aspect Box proportion used in layout scoring optional Whether the slot may stay empty layouts with an unfillable mandatory slot are discarded

docs.title: 13.2 The new kpi element
docs.text:
Presenton has no KPI element (its Infographic kinds such as gauge and progress_bar hold LLM-supplied values). DBD adds one to the SlideElement union:

databound_docs/templates/elements_ext.py
from databound_docs.templates.v2_port.elements import Font, Position, Size  # ported from Presenton


class Kpi(BaseModel):
    type: Literal["kpi"]
    position: Optional[Position] = None
    size: Optional[Size] = None
    value_font: Optional[Font] = None
    label_font: Optional[Font] = None
    delta_font: Optional[Font] = None
    layout: Literal["stacked", "inline"] = "stacked"
    show_sparkline: bool = False
    # Schema
    decorative: Literal[False] = False
    name: str
    data_slot: DataSlot                          # accepts ["kpi"], shapes ["scalar"]

The PPTX Renderer draws it as a group named dbd:kpi:<element_id> holding value, label and delta text boxes, plus an optional native LINE sparkline. The ported Presenton ChartSeries also gains typed x values, sizes and dates in DBD's copy, and bubble becomes a real ChartType, fixing the mismatch between the schema's CHART_TYPE_VALUES (which lists "bubble", presenton: servers/fastapi/templates/v2/schema.py:23-36) and the ChartType enum (which does not, elements.py:76-87).

docs.title: 13.3 A layout with data slots
docs.text:
Template tpl_exec_review v3, layout chart_takeaway (abridged)
{
  "id": "chart_takeaway",
  "description": "Title across the top, one chart on the left two thirds, a takeaway on the right",
  "elements": [
    {"type": "text", "name": "title", "decorative": false,
     "position": {"x": 64, "y": 40}, "size": {"width": 1152, "height": 72},
     "runs": [{"text": "Monthly revenue by product line"}], "max_length": 70, "min_length": 10},
    {"type": "chart", "name": "chart", "decorative": false,
     "position": {"x": 64, "y": 136}, "size": {"width": 768, "height": 520},
     "chart_type": "bar", "legend": true, "legend_position": "bottom",
     "data_slot": {"name": "chart", "accepts": ["chart", "table"],
                   "shapes": ["series", "xy"], "x_kind": ["temporal", "categorical"],
                   "series": [1, 8], "categories": [1, 24],
                   "native": ["column", "bar", "line", "area"], "aspect": "wide"}},
    {"type": "text", "name": "takeaway", "decorative": false,
     "position": {"x": 864, "y": 136}, "size": {"width": 352, "height": 520},
     "runs": [{"text": "Takeaway"}], "max_length": 420, "min_length": 40,
     "data_slot": {"name": "takeaway", "accepts": ["narrative"], "max_chars": 420}}
  ]
}

The chart element keeps its Presenton styling fields (chart_type, legend, legend_position), but categories and series are absent: they will never be filled by the LLM. A non-decorative text element without a data_slot (the title here) keeps Presenton's behavior, a string with minLength/maxLength, with one addition: the token-only pattern of Step 14.

docs.title: 13.4 Three ways a slot gets into a template
docs.text:
